rows.basis: [Learners underrate pretesting](claims/metacognitive-illusion-pretesting-underrated.md) [~M]
rows.change: Tell them why it helps; learners rank pretesting as the least effective strategy even when it helps them
rows.if: Learners resist answering questions on material they have not studied

rows.basis: [Active learning improves exam performance](claims/active-learning-improves-exam-performance.md) [+S]; [Lecture students are 1.5 times more likely to fail](claims/lecturing-increases-stem-failure-rates.md) [+M]
rows.change: Replace part of each lecture with tasks learners do in class (questions, problems, predictions, explanations) with feedback on what they produce; expect higher exam scores and fewer failing grades on average
rows.if: An undergraduate STEM course taught mainly by lecture, judged on the course exam and pass rate

rows.basis: [Active learning narrows achievement gaps](claims/active-learning-narrows-achievement-gaps.md) [+S] (two course studies: a disadvantaged-student gap in biology halved, a gender gap in physics closed at the highest dose); [Only high-intensity active learning narrows gaps](claims/high-intensity-active-learning-narrows-gaps.md) [+M]; [Gap effects vary widely across studies](claims/active-learning-gap-effects-vary-across-studies.md) [~M]; [Class size, level and discipline did not explain the variation](claims/class-size-level-discipline-not-significant-moderators.md) [~W] (null moderators, which the authors say are underpowered)
rows.change: Make the activity high-intensity and highly structured (regular graded preparation and in-class work every session), a large share of class time, not an occasional break in lecture; apply it to the whole class rather than to students singled out; track the gap per section, because results varied widely between courses
rows.if: The course has wide gaps in pass rates or exam scores between student groups, and narrowing them is a goal

rows.basis: [Benefits are greatest in classes of 50 or fewer](claims/active-learning-strongest-small-classes.md) [~M]
rows.change: Still convert time to activity, using formats that scale (individual responses, pair discussion, polls); expect a smaller average gain than in classes of 50 or fewer
rows.if: The class is a large lecture (well over 50 students)

rows.basis: [Clicker participation and homework completion each predict exam performance](claims/clicker-participation-and-homework-completion-predict-exam-performance.md) [+M]; [Explanations showing understanding predict exam performance](claims/homework-explanation-quality-predicts-exam-performance.md) [+M]; [No benefit for the lowest quartile](claims/any-clicker-pattern-beats-absence-except-lowest-quartile.md) [~M] (all one observational study of two introductory biology sections; not randomised)
rows.change: Follow each targeted question with a short written explanation of the same question after class, and read the explanations rather than the votes: presence for the question and a completed explanation each predicted the related exam item, an explanation showing understanding predicted it best, and for the lowest-scoring quarter of the class presence alone showed no exam benefit
rows.if: The course uses in-class response questions (clickers, polls)

rows.basis: [Video helps only when its interactivity matches or exceeds the comparison](claims/video-benefit-depends-on-relative-interactivity.md) [~M]; [Self-explanation prompts in video did not help at controlled time](claims/self-explanation-prompts-no-learning-benefit-controlled-time.md) [~M]
rows.change: Keep the learners' activity at least as interactive as what the video replaces (questions that need an answer, discussion, co-viewing with a peer); a video less interactive than the class it replaces showed no benefit. Do not count on embedded self-explanation prompts alone when viewing time is fixed
rows.if: Teaching moves to video or online

rows.basis: [Interactive instruction associated with achievement gains in Chicago](claims/interactive-instruction-positive-achievement-gains-chicago.md) [+W] (teacher-reported instruction; not a comparison of formats)
rows.change: The course-level comparisons above are undergraduate. One associational study across Chicago elementary schools found students of teachers reporting frequent interactive instruction gained about 5% more in a year than the city average in reading and mathematics; treat this as a lead, keep the guidance for novices, and check learning with an independent probe
rows.if: Learners are in primary or secondary school

rows.basis: [High-confidence errors are retained better after correction](claims/high-confidence-errors-improve-retention.md) [~M] (a review and one experiment, read from abstracts; mostly memory for answers, not course concepts)
rows.change: Ask for a committed answer (and, where quick, how sure they are) before explaining, then give immediate corrective feedback; do not steer away from confident wrong answers, since errors made with high confidence are corrected more durably once feedback arrives
rows.if: The activity asks learners to predict or answer before being told

rows.basis: [Minimal guidance is less effective for novices](claims/minimal-guidance-less-effective-for-novices.md) [~M]
rows.change: Give a worked example or short explanation before the task, and scaffolds and feedback during it; do not leave learners to discover the key content unaided
rows.if: Learners are meeting the topic for the first time (`novice`)

rows.basis: [Gains are larger on concept inventories](claims/active-learning-gains-larger-concept-inventories.md) [+M]; [Peer Instruction raised Force Concept Inventory scores at Harvard](claims/fci-gain-increased-peer-instruction-harvard.md) [+M] (one course compared across years, with other refinements added over time)
rows.change: Aim activities at the concepts and misconceptions the inventory targets; expect a larger gain there than on instructor-written exams
rows.if: The outcome that counts is conceptual understanding, measured by a concept inventory

rows.basis: [Content gains but no reasoning gains](claims/reformed-pedagogy-content-gains-but-no-reasoning-gains.md) [~W]
rows.change: Teach and assess the reasoning explicitly; content-focused active engagement alone left reasoning-test gains near zero in one course series
rows.if: The goal is general scientific reasoning, not course content

rows.basis: [Discussion promotes more active thinking; lecture is no worse for information](claims/discussion-promotes-more-active-thought-than-lecture.md) [~W]
rows.change: A clear explanation may do as well; spend the active time on applying, comparing and explaining rather than on receiving the information
rows.if: The goal is mainly to transmit information (terms, facts, a procedure to recognise)

rows.basis: [Constructive learning beats active and passive](claims/constructive-learning-beats-active-passive.md) [~W]; [Self-explanation improves understanding](claims/self-explanation-improves-conceptual-understanding.md) [+M] (immediate tests; delayed and classroom evidence is thin)
rows.change: Prefer tasks that make learners generate beyond the material (explain, predict, compare, justify) and, in pairs, build on each other's ideas, over highlighting or copying
rows.if: The brief asks which activity to use

rows.basis: [Teachers struggled to design constructive and interactive activities](claims/teachers-struggle-designing-interactive-activities.md) [~M]
rows.change: Give them ready-made generative and interactive tasks and review lesson plans with them; teachers trained in the framework rarely produced such tasks on their own
rows.if: The instructors are new to designing active tasks

rows.basis: [Learners in active classes felt they learned less](claims/active-learning-felt-learning-paradox.md) [~W]
rows.change: Tell learners that effortful sessions can feel less productive than a smooth lecture, and judge learning with an independent probe rather than ratings
rows.if: Learners will rate sessions, or the redesign will be judged by course evaluations

rows.basis: [Most comparisons differ on more than one feature](claims/most-comparisons-differ-on-multiple-features.md) [~M]; [Time on task is often unequal](claims/time-on-task-unequal-in-active-learning-comparisons.md) [~M] (in 44% of 59 studies, always with more home time for the active condition); [Active conditions more often add quizzes, homework and exam preparation](claims/active-learning-conditions-more-other-pedagogical-features.md) [~M] (quizzes in 36% of active against 6% of lecture conditions); [Most active conditions keep a substantial lecture component](claims/active-learning-courses-retain-lecture-component.md) [~M] (80% of 88 conditions)
rows.change: Record every feature that changed with the format (quizzes, homework, home study time, instructor) and hold what you can constant; otherwise the gain cannot be credited to the activities. Expect the "active" version to keep a lecture component and to add quizzes, homework and home preparation unless you decide otherwise
rows.if: The redesign will be evaluated against the old course

rows.basis: [Comfort highest for fully structured assignments](claims/nd-comfort-highest-fully-structured-assignments.md) [~W]; [Both groups prefer some instructor involvement](claims/nd-nt-prefer-some-instructor-involvement-in-person.md) [~W]
rows.change: Use fully structured tasks with defined roles and some instructor involvement, in person where possible, and avoid unannounced public presenting
rows.if: Some learners are neurodivergent or find group work hard

rows.basis: [Intelligent tutoring systems improve achievement over non-individualised instruction](claims/adaptive-learning-improves-outcomes.md) [+S]
rows.change: Use a system that selects tasks and step-level feedback from each learner's responses; expect a gain on aligned tests, smaller on standardised ones, and none over a human tutor or a small group
rows.if: The alternative is conventional, non-individualised instruction or a textbook

rows.basis: [Adaptive task difficulty did not improve second-graders' posttest](claims/task-difficulty-adaptation-no-learning-benefit-second-grade.md) [-M]; [The non-adaptive condition reached higher mastery](claims/non-adaptive-condition-higher-mastery-probabilities.md) [-M]
rows.change: Add adaptive support (hints, worked steps, feedback tied to the error) rather than relying on difficulty alone; one trial found difficulty-only adaptation no better than a fixed version, and its mastery gate held learners back
rows.if: The plan adapts only task difficulty, for young learners (early primary)

rows.basis: [Personalized paths reduced learning time and improved post-test scores](claims/personalized-paths-experiment-outcomes.md) [+M]; [Adaptive scaffolding policies improved posttest in a logic tutor](claims/adaptive-icap-scaffolding-improves-posttest-logic-tutor.md) [+M]
rows.change: Diagnose the parts with frequent short items and order each learner's path from the diagnosis; expect time saved as well as a modest post-test gain
rows.if: University learners, a cumulative topic with checkable parts

rows.basis: [Questioning benefit decays with impasse depth](claims/questioning-benefit-decays-with-impasse-depth.md) [+W]; [Repeating a scripted question lowers recovery](claims/repeating-scripted-question-lowers-recovery.md) [+W]
rows.change: Change the support as the impasse persists: after a failed question, address the learner's error rather than repeating the question
rows.if: A tutor (human or AI) responds to learners who are stuck

rows.basis: [Student mastery context improved tutor metrics](claims/student-context-personalization-improves-tutor-metrics.md) [+M]; [Generative AI tutors struggle to infer student knowledge](claims/genai-tutors-struggle-infer-student-knowledge.md) [~M]
rows.change: Pass the learner's mastery estimates for the skill and its prerequisites to the tutor, with an instruction to review weak prerequisites
rows.if: An AI tutor is used, and the platform holds mastery and practice history

rows.basis: [Guidance that helps novices can become redundant as expertise grows](claims/expertise-reversal-effect.md) [~M]; [Fading support promotes the transfer of responsibility](claims/fading-support-promotes-transfer-of-responsibility.md) [+S] (near transfer)
rows.change: Withdraw worked steps and hints as unassisted performance improves, checking unsupported items before each removal
rows.if: Learners improve quickly on a skill

rows.basis: [Constraints selectively affect inefficient strategies](claims/constraints-selectively-affect-inefficient-strategies.md) [~W] (simulated learners, not tested with people)
rows.change: Constrain choice where a learner's selections are inefficient (for example, risk-averse overpractice of mastered skills) and leave efficient selectors free, rather than constraining everyone
rows.if: Learners choose their own next tasks inside a mastery system

rows.basis: [Learning-styles matching does not improve learning](claims/learning-styles-matching-does-not-improve-learning.md) [-S]; in one series of media experiments a voice-plus-diagram format lifted sensing-preference learners above intuitive-preference learners given text, so format, not the match, drove the difference ([Intuitive learners outperform sensing learners](claims/intuitive-learners-outperform-sensing-learners.md) [-W])
rows.change: Adapt on responses to items and on prior knowledge instead
rows.if: The brief proposes adapting to learning styles or stated preferences

rows.basis: [Learner models are miscalibrated outside the data interval](claims/learner-models-miscalibrated-outside-data-interval.md) [~M]
rows.change: Treat estimates at the extremes (very low or very high predicted success) as least reliable: add a teacher check or an unassisted probe before repeated remediation or a fast skip
rows.if: Routing depends on a knowledge-tracing or learner model

rows.basis: [Violating temporal order inflates knowledge-tracing performance](claims/pkt-temporal-causality-violation-inflates-performance.md) [~M]; [A transformer model won EDM Cup 2023 with an AUC of 0.79](claims/transformer-kt-first-place-edm-cup-2023.md) [~M]
rows.change: Ask whether attempts were ordered by time in the evaluation, and how the model is calibrated, not only its AUC; leakage inflates reported accuracy
rows.if: A vendor reports the model's predictive accuracy (AUC)

rows.basis: [Personalized learning effects vary with fidelity](claims/personalized-learning-effects-vary-with-fidelity.md) [~M]; [Adult education programmes used learner data minimally](claims/adult-ed-minimal-learner-data-use.md) [~M]
rows.change: Plan for teachers to read and act on the diagnostic reports, and record use; judge the effect only where the adaptation was used
rows.if: A school or adult programme adopts a platform

rows.basis: [RL reward misalignment failure modes](claims/rl-reward-misalignment-failure-modes.md) [~W]
rows.change: Set the reward on learning measured without support, not on engagement or in-system correctness, and watch for learners who depend on scaffolding
rows.if: The system optimises its own reward (a reinforcement-learning policy)

rows.basis: [The guide treats an effect size of +0.25 or higher as substantively important, equivalent to raising performance at least 10 percentile points](claims/effect-size-025-substantively-important-threshold.md) [+W] (a reporting convention, not tested with readers)
rows.change: Lead with one sentence in percentile points or raw-score difference on a test they know, then the d and its interval; keep the p value in a note
rows.if: The reader is a teacher, leader or purchaser, `novice` at statistics, or has low confidence with numbers

rows.basis: untested proposal; the earlier page's source proposes the Task Force report as a teaching framework
rows.change: Run the four-session arc above; use real published pairs where significance and size disagree as the compared cases
rows.if: The learners are graduate students in educational research (a course on reading studies)

rows.basis: [ITS evaluation results depend strongly on test type: effects are large on locally developed tests (ES = 0.73) and small on standardized tests (ES = 0.13)](claims/test-type-moderates-its-effects.md) [+M]; [Language and early writing interventions showed larger effects on researcher-developed than standardized outcome measures, while phonological awareness, print knowledge, and decoding effects were comparable across measure types](claims/researcher-developed-measures-larger-language-effects.md) [~M] (tutoring systems and early literacy; the gap is not the same for every skill)
rows.change: Report it apart from any standardized outcome; compare its size only with other aligned-test effects; expect a smaller effect on a standardized test
rows.if: The outcome is a researcher-made or aligned test

rows.basis: [Greenwood et al. (1993) reported a statistically significant CWPT effect on CTBS-Reading, but the WWC-corrected analysis was not statistically significant](claims/cwpt-ctbs-effect-significance-discrepancy.md) [+M]; [Clustering effects vary by design but are typically large in education random-assignment evaluations](claims/clustering-effects-large-school-samples-education-trials.md) [+M]
rows.change: Test significance at the level assigned or correct for clustering; report the effect size either way; state the number of clusters
rows.if: The study randomized classes or schools

rows.basis: [The evaluation used a school-level cluster-randomized quasi-experiment (N = 50) that was powered only to detect large effects (d = 0.81)](claims/cluster-randomized-quasi-experiment-powered-for-large-effects.md) [+M] (pre-service teachers; carried to any small pilot)
rows.change: Report the effect size, interval and minimum detectable effect; call a non-significant result inconclusive; plan the next test rather than a verdict
rows.if: A small pilot of one course or class, or a single session only

rows.basis: Large Type M (magnitude) errors almost certainly exist when applying the statistical significance filter in education research [+M]; [Publication-bias assessments substantially reduce the intercept prediction, often indicating no positive transfer when the identified moderators are absent](claims/publication-bias-reduces-intercept-no-transfer-without-moderators.md) [+M] (test-enhanced learning transfer)
rows.change: Discount the reported size; look for a replication, a pre-registered trial or a bias-corrected meta-analytic estimate before adopting
rows.if: The decision rests on one significant study, or on studies found by searching for positive results

rows.basis: [MAB assignment overestimates effect sizes for normally distributed rewards, with greater overestimation for smaller true effects](claims/mab-overestimates-effect-sizes.md) [+M] (simulation)
rows.change: Report that assignment was adaptive and treat the effect size as likely overstated, especially a small one; confirm with a fixed-allocation comparison
rows.if: An online platform assigned learners adaptively (a multi-armed bandit or similar)

rows.basis: [Effect sizes of Pre-K Mathematics decreased over time as the intervention moved through successive scale-up phases](claims/pre-k-math-effect-sizes-decreased-over-scale-up.md) [~M] (one pre-K mathematics program)
rows.change: Expect the scaled effect to be smaller than the pilot's; set the adoption threshold against the scaled estimate, not the pilot's
rows.if: A program moves from pilot to wide use (a district, a state)

rows.basis: [Effect sizes based on mathematics tests are significantly larger than effect sizes based on reading tests in targeted secondary interventions](claims/math-test-effects-larger-than-reading.md) [~M]; [Interventions in higher Grades tend to have somewhat lower effect sizes; other study characteristics show few significant moderator effects](claims/grade-level-moderates-effect-size.md) [~M] (struggling learners, targeted interventions)
rows.change: Compare sizes only within the same subject and grade band; do not rank a mathematics effect above a reading effect on size alone
rows.if: Comparing effects across subjects or grades (a mathematics program against a reading program; primary against secondary)

rows.basis: [Within the explicit morphology instruction group, the pre-to-post gain ratio was above Blake's 1.2 minimum for morphological awareness (1.28) and below it for reading comprehension (1.06)](claims/emi-effect-size-larger-for-awareness-than-comprehension.md) [~M] (one EFL study reporting Blake's modified gain ratio from experimental-group pre-post means)
rows.change: Report the raw means and SDs as well, name the index and its own threshold, and do not compare it with d benchmarks
rows.if: The report uses a non-standard index (a gain ratio, a percentage gain, a pre-post change only)

rows.basis: [Self-regulated learning interventions have a moderate effect (0.65) on learning outcomes in online and blended environments](claims/srl-interventions-moderate-effect-online-blended.md) [~W] (the misreading is quoted on the claim page)
rows.change: Use the error as the worked contrast: show what a d of 0.65 means in percentile points and why it is not a percentage
rows.if: The report says an effect of 0.65 means a 65% improvement, or a reader made that error

rows.basis: [In a randomized trial of SRL interventions in an online mathematics preparation course, group and time interacted significantly on SRL knowledge, self-efficacy and the SRL overall score, with Group TDP (training + diary + peer feedback) showing the most prominent gains](claims/srl-web-training-peer-feedback-group-by-time-interaction-online-math-prep.md) [~W] (reported no per-outcome effect size)
rows.change: Give an effect size per primary outcome, with its interval, beside the omnibus test
rows.if: Several outcomes reported only as a multivariate test or interaction

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Keep it and its categories as given; add only what it lacks among: effect size with interval, comparison, measure type, horizon
rows.if: The brief names its own reporting template, standard or rubric (a journal's, a funder's, the Clearinghouse's)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: One study, 10 minutes extracting the numbers, 15 computing d and the percentile translation, 15 reading it against a supplied reference class, 5 writing the one-sentence verdict
rows.if: A fixed short time budget (a 45-minute professional-development slot for teachers)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Put the numbers in a shared table everyone can see, give the d calculation as a fill-in template, and collect each person's one-sentence translation in writing
rows.if: Mixed modes: some readers in the room, some remote or on phones; or a self-paced online module

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Give a worked example and an answer key so peers check each other's calculations; the facilitator reads only the final translations
rows.if: One facilitator for many teachers, or scarce facilitator time

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Give the translated effect, the comparison and the uncertainty in two sentences; put the effect sizes, intervals and test statistics in an appendix
rows.if: The audience is a board, funder or the public, who should see the conclusion and not the analysis

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Report effect sizes for groups only; suppress cells too small to protect privacy and say so; the learners or institution decide who sees individual results
rows.if: Data are from a small group of identifiable learners (one class, a small program)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Keep it whole: draft the full section once, then revise once against steps 1–8
rows.if: The brief wants a whole results section or evaluation report written, not separate exercises

rows.basis: [Analogical reasoning improves transfer](claims/comparing-contrasting-cases-improves-learning.md) [+M]
rows.change: Give two or more cases that share the principle, side by side, with a prompt to say what is the same and why
rows.if: The goal is using a principle on new cases

rows.basis: [Analogical reasoning improves transfer](claims/comparing-contrasting-cases-improves-learning.md) [+M] (moderator in the meta-analysis)
rows.change: Have learners compare first and state the principle after, connected to what they found
rows.if: The plan states the principle and then gives examples

rows.basis: [Comparing cases side by side improves learning and transfer](claims/comparing-contrasting-cases-improves-learning.md) [+M]
rows.change: Show both cases on one screen and ask for a written description of their similarities; reading the same cases separately gave far less transfer
rows.if: Learners work alone (`online-self-paced`)

rows.basis: [Comparing cases: procedural gain, no conceptual gain in one algebra study](claims/comparing-contrasting-cases-improves-learning.md) [~M]
rows.change: After learners compare solution methods, explain why each method works; comparison raised procedural knowledge and flexibility, not conceptual knowledge
rows.if: The goal is conceptual understanding in mathematics

rows.basis: [Multiple cases from different perspectives support transfer in ill-structured domains](claims/cognitive-flexibility-theory-multiple-cases.md) [~M]
rows.change: Revisit several cases under different themes and plan separate recall practice; transfer rose while factual recall favoured drill
rows.if: The domain is ill structured

rows.basis: [Analogical reasoning improves transfer](claims/comparing-contrasting-cases-improves-learning.md) [~M]
rows.change: Repeat the comparison or retrieve the principle later; benefits were larger on immediate tests
rows.if: The test that matters is delayed

rows.basis: [PAIR-C scaffolding: near-transfer gain, no far transfer](claims/pair-c-scaffolding-shows-mixed-evidence-for-emergent-phenomena-instruction.md) [~W]
rows.change: Add a cross-domain comparison and a fresh case from the far domain; in one study contrasting causal structures gave near but not far transfer
rows.if: Far transfer to another domain is the goal

rows.basis: untested proposal; no claim in the wiki tests a single explanatory analogy
rows.change: Check that learners can reason in the source first, ask them what corresponds to what, and name where the analogy breaks down
rows.if: The plan uses one explanatory analogy from a familiar source (water flow for current)

rows.basis: [Students evaluate GenAI analogies by structural correspondence](claims/students-audit-genai-analogy-structural-correspondence.md) [~W]; [Personalised analogies felt more engaging or memorable](claims/personalized-analogies-more-engaging-memorable.md) [~W]
rows.change: Have learners check the mapping between source and target and name where it breaks; learners found such analogies memorable but flagged specific mismatches
rows.if: Analogies are generated by AI or personalised to learners' interests

rows.basis: [Analogical reasoning improves transfer](claims/comparing-contrasting-cases-improves-learning.md) [+M]; [Comparing cases side by side improves learning and transfer](claims/comparing-contrasting-cases-improves-learning.md) [+M]
rows.change: Use comparison; the experiments recorded here used novice undergraduates (negotiation) and seventh graders (algebra). Supply both cases rather than relying on a source they are assumed to know
rows.if: Learners are novices in the domain of the cases

rows.basis: [Learner highlighting gives a small memory benefit but no reliable comprehension benefit](claims/annotating-improves-learning.md) [~M] (meta-analysis: 0.36 on memory, 0.20 on comprehension)
rows.change: Learner highlighting can stay, but tell readers what the reading is for and check one marked page early; do not expect it to help with understanding the whole text
rows.if: The goal is recall of specific content from a text, tested soon after

rows.basis: [Highlighting shows low utility](claims/highlighting-low-utility.md) [-M] (one primary study found underlining hurt inference questions); [Self-questioning improves comprehension](claims/self-questioning-improves-comprehension.md) [+M] (taught question generation; median 0.36 on standardized tests)
rows.change: Replace free highlighting with one written question or one-sentence summary per section, and teach question generation first (model it, then practise it)
rows.if: The goal is understanding the whole text, or making inferences across it

rows.basis: [Learner highlighting helped college students but not school students; instructor-supplied highlighting improved memory and comprehension](claims/annotating-improves-learning.md) [~M] (0.24 for school students; 0.44 for instructor highlighting)
rows.change: Do not assign unguided highlighting. Supply the key sentences already marked, and add a task that uses them (answer, explain, or ask a question about each)
rows.if: Learners are school students (`pre-k-12`)

rows.basis: [Test performance follows whatever is underlined, relevant or not](claims/relevancy-of-emphasis-directs-attention.md) [~M] (67 college freshmen, immediate test); the codes and the check are untested proposals
rows.change: Give the reading purpose and three to five margin codes (`?`, `claim`, `evidence`), mark the first paragraph together, and check that the marks fall on the main claims before readers go on alone
rows.if: Learners are `novice` on the topic and have no criteria for what matters

rows.basis: [Student-generated underlining was not significantly better than experimenter underlining](claims/experimenter-underlining-effective-as-student-underlining.md) [~M]; [Signaling essential content improves transfer from multimedia lessons](claims/signaling-principle-mayer-2008.md) [+M] (6 of 6 experiments, median d = 0.52)
rows.change: Mark only the content the outcomes and the test address; add headings and an overview; leave incidental detail unmarked
rows.if: The instructor can mark the text for learners (prepared readings, slides, a pre-highlighted edition)

rows.basis: [Scaffolded close reading improves comprehension for struggling readers](claims/scaffolded-close-reading-improves-comprehension-for-struggling-readers.md) [+M] (a package; annotation is one part and its share of the effect is not known)
rows.change: Use a close-reading routine across several weeks: annotate a short text, reread it, answer text-dependent questions, discuss
rows.if: Learners are struggling readers in middle or secondary school

rows.basis: [Prompting learners to self-explain improves understanding](claims/self-explanation-improves-conceptual-understanding.md) [+M] (g = .55, immediate tests; prompted explanation, not margin notes as such)
rows.change: Prompt a short explanation at each section ("why does this follow?", "how does this connect to the last section?") written in the margin, not a copied phrase
rows.if: Readers are asked to explain the text in their own words

rows.basis: [Summarizing each source did not beat rereading twice for integrated essays](claims/summarization-improves-learning.md) [~M] (295 adults; better summaries went with better essays)
rows.change: Do not require a summary of each source as the annotation; let readers reread, and if they do summarise, check the quality of the summaries before the essay
rows.if: The reading feeds an essay written from several sources

rows.basis: [Laptop note-takers transcribed more verbatim; a replication found no consistent difference](claims/laptop-notes-verbatim-shallower.md) [~M] (lecture notes, not text annotation)
rows.change: Ask for paraphrase, questions and links rather than copied text; do not ban devices on the strength of this evidence
rows.if: Learners annotate or take notes on laptops or tablets

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Put a question box after each section of the reader instead of relying on a highlighter, and show the learner's own questions back to them before the end-of-unit check
rows.if: Setting is `online-self-paced` with a digital text

rows.basis: untested proposal; the wiki has no claim on whether annotations used in a later discussion or essay improve it
rows.change: Ask for two annotated passages to bring as evidence, and begin the discussion from them; check afterwards whether learners used their notes
rows.if: A seminar, discussion or writing task follows the reading

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Give one reading purpose, have learners mark and annotate a short passage, then use the marks at once (pairs compare and answer two questions); do not promise lasting gains
rows.if: Only one session

rows.basis: [Instructional guidance that helps novices can become redundant or counterproductive as expertise grows.](claims/expertise-reversal-effect.md) [~M] (review of cognitive-load studies, not consultations; gives no crossover point)
rows.change: Drop the explanation and modelling steps; the learner presents work and their own critique, and the expert adds only what the learner missed; use peer critique between consultations
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` on this task, or already self-diagnose most errors

rows.basis: [Contingent scaffolding improves learning more than fixed or absent support.](claims/contingent-scaffolding-improves-learning.md) [+M] (fourth and fifth graders, long division, 8 per condition, one-to-one)
rows.change: Keep the consultation one-to-one or with two or three children, short (10 minutes), on one problem, with the expert moving up the question–hint–model ladder and back down after each success
rows.if: Learners are `child` (primary age)

rows.basis: [Mentor modelling and a school-wide behaviour program's strategies transferred to the mentee's classroom management practices](claims/mentor-modelling-strategies-transfer-mentee-behaviour-management.md) [+W] (one preservice teacher, qualitative case study)
rows.change: Hold consultations on real cases from the learner's work; the mentor models the decision on one case, then observes the learner on the next and debriefs; plan when the mentor stops being present
rows.if: Learners are `adult` professionals or trainees in a `workplace-clinical` setting

rows.basis: [Contingent scaffolding improves learning more than fixed or absent support.](claims/contingent-scaffolding-improves-learning.md) [+M] (interactive tutoring gave better transfer with similar immediate scores) and [Human tutoring has a medium effect over no tutoring, and in one small study students learned as well when tutors only prompted them as when tutors also explained and gave feedback](claims/tutoring-effectiveness-comes-from-scaffolding-and-feedback.md) [~M] (eighth graders, circulatory system)
rows.change: Have the expert ask and prompt more and explain less; include one changed problem in each consultation for the learner to reason through aloud
rows.if: Goal is a `concept`, `principle` or transfer, not only a `procedure`

rows.basis: untested proposal; content expertise alone did not predict learning in one meta-regression of problem-based-learning tutors ([In a re-analysis of PBL tutor-background data, neither a meta-regression nor subgroup comparisons found that tutor expertise predicts student learning](claims/tutor-background-meta-regression-not-predictive.md) [~M], PBL tutors, not guest experts)
rows.change: Brief them for ten minutes: ask the learner to explain first, give a hint before an answer, think aloud about what they notice; pair them with the course teacher, who manages questions and follow-up
rows.if: The expert is a content specialist or practitioner with no teaching experience (guest, clinician, engineer)

rows.basis: [In two secondary-school writing studies, peer reviewers' own performance predicted how helpful their feedback was but not how accurately it identified problems](claims/peer-feedback-accuracy-depends-on-expertise.md) [~M] (secondary and AP English writing: peers' expertise predicted helpfulness, not accuracy; with a well-specified rubric, accuracy did not differ by school performance)
rows.change: Give the peer a rubric and annotated strong and weak examples, ask for comments tied to criteria, and keep the instructor's review for conceptual errors
rows.if: The "expert" is a more knowledgeable peer

rows.basis: untested proposal; human and intelligent tutoring had similar effects over no tutoring in one review read from its abstract ([tutoring claim](claims/tutoring-effectiveness-comes-from-scaffolding-and-feedback.md) [~M])
rows.change: Use an asynchronous question queue: each question carries the learner's attempt; the expert answers the commonest ones with a recorded think-aloud and the rest in writing within a set time (say two working days); add an adaptive tutor or worked-feedback items for routine steps
rows.if: Setting is `online-self-paced`, no expert live

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Keep remote learners in the live exchange rather than giving them a recorded or written reply afterwards: take their prepared questions first, pair each with an in-room partner who describes what the expert is showing and relays follow-ups, and ask the expert to say aloud what they see, check and rule out
rows.if: Some learners join remotely (video or phone) while others are in the room with the expert

rows.basis: untested proposal; drop-in tutoring visits were usually unrelated to course grades in one observational study ([Tutoring center visits usually showed no significant difference in individual course performance, and sometimes tutored students performed worse](claims/tutoring-visits-no-course-grade-advantage.md) [~M], college tutoring centre, self-selected visitors)
rows.change: Collect question cards in advance, triage them, spend open time on the commonest stalls with a think-aloud, and book short individual slots for learners who have not come; do not count attendance as evidence of benefit
rows.if: `classroom` with one expert and a large group (office hours, drop-in)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Collect learners' questions beforehand and send them to the expert; spend the session on the expert's reasoning about two or three of them; set a follow-up task within a week that applies one point, reviewed by the course teacher; do not claim lasting change
rows.if: Time is one session only (a guest visit, a site visit)

rows.basis: [Passing individual microphones discouraged some students from asking questions during telelectures](claims/microphone-use-discourages-student-questions.md) [~W] (one 1972 course, students' reports); otherwise untested
rows.change: Accept written or anonymous questions, consult in pairs or small groups, give question stems; avoid formats that put one person on the spot in front of everyone
rows.if: Learners have low confidence, low status in the group, or are working in a second language

rows.basis: untested proposal; the staging follows [fading support](claims/fading-support-promotes-transfer-of-responsibility.md) [~S], which was tested on worked examples, not supervision
rows.change: Judge readiness on observed unaided performance on representative tasks, not on how well the learner discusses them with the expert; withdraw the expert's presence in stages (present, then on call, then reviewing afterwards)
rows.if: Stakes are high (licensure, patient or client safety)

rows.basis: untested proposal; one small comparison found fewer mentored than unmentored new teachers reached the most developed concern level and raised whether mentors held mentees back ([Teachers without mentors reached the impact level more often than mentored teachers, raising the question that mentoring may inhibit development](claims/mentors-may-inhibit-concern-development.md) [~W], associational, 39 teachers)
rows.change: Plan from the start when the mentor will ask more and tell less, and check at the midpoint whether the mentee is proposing their own solutions
rows.if: A long mentoring relationship (a year, a probation period)

rows.basis: [Assessment for learning improves achievement](claims/assessment-for-learning-improves-achievement.md) [+M]
rows.change: Gather evidence during the unit and use it before the unit test; expect a small overall gain, larger where learners self-assess
rows.if: School classes (`pre-k-12`), with achievement as the goal

rows.basis: [Self-assessment improves self-regulated learning](claims/self-assessment-improves-self-regulated-learning.md) [+M]; [Rubric-referenced self-assessment improved work](claims/rubrics-improve-student-work.md) [~M]
rows.change: Show the criteria with an exemplar before the attempt, have learners self-assess a draft, then revise
rows.if: Learners will judge their own work against criteria

rows.basis: [Self-assessment accuracy is low without training](claims/self-assessment-accuracy-is-low-without-training.md) [~M]; [Prior knowledge needed for accurate self-assessment](claims/prior-knowledge-needed-for-accurate-self-assessment.md) [~M]
rows.change: Train self-assessment with modelling examples before relying on it, and check self-ratings against scored work
rows.if: Learners are novices, or the tasks are unfamiliar

rows.basis: [Low-stress team-based learning format scored higher](claims/low-stress-tbl-higher-isat-scores.md) [~W]; [Formative assessment implementation barriers](claims/formative-assessment-implementation-barriers.md) [~W]
rows.change: Separate the formative evidence from the grade and lower the stakes on in-class checks; the one comparison in the wiki is confounded
rows.if: Assessment evidence will carry marks or be high-stakes

rows.basis: [Peer and self-assessment improve performance equally](claims/peer-self-assessment-improve-performance-equally.md) [+W]; [Peer assessment improves performance](claims/peer-assessment-improves-performance.md) [+M]
rows.change: Add peer assessment; its effect is about the same as self-assessment and does not depend on a fixed rubric
rows.if: Peers can review each other's work

rows.basis: [Diagnostic review gave larger writing gains](claims/diagnostic-review-larger-writing-gains.md) [+W]; [Group-by-cycle interactions for formative outcomes](claims/group-cycle-interactions-formative-outcomes.md) [~M]
rows.change: Schedule a diagnose–revise step in each cycle and judge the outcome after revision
rows.if: The course has repeated drafts (writing, projects)

rows.basis: [Formative assessment with explicit-reflective instruction gave higher post-test scores](claims/formative-assessment-embedded-explicit-reflective-higher-posttest-nos-sks.md) [+W]; [Higher retention four weeks later](claims/formative-assessment-embedded-explicit-reflective-higher-retention-nos-sks.md) [+W]
rows.change: Embed formative checks with reflection in the explicit instruction, and recheck four weeks later
rows.if: Pre-service teachers learning concepts such as the nature of science

rows.basis: [AI and teacher feedback gave equal project gains](claims/ai-teacher-feedback-equal-project-performance-gains.md) [~M]; [Reflective feedback beat direct GenAI feedback on delayed transfer](claims/agentic-designs-delayed-ai-free-transfer.md) [~M]; [Rubric-based AI feedback scaffolded learning and reduced teacher workload, per the authors](claims/rubric-ai-feedback-scaffolds-and-reduces-workload.md) [+W] (authors' interpretation, untested)
rows.change: AI feedback can match teacher feedback on a group project; prefer prompts that ask learners to reflect over handing them corrections
rows.if: Feedback will come from AI rather than the teacher

rows.basis: [Teacher feedback moves learning forward](claims/teacher-feedback-moves-learning-forward.md) [+W]
rows.change: Use the same cycle, with criteria and feedback in language the learners can act on
rows.if: English learners

rows.basis: [Students experience placement as a one-day isolated event with little advance information](claims/placement-perceived-one-shot-deal.md) [-W] (describes experience, no outcome measured)
rows.change: Treat it as summative: tell learners beforehand what it covers and what it decides, and gather formative evidence elsewhere; a single sitting offers no revision step
rows.if: The assessment is a one-off entry or placement test

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Make self-ratings private and ungraded, and compare them with an ungraded task before drawing conclusions
rows.if: Competitive or norm-graded classroom culture

rows.basis: [Authentic audiences improve student work](claims/authentic-audiences-improve-student-work.md) [+M] (two within-subject comparisons, grade 7 n=44 and grade 2; rated product quality only, no effect size)
rows.change: Address the piece to real outside readers on the same topic (a class in another school, a partner group) who will reply; keep the teacher's grade as a separate check
rows.if: A writing task in primary or middle school, normally written for the teacher's grade

rows.basis: [Learning by teaching improves tutor learning](claims/learning-by-teaching-improves-tutor-learning.md) [+M] (preparing and teaching: g = 0.56 on the tutor's domain knowledge; a teaching audience, not a publication audience)
rows.change: Have learners prepare to explain the material to a real audience of peers and then teach it with questions, rather than only produce a product
rows.if: The goal is content learning, measured apart from the product

rows.basis: [Public versus private reflection shows mixed effects](claims/public-vs-private-reflection-mixed.md) [~M] (one service-learning comparison, not randomised: 64% of private and 41% of public paragraphs analytic or integrative)
rows.change: Keep the analytic reflection private; make a shorter public post optional or a separate task
rows.if: The task is reflective writing (journals, service-learning reflection)

rows.basis: [Audience prior knowledge determines information density](claims/audience-prior-knowledge-determines-information-density.md) [+W] (an argument); [Skilled EFL writers keep readers in mind](claims/skilled-writers-audience-awareness.md) [+W] (nine skilled writers, no comparison)
rows.change: Add an audience-analysis step before drafting: who will read it, what they already know, and therefore what background must be given
rows.if: Learners are `novice` writers who write as if for the teacher

rows.basis: [Peer feedback improves writing](claims/peer-feedback-improves-writing.md) [+M] (higher education; large against no feedback, comparable to teacher feedback)
rows.change: Give peers the criteria and a structured feedback form, and require a revision in response before the final audience sees the work
rows.if: Peers will be the first audience and can respond

rows.basis: [Process writing improves writing quality](claims/process-writing-improves-writing-quality.md) [+M] (grades 1–12, ES = 0.34); [Rubric-referenced self-assessment improved essays](claims/rubrics-improve-student-work.md) [+M] (two non-randomised studies; rubric use also raised reported stress)
rows.change: Build at least one draft, response and revision cycle before sharing; publish criteria that say what a strong product looks like for this audience
rows.if: There is time for drafts

rows.basis: [Process writing gave no significant gain for struggling writers](claims/process-writing-improves-writing-quality.md) [~M]; the explicit-teaching addition is an untested proposal here
rows.change: Do not rely on the audience and the process cycle alone; add explicit teaching of planning and revising
rows.if: Learners are struggling writers

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Start with a small, known audience (one partner class, a closed group) and offer an anonymous or private option with the same reader-facing task; obtain consent before anything is public
rows.if: Learners are anxious about exposure, are minors, or the work is personal

rows.basis: [Public capstone showcases gave students an authentic audience](claims/public-capstone-epportfolio-showcase-audience-effect.md) [+W] (programme case report, self-report, no comparison)
rows.change: Announce the public showcase at the start of the course so it shapes earlier assignments; invite departmental and campus guests and collect their feedback
rows.if: A capstone or end-of-programme course in higher education

rows.basis: [Presenting prototypes to community partners created accountability beyond the grade](claims/community-presentation-created-accountability-pressure.md) [+W] (student reflections, one course)
rows.change: Co-plan the task with the partner, and have learners present a prototype to them before the final version
rows.if: The brief names a community partner

rows.basis: [Project-based learning improves achievement](claims/project-based-learning-improves-achievement.md) [+M] (meta-analysis against traditional instruction; moderated by subject, hours and IT support)
rows.change: Frame the unit as a project with a driving problem and a product someone outside the class will use, and allow enough instructional hours for it
rows.if: The brief asks for a real-world purpose rather than an audience (a project or a problem)

rows.basis: [Spontaneous responsiveness to real events can deepen inquiry](claims/spontaneous-authenticity-in-pbl-deepens-student-directed-inquiry.md) [~W] (one grade-3 classroom, an experienced teacher)
rows.change: Let the inquiry follow the event for a few lessons, then connect it back to the unit's goals
rows.if: A real event arises that matters to the learners, and the teacher has room to depart from the plan

rows.basis: [Autonomy support increases intrinsic motivation and engagement](claims/autonomy-supports-intrinsic-motivation.md) [+M]; [Autonomy-supportive versus controlling teaching](claims/autonomy-support-versus-controlling-teaching.md) [+W]
rows.change: Offer choices that change how the objective is reached (topic, medium, order), give a reason for required work, and use informational rather than controlling language
rows.if: The goal is sustained voluntary engagement or persistence with the subject

rows.basis: [Expected tangible rewards reduce later free-choice engagement](claims/rewards-undermine-intrinsic-motivation.md) [~M]
rows.change: Drop rewards for merely doing the task; keep feedback about competence, which did not undermine engagement
rows.if: The plan uses points, prizes or other tangible rewards for doing a task learners already find interesting

rows.basis: [Praise for intelligence undermines motivation after failure](claims/feedback-praise-reduces-learning.md) [~M]; [Intelligence praise against effort praise](claims/feedback-praise-reduces-learning.md) [~M]
rows.change: Praise the effort or strategy used, not the learner's intelligence
rows.if: Praise is part of the routine (children, after success)

rows.basis: [Learner pacing helped on complex material; learner control in general showed almost no effect](claims/learner-paced-beats-system-paced-complex-material.md) [~M]
rows.change: Do not expect control in general to raise achievement; if any control is given, give control of pace on complex, high element-interactivity material
rows.if: The goal is achievement, and the plan is to give learners control of the software or sequence

rows.basis: [Deciding on feedback after the trial improved motor retention](claims/self-controlled-kr-decided-after-trial-improves-motor-retention.md) [~M]; [Deciding only before the trial showed no benefit](claims/self-controlled-kr-decided-before-trial-shows-no-benefit-over-yoked.md) [~M]
rows.change: Let them ask after they have seen how an attempt went, not decide in advance; check whether this carries over from the motor task it was found on
rows.if: Learners can ask for feedback or hints during practice

rows.basis: [Not all students in connectivist courses could direct their own learning](claims/connectivist-courses-student-agency-problems.md) [~M]
rows.change: Keep the choice of topic or project, but supply a plan, milestones and a few vetted options; teach planning as in [Self-Regulated Learning](principles/self-regulated-learning.md)
rows.if: An open, self-directed course with little structure (`online-self-paced`, MOOC-style)

rows.basis: bounded choice is an untested proposal, bounded by [connectivist courses](claims/connectivist-courses-student-agency-problems.md) [~M]; [Process goals beat outcome goals for novices](claims/process-goals-outperform-outcome-goals-for-novices.md) [~M] (assigned goals, carried to choice untested)
rows.change: Offer two or three options that target the same objective, model how to choose, and widen the options as unsupported performance improves; state process goals (the steps to attend to) early, outcome goals once the skill holds
rows.if: Learners are new to the task (`novice`) and the brief asks for wide choice

rows.basis: [Autonomy at one level may inhibit another](claims/autonomy-at-one-level-may-inhibit-another.md) [~W]; [Orthographic mastery needs instruction](claims/orthographic-autonomy-requires-instruction.md) [~W]; [Big-book reading and cognitive autonomy](claims/big-book-reading-cognitive-autonomy.md) [+W]; [Co-construction with the teacher as scribe](claims/co-construction-scribe-teacher-fosters-composition-autonomy.md) [+W]; all from one report, argument and teacher report, no comparison
rows.change: Distinguish choosing *which activity* from thinking for oneself *within* it. Keep teacher-led activities in which children make their own connections (an open shared reading of a big book, a text the children compose with the teacher as scribe), and keep explicit teaching of the spelling system; do not rely on free choice of activity to reach it
rows.if: Young children (`child`, about five) in early literacy, and the brief asks for child-chosen activities

rows.basis: [Scaffolding and autonomy form self-reinforcing patterns](claims/scaffolding-autonomy-dynamics-form-self-reinforcing-attractor-states.md) [~M] (three music-lesson cases, carried to other tuition untested)
rows.change: Keep offering choices and reasons in explanatory rather than directive language for several sessions before judging; raise autonomy support in steps, not in one jump; watch a learner with little wish for control, whose pair may drift into a teacher-led pattern
rows.if: One-to-one tuition or coaching over many sessions, and the learner resists early choices

rows.basis: [Student-led discussion groups sustained online participation](claims/student-led-discussion-task-sustains-online-participation.md) [+W]; [The redesigned unit engaged students on all framework elements](claims/redesigned-unit-engaged-all-framework-elements.md) [+W] (one 40-student unit, one week compared with another, no learning measure)
rows.change: Give small groups a student-led discussion task: rotating leaders choose the topic, run the discussion and post a summary, and the task is assessed
rows.if: Online course in which discussion converges on the teacher (`online-instructor-led`, asynchronous boards)

rows.basis: [Teachers and students favoured shared over full student control](claims/claim-shared-control-roles-and-content.md) [~M]; [Collaboration starting when students signal readiness was preferred](claims/claim-collab-starts-when-students-ready.md) [~M] (stated preferences in a tool-design study, not outcomes)
rows.change: Share the decision: the teacher forms groups and learners choose roles, the teacher sets the collaboration content, and collaboration starts when learners signal they are ready
rows.if: Group work where learners might pick partners, roles or start times

rows.basis: [External mandate showed no direct relationship with deep revision](claims/external-mandate-no-direct-effect-deep-revision.md) [~M] (associational; no equivalence test)
rows.change: Explain why the tool helps and leave learners room in how they use it; do not count on the mandate to produce deep use: in one survey, a mandate showed no detectable direct link to deep revision
rows.if: Use of a tool (an AI writing assistant, a platform) is mandated and monitored

rows.basis: [Teacher support benefits depend on balance with student autonomy](claims/teacher-support-benefits-conditional-on-autonomy-balance.md) [~M]
rows.change: Use the teacher's support for motivation, and leave learners some unsupported problem solving
rows.if: A teacher is present in an AI-based or technology-rich lesson

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Add a learning measure at the stated horizon; enjoyment of a choice does not show that learning improved
rows.if: Success will be judged by satisfaction or enjoyment surveys

rows.basis: [Building empathy improves intergroup attitudes](claims/building-empathy-improves-intergroup-attitudes.md) [+M] (grades 4–6, cluster-randomised: about a third of an SD, up to 8–13 weeks)
rows.change: Run a programme over several weeks: first-person accounts from members of the group, each followed by a discussion of their perspective and of how much the group varies; measure attitudes again weeks later
rows.if: The goal is better attitudes towards a particular group, in a school class

rows.basis: [Building empathy improves intergroup attitudes](claims/building-empathy-improves-intergroup-attitudes.md) [~M] (a review of 418 experiments: most test light-touch interventions whose long-term impact is unclear)
rows.change: Use one concrete account, a prompt to take the person's perspective, and a comparison of readings; do not promise lasting attitude change, and re-measure later if you can
rows.if: Only one session or a single exercise

rows.basis: [The classroom programme raised attitudes but not registration for a contact event](claims/building-empathy-improves-intergroup-attitudes.md) [~M]; [Intergroup contact reduces prejudice](claims/diverse-schools-social-and-civic-benefits.md) [+W] (a meta-analysis cited in a policy report)
rows.change: Add a real, structured contact opportunity with the group, and measure the behaviour separately from attitude ratings
rows.if: The goal is behaviour (contact, cooperation, inclusion), not only attitudes

rows.basis: [Reading fiction gives at most a very small gain on theory-of-mind tasks](claims/reading-literary-fiction-improves-theory-of-mind.md) [~M] (g = .15–.16; a single literary passage showed no advantage in a 792-adult replication)
rows.change: Pair the reading with discussion and a written perspective task; do not expect a single passage to change social-cognitive performance
rows.if: The plan relies on reading a story, novel extract or film alone

rows.basis: [For the most stigmatized group the effect was weak at once and appeared 1–2 weeks later](claims/building-empathy-improves-intergroup-attitudes.md) [~M] (laboratory experiments with adults)
rows.change: Expect little change straight after the activity; avoid framing that asks learners to approve of the group; check again one to two weeks later
rows.if: The group is highly stigmatized for these learners

rows.basis: [SEL programmes improve social-emotional skills](claims/sel-programs-improve-social-emotional-skills.md) [+M] (ages 2–6: d = 0.30 social, 0.54 emotional competence); [Pretend play facilitates perspective taking](claims/pretend-play-facilitates-perspective-taking-abstract-thought.md) [+W] (a review)
rows.change: Use role-play and pretend play with adult support, inside a sequenced social-emotional curriculum, rather than discussion of perspectives
rows.if: Learners are young children (preschool or early primary)

rows.basis: [SEL programs improve social-emotional skills](claims/sel-programs-improve-social-emotional-skills.md) [+M]; [SEL benefits persist at follow-up](claims/sel-benefits-persist-follow-up.md) [+M] (empathy is not isolated in either)
rows.change: Choose a sequenced, active, focused and explicit programme, with perspective-taking taught as one skill among several; follow outcomes over the next year
rows.if: A school-wide or year-long programme

rows.basis: [A brief empathic-discipline exercise for teachers cut suspensions](claims/brief-intervention-empathic-discipline-cuts-suspensions.md) [+M] (middle-school teachers; the preregistered replication's overall effect was small and marginal, larger for previously suspended students)
rows.change: Give a brief online exercise on an empathic rather than punitive mindset about discipline, with students' own accounts of being disciplined
rows.if: The learners are teachers or staff who discipline students

rows.basis: [Students perceive that interaction in experiential learning fosters empathy](claims/students-interaction-empathy-perspective-taking.md) [+W] (12 interviews, self-report); [One-on-one contact with community partners disrupts stereotypes](claims/csl-one-on-one-partner-contact-disrupts-stereotypes.md) [+W] (a partner's report)
rows.change: Build in one-to-one contact with the people served and a structured reflection on what the learner understood of their view
rows.if: Higher education or adult learners in experiential programmes (practicums, service learning, study abroad)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Use recorded first-person accounts, a written summary of the speaker's view that the learner checks against the speaker's own words, and a private before-and-after rating
rows.if: Setting is `online-self-paced`

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Separate understanding from agreement: the learner first summarises the other view in terms its holder would accept, and only then states their own position
rows.if: The topic is politically or personally charged for these learners

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Add a measure not tied to the activity, taken at a delay, and an optional behavioural choice; self-report straight after an activity whose aim is obvious is open to demand
rows.if: Success is to be judged by self-reported empathy right after the activity

rows.basis: [SWPBIS and bullying](claims/swpbis-reduces-growth-teacher-reported-bullying.md) [+M]; [SWPBIS and peer rejection](claims/swpbis-reduces-growth-peer-rejection.md) [+M] (group-randomised trial, 37 Maryland elementary schools, teacher ratings)
rows.change: Adopt a schoolwide positive behaviour framework as the climate layer, keep it for four years, and track teacher-rated bullying and peer rejection each year against the expected rise
rows.if: Whole school, primary age (`child`), goal is less bullying over several years

rows.basis: [RWSA](claims/rwsa-hong-kong-less-bullying-empathy-gains.md) [+M] (quasi-experiment, grades 7–9, four Hong Kong schools, reported in a review)
rows.change: Implement a restorative whole-school approach in full (not partly), for two years, and measure student-reported bullying, empathy and self-esteem
rows.if: Secondary age (`adolescent`), goal is less bullying and more empathy

rows.basis: [Playworks, recess bullying](claims/playworks-reduced-teacher-reported-recess-bullying.md) [+M] (randomised experiment, teacher reports, no effect size printed)
rows.change: Organise recess with adult- or older-learner-led inclusive games and more adults outside; record incidents by place and time
rows.if: Incidents cluster at recess or lunch

rows.basis: [REMind, self-efficacy](claims/remind-increased-self-efficacy-for-defending.md) [+M] and [REMind, reflections](claims/remind-qualitative-perspective-taking-themes.md) [+M] (18 children aged 9–10, one pre/post play-test, no control); untested for actual defending
rows.change: Rehearse defending in role-play with comforting and getting help as options beside confronting; begin with fictional or robot characters
rows.if: Learners watch bullying but do not act, saying they are not confident or are afraid

rows.basis: [restorative responses need trained facilitators](claims/rj-bullying-response-requires-trained-facilitators.md) [~W] (narrative review)
rows.change: Meet them separately first; use a restorative meeting only with a trained facilitator and the target's free agreement, and offer another route
rows.if: The school wants to bring the two learners together to resolve it

rows.basis: [perceived severity predicts reaction](claims/perceived-severity-predicts-teacher-reaction.md) [+M] and [verbal rated more serious than relational](claims/verbal-rated-more-serious-than-relational-aggression.md) [~M] (Romanian teachers, survey; associational and descriptive)
rows.change: Run the staff case-sorting session with relational cases; agree one first response per case
rows.if: Staff disagree on what counts, or ignore exclusion and rumours

rows.basis: [IEP youth, bullying](claims/iep-youth-bullying-suspension-engagement.md) [+M] (national survey, associational); [ASD and cyberbullying](claims/asd-teens-cyberbullying-targets-missed-cues.md) [+W] (expert brief)
rows.change: Teach what bullying is, when and whom to tell, with frequent short conversations and agreed online rules with the family; check in with them directly rather than waiting for reports
rows.if: Learners with an IEP or autism

rows.basis: [transgender students](claims/transgender-students-twice-likely-bullying-fear.md) [+M] (California survey, associational); [gaps converged after SWPRD](claims/swprd-converged-bullying-perceptions.md) [+M] (one school, reported in a review, no statistics)
rows.change: Break every count down by group; add staff training and positive and restorative discipline schoolwide; check whether the gap closes
rows.if: Transgender, LGBTQ or racially minoritised learners report more bullying

rows.basis: untested proposal, from the earlier page
rows.change: Add the cyberbullying steps: save evidence, report to the platform, agree family contact, act when it affects school; teach these to learners as a short routine
rows.if: Bullying is online or on phones (`online`, phone-only)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Give remote learners a private written reporting route and a named adult; run bystander scenarios with chat and polls so remote learners choose moves too; watch the class chat as a supervised space
rows.if: Learners join remotely while others are in the room

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Keep the response sequence (step 6) and an anonymous reporting route first; use trained older learners to lead recess games and short scenarios; review reports weekly in 15 minutes
rows.if: One adult for a large group, or scarce facilitator time (volunteers, a counsellor with a short slot)

rows.basis: untested proposal; the controlled evidence comes from two- to four-year schoolwide programmes
rows.change: Do not call it a programme or expect less bullying: 10 minutes on the definition and roles, 20 minutes rehearsing two defending moves in one scenario, 10 minutes on how and where to report, 5 minutes for anonymous questions
rows.if: A single session or a fixed short slot (for example 45 minutes)

rows.basis: untested proposal; the REMind reflections point to low confidence as a reason for inaction ([REMind, reflections](claims/remind-qualitative-perspective-taking-themes.md) [~M]), carried from 9–10-year-olds
rows.change: Rehearse moves by acting them out, not by writing; use pictures or puppets for scenarios; accept a spoken or drawn report
rows.if: Learners have low confidence or low literacy

rows.basis: untested proposal; every claim here is about school-age learners
rows.change: Use the same definition and roles with cases from their own workplace; the organisation's own policy is the response sequence; reporting routes outside the line manager
rows.if: Adults in a work setting (staff, apprentices, a workplace)

rows.basis: untested proposal (wave-5 rule), with the claims in the rows above
rows.change: Keep it as given; change only what the evidence here says matters: schoolwide and multi-year reach, supervised unstructured times, rehearsed defending, and counts by group
rows.if: The brief names its own programme, survey, reporting form or behaviour policy

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: The target decides who is told and whether it is discussed; scenarios in class are anonymised or fictional; records are kept by the named adult only
rows.if: Reports are private or sensitive (named learners, sexual or identity-based bullying)

rows.basis: [CSTAG](claims/cstag-causal-reduces-discipline-increases-counseling.md) [+M] (randomised studies of a threat-assessment model, reported in a review; its entries report counselling and suspension, not bullying); [shooters not bullied loners](claims/shooters-not-bullied-loners.md) [~M] (review)
rows.change: Refer to the school's threat-assessment or mental-health route at once; prefer counselling and a parent conference to exclusion; do not treat bullying as the whole explanation
rows.if: A student makes a threat of violence, or a target shows signs of depression or suicidal thinking

rows.basis: [fear reduction and graduation](claims/bullying-fear-reduction-raises-graduation-rates.md) [+M]; [larger for previously victimised students](claims/bullying-reduction-effects-larger-for-prior-victimized-students.md) [+M]; [supportive environment](claims/supportive-environment-predicts-bullying-fear-reduction.md) [+M] (one Chicago study; the last is associational)
rows.change: Track students' fear of bullying and the school's supportive environment as leading measures; give most attention to students who were afraid of bullying on arrival
rows.if: Goal is attendance or graduation in high school

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Keep the product whole and real, and pair it with rehearsed defending and the reporting routes; do not count a campaign alone as prevention
rows.if: Learners make a product for a real audience (an anti-bullying campaign, a performance for younger classes)

rows.basis: [Positive Action, behaviour](claims/positive-action-positive-effects-behavior.md) [+M] (two elementary studies, 56 schools, WWC domain average 0.51); [Caring School Community, behaviour](claims/csc-potentially-positive-behavior-effects.md) [+M] (two K–6 studies, +8 percentile points, rated with reservations)
rows.change: Adopt a schoolwide programme with several components (classroom lessons, schoolwide climate, family involvement) and keep it for more than a year; record conduct, violence and absence from the start
rows.if: Whole school, primary age (`child`), goal is fewer conduct problems

rows.basis: [Caring School Community: no discernible academic effects](claims/csc-no-discernible-academic-effects.md) [~M]; [Positive Action: Hawaii trial found no significant state-test difference](claims/positive-action-no-significant-effect-state-test-scores.md) [~M] (although the WWC domain average for achievement was positive, [0.37](claims/positive-action-positive-effects-academic-achievement.md) [+M])
rows.change: Do not plan character education as the route to higher test scores; if you add it, keep academic time intact and measure achievement separately
rows.if: The goal is reading and maths scores

rows.basis: [curriculum plus service vs service alone](claims/bds-curriculum-adds-beyond-service-learning-alone.md) [~M] (one quasi-experiment, twelfth graders)
rows.change: Pair a short ethics curriculum (deciding between competing values) with a service project and reflection; the curriculum is what adds ethical awareness and perspective over service alone
rows.if: Secondary age (`adolescent`), goal is ethical judgement

rows.basis: [Building Decision Skills: no significant effect on self-esteem, general social responsibility or anticipated participation](claims/bds-null-self-esteem-general-responsibility.md) [-M] (qualifies the second-hand [service-learning gains](claims/service-learning-improves-civic-and-personal-outcomes.md) [~W])
rows.change: Keep the service, but do not promise these outcomes; measure them if they matter
rows.if: Goal is self-esteem or general social responsibility through service

rows.basis: [civic subject alone insufficient](claims/civic-subject-alone-insufficient.md) [+W] (authorial argument, Naval et al. review); [service learning](claims/service-learning-improves-civic-and-personal-outcomes.md) [+W] (reported second-hand)
rows.change: Keep a civic subject for its knowledge, and add service learning, project work and staff role models across courses and extracurricular life
rows.if: University students (`postsecondary`), goal is civic competence

rows.basis: [Positive Action reduced serious violence among boys but not girls](claims/positive-action-violence-reduced-boys-not-girls.md) [~M] (one grade 5 trial, Hawaii)
rows.change: Check results by group; do not assume a whole-group effect holds for each
rows.if: Boys and girls may respond differently, or the target is violence

rows.basis: untested proposal, from the earlier page's constraint on single teachers
rows.change: Run weekly class meetings and situational moral problems inside the class; keep the conflict-resolution response for your own room; tell families what you are doing; expect less reach
rows.if: Only one teacher, one classroom, the school is punitive or competitive

rows.basis: untested proposal; the programmes reviewed ran for a year or more
rows.change: Do not call it character education; use one real problem from the learners' own setting, one decision, and one reflection, and record it as a single activity
rows.if: Time is a single session or a short unit only

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Hold class meetings with a turn order and a shared written agenda; let remote learners propose problems in writing beforehand; make the service or responsibility something they can do where they are
rows.if: Learners join remotely, some in the room, or phone-only

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Rotate learner chairs early; keep a fixed 15-minute meeting format; let learners keep a short decision log the adult reads weekly
rows.if: One adult for a large group, or scarce facilitator time (volunteers, a youth worker with a short slot)

rows.basis: untested proposal; the claims here test school-age learners or argue about universities
rows.change: Use real cases from their own work and decide on them; the profession's own code is the shared commitment; no class meetings
rows.if: Adults in a work setting (staff, professional ethics)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Let learners show care and decisions by doing (roles, service, drama) before writing reflections; accept spoken or drawn reflections
rows.if: Learners have low confidence or low literacy, or the language of instruction is not their first

rows.basis: untested proposal (wave-5 rule); [moral inquiry over fixed principles](claims/moral-knowledge-product-of-moral-inquiry.md) [+W]
rows.change: Keep it; change only what the evidence here says matters: add action with reflection, make problems specific, and measure behaviour separately from attitudes
rows.if: The brief names its own programme, rubric, values list or meeting routine

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: The learner decides whether it is discussed openly; use anonymised or fictional versions in meetings; repair conversations stay with those involved
rows.if: Problems discussed are private or sensitive (a family matter, a conflict between named learners)

rows.basis: untested proposal; see [Community-Based Learning](principles/community-based-learning.md)
rows.change: Keep the product whole and real; the reflection happens alongside, not as a replacement test
rows.if: The brief wants a public product (a service project for a real partner, a performance)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Keep a record of conflicts and their repair; do not grade character
rows.if: High stakes: discipline decisions, exclusion

rows.basis: [Judgments of learning are often inaccurate](claims/fluent-illusions-mislead-self-assessment.md) [-M]; [Prior knowledge needed for accurate self-assessment](claims/prior-knowledge-needed-for-accurate-self-assessment.md) [~M]
rows.change: Follow the rating with one short unassisted task on the same content; act on the task, not on the rating alone
rows.if: The check-in asks learners how well they understood

rows.basis: [Self-assessment accuracy is low without training](claims/self-assessment-accuracy-is-low-without-training.md) [~M]
rows.change: Expect low accuracy in their self-reports; show a modelled example of judging one's own work before relying on the check-in
rows.if: Learners are new to the subject

rows.basis: [High-confidence errors improve retention after correction](claims/high-confidence-errors-improve-retention.md) [+M]
rows.change: Correct the answer straight away and explain it; confident errors corrected this way are well remembered
rows.if: A learner reports high confidence and then answers wrongly

rows.basis: [Contingent scaffolding improves learning](claims/contingent-scaffolding-improves-learning.md) [~M]
rows.change: Change the help given in the next activity according to the report and the task response, and record what was given
rows.if: The teacher can respond to individuals (tutoring, small groups)

rows.basis: [Teachers used Forms for well-being check-ins and anonymous voice](claims/forms-sel-checkins-anonymity.md) [~W]; [Students' self-assessments of well-being give useful information](claims/student-self-assessments-valuable-development-information.md) [~W]
rows.change: Use a brief private or anonymous form, read daily, and follow up individually with learners who report difficulty
rows.if: The check-in is about wellbeing or social-emotional state

rows.basis: [Belonging interventions improve outcomes](claims/belonging-interventions-improve-outcomes.md) [~W]
rows.change: Treat a check-in as a way to find out who needs support, not as the support itself; the tested interventions are belonging reframing, not check-ins
rows.if: First-year or transition learners, where belonging is a concern

rows.basis: [Self-monitoring improves self-regulation](claims/self-monitoring-improves-self-regulation.md) [+W]
rows.change: Turn the check-in into a self-monitoring prompt against a stated goal, with a suggested next step for each answer
rows.if: `online-self-paced`, with no instructor

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Switch to a private channel; public reports of confusion are likely to be withheld
rows.if: Answers will be visible to the class

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Act visibly on one report and see whether later reports become more specific
rows.if: Learners say "fine" every time

rows.basis: [Segmenting improves multimedia learning](claims/segmenting-improves-multimedia-learning.md) [+M]; [Learner-paced segments improved transfer](claims/segmenting-principle-mayer-2008.md) [+M]
rows.change: Break it into segments at conceptual breaks, with a pause or a "continue" button between them
rows.if: The content is a narrated animation or explainer video

rows.basis: [Long recorded lectures impeded focus](claims/long-recorded-lectures-impeded-focus.md) [+W]; [Segmenting improves multimedia learning](claims/segmenting-improves-multimedia-learning.md) [+M]
rows.change: Split long recordings into several shorter videos, each on one idea
rows.if: Recorded lectures for `online-self-paced` study

rows.basis: [Segmenting effects confirmed for system-paced segmentation](claims/segmenting-effects-confirmed-system-paced.md) [+M]
rows.change: Segment it; the segmenting effects were confirmed for system-paced segmentation
rows.if: The pace is set by the system (a broadcast, a live lecture, autoplay video)

rows.basis: [Learner pacing helped on complex material; learner control in general showed almost no effect](claims/learner-paced-beats-system-paced-complex-material.md) [~M]
