rows.change: Enlarge print (a proposal: 18-point or larger, high contrast, plain font), light the materials, read aloud what is written on the board, give materials in advance to view on their own device at their own size
rows.if: Learners with low vision

rows.basis: [Spoken–written advantages are larger for nonfluent and second-language readers](claims/reader-fluency-prior-knowledge-moderate-redundancy.md) [~M] (readers of the print, not non-readers); [show and do](claims/show-and-do-method-hearing-impaired-students.md) [+W]
rows.change: Carry the visual half with pictures, objects and demonstration, not text; when they can read some print, use key words only. Nonfluent readers gained most from spoken plus written words, so add print as reading grows
rows.if: Learners with low literacy, or who cannot read the language of the print

rows.basis: [Captioning second-language videos](claims/captioning-second-language-videos-large-benefits.md) [+M]; [bimodal captioned input](claims/bimodal-captioned-input-improves-segmentation.md) [+W]
rows.change: Turn on same-language captions for comprehension and new vocabulary; for a listening-skill goal, listen once without, once with, once without
rows.if: Second-language learners listening to recorded or video material

rows.basis: [Images or animation remove the spoken–written advantage](claims/images-animation-eliminate-redundancy-benefit.md) [~M]; [modality effect](claims/modality-effect-narration-over-text.md) [~S] (hearing learners; its own Discussion excludes learners with hearing impairments)
rows.change: Key terms beside the picture, full text on paper afterwards; do not put a full transcript on the same screen
rows.if: A diagram, map, slide picture or live demonstration is explained aloud

rows.basis: [System-paced but not learner-paced advantage](claims/system-paced-moderates-verbal-redundancy.md) [~M]; [modality effect absent when self-paced](claims/modality-effect-moderated-by-pacing.md) [~M]
rows.change: Give captions or a transcript the learner can switch on, plus pause and replay; no need to force both channels at once
rows.if: `online-self-paced` recordings

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Turn on live captions in the video call; type new words in the chat as you say them; send the handout before the session; for phone-only learners, send the key words and script by text message beforehand; use a microphone in the room so remote audio is clear; repeat every in-room question into the microphone
rows.if: Mixed modes: some learners join remotely, or by phone only

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Use a microphone or sound-field system if available; write in large print on a board everyone can see; repeat every question aloud before answering; give each learner the printed copy rather than relying on the board
rows.if: One teacher with a large group or a large hall

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Do the room fixes and written support from the start, with no fading; hand out the full text at the end; ask once, to the whole group, whether everyone can hear and see
rows.if: A single session only (a talk, a one-off workshop)

rows.basis: untested; [rote drills and fast-paced activities disadvantage older learners](claims/rote-drills-disadvantage-older-learners.md) [~M] (a digest's assertion)
rows.change: Make written copies, front seats and repetition the default for everyone, so no one has to ask; check privately, never in front of the group; avoid speed games and calling on learners cold
rows.if: Learners with low confidence who may hide a hearing or vision difficulty

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: The learner decides who knows; provide the supports to all, record needs only with the learner's agreement, and let the learner choose the seat
rows.if: Information about a learner's hearing or eyesight is private

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Explain away from the noise, then demonstrate on the floor; give a laminated written job aid with the key steps in the learner's own terms; agree visual signals for the noisy part
rows.if: `adult-workplace` training in a noisy setting (a shop floor, a ward)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Prepare the handout and key-word cards once and reuse them; a one-line room checklist (light, doors, face the group, repeat questions) for every volunteer; captions switched on by default
rows.if: Scarce facilitator time (volunteers, one tutor checking in briefly)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Keep them as given; add the written copy, large print and room fixes to them; change only the channel, not the content or the criteria
rows.if: The brief names its own materials, routine or check (its own dialogue, worksheet, rubric)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Spend no more than 5 minutes on room fixes and the private check in the first session (1–2 minutes thereafter); keep spoken segments to 2–3 minutes with a written recap; no extra activities
rows.if: A fixed short time budget (for example a 60-minute class)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Keep the performance whole; support it with a cue card of key phrases and a quiet room, not by splitting it into written items; a presenter to an audience uses a microphone and slides with key words, not full text
rows.if: The task is a whole performance kept whole (a conversation, a role-play, a presentation to a real audience)

rows.basis: untested; the evidence above is from adults
rows.change: The same moves apply (the digest notes these problems are not only older learners'); coordinate with the learner's specialist support and any amplification they use
rows.if: `child` or `adolescent` learners with a hearing or vision loss

rows.basis: [Correct word inference in reading requires knowing roughly 95-98% of surrounding words…](claims/vocabulary-coverage-thresholds-for-inference.md) [+M] (second-hand, one review); ratio untested
rows.change: Lead with deliberate study (about two thirds of vocabulary time); use graded or simplified texts with most unknown words glossed; check coverage on a 100-word sample before any text
rows.if: Learners are `novice` in the language (beginners, below about the first thousand words)

rows.basis: [Incidental vocabulary exposure produces reliable learning, but learners pick up only a small share…](claims/incidental-vocabulary-exposure-limited.md) [~S] (why some deliberate study stays even for strong readers); ratio untested
rows.change: Shift most time to extensive reading and listening with few glosses; keep deliberate study for low-frequency words in their field and for the after-input routine
rows.if: Learners are `advanced`, already at about 95% coverage of their texts

rows.basis: [Pairing Contextual Encounters…](claims/pairing-contextual-encounters-with-explicit-instruction-produces-stronger-vocabulary-outcomes-than-either-alone.md) [+M] (a meta-analysis of vocabulary instruction, population not stated in the entry); most other claims here are second-language and university, so carried
rows.change: Keep the same combination: read aloud and talk about texts, pre-teach two or three words, and reuse them in talk; expect taught-word gains
rows.if: Learners are `child` first-language readers, not second-language learners

rows.basis: untested; carried from university second-language evidence
rows.change: Take the input from their real documents, manuals and conversations; pre-teach the terms each document needs; keep a team word list from what they meet; check use in the job task
rows.if: Adults in work settings learning a job's terms in a second language

rows.basis: [Adult ESL students who read a short story could use incidentally acquired words in sentences…](claims/incidental-reading-enables-productive-word-use.md) [~M] (second-hand, adult ESL)
rows.change: Keep the after-input routine for every text and add one speaking or writing task per week that needs the kept words; keep the sentence the word was met in
rows.if: The goal is productive use (speaking, writing), not only reading

rows.basis: [L2 learners pick up vocabulary incidentally from meaning-focused input…](claims/incidental-vocabulary-learning-through-reading-for-meaning.md) [+M] (listening yielded similar proportions of words learned to reading; viewing lower)
rows.change: Run the input as listening (stories, audio, video with pictures) and the deliberate study orally with pictures and actions; add reading once decoding allows
rows.if: Learners have low literacy, or the language uses a script they cannot yet read

rows.basis: [Listening to vocabulary lessons while physically active…](claims/lwpa-outperforms-traditional-vocabulary-learning.md) [+M] (ESL students, phone audio added to class teaching); [Supplemental computer-based spaced repetition…](claims/spaced-repetition-supplement-triples-vocabulary-retention.md) [+M] (EFL cadets, alongside classroom teaching, not instead of it); in-app glossing carried from [Marginal glosses, dictionary use, and repeated occurrence…](claims/marginal-glosses-dictionary-recurrence-improve-incidental-learning.md) [+M] (printed text)
rows.change: Put graded readings or audio with tap-to-see glosses in the app; schedule spaced recall of words the learner taps or saves; after each reading ask for one typed or spoken use of a saved word
rows.if: Setting is `online-self-paced`, phone-only, or no teacher present

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Share the text and its glosses on screen or in a shared document; take after-input uses in the chat as well as aloud; set the extensive reading as individual work both groups do the same way
rows.if: Some learners are remote and some in the room

rows.basis: untested proposal; the review part rests on [Supplemental computer-based spaced repetition…](claims/spaced-repetition-supplement-triples-vocabulary-retention.md) [+M]
rows.change: Pre-teach to everyone at once; let input and spaced review run on readers, audio or an app; in the check-in look at one thing: two or three uses of kept words from the week's reading
rows.if: One teacher with a large group, or scarce facilitator time (a volunteer, a short weekly check-in)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: 5 minutes pre-teaching 3 words, 15 minutes reading a short glossed text where they recur, 5 minutes keeping 3 words with their sentences, 5 minutes using them; give the words on a card for later review; do not claim retention
rows.if: A single session only, or a fixed short time budget (for example 30 minutes)

rows.basis: untested proposal; the 98% figure from [Correct word inference in reading requires knowing roughly 95-98%…](claims/vocabulary-coverage-thresholds-for-inference.md) [+M]
rows.change: Start with texts at 98% coverage or more and glossed; let learners mark unknown words privately; make the after-input routine written before spoken
rows.if: Learners have low confidence or anxiety about not understanding

rows.basis: [Combining intentional and incidental vocabulary learning…](claims/combined-intentional-incidental-greater-gains.md) [+M]; [Incidental vocabulary gains show retention problems…](claims/incidental-vocabulary-retention-problems.md) [~M]
rows.change: Keep the routine; change only what the evidence says matters: check coverage of the texts, pre-teach a few words before each, gloss in the margin, and bring kept words back on a schedule
rows.if: The brief names its own routine (an extensive reading programme, a vocabulary log, a word wall, a set textbook glossary)

rows.basis: untested
rows.change: Teach from that list in its own categories; choose input texts in which its words recur, rather than replacing the list
rows.if: The brief gives its own word list or categories (a course list, a frequency band, an exam list, a job glossary)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: The learner decides what goes in it and who sees it; check learning through a separate use task, not by reading the log
rows.if: Learners keep a private reading log or word journal

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Feed the performance with reading and listening on its topic and pre-teach its key words; rehearse parts of the real task; let the performance run whole rather than becoming a vocabulary test
rows.if: The output is a performance or product for a real audience (a presentation, a client conversation, a published text) that the brief wants kept whole

rows.basis: [Intentional vocabulary learning yields higher, faster gains…](claims/intentional-beats-incidental-vocabulary-gains.md) [+M] (second-hand, one direct comparison)
rows.change: Raise the deliberate share for the listed words, with spaced recall until the exam; keep input at high coverage so reading speed grows; do not rely on input to supply listed words
rows.if: Stakes are high (an exam with a set word list, a reading test in a fixed time)

rows.basis: [STEM PLC participation shifts instruction toward student reasoning](claims/stem-plc-instructional-practice-shifts.md) [+W]; [PLC participation changed teachers' norms, understanding and practice](claims/plc-participation-changes-teacher-norms-understanding-practice.md) [+W]; [STEM PLC participation improves teachers' understanding of or preparedness to teach content](claims/stem-plc-teacher-knowledge-attitude-gains.md) [+W] (a knowledge synthesis judging this "moderately substantiated")
rows.change: Meet regularly over a term or more around students' work and thinking; record changes in practice as descriptions, since the reviews report them without comparison groups; give the sessions content and pedagogical-content focus, since that is where the reviews find teachers' knowledge and preparedness changing
rows.if: Members are mathematics or science teachers and the aim is changed teaching

rows.basis: [PLC at Work: +0.08 in mathematics](claims/plc-at-work-significant-math-effect.md) [~W]; [vPLC with ASSISTments: no significant overall effect](claims/vplc-assistments-no-significant-overall-effect.md) [~W]; [Mathematics-only studies give existence proof, not a link to formal assessment results](claims/stem-plc-math-student-learning-existence-proof.md) [~W]
rows.change: Expect small or no measured effects within two years, possibly only in mathematics or for lower-attaining students; plan to measure students, not only teachers
rows.if: The aim is a rise in students' test scores

rows.basis: [PLC nurtures teacher metacognition](claims/plc-nurtures-teacher-metacognition.md) [+W]; [Lower and higher levels of teacher metacognition in PLCs](claims/plc-metacognition-lower-and-higher-levels.md) [+W] (three participants, all PLC leaders)
rows.change: Prompt reflection at two levels, on what members did and on how they reflect, and record it with interviews about specific episodes (stimulated recall) rather than a satisfaction survey
rows.if: The aim is teachers' reflection on their own practice (metacognition)

rows.basis: [A facilitated CoP helped isolated American Indian Education Directors build relationships](claims/cop-relationships-combat-aie-director-isolation.md) [+W]; [Principal networks support sharing practice and problem solving](claims/principal-networks-professional-learning-communities.md) [+W] (participant reports and a narrative review)
rows.change: Form a network across organisations that meets regularly on members' own problems of practice, with a facilitator who plans sessions around what members say they need; expect relationships and shared problem solving first, and observe practice separately
rows.if: Members are isolated in their roles (principals, one specialist per school, district or state)

rows.basis: [Cross-grade, cross-school PLC supported implementation](claims/pktp-plc-supported-implementation.md) [+W] (one programme's first year; the facilitator recommendation is the evaluators', untested)
rows.change: Meet monthly across the year with consistent attendance from every site, and give it an external facilitator who keeps one vision across the sites
rows.if: The community spans grades, schools or organisations to carry out one programme (a transition between phases, a shared curriculum)

rows.basis: [PLC formulations trivialize practice](claims/plc-literature-trivializes-teacher-practice.md) [~W]; [Teacher resistance as agency](claims/teacher-resistance-agency-challenges-plc.md) [~W] (argument only)
rows.change: Put the practice the reform asks for, and members' reasons for doubting it, on the agenda; do not define success as members coming to agree with the reform's goals
rows.if: The community is mandated as part of a reform and some members resist it

rows.basis: [PLCs with a teacher leader were more productive](claims/teacher-leader-more-productive-plc.md) [+W]
rows.change: Appoint a teacher leader to plan sessions, keep the focus and deepen discussion
rows.if: The group has no designated leader

rows.basis: [Trust norms are prerequisites for critical inquiry](claims/plc-norms-three-categories-trust-prerequisite.md) [+W]
rows.change: Set and state trust norms first (criticism is of practices, not people), then introduce critique
rows.if: The group is new and the brief wants members to critique each other's practice

rows.basis: [Disagreements within a PLC can catalyse learning](claims/plc-disagreements-catalyze-learning.md) [+W]
rows.change: Keep the disagreement on the agenda and ask each side for its reasons rather than adjourning to avoid conflict
rows.if: Members disagree about practice

rows.basis: [Productive norms develop over time](claims/plc-norms-three-categories-trust-prerequisite.md) [~W]
rows.change: Do not expect the norms the reviews describe; use a fixed protocol for the sessions and treat outcomes as provisional
rows.if: The community meets only once or for a few weeks

rows.basis: [Online communities must be designed and scaffolded](claims/online-communities-must-be-designed-and-scaffolded.md) [+W]; [Fortnightly web conferences supported community formation](claims/web-conferences-support-online-community.md) [+W]
rows.change: Plan the interaction deliberately: scheduled synchronous sessions with open discussion, and tasks that require contribution
rows.if: The community is online or members are dispersed

rows.basis: [Small rural staffs forced cross-subject PLCs](claims/small-rural-staffs-cross-subject-plcs-isolation.md) [~W]; [Distance and bandwidth derailed cross-school PLC plans](claims/rural-distance-and-bandwidth-derail-plans-for-cross-school-plcs.md) [~W]
rows.change: Check bandwidth before planning cross-school online groups, and pair teachers with same-subject colleagues elsewhere where cross-subject groups leave them isolated
rows.if: A small rural school, with too few teachers for same-subject groups

rows.basis: The mathematics PLC review, which finds the objects and reports that outcomes matched them completely in only 3 of 32 studies (that finding has no claim page in the wiki): [Three objects of mathematics PLCs](claims/plc-mathematics-three-objects-repertoire-most-common.md) [~W]
rows.change: Observe what members actually change, including unintended outcomes, rather than assuming it matches the object; choose materials that fit the object (step 1)
rows.if: The community has a stated object (a curriculum, a routine)

rows.basis: [Nonparticipation can invalidate learner identities](claims/cop-nonparticipation-invalidates-learner-identities.md) [-W]
rows.change: Decide in advance what a valued peripheral contribution looks like, so non-central members are not read as failing
rows.if: Learners, such as language learners, may stay at the edge of the community

rows.basis: [Service learning and in-class civic learning predict civic commitment](claims/service-learning-and-in-class-civic-learning-strongest-predictors-civic-commitment.md) [+W]
rows.change: Combine service learning with in-class discussion of civic issues; these were the experiences most associated with later commitment
rows.if: High-school students, with civic commitment as the goal

rows.basis: [A syllabus linking service to content goes with civic competence](claims/syllabus-service-content-connection-strongest-pedagogical-relationship.md) [+W]
rows.change: Name in the syllabus and the brief which concepts the community work exercises, and assess them separately from the service; the wiki holds no test of content learning
rows.if: The course must also teach its content

rows.basis: [Guided reflection yields more analytic paragraphs](claims/guided-reflection-yields-more-higher-order-paragraphs-than-free.md) [+W]
rows.change: Give guided prompts that name a concept and ask for analysis, not free journals
rows.if: Learners will write reflections

rows.basis: [Exploration of diversity goes with all civic outcomes](claims/diversity-enhances-all-civic-competence-outcomes.md) [+W]
rows.change: Include explicit exploration of that diversity in class and in reflection
rows.if: The partner or the student group differs in background from most learners

rows.basis: [Peer mentoring went with higher civic action](claims/peer-mentoring-increases-civic-action-service-learning.md) [+W]
rows.change: Assign trained peer mentors to service-learning students
rows.if: A large course in which the instructor cannot mentor each student

rows.basis: [Co-planning gives partners a voice](claims/csl-co-planning-gives-community-partners-voice-in-project.md) [~W]; [Partner conflict goes with worse social-justice attitudes](claims/community-partner-conflict-negatively-correlates-social-justice.md) [~W]
rows.change: Co-plan the project with the partner, check the relationship during the term, and act on conflict early
rows.if: The partner is new, or the brief mentions past friction with partners

rows.basis: [Community projects need conceptual framing](claims/community-projects-need-conceptual-framing-to-avoid-narrowing-the-learning-object.md) [~W]
rows.change: Anchor the project in named disciplinary concepts and hold a discussion with students, teachers and partners about its purpose, so it does not narrow to making money
rows.if: Middle-school students run a project with local businesses

rows.basis: [Curriculum plus service added only for ethical awareness](claims/bds-curriculum-adds-beyond-service-learning-alone.md) [~W]
rows.change: Pair the service with a values curriculum; the curriculum added to service alone only for ethical awareness and perspective
rows.if: Secondary students study ethics or values alongside service

rows.basis: [Three lessons from an integrated planetary health course](claims/planetary-health-course-three-key-lessons.md) [~W]
rows.change: Build in flexibility in schedule and scope and agree roles with partners on equal terms
rows.if: The course links partners in several countries (collaborative online international learning)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Treat it as exposure, not as the relationship the page describes; add structured reflection tied to concepts
rows.if: The service is a one-off visit or a few hours

rows.basis: [Discussion boards generated no negative feedback](claims/discussion-board-no-negative-feedback-synchrony-required.md) [~W]
rows.change: Add a synchronous channel, text chat or video, where errors get corrected; the board produced no corrective feedback
rows.if: Discussion is on an asynchronous board and accuracy matters (for example second-language use)

rows.basis: [Social presence most associated with metacognition](claims/social-presence-strongest-metacognition-association-cbi.md) [~W]; [Co-regulation relates more strongly to the presences](claims/co-regulation-stronger-presence-relationships-than-self-regulation.md) [+W]
rows.change: Build in social presence early (introductions, replying to named peers); it was the presence most associated with self-reported regulation, an association only
rows.if: The goal includes learners regulating their own and each other's work in an online case course

rows.basis: [Uneven presence profile in an online MBA](claims/coi-presence-uneven-profile-mba.md) [~W]
rows.change: Put it first into clear organisation (topics, instructions, due dates), the teaching-presence items rated highest, then into facilitation
rows.if: Facilitator time is limited

rows.basis: [Uneven presence profile in an online MBA](claims/coi-presence-uneven-profile-mba.md) [~W]
rows.change: Add prompts that ask the group to integrate, test and state a resolution; resolution items were rated lowest
rows.if: Threads explore ideas but never reach a conclusion

rows.basis: [Structuring interdependence did not change achievement online](claims/interdependence-type-no-achievement-effect-asynchronous.md) [~M]
rows.change: Use them to organise the discussion, not as the means of raising achievement, and check each learner's posttest
rows.if: Online small groups will be given roles or group rewards to raise achievement

rows.basis: [Interaction counts correlated with posttest scores](claims/interaction-quantity-correlates-posttest-online-groups.md) [~W]
rows.change: Judge on an individual task instead; more interactions went with higher posttest scores, which may reflect stronger learners posting more
rows.if: Success will be judged by number of posts

rows.basis: [Online labs judged better with instructor scaffolds](claims/online-labs-better-with-instructor-scaffolds.md) [+W]
rows.change: Have the instructor present online during the lab with prompts before, during and after that direct attention to key steps
rows.if: The course includes online laboratory exercises

rows.basis: [Peer monitoring goes beyond social presence](claims/peer-monitoring-exceeds-social-presence.md) [~W]
rows.change: Make each member's professional expertise visible early; these learners judged peers by what they could contribute, not only by warmth
rows.if: Learners are working professionals (for example MBA students)

rows.basis: [Over-reliance on generative AI risks presence and skills](claims/gai-overreliance-risks-presence-and-skills.md) [-W]
rows.change: Ask for posts that respond to named peers and to the learner's own experience, and keep instructor contact human
rows.if: Learners may use generative AI to write their posts

rows.basis: [Fortnightly web conferences supported community formation](claims/web-conferences-support-online-community.md) [+W]
rows.change: Schedule recurring synchronous sessions, such as fortnightly web conferences with open discussion
rows.if: A cohort must form a community in a fully online unit

rows.basis: [Raters differed in severity](claims/raters-differed-severity-mfrm.md) [~M]; [Engineering rubric scorers differed by 1.2 of 9 points](claims/engineering-rubric-low-scoring-reliability.md) [-W]
rows.change: Calibrate them on common samples and check their spread before relying on a judgement; raters on one scale differed in severity
rows.if: Several assessors will score the same kind of performance

rows.basis: [Mean-classification cut-score method more robust to outliers](claims/mean-classification-cut-score-method-robust.md) [~W]
rows.change: Use a cut-score method that resists one deviant rating, and record the method
rows.if: A panel will set the pass threshold

rows.basis: [Explicit rubric conditions reduced AI disagreement](claims/explicit-rubric-conditions-reduce-ai-disagreement.md) [~W]; [AI not yet best practice for competency assessment](claims/ai-not-best-practice-competency-based-assessment.md) [~W]
rows.change: Write the required conditions into the rubric explicitly, keep human review of borderline and high-stakes decisions, and check agreement with human scorers
rows.if: AI will score responses

rows.basis: [Rubric-referenced self-assessment improved work](claims/rubrics-improve-student-work.md) [~M]
rows.change: Share the criteria with an exemplar before the attempt and have learners self-assess a draft against them
rows.if: Learners should improve, not only be certified

rows.basis: [Mastery learning improves outcomes](claims/mastery-learning-improves-outcomes.md) [+M]
rows.change: Allow reassessment after correction on a comparable but changed task
rows.if: The judgement controls progression to the next unit

rows.basis: [Placement test precision declines above the 40th percentile](claims/cmi-ela-test-precision-declines-above-40th-percentile.md) [~W]
rows.change: Check measurement precision at the cut scores that matter, not only overall reliability
rows.if: A test places learners into levels

rows.basis: [Statistical item selection conflicts with criterion-referenced definitions](claims/statistical-item-selection-conflicts-criterion-referenced-definition.md) [~W]; [Criterion-referenced tests need construct validation](claims/criterion-referenced-tests-need-construct-validation.md) [~W]
rows.change: Choose items that represent the competency domain, not those that discriminate best between learners
rows.if: The test was built by picking items that spread learners out

rows.basis: [Adaptive mastery testing reduces length and preserves decisions](claims/adaptive-mastery-testing-reduces-length-preserves-decisions.md) [~W]
rows.change: Use an adaptive mastery test; in one military-training simulation it shortened tests by 30–81% with the same decision for 96% of trainees
rows.if: Checks must be short

rows.basis: [Static assessment misses developing functions](claims/static-assessment-misses-emerging-functions.md) [~W]
rows.change: Add an assisted attempt beside the unassisted one, and record what help made the difference
rows.if: Learners whose capability is still emerging (young children, early stages)

rows.basis: [Process goals outperform outcome goals for novices](claims/process-goals-outperform-outcome-goals-for-novices.md) [~M] (high-school writers learning one revision skill; a goal-setting finding carried to assessment criteria); [Fading support transfers responsibility](claims/fading-support-promotes-transfer-of-responsibility.md) [~M]
rows.change: Frame early attempts and feedback around the process criteria (the steps and strategy), and judge against the outcome threshold once the process is in place; withdraw prompts across attempts before the judgement that counts
rows.if: Learners are novices on the task being judged

rows.basis: Authors' account of their own writing courses, untested: [a contract guarantees a B for completed activities](claims/contract-guarantees-b-for-completion-not-quality.md) [~W]; [decoupling evaluation from grades eases feedback](claims/decoupling-evaluation-from-grades-improves-feedback.md) [~W]; [contract grading yields more student work](claims/contract-yields-more-student-work.md) [~W]; [fourteen weeks of contract work warrants a B](claims/fourteen-weeks-contract-work-warrants-b.md) [~W]
rows.change: Consider separating feedback on drafts from the grade up to a stated level, for example a grade guaranteed for completing specified work, with judged quality deciding only the grades above it; record that this credits completion, not demonstrated capability
rows.if: Drafts need frank feedback, but every judgement also counts toward the grade (writing courses)

rows.basis: [Board certification identifies more expert teachers](claims/board-certification-identifies-more-expert-teachers.md) [+W]; [Certified teachers differ only on observation scores, not value added](claims/experience-credentials-teacher-evaluation-scores.md) [~M]
rows.change: Say which later outcome the certification is meant to predict, and check it against that outcome; a credential can agree with observation scores and not with student-learning measures
rows.if: Practising professionals will be certified on portfolios or observed practice (teachers)

rows.basis: [Performance assessments expand opportunities to demonstrate mastery](claims/performance-assessments-expand-mastery-demonstration-opportunities.md) [~W]
rows.change: Give learners more than one occasion to demonstrate each competency, and record the conditions of each
rows.if: Graduation or certification will rest on performance assessments

rows.basis: [Fading condition outperformed generic and concrete conditions](claims/fading-condition-outperformed-generic-and-concrete.md) [+W]; [Manipulatives require connection to concept](claims/manipulatives-require-connection-to-concept.md) [+M]
rows.change: Use all three stages, with the links in steps 3–4
rows.if: Learners are novices who cannot yet say what the symbols mean

rows.basis: [Expertise reversal](claims/expertise-reversal-effect.md) [~M], carried from guidance formats to concrete representations, untested for them here
rows.change: Start at the abstract stage; keep a drawing ready to point back to on errors
rows.if: Learners are advanced and already read the notation (`high-prior-knowledge`)

rows.basis: [Manipulatives improve math learning](claims/manipulatives-improve-math-learning.md) [+M] (kindergarten to college); the longer stage is an untested proposal
rows.change: Keep the concrete stage longer, across several sessions, with the teacher's words naming the relation as children act
rows.if: Young children (early primary, kindergarten)

rows.basis: [Fading condition outperformed generic and concrete conditions](claims/fading-condition-outperformed-generic-and-concrete.md) [+W] (undergraduates); the length is untested
rows.change: Use a short concrete stage (one session or less) and move to iconic quickly
rows.if: Adults or undergraduates learning a formal structure

rows.basis: [Manipulatives improve math learning](claims/manipulatives-improve-math-learning.md) [+M]
rows.change: The concrete stage still helps; expect most of the gain on retention, less on problem solving and transfer
rows.if: The goal is retention of a procedure more than transfer

rows.basis: untested proposal; the need for the link rests on [Manipulatives require connection to concept](claims/manipulatives-require-connection-to-concept.md) [+M]
rows.change: Build the links into the material: each drawing shown beside its object and its symbol, with a prompt to say which part matches which
rows.if: Self-paced online, no teacher to make the links

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Show the object, then the same scene redrawn as a diagram, then the symbol, with a pause and a question at each change; do not cut straight from object to equation
rows.if: System-paced video or slides

rows.basis: [Physical experience enhances science learning](claims/physical-experience-enhances-science-learning.md) [~M] (virtual and physical manipulation were equally effective for undergraduates' heat and temperature concepts)
rows.change: Use virtual objects learners move on screen for the concrete stage
rows.if: Phone-only, or no physical materials

rows.basis: untested proposal; cost of irrelevant detail carried from [Decorative illustrations](claims/seductive-details-effect.md) [-M]
rows.change: Keep the scene plain enough that the structure stands out, and still end with the notation; a vivid scene is not the abstract stage
rows.if: VR or a rich simulation

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Use the iconic stage as the first stage (a drawing learners mark or cut out), then the notation
rows.if: Print only

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Run all three stages in one session at about 10 minutes each, and end on two items in notation
rows.if: A single session

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: One stage per day across three days, opening each day with one item from the previous stage
rows.if: A fixed short time budget (10 minutes a day)

rows.basis: [Unfolding knowledge elements produces deeper conceptual learning opportunities](claims/unfolding-knowledge-elements-produces-deeper-conceptual-learning-opportunities.md) [+W] (opportunities in the discourse, not measured learning)
rows.change: Do the concrete stage as a demonstration with a few learners acting it out, the iconic stage individually on paper; in discussion, take a learner's symbolic answer back down to the drawing or the object before moving on
rows.if: One teacher for many learners

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Keep the concrete and iconic stages, which need little text; add the spoken and written word for each part as it is linked to the symbol
rows.if: Low literacy, or learning in a second language

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Keep the concrete stage tactile; make the iconic stage a raised-line or tactile diagram before braille or spoken notation
rows.if: Learners with a visual impairment

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: No change to the stages; give the linking talk in captions or sign beside the object
rows.if: Learners with a hearing impairment

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Keep them as given; add only the iconic step and the spoken links if they are missing
rows.if: The brief's own manipulatives, curriculum materials, routine or rubric

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Run it as given; add no test it did not ask for. If it tests only with the objects present, say that it cannot show the abstract stage was reached
rows.if: The brief's own assessment

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Not applicable to the order of representations; no change
rows.if: Private or personal material

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Keep the task whole; apply the stages to the one formal idea inside it the task needs
rows.if: A whole task kept whole (an authentic problem, a project)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Keep the stages short and spend the saved time on practice in the notation the exam uses; the exam judges the abstract stage only
rows.if: High stakes (a qualifying exam in notation)

rows.basis: [Abstract and concrete animation do not differ](claims/abstract-concrete-representation-no-difference.md) [~M]
rows.change: Expect no difference between them by themselves; the choice that matters is the order and the links
rows.if: A concrete and an abstract version of the same animation are on offer, with no sequence

rows.basis: [Comparing cases side by side improves learning](claims/comparing-contrasting-cases-improves-learning.md) [+M] (carried from case comparison; not a test of this move); [expertise reversal](claims/expertise-reversal-effect.md) [~M] (review of cognitive-load studies; the reverse case)
rows.change: Supply the alternative (a rival explanation, a second case, the common misconception) and ask learners to make its best case, side by side with their own; drop to self-generated alternatives only when they meet the threshold in the arc above
rows.if: Learners are `novice` in the domain, or their alternatives are implausible

rows.basis: [Instructional guidance that helps novices can become redundant or counterproductive as expertise grows.](claims/expertise-reversal-effect.md) [~M] (cognitive-load studies, carried to this prompt); the red-team form is untested
rows.change: Prompt only, with no supplied alternative; use the red-team version (one person argues against the leading proposal) on consequential decisions
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` or practising professionals

rows.basis: [Conflict-based instruction improves science conceptual learning](claims/cognitive-disequilibrium-motivates-conceptual-change.md) [+M] (meta-analyses of science-education studies; staged contradiction helped only confused learners in one small experiment); [refutation text](claims/misconceptions-interfere-with-new-learning.md) [+M] (no developmental pattern found in the review)
rows.change: Predict–observe–explain: commit to a prediction, ask "how would someone who thinks the opposite explain it?", show the phenomenon, then discuss which account fits; use a refutation text that names the misconception and answers it
rows.if: Learners are `child` or `adolescent`, in science, holding an everyday misconception

rows.basis: [Argumentation improves reasoning](claims/argumentation-improves-reasoning.md) [+M] (online science argumentation meta-analysis, 46 studies; one multiyear dialogue intervention with young adolescents); [prompted peer feedback raised addressing the opposing view](claims/ps-genai-pf-improves-rebuttals-and-opposing-view.md) [+W] (one study, 12 groups)
rows.change: Add a required counterargument-and-rebuttal paragraph: the strongest objection to the learner's thesis, then the reply; score it with the brief's rubric
rows.if: The goal is argument writing (`complex-skill`)

rows.basis: [Prior Knowledge Needed For Accurate Self Assessment](claims/prior-knowledge-needed-for-accurate-self-assessment.md) [~M] (lowest performers grossly overconfident in one undergraduate course; it does not test this remedy)
rows.change: Rate confidence before and after the opposite step, then score against the outcome; show each learner their own record across several judgments
rows.if: The goal is calibrated confidence

rows.basis: [Comparing cases side by side](claims/comparing-contrasting-cases-improves-learning.md) [+M] (seventh-grade algebra: method comparison raised procedural knowledge and flexibility, not conceptual knowledge)
rows.change: Do not use the move; contrast two worked methods side by side and ask which suits which problem
rows.if: The task is a procedure with one correct method

rows.basis: [A systematic review of bias-mitigation training names considering the opposite as a previously validated way to reduce judgment biases, without testing it itself](claims/considering-the-opposite-reduces-bias.md) [+M], carried to clinical judgment, where it is untested in the wiki
rows.change: A diagnostic time-out before the decision is final: list the findings that do not fit, name the most dangerous alternative, say what test would separate them
rows.if: Adults in work settings (`workplace-clinical`), e.g. diagnosis

rows.basis: untested; from the earlier page's warning about paralysis
rows.change: One alternative, a fixed short time, then commit; record what was considered; never make it open-ended
rows.if: The decision must be made quickly, or stakes are high and time is short

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: A required field before submission: "the strongest reason you could be wrong"; then show the expert's alternative and the deciding evidence
rows.if: `online-self-paced`, or phone only

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Do the commit and the alternative in writing in one shared space (chat or a shared document) so remote learners contribute on equal terms; pair across modes for the "best case for the other side" step
rows.if: Some learners remote and some in the room

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: A printed or on-screen prompt card does the prompting; partners swap and write the case against each other's judgment; the facilitator reads three to five at random and gives whole-group feedback on the commonest weak alternative
rows.if: One teacher for many learners, or scarce facilitator time (a volunteer, a busy shift)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: One judgment: 2 minutes to commit with a confidence rating, 4 minutes for the opposite case, 2 minutes to see the evidence and decide again, 2 minutes on what changed; claim nothing about a habit
rows.if: A single session only, or a fixed short time budget (say 10 minutes)

rows.basis: [Critical disposition is least spontaneous when confronting one's most basic prejudices](claims/critical-temper-weakest-on-basic-prejudices.md) [~W] (theoretical argument only)
rows.change: Begin on low-stakes questions; let the learner keep their reasons for the opposite private and choose what to share; never require a learner to argue against their own identity in public
rows.if: The question touches learners' convictions, identity or private experience

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Do it orally or with a sentence starter ("Someone who disagrees would say … because …"); frame the alternative as another person's view, not the learner's error
rows.if: Learners have low confidence or low literacy

rows.basis: [Peer conflicts worked only for students prepared to reflect](claims/peer-conflicts-conditional-on-reflection.md) [~M] (seven dyads, qualitative)
rows.change: Do not rely on the conflict itself; after the discussion, each learner writes alone what they now think and what changed
rows.if: Disagreement arises among peers in group work

rows.basis: [Conflict with a decision-support system's output induces deeper reflection than confirmation](claims/conflict-seed-induces-deeper-reflection.md) [+W] (reported second-hand in a review, no detail)
rows.change: Have the learner judge first, then compare with the tool's answer and argue against whichever answer they now favour
rows.if: Learners use an AI tool or decision-support output

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Keep it; add one line to it: "the strongest alternative, and why you reject or accept it". Do not replace the routine
rows.if: The brief names its own routine (a claim–evidence–reasoning frame, a diagnostic checklist, a critique protocol)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Judge the quality of the alternative with those criteria, and add no test or quiz the brief did not ask for
rows.if: The brief gives its own categories, criteria or rubric

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Keep the opposite-consideration in drafting notes; in the final product address the strongest objection only where that audience expects it
rows.if: The output is a product or performance for a real audience (a published essay, a client design review)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Put the prompt at the commit point inside the task, not as a separate exercise before or after it
rows.if: The brief wants a whole task kept whole (a full case, a simulation)

rows.basis: untested proposal; resembles [refutation text](claims/misconceptions-interfere-with-new-learning.md) [+M]
rows.change: Use that error as the alternative: learners make the best case for it, then show what evidence rules it out
rows.if: The brief reports an error learners actually made

rows.basis: [Split attention degrades learning](claims/split-attention-effect-degrades-learning.md) [+M] (g = 0.63, 58 comparisons)
rows.change: Put labels on the diagram parts and the text beside the region it explains, all on one page or screen
rows.if: Novice learners; a diagram with a separate legend, or text on another page or screen

rows.basis: [Integration helps most with complex material](claims/element-interactivity-moderates-contiguity-effect.md) [+M] (d = 0.78 high vs 0.28 low)
rows.change: Integrate first here; this is where the effect is largest
rows.if: The material has many interacting parts (a circuit, a body system, a proof)

rows.basis: [Integration helps most with complex material](claims/element-interactivity-moderates-contiguity-effect.md) [~M]; [design principles matter less in simple media](claims/design-principle-effects-moderated-by-pacing-and-complexity.md) [~M]
rows.change: Integration is low priority; fix it if cheap, spend design time elsewhere
rows.if: The material is simple, with few interacting parts

rows.basis: [Integration reverses into redundancy for experienced trainees](claims/expertise-reversal-split-attention-redundancy-review.md) [-M]; [guidance that helps novices can become redundant](claims/expertise-reversal-effect.md) [~S]; qualified by [prior knowledge did not moderate design-principle effects overall](claims/design-principle-effects-moderated-by-pacing-and-complexity.md) [~M]
rows.change: Drop the explanatory text and give the diagram alone or with key labels; check with a changed-condition question
rows.if: Learners are advanced on this content (`advanced`), or already read this kind of diagram fluently

rows.basis: [Redundant integrated notes retarded more knowledgeable learners](claims/expertise-reversal-split-attention-redundancy-review.md) [~M]
rows.change: Do not integrate; cut the redundant source, or keep it apart where learners can ignore it
rows.if: The text restates what the picture already shows, or each source makes sense alone

rows.basis: [Mayer's temporal tests, 8 of 8](claims/contiguity-principles-mayer-2008.md) [+M]; [design principles matter more when system-paced](claims/design-principle-effects-moderated-by-pacing-and-complexity.md) [+M]
rows.change: Synchronise each sentence of narration with its part of the animation; no "explain, then show"
rows.if: System-paced video or narrated animation

rows.basis: [Mayer's spatial and temporal tests](claims/contiguity-principles-mayer-2008.md) [+M], carried from computer and paper lessons to live lectures, which they did not test
rows.change: Put labels on the slide's figure; talk about each part while it is shown and pointed to, not before or after
rows.if: A live lecture with slides

rows.basis: [Static and dynamic presentations did not differ](claims/static-dynamic-presentation-no-moderation.md) [~M]; [Mayer's paper-based tests](claims/contiguity-principles-mayer-2008.md) [+M]
rows.change: Labels on the figure; text on the same page as its figure; never "see Figure 3 overleaf"
rows.if: Print: a textbook, worksheet or handout

rows.basis: [Design principles matter less when learner-paced](claims/design-principle-effects-moderated-by-pacing-and-complexity.md) [~M] (g = 0.27 vs 0.41)
rows.change: Integrate anyway; expect a smaller gain than in system-paced media
rows.if: Self-paced online course (`online-self-paced`), learners can pause and scroll

rows.basis: [Modality effect](claims/modality-effect-narration-over-text.md) [+S]; [pacing reverses it](claims/modality-effect-moderated-by-pacing.md) [~M] (d = 0.93 system-paced, −0.14 self-paced)
rows.change: System-paced: speak the explanation while learners look at the object. Self-paced: keep printed words, placed in the line of sight
rows.if: Text and object cannot share a space (equipment and a manual, two monitors)

rows.basis: [Co-located guidance matters most when instruction and task share a spatial frame](claims/spatial-colocation-benefit-task-dependent.md) [~W] (authors' interpretation of one study)
rows.change: Co-locate guidance with the work where the task is spatial (drawing, assembly); symbolic instructions can stay on a screen
rows.if: VR, AR or a projected guide on a physical task

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Put labels on the figure, or reveal a label beside its part on tap; never put the explanation on a different screen from the figure
rows.if: Phone-only, small screen

rows.basis: [Integrated worked examples restore their advantage](claims/split-attention-effect-in-worked-examples.md) [+M]
rows.change: Write each step's explanation into the diagram where it applies, not in a block beside it
rows.if: Worked examples in mathematics or science (geometry, circuits)

rows.basis: [Education level did not consistently moderate design-principle effects](claims/design-principle-effects-moderated-by-pacing-and-complexity.md) [~M]; the contiguity meta-analyses here are not broken down by age
rows.change: Use the same integrated layouts; check understanding with a short "what happens if" question
rows.if: Children in primary school

rows.basis: [Integrated notes helped low language-competence learners](claims/expertise-reversal-split-attention-redundancy-review.md) [+M]; [captioning second-language video](claims/captioning-second-language-videos-large-benefits.md) [+M]
rows.change: Integrate short explanatory notes into the text or figure; add captions to second-language video
rows.if: Learners read in a second language, or have low literacy

rows.basis: untested proposal; the temporal and modality evidence assumes learners hear the narration
rows.change: Keep printed words placed beside the picture, not narration; give pause control
rows.if: Learners are deaf or hard of hearing

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Keep the description of each part with that part: in a tactile diagram, braille labels on the part; in audio description, describe each part as it is presented
rows.if: Learners are blind or have low vision

rows.basis: untested proposal; the effects are on [immediate tests of short lessons](claims/integration-of-related-elements-large-mean-effect.md) [+M]
rows.change: Integrate the existing materials; it moves words rather than adding them, so it costs no learner time
rows.if: A single session, or a fixed short time budget

rows.basis: [Effects larger one-to-one but still large under group testing](claims/testing-format-moderates-contiguity-effect.md) [~M] (d = .89 vs .65)
rows.change: Integrate the shared materials once; the benefit holds in group-tested settings
rows.if: One teacher with a large class, or group testing

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Keep them as given; re-lay out the existing figures and text and retime the narration, add no test the brief did not ask for, and judge with the brief's own assessment
rows.if: The brief supplies its own materials, routine, rubric or assessment

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Annotate inside the same view, as a layer on the image, rather than in a separate document that must be shared alongside it
rows.if: The material is private (patients' images, learners' own work)

rows.basis: [Integrated worked examples](claims/split-attention-effect-in-worked-examples.md) [+M]; extending it to whole tasks is untested
rows.change: Integrate the guidance into the task environment (labels on the device or interface, prompts at the step) instead of a separate manual
rows.if: A whole task kept whole (a real device, a full case)

rows.basis: untested; the effects here were measured soon after short lessons
rows.change: Do not rely on the effect alone to carry to delayed or on-the-job performance; test that performance directly
rows.if: High stakes: a certification exam, clinical or safety training

rows.basis: [Load measures did not explain the integration benefit](claims/cognitive-load-reduction-improves-learning.md) [~S]
rows.change: Judge by an explanation or transfer question instead
rows.if: Success is to be judged by learners' effort or load ratings

rows.basis: [Group rewards on every member's individual learning](claims/cooperative-learning-group-rewards-and-individual-accountability.md) [+M]
rows.change: Recognise teams by the sum or average of each member's individual quiz results, announced in advance, rather than by a single group product
rows.if: School-age learners, a unit of four weeks or more, an achievement goal

rows.basis: [Small-group learning improves undergraduate STEM achievement](claims/small-group-learning-improves-stem-achievement.md) [+M]
rows.change: Use structured small-group work in class sessions; expect a programme-level gain, smaller in studies where the investigator did not teach the course and not significant at two-year colleges
rows.if: An undergraduate STEM course

rows.basis: [Secondary studies: STAD most, Jigsaw least successful](claims/secondary-cooperative-learning-newmann-thompson.md) [~W]
rows.change: Add an individual quiz that counts toward the team's recognition; in secondary studies jigsaw was the least successful method, perhaps for lack of it
rows.if: The plan is a jigsaw with a shared group grade

rows.basis: [Science-classroom studies are mixed](claims/cooperative-learning-science-studies-mixed.md) [~W]; [Poor group leaders undermined discussion](claims/cooperative-conceptual-change-chemistry-misconceptions.md) [~W]
rows.change: Do not assume groups beat pair or individual work; check each learner's concept individually, and coach student group leaders not to rush
rows.if: The goal is conceptual change in science

rows.basis: [Structuring interdependence did not change achievement online](claims/interdependence-type-no-achievement-effect-asynchronous.md) [~M]; [Interdependence type shifted the kind of interaction](claims/interdependence-type-shifts-interaction-nature.md) [~W]
rows.change: Use roles to organise the group's process, but do not expect roles or rewards to raise achievement; check each member's posttest
rows.if: Groups work asynchronously online

rows.basis: [Cooperative learning and gifted students](claims/cooperative-learning-gifted-students.md) [~W]
rows.change: Give them explaining roles and an individual challenge as well, and check their own gains; long-term evidence for this group is lacking
rows.if: The group includes gifted or high-ability learners

rows.basis: [The cooperative component's added benefit was not confirmed](claims/circ-cooperative-component-benefit-unconfirmed.md) [~M]
rows.change: Keep the explicit instruction central; the cooperative component did not add significantly over it with the same materials
rows.if: The goal is reading comprehension in grades 3–4, with explicit strategy instruction available

rows.basis: [Cooperative learning in language classes](claims/cooperative-learning-language-class-outcomes.md) [+W]
rows.change: Use cooperative groups for speaking practice, which gave learners more turns than teacher-led classes
rows.if: A second-language class

rows.basis: [Peer tutoring improves achievement](claims/peer-tutoring-improves-achievement.md) [+M]; [Structured peer tutoring outperforms unstructured](claims/structured-peer-tutoring-outperforms-unstructured.md) [+M]
rows.change: Use structured peer tutoring with scripted roles rather than unstructured pairing
rows.if: Learners are primary pupils who need practice in a basic skill

rows.basis: [A cooperative technique improved attitudes to cooperativeness](claims/ccct-improved-cooperativeness-attitudes.md) [~W]; [Unequal participation and time constraints noted](claims/ccct-qualitative-strengths-challenges.md) [~W]
rows.change: Run a structured cooperative technique and measure attitudes to cooperation separately from achievement; watch for unequal participation
rows.if: Learners are trainee teachers and cooperation is itself an outcome

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Use a brief structure with individual answers before and after the group step; do not expect the multi-week effect
rows.if: One session only

rows.basis: [Items should represent essential skills in a teaching hierarchy](claims/criterion-referenced-items-should-represent-essential-skills-in-a-teaching-hierarchy.md) [+W] (an argument about reading tests, carried to other domains)
rows.change: Use short criterion-referenced checks on the first skills in the teaching order, three to five items per skill; report mastered / not yet per skill; no percentiles
rows.if: The decision is what to teach next for `novice` learners early in a domain

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Add items at the upper skills of the hierarchy, or a broader task, so the check is not at ceiling; if relative standing matters (an enrichment place), use a norm-referenced score from an above-level test and a work sample
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` or near the top of the range

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Do not use one sitting for a placement; use an individually administered criterion-referenced check with pictures and spoken instructions over two or three occasions; re-check within the year
rows.if: Learners are young children (`child`) in screening or readiness testing

rows.basis: [SAT underpredicts girls' performance](claims/sat-underpredicts-girls-performance.md) [~W]; [MIT lower SAT math, equal performance](claims/mit-lower-sat-math-scores-equal-performance.md) [~W] (1987 testimony, no data printed)
rows.change: Use the norm-referenced score with at least one other piece of evidence; look again at everyone near the cut; check the norm group fits the applicants
rows.if: The decision is selection for limited places (a programme, a scholarship, admission)

rows.basis: [Identification tests cannot fully determine learning potential](claims/traditional-identification-tests-fail-learning-potential.md) [~W] (a review section); [diverse students under-identified nationwide](claims/gifted-underrepresentation-diverse-students.md) [~W] (an issue brief); the dual-measure requirement is the earlier page's
rows.change: Build a diagnostic profile: a norm-referenced aptitude or ability measure plus achievement, classroom observation and a classroom-learning task; screen all learners rather than relying on referral; compare identification rates by group with enrolment
rows.if: The decision is gifted or special-education identification

rows.basis: [Statistical item selection undermines criterion-referenced definitions](claims/statistical-item-selection-conflicts-criterion-referenced-definition.md) [+W]; [criterion-referenced tests need construct validation](claims/criterion-referenced-tests-need-construct-validation.md) [+W] (both Nitko 1970, arguments)
rows.change: Define skills before items; keep items that nearly everyone passes after teaching; set the cut by a stated panel or rule before scoring; check a sample of classifications against real tasks once a term
rows.if: You are writing your own criterion-referenced test

rows.basis: [DC lowest at the distribution peak](claims/dc-lowest-at-score-distribution-peak.md) [~M] (simulated data, a measurement property, not a test of the remedy)
rows.change: Expect the least consistent decisions there: give near-cut learners a second, parallel check before deciding, or report "borderline" as its own category
rows.if: Most learners score close to the cut (a pass/fail examination where the cut sits at the most common score)

rows.basis: [Mean-classification method more robust to outliers](claims/mean-classification-cut-score-method-robust.md) [~M]; [agreement 71% to 97%](claims/body-of-work-agreement-rates-71-97.md) [~M] (one state's alternate portfolio assessment for students with significant disabilities, carried to other assessments)
rows.change: Use independent classification of real work samples, compute the cut from each sample's mean classification, and report panelist agreement with the cut
rows.if: A panel will set the cut (a programme standard, a licensing threshold)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Do not read a low percentile as low subject knowledge; check the norm group included learners with this language background; add a low-language criterion-referenced check (spoken, pictorial, or practical) on the same skills
rows.if: Learners take the test in a second language, or have low literacy

rows.basis: untested; the reason not to rank is Gentile's argument ([competitive grading pits students against each other](claims/competitive-grading-pits-students-against-each-other.md) [-W])
rows.change: Report criterion-referenced results privately and per skill ("not yet" with the next step), never as a rank; keep norm-referenced results out of routine feedback
rows.if: Learners have low confidence or are anxious about tests

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: The learner (or family, for a child) decides who sees the full profile; share with teachers only the skills to teach and the supports agreed; never post or rank
rows.if: Results are private or sensitive (a diagnostic profile, a disability assessment)

rows.basis: untested proposal; the threshold model is [Competency-Based Assessment](principles/competency-based-assessment.md)'s
rows.change: Use a criterion-referenced judgment on tasks sampled from the job, with the cut set before scoring; use a norm-referenced score only if places are limited, and then with a work sample
rows.if: Adults in work settings: licensing, certification or job entry

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Judge the whole performance against criteria the audience would recognize; do not split it into paper items to get skill scores; record per-criterion notes from the one performance instead
rows.if: The brief wants a whole-task performance kept whole (a recital, a clinical scenario, a product for a real audience)

rows.basis: untested; the three changes follow steps 4, 5 and 9
rows.change: Keep them as the criteria; change only what the evidence here says matters: set the levels before scoring, report per criterion rather than as a rank, and take a second look at learners on a level boundary
rows.if: The brief names its own rubric, categories or reporting levels

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Check two or three skills with three items each rather than every skill thinly; rotate skills across checks
rows.if: A fixed short time budget (one 15-minute slot per check)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Use a criterion-referenced placement check on the entry skills, 20 to 30 minutes; treat near-cut results as provisional and re-check in the first week of teaching
rows.if: Only a single session is available (a one-off placement)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Give the same items, time and aids in every mode, or record the difference beside each result; keep items short and single-screen for phones; compare results by mode before pooling
rows.if: Mixed modes: some learners in the room, some remote, some on phones only

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Learners self-score short checks against an answer key with worked reasons; the teacher spends contact time only on near-cut learners and the skill most learners have not mastered
rows.if: One teacher for many learners, or facilitator time is scarce (volunteers, a short weekly session)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Report the percentage reaching each level with the number tested, and the level definitions; do not compare schools on a norm-referenced percentile alone; see [High-Stakes Testing and Accountability Effects](principles/summative-assessment.md)
rows.if: Results are reported for accountability (school, district or programme reports)

rows.basis: untested; from the earlier page
rows.change: List the candidate explanations and gather one observation that separates them (a task in the test's format, a look at what the test covers) before changing either
rows.if: A parent or learner asks why a classroom grade and a test score disagree

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Teach the difference with short worked examples and a tap-to-sort activity (statements sorted into "tells you what I can do" and "tells you how I rank"), and assess with auto-scored items against a stated criterion; do not ask learners to write test items on a phone
rows.if: Self-paced mobile study for school-age learners with no live teacher

rows.basis: [Advance organizers aided learning in a 1980 meta-analysis, but activating prior topic knowledge did not improve primary pupils' text comprehension in one experiment](claims/activation-improves-learning.md) [~M] (carried from topic-knowledge activation in reading to cultural connection)
rows.change: Teach the concept explicitly first, with one familiar context as the example; ask for learners' own contexts only after they can explain the concept once
rows.if: Learners are `novice` on the content and have little experience related to it

rows.basis: [Many practices in adult literacy programs violate principles of learning for adults, including short-timeframe funding, isolated individualized learning, ignored learner experience, and non-meaningful materials](claims/adult-literacy-programs-violate-adult-learning-principles.md) [+W] (a 1993 handbook's review of earlier writing, naming ignored learner experience and reused elementary materials as common faults; no data, and no test of the alternative)
rows.change: Make cases from learners' work and lives the main material from the second session; ask each learner for one case per unit, and compare across them; avoid leftover school-age materials
rows.if: Learners are `adult`, in work or with family responsibilities

rows.basis: [Assessment tasks built on family-identified funds of knowledge elicited computational thinking from K-2 children in a small design-based study that made no comparison with standard assessment](claims/funds-of-knowledge-tasks-reveal-computational-thinking.md) [+M] (13 children, two tasks, no comparison with a standard task; resource-intensive)
rows.change: Build assessment tasks from practices families describe in interviews, as play with cards and objects, and ask children to justify their choices
rows.if: Learners are young children (`child`, K-2)

rows.basis: [Teachers doing household ethnography had readier entree to families than anthropologists and were welcomed without suspicion in the Tucson project.](claims/teachers-have-readier-household-entree-than-anthropologists.md) [+W]; [In the Tucson household ethnography, exchanges within households' social networks were often reciprocal and built mutual trust through shared practical activities.](claims/household-exchange-networks-are-reciprocal-and-build-trust.md) [+W]; [Teacher Researcher Difficulties Eased By Reflective Labs](claims/teacher-researcher-difficulties-eased-by-reflective-labs.md) [+W] (one project's digest, `q1`, no learner outcome; the visit numbers are untested)
rows.change: Approach each visit as an exchange (bring something, ask about practices and skills, not problems); meet as a teacher study group every few weeks to turn what was found into tasks; plan two or three visits per teacher a term, not one per child
rows.if: Teachers can visit learners' families (school-age learners)

rows.basis: [Positioning personal experience as an epistemic resource supports expansion from inward to outward critical orientations](claims/positioning-personal-experience-as-epistemic-resource-supports-critical-orientation-expansion.md) [+W] (69 students, 12th-grade English, one site); [Agentic engagement with lively data supports epistemically just crisis sensemaking](claims/lively-data-and-agentic-positions-support-epistemically-just-crisis-sensemaking.md) [+W] (four minority youth using their own and their community's experience as evidence beside official COVID-19 data; observed outside instruction, not a design)
rows.change: Start from learners' own experience of the topic, then add readings and structured discussion that move it to systemic causes over several weeks; collect writing at the start and end
rows.if: Goal is critical analysis or civic understanding (`attitude-motivation`, `principle`)

rows.basis: [Learners invest more effort in tasks they perceive as interesting, personally important, or useful to their future goals.](claims/task-value-increases-motivation-and-engagement.md) [+M] (reviews of utility-value writing; the trade-off with practice is untested)
rows.change: Keep connections to one opening example and a short weekly utility-value reflection; do not cut practice time for them
rows.if: Goal is a `procedure` or `verbal-association` assessed on a standard test

rows.basis: [Multimodal, culturally grounded formative assessment supports engagement and agency](claims/multimodal-culturally-grounded-assessment-supports-engagement-and-agency.md) [+W] (youth aged 11–17 in two dance centres, researchers known to the sites; untested in a classroom with a new teacher)
rows.change: Accept movement, music and vernacular language as responses in formative checks, and say the check is a conversation
rows.if: Setting is informal or community-based (after-school, a community centre)

rows.basis: [Embodied dance improvisation supports physics engagement and sense-making](claims/embodied-dance-improvisation-supports-physics-engagement-and-sensemaking.md) [+W]; [The authors report that the kinesthetic experience enhances student understanding and that a student project provides evidence of the approach's effectiveness](claims/kinesthetic-experience-enhances-understanding-physics-of-dance.md) [+W] (a college physics-of-dance course; the authors' conviction, no outcome measure); [Two-force-plate recording revealed individual left-right impulse asymmetries in student jumps while total takeoff and landing impulses remained comparable](claims/two-force-plate-impulse-asymmetry-student-project.md) [+W] (one student-conceived project on dancers' own jumps; shows what such a project can find, not that it teaches more)
rows.change: Make the learner's own movement the data: record it (video, force plates, timers), have learners compute the quantity from it, and let each pose a final question about their own practice
rows.if: Learners bring a practised physical skill (dance, a sport, a trade) to a science or mathematics course

rows.basis: [A substantial fraction of students reported increased interest in physics and ability to connect physics to their life science majors and careers](claims/life-science-examples-increase-interest-and-relevance.md) [+W] (a redesigned introductory physics course; 9 of 15 interviewees gave a correct example; no comparison course); [Students and faculty value real-world examples in gateway math, but limited resources and training often lead to procedural instruction](claims/real-world-relevance-gateway-math-procedural-instruction.md) [~W] (provide the examples centrally: faculty without time or training fall back on procedure)
rows.change: Draw worked examples from the field learners are heading into (biology for life-science majors), and ask each learner for one correct example linking the concept to their own interest or career
rows.if: A college service or gateway course taught to students from other majors

rows.basis: untested
rows.change: Give prompts that ask the learner to write their own example and explain the concept in it, with a bank of worked examples from several contexts; require no public sharing
rows.if: Setting is `online-self-paced`, no teacher present

rows.basis: [International students wanted more global cases and closer connections between case analyses and their local work contexts](claims/lack-of-global-cases-local-relevance.md) [+W] (interviews with international students in one case study of U.S. online courses; students' preferences, no learning outcome)
rows.change: Balance cases from several countries rather than one national setting, and ask each learner to apply each case to a practical issue in their own workplace or country
rows.if: Learners are spread across countries (an international or online cohort)

rows.basis: untested; from the earlier page's constraints (stereotyping, uneven familiarity)
rows.change: Use a private intake to collect contexts; draw examples from what learners wrote, not from assumptions about groups; offer several entry points per idea
rows.if: A large, mixed group, and the teacher does not know learners' communities

rows.basis: [Community projects need conceptual framing to avoid narrowing the learning object](claims/community-projects-need-conceptual-framing-to-avoid-narrowing-the-learning-object.md) [~W] (one case study)
rows.change: Name the concepts the project must use in advance, and hold a structured discussion with all groups midway about what the project means
rows.if: The design partners with a community organisation or local businesses

rows.basis: [Personal connection to data supports critical data-literacy stance-taking](claims/personal-connection-to-data-supports-critical-data-literacy-stance-taking.md) [~M] (prospective teachers; it occurred in all groups in one course and 1 of 6 in the other, tracking the instructor's framing)
rows.change: Plan explicit prompts that ask learners where they stand in what the data or text describes; do not expect personal connection to arise unprompted
rows.if: The instructor does not usually raise social or ethical questions in this course

rows.basis: [Belonging Interventions Improve Outcomes](claims/belonging-interventions-improve-outcomes.md) [~M] (worked only where groups had opportunities to belong); [A brief values-affirmation writing exercise raised African American seventh-graders' grades in two small field experiments, but a large same-district replication found no effect](claims/self-affirmation-improves-outcomes.md) [~M] (a close replication found no benefit)
rows.change: Do not rely on one brief identity-related writing exercise; pair any belonging or values message with lasting structural support (check-ins, groups learners can join)
rows.if: Learners from groups stereotyped in the domain are at a transition (entry to a school, college or field) and stakes are high

rows.basis: [Staff at one university Indigenous centre report that many students, Indigenous and non-Indigenous, show keen interest in local Indigenous culture and take part avidly when it is taught](claims/local-indigenous-culture-student-interest.md) [+W] (one university Indigenous centre; students' interest reported without numbers; who teaches is the authors' proposal, untested); [When AI/AN communities design their own place-, culture-, and language-based education programs, students' school engagement and learning flourish](claims/culture-based-programs-flourish-engagement.md) [+W] (a narrative review citing two earlier sources, no effect size; supports community authorship of the programme, not a teacher-built connection)
rows.change: Involve the people who hold that knowledge in planning and, where they agree, in teaching it; do not have the teacher narrate a community's knowledge on its behalf
rows.if: The connection draws on a local community's knowledge (for example local Indigenous knowledge), not the individual learner's

rows.basis: untested
rows.change: Use one private prompt for a learner-supplied context and one explanation prompt; record what learners offer and claim nothing about lasting change
rows.if: Time is one session only

rows.basis: untested; from the earlier page's constraints
rows.change: Make every personal prompt optional and private first; offer composite or fictional cases as equal alternatives; never ask a learner to represent a group
rows.if: Learners do not want to share personal experience (refugees, people in recovery, a mixed workplace)

rows.basis: Wait time: [Reviews of classroom studies, read from their abstracts, associate longer teacher wait time with longer, higher-cognitive-level student responses, with no effect size recorded](claims/increasing-wait-time-improves-response-quality.md) [+M] (reviews across grade levels, not by culture). Family conversation: untested
rows.change: Teach each convention by modelling and short practice ("now we think for three seconds, then whisper to your partner"); prefer choral and whiteboard response; talk with families about how questions and help work at home
rows.if: Learners are `child` (primary age)

rows.basis: Correction: [empathic discipline](claims/brief-intervention-empathic-discipline-cuts-suspensions.md) [+M] (US middle-school maths teachers). Rest untested
rows.change: Name conventions openly and invite learners to say where their norms differ; avoid public correction in front of peers; watch for learners who define themselves against school (step 10)
rows.if: Learners are `adolescent`

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Ask directly about expectations of hierarchy, questioning a trainer, and group versus individual credit; never treat silence as lack of knowledge; give written or private ways to raise a question
rows.if: Learners are `adult`, in `adult-workplace` or professional training

rows.basis: untested proposal; the wait-time reviews are of face-to-face classrooms
rows.change: Lengthen wait time further for remote learners (audio delay); take every whole-class answer through a poll or chat that both groups use; do not read camera-off or looking away as disengagement; call on remote learners only after a private check
rows.if: Mixed mode: some remote, some in the room, or phone-only

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Leave response windows open rather than timed; give discussion-board options to post after reading others or to reply privately; state the platform's conventions on help and copying in plain terms
rows.if: `online-self-paced`, no teacher present
