rows.basis: Wait time in classrooms: [Questioning Strategies Improve Learning](claims/questioning-strategies-improve-learning.md) [+M]. Tally and response modes: untested
rows.change: Use all-student response (cards, whiteboards, polls) for most questions and a simple tally of who answers publicly; correct conduct with low-profile moves first
rows.if: One teacher, a large class

rows.basis: Wait time: [Reviews of classroom studies, read from their abstracts, associate longer teacher wait time with longer, higher-cognitive-level student responses, with no effect size recorded](claims/increasing-wait-time-improves-response-quality.md) [+M]. The selection of three is untested
rows.change: Keep three moves only: three-second wait time, pair-before-share, and "ask before you name it" for conduct; skip the audit and arc
rows.if: Scarce facilitator time: volunteers, a busy shift, a tutor checking in briefly

rows.basis: Belonging boundary: [Belonging Interventions Improve Outcomes](claims/belonging-interventions-improve-outcomes.md) [~M] (college entry). Rest untested
rows.change: State the session's conventions at the start (how to answer, how to ask for help, what counts as working together); use written or paired answers before any public one; do not run a one-off identity or belonging exercise and expect a lasting change
rows.if: A single session only

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Give private and oral options (tell a partner, then the partner reports), more wait time, no cold-calling until the learner has answered correctly in private
rows.if: Learners with low confidence or low literacy, or learning in a second language

rows.basis: [Questioning Strategies Improve Learning](claims/questioning-strategies-improve-learning.md) [+M] (higher-cognitive questions and wait time; not tested by culture)
rows.change: Choral and quick-fire response are fine for well-practised content; keep long wait time and pair talk for questions that need reasoning
rows.if: Goal is recall or fluency (`verbal-association`, `procedure`) rather than reasoning

rows.basis: [Cooperative Learning Improves Achievement](claims/cooperative-learning-improves-achievement.md) [+M]; [group rewards and individual accountability](claims/cooperative-learning-group-rewards-and-individual-accountability.md) [+M] (schools; not tested by culture)
rows.change: Add cooperative parts in which recognition rests on each member's individual learning; state before each task what help is allowed
rows.if: Grading or the activity is competitive and must stay so (curve, ranking, competitions)

rows.basis: [empathic discipline](claims/brief-intervention-empathic-discipline-cuts-suspensions.md) [+M] (US middle schools; the overall effect in the replication was marginal, the disparity effect larger)
rows.change: Give staff a brief empathic-discipline exercise and a "describe, ask, then act" routine; tally corrections by group each week; check that school policy does not undo it
rows.if: Discipline stakes are high (exclusion, suspension), or one group is corrected far more often

rows.basis: [Belonging Interventions Improve Outcomes](claims/belonging-interventions-improve-outcomes.md) [~M]; [self-affirmation](claims/self-affirmation-improves-outcomes.md) [~M]; [teacher expectation effects](claims/teacher-expectation-effects-on-achievement.md) [~M] (one Dutch associational study)
rows.change: Change daily norms and the opportunities to belong before adding a brief belonging or affirmation exercise; ground judgements of ability in work samples, not in participation style
rows.if: Learners come from groups stereotyped as not belonging, or tracked low

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Rehearse in pairs or small groups first; offer a group presentation or a recorded one as well as a solo live one; agree in advance what questions the audience may ask
rows.if: A product or performance for a real audience (presentation, recital, pitch)

rows.basis: untested; from the earlier page
rows.change: Still run the audit and teach the conventions; diversity of class, religion, home language and schooling is usually present
rows.if: The class looks culturally homogeneous

rows.basis: Wait time: [Reviews of classroom studies, read from their abstracts, associate longer teacher wait time with longer, higher-cognitive-level student responses, with no effect size recorded](claims/increasing-wait-time-improves-response-quality.md) [+M]. Rest untested
rows.change: Keep it; change only what the evidence says matters: at least three seconds of wait time inside it, one private or written answer before any public one, and a weekly check of who it calls on and who it corrects
rows.if: The brief names its own routine (its own participation protocol, cold-call policy, class charter or behaviour plan)

rows.basis: [Process goals lead to better skill acquisition for novices than outcome goals.](claims/process-goals-outperform-outcome-goals-for-novices.md) [+M] (high-school writing revision, carried to debrief focus); [Self Assessment Accuracy Is Low Without Training](claims/self-assessment-accuracy-is-low-without-training.md) [~M]
rows.change: Facilitator-led throughout; give the criterion or a model performance before analysis; ask about cues and steps, not outcomes; name what the expert would have noticed; one change each, stated as an action
rows.if: Learners are `novice` on the task (first simulations, first placements)

rows.basis: [Instructional guidance that helps novices can become redundant or counterproductive as expertise grows.](claims/expertise-reversal-effect.md) [~M] (cognitive-load studies; no study of debriefs)
rows.change: Learners choose the decision points and lead; the facilitator asks for alternatives considered and the reasoning behind them, and adds only what was missed; keep it shorter
rows.if: Learners are `advanced`, or experienced practitioners

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Five minutes, oral, teacher-led, three questions (what happened, what was tricky, what we will do next time), straight after the activity; one class change written on the board and read out next time
rows.if: Learners are `child`ren (primary age)

rows.basis: untested proposal; from the earlier page's examples
rows.change: Use an after-action format (what was planned, what happened, why the difference, what to keep and what to change); keep it separate from performance appraisal and from any incident investigation; write the changes into the team's next briefing
rows.if: `adult` learners in a work setting, after a real shift, project or incident

rows.basis: [Simulation Based Education With Deliberate Practice Improves Clinical Outcomes](claims/simulation-based-education-with-deliberate-practice-improves-clinical-outcomes.md) [+M] (14 studies, health professions); [Simulation Based Education Improves Outcomes](claims/simulation-based-education-improves-outcomes.md) [~M]: could not isolate feedback as the active feature
rows.change: Treat the debrief as the feedback step of a repeated attempt: debrief against a stated mastery standard, then rerun the scenario or a changed one until the standard is met
rows.if: Goal is a `procedure` or psychomotor skill in `workplace-clinical` training

rows.basis: [Prompting learners to self-explain…](claims/self-explanation-improves-conceptual-understanding.md) [+M] (immediate tests, study of examples and text; carried to debriefs)
rows.change: Spend most of the time on the learners' reasoning at two or three decision points; end with the general rule stated in the learner's words and tested on a new case
rows.if: Goal is judgement, a `concept` or a `principle` (diagnostic reasoning, a negotiation, an ethical decision)

rows.basis: untested proposal; from the earlier page's constraints
rows.change: Lengthen the reactions phase; check everyone is settled before analysis; move personal distress to a separate, private conversation; never analyse the performance of someone visibly upset in front of the group
rows.if: The experience was emotionally charged or high-stress

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Everyone writes their first answers (what happened, one decision point) in a shared chat or document before talking; the facilitator calls on remote learners first at each phase; share the recording or the timeline on screen; phone-only learners send a voice note or a two-line text
rows.if: Some learners join remotely while others are in the room, or some are on phones only

rows.basis: [Reflective Practice Improves Outcomes When Structured](claims/reflective-practice-improves-outcomes-when-structured.md) [+M] (classroom engineering course); [Metacognitive prompts improve learning](claims/metacognitive-prompts-improve-learning.md) [+M] (computer-based environments)
rows.change: Replace the live debrief with a written self-debrief: three to five specific questions tied to the criteria, then a model performance or expert commentary to compare with, then one change for the next module, shown back at its start
rows.if: `online-self-paced`, no facilitator

rows.basis: [Peer Discussion Improves Conceptual Understanding](claims/peer-discussion-improves-conceptual-understanding.md) [+M] (peers then instructor; undergraduate classes); peers who share a misconception may reinforce it, untested
rows.change: Debrief in threes or fours against a written protocol for 10 minutes; then the whole group on the most common gap, with the facilitator's explanation after the groups have reported
rows.if: One facilitator for a large group

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: A three-question debrief straight after, in five minutes: what happened at the key moment, one thing to keep, one change; the leader corrects any wrong rule in one sentence; changes go in a shared log; a full debrief only for critical or new events
rows.if: Scarce facilitator time (volunteers, a busy shift, a supervisor who can give five minutes)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: One short experience, a debrief of at least equal length, then a two-minute retry of the key moment with the change; do not claim retention
rows.if: One session only (`single-session`)

rows.basis: [Reflective Practice Improves Outcomes When Structured](claims/reflective-practice-improves-outcomes-when-structured.md) [+M]; [Feedback Most Effective At Task And Process Levels](claims/feedback-most-effective-at-task-and-process-levels.md) [+S] (neither compares debrief models)
rows.change: Keep it. Check only that it reaches the learners' reasoning at specific decision points, gives task- and process-level feedback against a stated criterion, and ends with one written change for a next attempt; add whichever of those is missing as one question
rows.if: The brief names its own debrief model (plus/delta, PEARLS, GAS, an after-action review, the "What? So what? Now what?" questions)

rows.basis: [Feedback Most Effective At Task And Process Levels](claims/feedback-most-effective-at-task-and-process-levels.md) [+S] (feedback aimed at the self lost effect); separation from grading untested
rows.change: Separate the formative debrief from grading in time and by person where possible; talk about actions and decisions, never traits; record what was agreed, not who erred
rows.if: The performance is assessed or high-stakes, or the team must keep working together

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Debrief the team privately before any public review; use audience responses as evidence in the debrief, not as its verdict; keep the analysis out of anything the audience sees
rows.if: The product or performance was for a real audience (a public performance, a client deliverable, a community event)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Take first answers privately, orally or drawn, with sentence frames ("I saw…", "I decided… because…"); in the group, ask for actions, not explanations, from anyone not ready; judge the analysis, not the language
rows.if: Learners have low confidence or literacy, or speak in a second language

rows.basis: [Instructional guidance that helps novices can become redundant or counterproductive as expertise grows.](claims/expertise-reversal-effect.md) [~M] (review of cognitive-load studies, carried to skill refinement); [process goals for novices](claims/process-goals-outperform-outcome-goals-for-novices.md) [~M]
rows.change: Do not isolate components yet: model the whole task, use guided practice with support, and set process goals; start targeted refinement only once the learner can perform unaided
rows.if: Learners are `novice` on this task, at first exposure

rows.basis: [Process goals lead to better skill acquisition for novices than outcome goals.](claims/process-goals-outperform-outcome-goals-for-novices.md) [~M] (reports that a shift to outcome goals after mastery can help; high-school writing)
rows.change: Let the learner pick the component from their own log, raise the standard, use outcome targets beside process goals, and give feedback mainly when the log shows a plateau
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` and have plateaued

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: The teacher chooses the component and writes the goal in the child's words; drills of five to ten minutes; a visible chart of attempts that met the standard; whole-task attempt at the end
rows.if: Learners are `child` (primary age)

rows.basis: [Deliberate practice and performance across domains](claims/deliberate-practice-improves-performance.md) [~M] (correlational meta-analysis: practice hours explain far more of performance in games, music and sports than in education or the professions; not a test of a design); [Goal setting improves performance](claims/goal-setting-improves-performance.md) [~S] (goal effects smaller on complex work and laboratory tasks)
rows.change: Build the standard first: three or four annotated exemplars at different levels and a short rubric; expect smaller and slower gains than in sport or music, and check gains on new whole tasks; expect the component goal to push less than on a simple task
rows.if: Goal is a diffuse performance (`complex-skill` such as essay writing, teaching, leading a meeting)

rows.basis: [Simulation-based education with deliberate practice improves clinical outcomes](claims/simulation-based-education-with-deliberate-practice-improves-clinical-outcomes.md) [+M] (14 studies, health professions, procedural skills, against traditional clinical education)
rows.change: Use a simulator or part-task trainer with a mastery standard per step, immediate expert or device feedback, repetition until the standard is met and rising difficulty; add booster sessions later
rows.if: Goal is a `procedure` or psychomotor skill in `workplace-clinical` training

rows.basis: [Retrieval practice and spaced retrieval improve achievement and retention by medium amounts, while interleaving helps category learning only for some materials and blocking beats it for words](claims/desirable-difficulties-enhance-learning.md) [~S] (spaced retrieval beats massed; interleaving helps some materials and not words); see [Retrieval Practice](principles/retrieval-practice.md)
rows.change: Use spaced retrieval practice with corrective feedback instead of component drills
rows.if: Goal is recall of facts or vocabulary (`verbal-association`)

rows.basis: [Self-regulated learning models treat self-monitoring as a core process through which learners notice gaps and adjust strategy](claims/self-monitoring-improves-self-regulation.md) [+M] (reviews; untested within deliberate practice or online)
rows.change: Give items with automatic checking or a worked answer to compare; have the learner score against annotated exemplars and keep an error log; require one whole-task submission per session reviewed by a person or a rubric-based check
rows.if: Setting is `online-self-paced`, no coach present

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Work on the component most of the class misses; pairs score each other's attempts on that one rubric line; the teacher scans every whole-task attempt at the end and gives whole-class feedback on the commonest error
rows.if: `classroom` with one teacher and a large group

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: One component, three rounds of three to five attempts, then a scored whole-task attempt; report the change against the baseline as immediate only, not as retained
rows.if: Time is one session only

rows.basis: [Deliberate practice interventions produce higher real estate licensing exam pass rates](claims/deliberate-practice-raises-licensing-pass-rate.md) [+W] (one dissertation, two self-selected groups, no effect size)
rows.change: Choose components from an item analysis of practice exams, practice in the exam's format with feedback on each item, and run timed whole exams at intervals
rows.if: Stakes are high (licensing or certification exam)

rows.basis: untested; a practitioner assertion that over-challenge with too little support leads to giving up ([Imbalanced challenge and support causes novice library learners to give up or remain dependent](claims/challenge-support-imbalance-effects-novice-learners.md) [~W], no data)
rows.change: Shorten sessions, lower the step to the next standard, show the log of attempts that met it, and let the learner choose which component to work on next
rows.if: Learners are giving up, or the practice feels punitive

rows.basis: [Feedback improves learning by a medium amount on average, but its effect varies widely with the information it carries, and more than a third of feedback interventions reduce performance](claims/feedback-improves-learning.md) [~S] (more than a third of feedback interventions reduced performance, more so when they drew attention to the self; work and laboratory as well as education)
rows.change: Replace it with feedback about the attempt against the standard and the change to make next
rows.if: Feedback is mostly praise, grades or comparison with others

rows.basis: [Brief empathic-discipline exercise reduced suspensions](claims/brief-intervention-empathic-discipline-cuts-suspensions.md) [~S] (one targeted belief about discipline, middle-school mathematics teachers; carried to other decisions, untested); otherwise untested
rows.change: Run the scenario step (20–30 minutes), one group comparison of readings (15 minutes), and one written decision change with a named follow-up check (10 minutes); arrange for a peer tally or data review a few weeks later, even by email. Do not claim lasting change from the session
rows.if: A single session only (one workshop, one in-service hour)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Five minutes for one tally or data point, ten for one educator's case and the assumption it shows, five for each person's one changed decision; rotate whose data is discussed
rows.if: A fixed short time budget inside routine meetings (e.g. 20 minutes a month)

rows.basis: [Brief empathic-discipline exercise reduced suspensions](claims/brief-intervention-empathic-discipline-cuts-suspensions.md) [~S] (its Discussion notes a climate that rewards exclusion can erase gains [-W])
rows.change: Start with a reading of misbehaviour as a moment to keep the relationship, with a written reflection on how the educator would respond; track referrals or suspensions by group each term, and look at policies that require exclusion beside individual practice
rows.if: The decision is discipline, referrals or exclusion

rows.basis: untested here; [teacher expectation bias predicted later performance](claims/teacher-expectation-effects-on-achievement.md) [~M] is a reason to look (Dutch secondary cohort, associational)
rows.change: Use a peer tally or analytics of calls and praise by learner over one lesson, repeat after a named change; pair with the wait-time and private-response options in [Culturally Responsive Classroom Norms](principles/culturally-responsive-classroom-norms.md)
rows.if: The decision is who is called on, praised or corrected

rows.basis: [Teacher expectation bias predicted later performance](claims/teacher-expectation-effects-on-achievement.md) [~M] (associational; does not show that expectations cause the difference); [deficit perceptions are said to lower expectations](claims/deficit-view-of-minority-households-lowers-academic-expectations.md) [+W] (asserted, no evidence offered)
rows.change: Examine a sample of judgements against an independent measure (a common task scored blind); write explicit criteria before grading the next set
rows.if: The decision is expectations, grading or tracking

rows.basis: untested; household-research reports are from practising teachers ([funds of knowledge research raised teachers' expectations](claims/funds-of-knowledge-research-raises-teacher-expectations.md) [+W])
rows.change: Use more scenarios and other people's anonymised classrooms, fewer own-classroom tallies at first; include one visit or interview with a family or community member
rows.if: Educators are new or preservice

rows.basis: [Fluent illusions mislead self-assessment](claims/fluent-illusions-mislead-self-assessment.md) [~M] (adults judging their own learning in the laboratory; carried to judging one's own practice)
rows.change: Lead with their own tally rather than a discussion of bias; ask them to predict the tally first and compare
rows.if: Educators are experienced and confident they "treat everyone the same"

rows.basis: [Reflective study groups as a safe, non-judgemental place to think aloud](claims/teacher-researcher-difficulties-eased-by-reflective-labs.md) [~W] (one digest, teacher reports); otherwise untested
rows.change: Frame each session as examining decisions, not people; start with simulated cases; keep the naming of assumptions private for the first cycles and share only the changed decision
rows.if: Educators are defensive, or attendance is mandated

rows.basis: untested
rows.change: Use the workplace's own data (where staff come from, prior jobs, how names are read, first associations with nationalities and job titles), as in [stereotype-awareness activities for supervisors](strategies/stereotype-awareness-cultural-activities.md); the decision examined is allocation of tasks, feedback and promotion, tallied over a month
rows.if: Adults in work settings (supervisors, trainers of a diverse workforce)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Tally participation by channel (voice, chat, camera, in-room) as well as by learner; check who is addressed first and whose chat is answered; ask remote learners separately and anonymously
rows.if: Teaching is online, or mixed mode (some learners remote, some in the room; some on phones)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Pair educators to observe each other with a one-page tally; the facilitator reads only each pair's one-line summary and changed decision, and meets the group once per cycle
rows.if: One facilitator or coach for many educators, or scarce facilitator time (a busy term, volunteer coaches)

rows.basis: untested proposal; the external-evidence check rests on [fluent illusions mislead self-assessment](claims/fluent-illusions-mislead-self-assessment.md) [~M] (carried)
rows.change: Keep it; change only what the evidence says matters: add one external data point to each cycle and require one named decision change with a follow-up check
rows.if: The brief names its own routine for this (its own observation protocol, reflection prompt, equity rubric or audit checklist)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Tally and review in those categories; do not substitute this page's examples
rows.if: The brief gives its own categories (the institution's learner groups, a district equity framework, the course team's audit headings)

rows.basis: untested proposal; from the earlier page's caution about defensiveness
rows.change: The educator controls who sees it: journals and assumption notes stay with the educator; the group sees only the tally and the changed decision; no grading of disclosures
rows.if: Reflection touches private or sensitive material (an educator's own identity, experiences of racism, journal entries about bias)

rows.basis: [Strength language often appeared without naming an actual strength](claims/coach-wright-topics-track-asset-deficit-mindsets.md) [~M] (simulation responses, associational)
rows.change: Assess decisions in a scenario (what the educator notices and would do) and changes in tallies, not attitudes or vocabulary; check that "strengths" language names an actual strength
rows.if: High stakes (required training, accreditation, a performance review)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Rehearse the whole conversation in a simulation or role play with debrief, rather than splitting it into knowledge items; record what the educator noticed and said
rows.if: The brief wants a whole difficult interaction rehearsed (a parent meeting, a disciplinary conversation, a complaint about bias)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Have members of that audience or community review examples, cases and images before release; record what they changed
rows.if: The product is materials or a course for a real audience

rows.basis: [Contingent scaffolding improves learning more than fixed or absent support.](claims/contingent-scaffolding-improves-learning.md) [~M] (one-to-one tutoring, carried to software)
rows.change: Use items close to worked examples, the full cue–hint–worked-step ladder, an explanation prompt every three to five items, and feedback on every item
rows.if: Learners are `novice` on the task

rows.basis: [Instructional guidance that helps novices can become redundant or counterproductive as expertise grows.](claims/expertise-reversal-effect.md) [~M] (a cognitive-load review; gives no crossover point)
rows.change: Remove most hints and prompts; give mixed, whole-task items and feedback only on request
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` on the task, or succeed unaided on the first set

rows.basis: session length and supervision are untested proposals; the substitution rests on [Physical and virtual instructional materials are equally effective for teaching fourth- and fifth-graders to design unconfounded experiments when instructional method is controlled](claims/physical-virtual-materials-equal-cvs-learning.md) [+M] (one science skill; no difference found, equivalence not tested). Online-versus-classroom comparisons for school-age learners are almost absent: [A systematic search found almost no rigorous studies contrasting online and face-to-face instruction for K–12 students: none with computable effect sizes through 2006, and only five meeting meta-analysis criteria through July 2008.](claims/few-rigorous-k12-online-studies.md) [~M]
rows.change: Use short sessions (10 minutes or less), supervised by an adult in the room; give feedback that needs little reading; avoid open typed answers. A simulation can stand in for physical materials if the same instruction goes with it
rows.if: Learners are `child` (primary age)

rows.basis: untested proposal; contact task from [Online attrition during Orientation Week is twice that of onground classes' first week](claims/orientation-week-attrition-double-online.md) [~M] (university continuing education)
rows.change: Use short sets on a phone that can be done in one sitting, and tasks taken from their own work; keep the first-week contact task
rows.if: Learners are `adult` or professionals studying around work

rows.basis: [Intelligent tutoring systems improve achievement over non-individualised instruction](claims/adaptive-learning-improves-outcomes.md) [+S] (tutoring-system meta-analyses; gains smaller on standardised than on locally developed tests)
rows.change: Put the bulk of practice online with automatic checking; use an intelligent tutor if one exists for the domain
rows.if: Goal is a `procedure` or `verbal-association` with checkable answers

rows.basis: [Prompting learners to self-explain improves understanding and problem solving on immediate tests by a moderate average amount, with little evidence yet on delayed or classroom gains.](claims/self-explanation-improves-conceptual-understanding.md) [+S] (not specific to digital delivery)
rows.change: Keep answer-checking, but add explanation prompts and changed items; hold discussion of reasons in a live or threaded session
rows.if: Goal is a `concept`, a `principle`, or transfer

rows.basis: [Self-regulated learning interventions have a moderate effect (0.65) on learning outcomes in online and blended environments](claims/srl-interventions-moderate-effect-online-blended.md) [+M] (15 studies); a diary alone did not help in one course ([A daily learning diary alone (Group D) did not produce statistically significant pre-post gains on any measured outcome in an online mathematics preparation course](claims/learning-diary-alone-no-significant-srl-gains-online-math-prep-course.md) [~M])
rows.change: Add the contact task in week 1, a fixed weekly rhythm with a deadline, visible progress against a criterion, and a weekly plan prompt; check logins by day 3
rows.if: Setting is `online-self-paced`, no teacher present

rows.basis: untested proposal; contingent-support evidence is one-to-one ([Contingent scaffolding improves learning more than fixed or absent support.](claims/contingent-scaffolding-improves-learning.md) [~M])
rows.change: Use the software for individual practice and hints while the teacher watches the class's results live and goes to those who are stuck; use class time for what the software cannot do (discussion of reasons, whole tasks)
rows.if: `classroom`, one teacher and a large group, devices available

rows.basis: untested proposal; learning a new interface costs time the method needs
rows.change: Do not introduce a new platform; use the classroom, or one familiar tool, for practice with feedback
rows.if: Time is short (one or two sessions)

rows.basis: [Laptop note-takers transcribed more verbatim and did worse on conceptual questions than longhand note-takers in one set of experiments, but a direct replication found no consistent difference in test performance](claims/laptop-notes-verbatim-shallower.md) [~M] (college students; a replication found no consistent difference)
rows.change: Ask learners to summarise in their own words, not transcribe; do not ban devices on the strength of the longhand evidence
rows.if: Note-taking during lectures on laptops or tablets is planned

rows.basis: untested proposal; its reasoning is Salomon's distinction between what a learner does with the tool and what remains when working alone ([Salomon distinguishes effects with the computer (system performance) from effects of the computer (cognitive residue on the solo performer)](claims/effects-with-versus-effects-of-computer.md) [+W], a conceptual argument reported second-hand)
rows.change: Judge readiness only on unaided items done without hints; keep a log of hints used; give at least one supervised check in the final assessment's format
rows.if: Stakes are high, or the final assessment is unaided and supervised

rows.basis: untested proposal, from the earlier page; the condition is documented in [Individual internet penetration in rural Bangladesh (36.5%) is about half the urban rate (71.4%), which one case-study preprint argues puts cloud-dependent AI tools out of reach for rural learners](claims/rural-urban-connectivity-exclusion-bangladesh.md) [~W] (survey figures for one country; no offline design tested) and, for adult education, [Learners used products outside class despite infrastructure limits: 65% of surveyed students reported doing software work outside class while mobile access was largely unavailable](claims/adult-ed-out-of-class-use-mobile-gap.md) [~W] (a survey at fourteen sites; smartphone ownership figures are second-hand)
rows.change: Make every required activity available offline or on paper, use low-bandwidth formats (text, short audio, captioned video), and grade nothing that some learners cannot reach. Check that the software runs on the phones learners own, since out-of-class work may otherwise depend on finding a computer
rows.if: Access is uneven (shared devices, poor bandwidth, accessibility needs)

rows.basis: [Review reports a field experiment in which GPT access improved supported practice but was followed by poorer unaided test performance, mitigated by a guarded tutor](claims/gpt4-access-harms-learning-after-withdrawal.md) [~M] (one high-school mathematics trial, reported second-hand); a structured tutor raised post-test scores over a no-tutor arm in one small preregistered field experiment ([Access to a structured conversational AI tutor increased post-test content scores over a no-AI holdout with ambient consumer AI available](claims/structured-ai-tutor-raises-post-test-scores-field-experiment.md) [+M]; 46 analysed). Unrestricted access in a 35-minute learning phase raised unaided scores straight after (0.28 SD) and by 0.21 SD a week later, not significant ([AI access raises immediate unaided test scores by 7.2 percentage points (0.28 SD) after a timed learning phase](claims/genai-access-raises-immediate-test-scores.md) [~M], [One week later, the AI-access group's lead on unaided assessments shrinks to 3.9 pp (0.21 SD), short of statistical significance (p = 0.068)](claims/genai-learning-gain-persists-one-week.md) [~M]), so unrestricted access does not always harm; the configuration and the task decide. Errors and lack of real-time response were the weaknesses learners named in one music study ([Students identified weaknesses in the AI feedback model: lack of real-time feedback, software/economic access barriers, and occasional incorrect or inconsistent outputs](claims/genai-feedback-weaknesses-realtime-and-errors.md) [~W])
rows.change: Use a tutor set to withhold final answers and give graded hints, not a general chatbot; judge readiness only on unaided items with the tool removed, both straight after and a week later; ask learners to check its output, and record errors it makes
rows.if: A generative-AI chatbot or tutor is part of the plan

rows.basis: [Minimal guidance is less effective for novices](claims/minimal-guidance-less-effective-for-novices.md) [+S]; [Explicit instruction beats unassisted discovery](claims/minimal-guidance-less-effective-for-novices.md) [+M]
rows.change: Explain and model the method, then guide practice with checks and feedback; do not leave them to find the method unaided
rows.if: Learners are new to the target and cannot start a representative item

rows.basis: [Teacher-guided inquiry outperforms student-led](claims/teacher-guided-inquiry-outperforms-student-led.md) [+S]; [Enhanced discovery beats other instruction](claims/enhanced-discovery-beats-other-instruction.md) [~M]
rows.change: Keep it, but guide it: feedback, worked examples, prompts and teacher-led steps inside the inquiry. The evidence favours guided discovery as much as explicit teaching, and favours neither over the other
rows.if: The brief asks for inquiry or discovery learning

rows.basis: [Productive failure improves conceptual learning](claims/productive-failure-improves-conceptual-learning.md) [~S]
rows.change: Consider a short, designed problem attempt before the explanation, then teach the canonical method
rows.if: The goal is conceptual understanding or transfer, and the learners are secondary-school age or older

rows.basis: [Productive failure improves conceptual learning](claims/productive-failure-improves-conceptual-learning.md) [+S]
rows.change: Teach first; a problem-first phase showed no gain for procedures and reversed for second to fifth graders
rows.if: The goal is a procedure, or the learners are in the early primary grades

rows.basis: [Expertise reversal effect](claims/expertise-reversal-effect.md) [~S]; [Guidance advantage recedes with high prior knowledge](claims/guidance-advantage-recedes-with-high-prior-knowledge.md) [~M]
rows.change: Shorten or skip the explanation for them and move to varied independent practice; full guidance can become redundant
rows.if: Some learners already succeed unaided and can say why

rows.basis: [Age moderates discovery effects](claims/age-moderates-discovery-effects.md) [+M]
rows.change: Avoid unassisted discovery in particular; adolescents lost most from it in the meta-analysis's age moderator
rows.if: Learners are adolescents

rows.basis: [Age moderates discovery effects](claims/age-moderates-discovery-effects.md) [~M]
rows.change: Guided discovery with feedback is a defensible alternative to explicit teaching; adults gained most from enhanced discovery
rows.if: Learners are adults and the brief values exploration

rows.basis: [Instruction effect peaks then diminishes](claims/instruction-positive-effect-peaks-then-diminishes.md) [~M]; [Direct instruction's advantages do not persist](claims/direct-instruction-advantages-vanish-long-term.md) [~M]
rows.change: Add practice and review after the lesson and check at the delay; an end-of-instruction peak can fall back toward the starting level
rows.if: The outcome is judged weeks or months after teaching

rows.basis: [Explicit L2 grammar instruction is superior to implicit](claims/explicit-l2-grammar-instruction-superior-to-implicit.md) [+S]; [Rules are learned faster when used in communicative tasks](claims/explicit-rules-learned-faster-in-communicative-tasks.md) [+M]
rows.change: Teach the rule explicitly, then have learners use it in communicative tasks
rows.if: The target is second-language grammar

rows.basis: [Active learning improves exam performance](claims/active-learning-improves-exam-performance.md) [+M]
rows.change: Build learner activity (attempts, checks, discussion) into the explanation; explicit does not mean lecture alone
rows.if: Class time is mostly lecture

rows.basis: [Disciplinary Literacy Instruction Improves Comprehension](claims/disciplinary-literacy-instruction-improves-comprehension.md) [+M] (ninth- and eleventh-graders, against usual or textbook instruction)
rows.change: Use the default design as written, over a semester: one practice at a time, modelled, then text sets in pairs, then unaided arguments
rows.if: Learners are `adolescent`, reading adequately but new to the discipline's texts

rows.basis: [Automatic word recognition frees resources for comprehension](claims/automatic-word-recognition-frees-resources-for-comprehension.md) [~W] (a mechanism from theory and review, not tested as an intervention); text supports in [Accessible Vocabulary & Syntax](principles/accessible-vocabulary-syntax.md)
rows.change: Keep the discipline's texts but shorten them, gloss terms, read them aloud first; run fluency and vocabulary work alongside; reduce to one question at a time on the card
rows.if: Learners still decode slowly or have low literacy

rows.basis: untested; from the folded page's strategy ([two-question-set strategy](strategies/strategy-imagining-past-two-question-sets.md), no claim). The tested studies were with high-school students
rows.change: Use one or two questions per source; let learners draw a picture or make a collage captioned with a quotation from the source; keep the rule that each picture points to its source
rows.if: Learners are `child` (primary age)

rows.basis: [Instructional guidance that helps novices can become redundant or counterproductive as expertise grows.](claims/expertise-reversal-effect.md) [~M] (cognitive-load studies, not disciplinary reading)
rows.change: Skip most modelling; give harder or contested texts, ask for critique of a published argument, and check with one unaided text set before deciding
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` (upper-level undergraduates, graduate students) or already read as insiders

rows.basis: untested proposal; no claim here tests disciplinary literacy with adults
rows.change: Use texts from their own work; model the profession's reading questions; keep sessions short and tied to a decision they must make with the text
rows.if: `adult` learners in work settings (nurses reading research, engineers reading standards, analysts reading reports)

rows.basis: [Disciplinary Literacy Instruction Improves Comprehension](claims/disciplinary-literacy-instruction-improves-comprehension.md) [~M] (comprehension gains, no gain in essays; the authors attribute it to too little writing support)
rows.change: Add explicit steps from discussion to writing: a shared outline, a model paragraph in the genre, a draft with feedback on the use of evidence, then an unaided draft
rows.if: The goal is disciplinary **writing** (essays, lab reports, explanations)

rows.basis: [Students learning from World History Project ... continuity and change](claims/whp-students-continuity-change-outcomes.md) [+M] and [comparable competency in the other five skills](claims/whp-comparable-other-five-skills.md) [~M] (one evaluation of one curriculum); [conceptually decoupled](claims/historical-thinking-dimensions-conceptually-decoupled.md) [~M]
rows.change: Teach and score each practice separately, give each its own lessons, and expect gains only where instruction targeted it
rows.if: The goal is several historical thinking skills at once

rows.basis: untested as a move; the starting state is described in [students approach the past with common sense, including presentism](claims/novice-presentism-common-sense-historical-understanding.md) [~M] (a review, not a test)
rows.change: Add a contextualisation step: before judging, learners list what people at the time could know and believed, citing a source for each
rows.if: Learners judge the past by present-day values

rows.basis: [Civic Online Reasoning Instruction Improves Evaluation](claims/civic-online-reasoning-instruction-improves-evaluation.md) [+M] (high-school and university students, 2–8 lessons); historians' sourcing did not carry to websites ([checklist claim](claims/checklist-evaluation-ineffective-online.md) [~M])
rows.change: Teach lateral reading (leave the page, search what others say about the source) rather than document sourcing; use [Evaluating Sources](principles/evaluating-sources.md)
rows.if: The task is judging websites or online claims, not the discipline's own texts

rows.basis: [Teachers find World History Project overwhelming in their initial adoption year](claims/whp-first-year-overwhelm-and-modifications.md) [~M] (teacher interviews, one curriculum)
rows.change: Start from the curriculum's modelled lessons; select a few activities rather than all; plan the scaffolds teachers will add, and give planning time in the first year
rows.if: The teacher lacks deep disciplinary knowledge, or is adopting a new curriculum

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Model to the whole class; run text sets in pairs with one question card each; collect one written quotation-backed answer per pair per lesson and respond to the commonest gap the next day
rows.if: One teacher with a large class

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Give each learner a fixed question card and annotated model text; the facilitator checks only one thing per visit: does each interpretation cite a source?
rows.if: Scarce facilitator time (a volunteer tutor, short check-ins)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Send the text pack before the session, both printed (posted or handed out) and as a single phone-readable file (short excerpts in large plain text, not scanned PDFs or wide tables); number the lines so anyone can point to a quotation by line number; no task requires shared editing, a laptop or a live link: phone-only learners answer each question card item by text message, a voice note or on paper photographed afterwards; pair a remote learner with a room learner by phone call for the argument step
rows.if: Mixed modes (some remote, some in the room) or some learners phone-only

rows.basis: untested proposal; the tested curricula ran a semester or more
rows.change: Session 1 (about 60 min): model one practice on one short text (15 min), neutral expert-beside-novice readings (10 min), guided practice in pairs on a two-text set with the question card (25 min), one quoted answer each (10 min). Between sessions: nothing required, or one optional question on a printed text. Session 2 (about 60 min): two-minute recap of the card, unaided practice on a new text set (25 min), a short argument from the texts (20 min), scored on the brief's rubric strands (10 min). Teach one practice, not three; claim only what session 2's unaided task shows
rows.if: Two sessions only

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Shorter texts (half a page), one practice per session, talk before writing, the question card printed so nothing must be remembered; put the unaided task early in session 2, not at the end
rows.if: Learners are tired (evening classes after work, apprentices after a shift)

rows.basis: untested proposal; the tested curricula ran a semester or more
rows.change: Model one practice on one short text (15 min), set an expert and a novice reading side by side (10 min), guided practice on one new text (20 min), one unaided question with a quotation (5 min); do not claim a lasting gain
rows.if: Single session only

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Run one question from the card on one short source each lesson, with a one-line quoted answer; rotate practices every two weeks
rows.if: Fixed short time budget (e.g. 10 minutes a lesson inside a content course)

rows.basis: untested; follows the tested package, not the brief's tool
rows.change: Keep it, and use the rubric's strands as the assessment, scored strand by strand; say which disciplinary practice serves which strand; change only what the evidence says matters: one practice targeted at a time, the discipline's own texts, every interpretation tied to a source
rows.if: The brief names its own routine or rubric (a school's document-analysis sheet, a lab-report template, a rubric with named strands, its own categories)

rows.basis: [Disciplinary variation emerged in communication assessment](claims/disciplinary-variation-communication-assessment.md) [~W] (authors' interpretation of focus groups; STEM teachers stressing precision, humanities teachers audience)
rows.change: Use the brief's own criteria, but let each discipline weight them in its own way, and score disciplines separately
rows.if: Assessment criteria differ by subject (a cross-school rubric for communication or writing)

rows.basis: untested; see [Authentic Audiences & Purposes](principles/authentic-audiences-purposes.md)
rows.change: Keep the audience; require that every claim in the product is traceable to a cited source in a notes page the audience can see or a reviewer can check
rows.if: Products or performances for a real audience (a museum label, a public history podcast, a science briefing)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Keep it whole; give the practices as checkpoints inside it (sourcing before interpreting, corroboration before claiming), not as separate worksheets
rows.if: A whole-task performance the brief wants kept whole (a full document-based inquiry, an investigation report)

rows.basis: [AI literacy requires discipline-specific calibration beyond prompt-writing skills](claims/ai-literacy-discipline-specific-calibration.md) [+W] (a review's endorsement of a framework; no data)
rows.change: Teach the discipline's standard for checking a summary against its sources: compare each AI claim with the text, name what it left out
rows.if: Learners use AI tools to read or summarise texts

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Learners decide what is shared beyond the teacher; work from published or consented sources for class discussion; anonymise any personal source used
rows.if: Private or sensitive material (family histories, community testimony, patients' records in a health course)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Practise in the exam's form late in the arc, but keep the practices taught in the discipline's texts earlier; judge readiness on unaided responses to unseen texts
rows.if: High stakes (a document-based exam, a qualification)

rows.basis: [BIPOC students perceived statistics as a neutral subject and did not discern explicit racial or cultural inclusion in the courseware, generally viewing that neutrality as appropriate](claims/students-perceive-statistics-as-neutral-subject.md) [~W] (undergraduate statistics interviews; a limit on, not a test of, the move)
rows.change: Start from a shared data set or case in the subject itself where outcomes differ by race, and ask what explains the difference; do not open with identity or experience. Name race plainly when the data show it, even if learners call it culture or background; some learners will judge the connection inappropriate, so record that as an observation and keep naming it in the analysis
rows.if: Learners are `novice` on the topic, or describe their subject as neutral and see race as irrelevant to it

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Shorten the norm-setting to a check of existing norms; move to learner-chosen cases and learner-led segments from the second session; ask for analysis of a practice they control
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` (graduate students, experienced practitioners, people with long lived experience of the topic)

rows.basis: untested proposal; see [Talking to young children about race and racism](strategies/talking_to_young_children_about_race_and_racism.md)
rows.change: Use picture books and short stories as the shared object; keep sessions to 15–20 minutes; the adult names race plainly and answers questions honestly; drawing or play as the private response; tell families what will be discussed
rows.if: Learners are `child` (primary age)

rows.basis: [Building Empathy Improves Intergroup Attitudes](claims/building-empathy-improves-intergroup-attitudes.md) [~M] (9 distinct studies in its table; a month-long program raised positive affect in grades 4–6 in Israel but not contact behavior; a review of 418 experiments flags publication bias and light-touch designs)
rows.change: Use a sustained program (several weeks) of concrete accounts from members of the group plus discussion of variation within the group and similarity across groups; measure attitudes weeks later, and do not expect behavior to follow
rows.if: Goal is attitudes toward a group (`attitude-motivation`), not analysis

rows.basis: [Racial, ethnic, and cultural identity development emerged as the core need for students of color beyond academic subjects](claims/identity-core-of-sead-for-students-of-color.md) [+W] (focus groups with families and students of color naming the need; does not test affinity groups)
rows.change: Add affinity-group time before mixed discussion (one session in three, 20–30 minutes) and material on learners' own histories and cultures; let learners choose whether to join
rows.if: Goal includes learners of color developing their own racial or cultural identity

rows.basis: untested proposal, from the earlier page ("forced participation")
rows.change: Use cases, not experience, as the object; give no prompt that makes their membership visible; check in privately after the session; offer a written route for anything they want the facilitator to know
rows.if: One learner is the only member of the group under discussion

rows.basis: Trust: [Continuous improvement for equity requires trust and courageous conversations; without trusting relationships, the improvement process will not help](claims/ci-equity-requires-trust-and-courageous-conversations.md) [+W] (one qualitative report of education leaders). Case choice: carried from [Some SSWs hold deficit-based racial attitudes, conflating structural constraints with immigrant cultural values and misreading trauma responses](claims/ssws-deficit-racial-attitudes.md) [~W] (school social workers' open responses; shows what practitioners' cases can surface, does not test a training)
rows.change: Use cases from the learners' own practice (a referral decision, a discipline record, an assessment); include practice at raising race with a client, student or patient through role-play with a debrief; build trust in the team before asking about the team's own data
rows.if: `adult-workplace` or professional training (teachers, social workers, counsellors, clinicians, managers)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Run the private written entry in a shared document or chat everyone can reach; pair remote learners with each other, not one remote learner with an in-room pair; have a second person monitor the chat during whole-group talk; give remote learners a private channel to the facilitator
rows.if: Some learners join remotely while others are in the room, or some are on a phone only

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Do not run open discussion of race unmoderated; use asynchronous written responses to a shared object with norms stated at the start, a moderator who reads posts within a set window (e.g. 24 hours), and a private reflection to close
rows.if: `online-self-paced`, no facilitator present

rows.basis: untested proposal; responsive facilitation evidence is mostly one-to-one ([Contingent scaffolding improves learning more than fixed or absent support.](claims/contingent-scaffolding-improves-learning.md) [~M], carried from tutoring)
rows.change: Keep open talk in small groups with a one-page discussion guide and named roles (reader, recorder, norm-keeper); the facilitator circulates and takes only the whole-group close; collect private written debriefs and read them before the next session
rows.if: One facilitator for a large group (40 or more), or facilitator time is scarce (volunteers, a short shift, a tutor checking in briefly)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Use one shared object, private written entry, pairs, a short whole-group discussion and a private debrief; do not ask for personal disclosure; name what will not be resolved today and where learners can go next
rows.if: A single session only

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: 5 minutes norms, 5 minutes reading or viewing the object, 6 minutes private writing, 10 minutes pairs, 12 minutes whole group, 7 minutes debrief (5 private, 2 close); drop the whole-group segment before the debrief
rows.if: A fixed short time budget (e.g. 45 minutes)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Read the shared object aloud or use a short video; allow drawn, spoken-to-a-partner or recorded private responses; let pairs report rather than individuals
rows.if: Learners have low confidence in speaking, or low literacy

rows.basis: untested proposal, from the earlier page ("optionality and boundaries")
rows.change: The learner decides who sees it: private reflection stays with the learner unless they choose to share it; confidentiality applies to what peers say; tell learners in advance anything the facilitator is required to report
rows.if: The material is private or sensitive (learners' own experience of racism, family history)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Keep the named routine and its categories; add only what it lacks among private written entry, optional disclosure and a closing debrief
rows.if: The brief names its own routine (its own discussion protocol, community agreements, circle process or rubric)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Keep the performance whole; place norm-setting and a private written entry before it and the debrief after it; agree with learners what of their own experience, if any, will be in a public product, and keep it out unless they choose otherwise
rows.if: The brief wants a whole-task performance kept whole (a mock community meeting, a case conference, a policy hearing) or a product for a real audience

rows.basis: [Payne argues that color-blind ideology in schools precludes discussion of how outcomes and privilege are distributed by race](claims/colorblindness-blocks-distribution-discussion.md) [+W] and [Payne suspects that a school's inability to talk openly about race predicts its capacity for change](claims/racial-reticence-predicts-school-change-capacity.md) [+W] (one theoretical argument on Chicago schools; the correcting move is untested)
rows.change: The facilitator restates the point naming race and asks the group to say it too; keep "culture" for cultural matters; count how often naming had to be prompted, early against late sessions
rows.if: Talk slides to euphemism ("cultural differences", "diversity", "background", "urban") where the object is about race

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Discomfort (uncertainty, unease, defensiveness, emotion while still engaging the evidence): name it as expected, keep going, offer private writing. Harm (stereotype stated as fact, a remark aimed at a person, dismissing someone's account, pressing someone to represent a group): stop the exchange, name the remark and the norm, return to the object, check in privately with the person targeted. Share this distinction with learners in the norm-setting
rows.if: Learners say they feel uncomfortable, or the brief asks the facilitator to distinguish discomfort from harm

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Build the session around those criteria as given: show them at the start, make each segment the place one criterion is practised (the private entry for evidence, the euphemism move for naming race, the debrief for discomfort and harm), use the same words in prompts and feedback, and assess against them, not against criteria of your own
rows.if: The brief gives its own assessment criteria or rubric (for example: names race specifically, uses evidence, distinguishes discomfort from harm, listens and responds)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Grade the analysis of the shared object against stated criteria, never a learner's disclosure, opinion or identity; say this in advance
rows.if: Stakes are high (a graded assessment, a professional licence, a public event)

rows.basis: [Race prompts elicit culturally stereotyped feedback: Black, Hispanic, and Asian students are positioned through cultural or linguistic stereotypes while White students receive argument-structure feedback](claims/race-prompts-cultural-stereotype-feedback.md) [~W] (LLM feedback on the same essays under different race prompts; carried to this setting)
rows.change: Do not put a learner's race in the tool's prompt or profile; review a sample of its feedback for stereotyped framing before learners see it
rows.if: The design uses an AI tool to give feedback on learners' writing about race or identity

rows.basis: [Payne argues that color-blind ideology in schools precludes discussion of how outcomes and privilege are distributed by race](claims/colorblindness-blocks-distribution-discussion.md) [+W] and [Payne suspects that a school's inability to talk openly about race predicts its capacity for change](claims/racial-reticence-predicts-school-change-capacity.md) [+W] (both one theoretical argument from Chicago schools)
rows.change: Start with outcome data disaggregated by race as the shared object, with a facilitator from outside the team if trust is low; treat the difficulty itself as information about the group
rows.if: The institution or community avoids naming race, or a staff group cannot discuss it

rows.basis: [Chunking reduces working memory load by grouping information into fewer, more meaningful units.](claims/chunking-reduces-working-memory-load.md) [~S] (its Discussion: imposed chunking helps only until the learner can chunk unaided; carried from memory research)
rows.change: Give them a blank template rather than a laid-out representation, fewer assigned roles, and judge them on the unaided check from the first session
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` on this task, or already succeed alone

rows.basis: [Review reports a developmental shift in cognitive offloading: children under-use external aids while adolescents over-rely on them](claims/developmental-shift-cognitive-offloading.md) [~W] (one word-pair memory study, reported second-hand)
rows.change: Prompt them to use the external aid (write it down, look at the board) and show when it would have helped; the prediction-and-feedback check is about under-use, not over-use
rows.if: Learners are `child` (primary age)

rows.basis: Developmental claim above [~W]; [Bounded AI support outperformed open collaboration on all four Week 8 independent no-AI outcomes, though exact wild-cluster p values sat at the 0.050–0.063 boundary](claims/bounded-beats-open-week8-independent-outcomes.md) [+M] (one quasi-experiment, six classes); the tool decision is modelled in [Technology Augments, Not Supplants](principles/technology-augments-not-supplants-processes.md)
rows.change: Bound the tool to hints and checks, run the prediction-and-feedback check of step 6 on every practice set, and keep the unaided check
rows.if: Learners are `adolescent`, or have an AI assistant in reach

rows.basis: Untested proposal; [Salomon distinguishes effects with the computer (system performance) from effects of the computer (cognitive residue on the solo performer)](claims/effects-with-versus-effects-of-computer.md) [+M] names the choice, it does not test it
rows.change: Treat the job aid as part of the performance: train with the real aid, judge the team's performance with it present, and check unaided only the steps the job requires from memory (an emergency, a step done away from the aid)
rows.if: Adults in work settings, where the checklist, system or colleague will be there on the job

rows.basis: Untested proposal; writing into a shared artifact is argued, not shown, to deepen the writer's own knowledge ([Externalizing knowledge into a wiki can itself produce individual learning through deeper processing](claims/externalization-produces-individual-learning.md) [+W], theoretical); [Among AI-exposed students, open collaboration predicted higher aggregate offloading, which was associated with lower Week 8 higher-order thinking (indirect estimate −0.34)](claims/offloading-mediation-lower-independent-hot.md) [~M] (exploratory, one study, AI tool rather than peers)
rows.change: Keep the reasoning steps with each learner; the shared representation records the group's results, not the reasoning; every learner writes some entries in their own words and takes a turn explaining the representation unaided
rows.if: Goal is the learner's unaided understanding (`concept`, `principle`) for an individual exam

rows.basis: [In Experiment 1, a five-trial metacognitive prediction-plus-feedback intervention significantly reduced reminder bias, producing more optimal reminder-setting behaviour](claims/metacognitive-feedback-reduces-reminder-bias.md) [+M]; [An effort-based reward did not significantly reduce answer offloading or improve unaided performance](claims/effort-based-reward-no-effect-offloading-or-unaided-performance.md) [~M]; [Participants still offload more than optimal under loss framing](claims/reminder-bias-persists-under-loss-framing.md) [~M] (all online adult samples)
rows.change: Ask for a prediction before each aided item and show the unaided result after; do not substitute a reward for effort or a warning worded as a loss
rows.if: Learners keep reaching for the aid or the answer before trying

rows.basis: [In Experiment 1, lower confidence predicted greater offloading beyond objective performance in the no-feedback group, but not in the feedback group](claims/confidence-predicts-offloading-no-feedback-only.md) [+M] (online adults, memory task); the visual layout is an untested proposal
rows.change: Expect over-reliance driven by low confidence: show them their own unaided accuracy early so the decision rests on evidence; make the shared representation visual (icons, a fixed grid) with few words
rows.if: Learners have low confidence, or low literacy

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Keep one shared representation online that both sites edit, with one person in the room assigned to keep it current aloud for remote members; on phones, keep it to one screen of short entries and move detail into linked items
rows.if: Some learners remote, some in the room; or phone-only

rows.basis: Mostly untested; in one qualitative comparison of nursing problem-based-learning groups, the interactive-whiteboard group needed less late-stage teacher scaffolding than the traditional-whiteboard group ([The IW-supported group needed less teacher scaffolding in the late problem-solving stage, where nurse and instructor discourse decreased, while scaffolding increased from early to late stage in the TW condition](claims/iw-group-less-late-stage-scaffolding.md) [+W]); contingent support is better supported one-to-one than at class scale ([Contingent scaffolding improves learning more than fixed or absent support.](claims/contingent-scaffolding-improves-learning.md) [~M])
rows.change: Read each group's shared representation and role line instead of listening in; spend the check-in only on groups whose progress line has not moved or whose unaided check failed; when a group's work is visible on a shared board, use the freed time to raise the challenge rather than supply information
rows.if: One teacher for many groups, or scarce facilitator time (volunteers, a short check-in)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Use a laid-out representation and assigned roles throughout; spend the last 10 minutes on one unaided item per learner; report the session's result as performance with aids and one unaided check, not as learning that lasts
rows.if: A single session only

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: 2 minutes roles, 12 minutes joint work, 6 minutes unaided check; drop the prediction step if the brief has no aid decision to train
rows.if: A fixed short time budget (for example 20 minutes)

rows.basis: Untested proposal (wave lesson: a brief's own routine is kept)
rows.change: Keep it as the shared representation and the criteria; change only the layout so roles and progress are visible, and add the unaided check beside it only if an unaided outcome is wanted
rows.if: The brief names its own checklist, template, representation or rubric

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Lay out the shared representation in those categories, not in this page's goal–roles–state headings
rows.if: The brief uses its own categories for the work

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Keep the shared representation to what the group needs to coordinate; each learner keeps personal material in their own space and decides what enters the shared one
rows.if: Material is private or sensitive (personal reflections, client records)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Distribute by role inside the whole task rather than splitting it into separate pieces; debrief afterwards with the shared record; the unaided check is a short individual run-through of one role
rows.if: A whole-task performance the brief wants kept whole (a simulation, a ward round, a performance for a real audience)

rows.basis: Untested as a design; a review reports that people offload the higher-value intentions more readily, leaving memory with the low-value ones if the aid fails ([Higher-value intentions are more likely to be offloaded than lower-value ones](claims/value-drives-offloading-selection.md) [~W], one study reported second-hand, adults, a memory task)
rows.change: Keep the checklist in use as part of the system; add a check that each learner can say why each item is on it and what to do if the aid is unavailable, starting with the highest-stakes items
rows.if: An error on the job is costly (safety, compliance)

rows.basis: [In the learning phase, group experience and information distribution each produce significant multivariate effects on performance, mental effort, and efficiency, without interacting](claims/zambrano-2019-learning-phase-manova-main-effects.md) [+M] (one experiment, 240 secondary students in groups of three, break-even problems); whether one practice task builds the same experience is untested
rows.change: Keep the same groups for the whole unit and rotate roles inside them; if groups must be new, give them one short collaboration on a similar task before the main one
rows.if: Groups are newly formed, or the brief regroups learners every session

rows.basis: [Groups using the Graphical Debate-tool constructed representations of significantly higher quality than groups using the Textual Debate-tool, for both debate positions.](claims/gd-tool-higher-quality-representations.md) [+M]; [The number of items groups placed in their representations was negatively correlated with the average quality of those items.](claims/item-quantity-quality-tradeoff-representations.md) [~W] (one study, 39 groups of eleventh-graders; group products only; the essay advantage disappeared on longer topics, so splitting is an untested response to that)
rows.change: Give the group a graphical argument map (positions, grounds and counter-arguments as linked boxes) rather than a shared text; ask for few, well-grounded entries; split a long topic into short sections, each mapped separately
rows.if: The task is an argument, debate or case judgement

rows.basis: [Graphic organizers for novices](claims/graphic-organizers-support-novice-comprehension.md) [~M] (lower-ability learners benefited from maps, higher-ability did not, in small, low-powered subsets)
rows.change: Supply a complete, labelled visual first, with linking prompts; then ask for a drawing of named parts and relations, keeping a partly completed diagram for a learner who cannot start
rows.if: Learners are `novice` on this content

rows.basis: [Graphic organizers for novices](claims/graphic-organizers-support-novice-comprehension.md) [~M] (the higher-ability subset showed no benefit; the authors say this cannot show maps fail them); the redraw is untested
rows.change: Drop most supplied visuals; ask for a redraw from memory or a learner-made summary diagram, checked against a model
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` on this content

rows.basis: Supplied: [text with graphics](claims/dual-coding-improves-learning.md) [+M] (effect held across grade levels). Drawing: [drawing in STEM](claims/drawing-improves-learning.md) [~M] (benefit larger in middle and high school than in primary)
rows.change: Supply pictures and flow diagrams with the text; have children label or complete them rather than draw freely
rows.if: Learners are `child` (primary age)

rows.basis: [Drawing in STEM](claims/drawing-improves-learning.md) [+M] (STEM only, abstract read)
rows.change: Add learner drawing of the process or system, with a model to compare against
rows.if: Learners are `adolescent` or `adult`, goal is a `principle` in science or mathematics

rows.basis: L2: [text-plus-picture glosses](claims/multimodal-glosses-improve-incidental-vocabulary-learning.md) [+W] (one study of 90 Iranian EFL learners, immediate recall, reported second-hand). Disabilities: [mnemonic instruction](claims/mnemonic-instruction-improves-recall-for-students-with-disabilities.md) [+M] (mnemonics broadly, not only pictorial ones)
rows.change: Pair each new word with a picture and a short text gloss; for students with learning disabilities, teach a keyword-image mnemonic
rows.if: Goal is `verbal-association` (vocabulary, names, facts), including second-language vocabulary

rows.basis: [Concept mapping](claims/concept-mapping-improves-learning.md) [+M] (STEM and non-STEM; constructing showed more benefit than studying, against different comparisons)
rows.change: Have learners build and revise a concept map across sessions, with labelled links, starting from given nodes
rows.if: Goal is a `concept` or hierarchy to be understood across a unit

rows.basis: [Drawing in STEM](claims/drawing-improves-learning.md) [+M] (online drawing benefited more from instructor-provided scaffolds than paper-based drawing); against: in one tablet experiment the two supports tested did not beat unsupported drawing, and [local support lowered recognition](claims/drawing-no-recognition-benefit-local-worse.md) [-M] and [raised rated difficulty](claims/drawing-support-increased-perceived-difficulty.md) [-M]
rows.change: Build a model drawing to compare with and a self-check list into the material; offer a drawing template as optional, and if the platform adds drawing aids (highlighting where to draw, prompts per part), compare them with plain drawing before keeping them
rows.if: `online-self-paced`, no teacher present

rows.basis: [The same graph helped on one problem and hurt on another](claims/graph-helpful-harmful-contrasting-cases.md) [~M] (36 engineering-physics students; correctness .25 to .70 on one problem, .38 to .10 on another; with the graph, less use of prior knowledge and more "this must be correct"); [no overall effect of graphs on correctness](claims/no-overall-multimedia-effect-vector-calculus.md) [-M] (56% against 52%)
rows.change: Before they answer, ask what the graph shows and how it bears on the question; ask them to check an answer against the problem statement, not only against the graph; review which problems the graph actually informs
rows.if: Learners solve problems with a graph or diagram supplied (physics, mathematics, engineering)

rows.basis: [With an image, undergraduates rated their ability to draw the process higher](claims/image-condition-inflated-draw-judgment-magnitude.md) [~M] (d = 0.32) though [test scores did not differ](claims/instructional-visuals-no-effect-test-performance-or-test-explain-accuracy.md) [-M]; [image-group learners judged by recalling the picture, text-only learners by generating their own image](claims/internal-vs-external-visual-cue-use-draw-judgments.md) [~M] (self-reports of 18 and 23 learners, biology and chemistry)
rows.change: Replace "rate how well you understand" with a redraw or explain-from-memory check after an illustrated text
rows.if: Learners decide for themselves when they understand (self-study, revision, an adaptive course using self-ratings)

rows.basis: [Concept mapping against retrieval](claims/concept-mapping-improves-learning.md) [~M] (undergraduates, science text, time matched, one-week test)
rows.change: Keep the supplied visual; replace building a map while viewing with redrawing or explaining it from memory
rows.if: Little time, or the goal is recall a week later

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Collect a sample of learner drawings each session, show one correct and one common error to the class, then have everyone compare their own with the model
rows.if: Large class, one teacher

rows.basis: [Verbal tests may underestimate knowledge](claims/verbal-achievement-tests-may-underestimate-via-symbolic-mismatch.md) [~W] (an argument in a review, not a tested result); [text with graphics](claims/dual-coding-improves-learning.md) [+M] (larger effect on open-ended items)
rows.change: Include items that ask for a diagram or a prediction from one; decide whether the visual may be consulted
rows.if: Assessment is high-stakes or verbal only

rows.basis: [Learning-styles matching](claims/learning-styles-matching-does-not-improve-learning.md) [-S] (systematic review; 5th graders showed no style × modality interaction)
rows.change: Give the visual to every learner where the content has a visual structure; do not sort learners or build matched versions
rows.if: The brief describes "visual learners" or asks for materials matched to learning styles

rows.basis: [Decorative illustrations](claims/seductive-details-effect.md) [-M] (no learning gain; a small comprehension cost for undergraduates, η² = .04)
rows.change: Keep only images that show what the words describe; if an image must stay for branding, keep it away from the explanatory visual
rows.if: The designer wants images for appeal or engagement

rows.basis: [Difficulty adjusting to kindergarten and first grade can put young children at academic risk](claims/kindergarten-transition-difficulty-academic-risk.md) [+W] (a fact sheet's assertion, no data); family meetings: [transition programme interviews](claims/transition-program-benefits-families-without-preschool-experience.md) [+W]; play and movement: untested, from the earlier page
rows.change: Observe in play and short one-to-one tasks rather than a written test; plan play and movement into the day as teacher-side readiness; meet families before the start
rows.if: Children are entering kindergarten or first grade (`child`, early years)

rows.basis: [Redshirting kindergartners likely carries costs that outweigh its academic benefits](claims/redshirting-costs-outweigh-academic-benefits.md) [+W]; [At the end of first grade, children whose kindergarten entry was delayed were behind their classmates who began kindergarten on time in math](claims/delayed-entrants-behind-in-math-first-grade.md) [+M], though [they were slightly ahead in reading](claims/delayed-entrants-slightly-higher-reading-first-grade.md) [~M]; US data, associational except one regression discontinuity
rows.change: Recommend on-time entry with the entry check and bridging above; record the specific concern and plan an adjustment for it
rows.if: A family or school is considering holding a child back a year, or having a child repeat kindergarten

rows.basis: Untested; the expertise argument for letting learners skip is [Instructional guidance that helps novices can become redundant or counterproductive as expertise grows.](claims/expertise-reversal-effect.md) [~M] (carried from cognitive-load studies, not entry decisions)
rows.change: Five to eight unaided prerequisite items in the first session, no grade; a bridging resource per missed item, worked within the first two weeks; let those who pass skip it
rows.if: Learners are older students or adults entering a course with prerequisites (`adult`, adults in work settings)

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page's caution that criteria built on typically developing children misclassify; see [Universal Design for Learning](principles/universal-design-for-learning.md)
rows.change: Write the check so it measures the capability, not the route (allow pointing, speaking, assistive tools); plan the accommodation before the start; do not read a gap in the route as a lack of readiness
rows.if: Learners have disabilities or atypical development, or a sensory or physical need

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Check prerequisites in the learner's stronger language or by doing, not only in writing; keep the check private and ungraded; tell learners what it is for
rows.if: Learners are in a second language, or have low literacy or low confidence

rows.basis: [Good attendance is more strongly related to academic gains for students who enter preschool with lower incoming skills…](claims/attendance-benefits-strongest-low-incoming-skills.md) [+M] (Chicago preschool, associational); [families without preschool experience](claims/transition-program-benefits-families-without-preschool-experience.md) [+W]
rows.change: Give families concrete home activities before entry; prioritise attendance follow-up for learners who started with gaps
rows.if: Many learners come from families with fewer resources, or without preschool

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Use a group-administered check of five items with one observed task per learner over the first week; one bridging group, not one per learner; recheck at six weeks only
rows.if: One teacher with a large intake, or scarce facilitator time (volunteers, a short check-in)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Give the same short check as a phone-friendly form with the same items; hold the bridging segment as a short live or recorded session all can join; observe remote learners on one task by video or a submitted photo
rows.if: Mixed modes: some learners join remotely or on a phone, others in the room
