rows.change: Use the same three parts; time the first framed critique for the transition point (first assignment of the course or programme)
rows.if: The difference is a stereotype in the domain rather than between teacher and learner (women in engineering, first-generation students, adults returning to study)

rows.basis: untested proposal (wave 6 lesson)
rows.change: Use them as "the standard" in the framing sentence and the critique; do not substitute this page's or another rubric
rows.if: The brief names its own rubric, criteria or categories

rows.basis: untested proposal (wave 5 lesson)
rows.change: Keep it; add only the standard-and-assurance sentence and a revision date, and check the "grow" part names a next step
rows.if: The brief names its own feedback routine (glow-and-grow, a comment template, a conference script)

rows.basis: untested proposal; a template with no personal clause is expected to read as generic
rows.change: Write one framing sentence once and reuse it, but add one clause that names something in this learner's work; cap the critique at two points; a fixed time budget of about 2–3 minutes per piece: 30 seconds for the framing, 1–2 minutes for two critiques with next steps, 30 seconds for the revision date
rows.if: One teacher for many learners, or scarce facilitator time (volunteers, a busy shift, a tutor checking in briefly)

rows.basis: untested; carried from the belonging message's "common and passing" framing ([Belonging Interventions Improve Outcomes](claims/belonging-interventions-improve-outcomes.md) [~M])
rows.change: A system cannot credibly state personal belief; state the standard, the specific gap and the next step, and say that learners at this point commonly reach the standard on revision (only if your data show it); route learners who stall to a person
rows.if: `online-self-paced`, automated feedback, no instructor present

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Give critical feedback privately, in writing or one-to-one, never in front of the group or the camera; on a phone, put the standard and assurance in the first line and one next step in the second, with the full comments attached
rows.if: Mixed modes (some remote, some in the room) or phone-only learners

rows.basis: [A brief values-affirmation writing exercise raised African American seventh-graders' grades in two small field experiments, but a large same-district replication found no effect](claims/self-affirmation-improves-outcomes.md) [~M] and [Growth-mindset interventions have weak average effects on achievement, including a negligible GPA gain (d = 0.11) for lower-achieving US ninth-graders in one preregistered national trial](claims/growth-mindset-improves-achievement.md) [~M]: one-off identity-targeted messages are fragile
rows.change: Consistency cannot build; make the assurance concrete by pointing to evidence in the work, and give one revision in the session; claim no lasting effect
rows.if: A single session only (one workshop, one assessed piece, a one-off review)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Give the framed critique on a draft before the summative submission; keep the grade and its justification separate from the developmental comments
rows.if: High stakes (a summative grade, certification, a placement decision)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Speak the three parts, or write them in plain language; one critique at a time; ask the learner to say back the next step before they start
rows.if: Learners with low confidence, low literacy, or working in a second language

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: The learner controls who sees the work and the feedback; comment only to the learner; ask before mentioning it to parents or colleagues
rows.if: Private or sensitive work (personal writing, identity, a disclosure)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Hold the critique to the audience's standard, on the whole product, before release; the assurance is that the learner can get it ready for that audience
rows.if: A product or performance for a real audience, which the brief wants kept whole

rows.basis: untested; the earlier page. [Parent involvement is associated with higher academic achievement in meta-analyses of mostly correlational studies](claims/parent-involvement-improves-achievement.md) [+W], carried: parents' high expectations and communication about school go with achievement (correlational)
rows.change: Specific positive, the concern with evidence, the standard and your belief in the student, one thing to support at home; offer an interpreter where needed
rows.if: A conversation with parents or guardians

rows.basis: [A brief online empathic-discipline exercise for teachers halved suspensions in one randomized field experiment, while its preregistered replication found a small, marginal overall effect but narrowed group disparities](claims/brief-intervention-empathic-discipline-cuts-suspensions.md) [~M] (a teacher-side exercise narrowed a racial disparity in suspensions; small overall effect in the preregistered replication) and [Belonging Interventions Improve Outcomes](claims/belonging-interventions-improve-outcomes.md) [~M] (effect only where the context afforded belonging)
rows.change: Raise it as a design constraint: the framing alone will not hold; pair it with changes on the teacher side
rows.if: The institution's grading, discipline or placement practice contradicts the message

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Design it as practice for the feedback-giver: model one annotated example, have them rewrite a real critique in the three-part form (criterion, high standard, assurance plus a specific next step) against the brief's own rubric, rehearse it in role-play with a peer playing the learner, and review recordings or notes against a short checklist before the real assessment
rows.if: The learner is the person who gives the feedback (a tutor, mentor or assessor being trained)

rows.basis: [Worked examples improve mathematics performance](claims/worked-examples-improve-math-performance.md) [+M]; [Worked examples reduce novice search](claims/worked-examples-reduce-novice-search.md) [+M]
rows.change: Replace some early practice problems with fully worked examples to study, before asking for unaided solutions; expect the gain on problems with the same structure as the examples, since in the original algebra experiments it did not reach differently structured problems
rows.if: Learners are new to this task type, and it is a structured problem (algebra, circuits, probability)

rows.basis: [Worked examples beat unassisted discovery by the widest margin](claims/worked-examples-largest-advantage-over-unassisted-discovery.md) [+M]
rows.change: Give worked examples rather than leaving novices to discover the method; in the meta-analysis they were the strongest comparison against unassisted discovery
rows.if: The lesson was planned as unaided discovery

rows.basis: [Example-first beat problem-first on an immediate test](claims/worked-example-problem-sequences.md) [+M]; [Order advantage not detected at the final test](claims/identical-example-problem-order-advantage-not-detected-at-final-test.md) [~M]; [Example–problem pairs more efficient for gifted and nongifted pupils](claims/example-problem-pairs-more-efficient-both-gifted-nongifted.md) [+M]
rows.change: Put each example before its paired problem, not after; judge the order on an immediate test, since with identical pairs the early advantage was not detected at the final test. With primary pupils, gifted and nongifted alike, example-first reached the same test score for less reported effort: an efficiency gain, not a higher score
rows.if: Examples and practice problems alternate

rows.basis: [Worked examples become less effective as expertise grows](claims/worked-examples-less-effective-with-expertise.md) [~M]; [With experience, examples became redundant](claims/expertise-reversal-worked-examples-review.md) [~M]
rows.change: Replace full examples with completion problems or independent practice; check first with an unsupported changed problem
rows.if: Learners already solve these problems reliably

rows.basis: [Lower-prior-knowledge learners did better with full than completion examples](claims/lower-prior-knowledge-learners-score-higher-with-full-than-completion-worked-examples.md) [+M]; [Prior knowledge, example type and task difficulty interact on the posttest](claims/prior-knowledge-worked-example-task-difficulty-three-way-interaction-on-algebra-posttest.md) [~M]
rows.change: Give full worked examples to the learners with less prior knowledge; completion examples can go to those with more, but the higher-prior-knowledge advantage for completion examples was not significant, and the pattern depended on task difficulty, so check with a pretest and an unsupported problem rather than assuming the switch
rows.if: Prior knowledge varies widely in the class

rows.basis: [Low-prior-knowledge students learned most conceptual understanding from worked-out examples](claims/low-prior-knowledge-worked-examples-best-conceptual-understanding.md) [+M]
rows.change: Open with worked-out examples; move to open questions and argument once learners have the prior knowledge to use them, since for low-prior-knowledge students questions plus arguments was the weakest condition
rows.if: The goal is conceptual understanding in a new university subject (statistics), and learners start with little prior knowledge

rows.basis: [Worked-example preparation beat inventing on transfer](claims/worked-example-preparation-higher-transfer-than-inventing.md) [+M]; [Applying canonical criteria mediated the transfer advantage](claims/canonical-criteria-application-mediates-transfer-advantage.md) [+M]
rows.change: Prepare with a worked example of the judgement rather than an open inventing problem; during the later lesson, look for learners applying the canonical criteria, which was the process that carried the transfer gain
rows.if: Learners prepare for later instruction in an ill-structured task (pre-service teachers judging the quality of learning strategies)

rows.basis: [Productive failure improves conceptual learning](claims/productive-failure-improves-conceptual-learning.md) [~M]
rows.change: Example-first is not the only defensible order here: a designed problem-solving attempt followed by instruction did better on conceptual knowledge and transfer in a meta-analysis (not for procedural knowledge, and not for grades 2–5). Use worked examples first for procedural goals and young pupils
rows.if: The goal is conceptual understanding of a new mathematics concept, and there is time for a designed problem-solving phase before instruction

rows.basis: [Correct exemplars improved explanations more than error-displaying examples](claims/correct-exemplars-improve-pst-fraction-explanations.md) [+M]
rows.change: Give a correct and complete exemplar to compare against their own explanation, rather than examples built from common errors
rows.if: Adult learners revise their own explanations (pre-service teachers explaining fraction comparisons)

rows.basis: [Fading worked steps eases the move to problem solving](claims/fading-worked-steps-facilitates-example-to-problem-transition.md) [+M]; [Backward fading and principle prompts supported transfer](claims/fading-and-principle-prompts-improve-probability-transfer.md) [+M]
rows.change: Fade the worked steps one at a time across examples, rather than jumping from a full example to a bare problem
rows.if: Several sessions should move learners to solving alone

rows.basis: [Backward fading and principle prompts supported transfer](claims/fading-and-principle-prompts-improve-probability-transfer.md) [+M]; [Subgoal labels enhance transfer](claims/subgoal-labels-worked-examples-transfer.md) [+W]
rows.change: Ask learners to name the principle behind each step, and label the subgoals in the example
rows.if: The goal is transfer to problems that look different

rows.basis: [Split-attention examples lose their advantage](claims/split-attention-effect-in-worked-examples.md) [~M]
rows.change: Put the explanation on the diagram, next to the part it refers to; split-source examples lost their advantage over practice
rows.if: The example uses a diagram with its explanation printed separately

rows.basis: [Erroneous examples build conceptual knowledge](claims/erroneous-examples-build-conceptual-knowledge.md) [+M]; [Correct exemplars improved explanations more than error-displaying examples](claims/correct-exemplars-improve-pst-fraction-explanations.md) [~M]
rows.change: Add incorrect examples for learners to compare with correct ones, alongside a correct model; when learners are revising their own explanations, examples made only of errors did worse than a correct and complete exemplar
rows.if: The goal is conceptual understanding where learners hold known misconceptions

rows.basis: [Worked examples between game rounds improved understanding](claims/worked-examples-improve-knowledge-map-content-understanding-in-a-puzzle-game.md) [+M]; [Gains stayed small relative to experts](claims/worked-example-gains-in-a-puzzle-game-remain-small-relative-to-expert-knowledge-maps.md) [~M]
rows.change: Insert worked examples between rounds of play; expect gains to remain far below expert performance
rows.if: Training uses a game or simulation

rows.basis: [Solved problems improve algebra achievement, on minimal evidence](claims/solved-problems-improve-algebra-achievement.md) [~W]
rows.change: Use solved problems with questions about the reasoning, but treat the evidence as thin; one study found solved problems worse than reflective questioning
rows.if: Middle or high school algebra classes

rows.basis: [Whole-task practice improves transfer (design argument)](claims/whole-task-performance-improves-transfer.md) [+W]; [Varied tasks of one type enable transfer](claims/task-variety-enables-transfer-same-task-type.md) [+W]
rows.change: Organise the programme around whole tasks in classes from simple to complex, with varied tasks within each class
rows.if: The goal is transfer of a complex skill to varied situations

rows.basis: [Part-task practice reduces load for novices](claims/part-task-practice-reduces-load-for-novices.md) [+M]
rows.change: Start with brief practice on isolated elements, then move to the whole task
rows.if: Learners are complete novices and the task has many interacting elements

rows.basis: [Fading support promotes transfer of responsibility](claims/fading-support-promotes-transfer-of-responsibility.md) [+M]
rows.change: Fade support from worked examples to completion tasks to independent tasks
rows.if: Within a task class

rows.basis: [Lower-prior-knowledge learners do better with full worked examples](claims/lower-prior-knowledge-learners-score-higher-with-full-than-completion-worked-examples.md) [~M]
rows.change: Give lower-prior-knowledge learners full worked examples longer, and move higher-prior-knowledge learners to completion tasks sooner
rows.if: Learners in one class differ in prior knowledge

rows.basis: [Worked-example guidance becomes less effective with expertise](claims/worked-examples-less-effective-with-expertise.md) [~M]
rows.change: Start in a later task class or with less support; full guidance becomes redundant
rows.if: Learners arrive experienced in the skill

rows.basis: [Contingent scaffolding improves learning](claims/contingent-scaffolding-improves-learning.md) [+M]
rows.change: Adjust support to the last response: more after a failure, less after a success
rows.if: A tutor or adaptive system can watch the attempts

rows.basis: [No knowledge difference between lecture and 4C/ID](claims/no-knowledge-difference-lecture-vs-4cid-consent-training.md) [~M]; [4C/ID's OSCE advantage was not significant](claims/osce-advantage-4cid-not-significant.md) [~M]
rows.change: Do not expect a knowledge-test gain over a lecture; judge the design on a whole-task performance check (for example an OSCE), and power the comparison
rows.if: A short professional workshop judged by a knowledge test

rows.basis: [Scaffolded task progression shifts novices toward diagnosis](claims/scaffolded-task-progression-diagnostic-shift.md) [+W]
rows.change: Sequence task classes from completing to fixing to building; diagnostic reasoning appeared as tasks moved on
rows.if: Learners are learning to program or troubleshoot

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Add short part-task practice or a job aid for that routine only
rows.if: One routine is slow or error-prone inside otherwise sound whole-task work

rows.basis: [Agents as coaches and tutors are most useful with novices](claims/agents-most-effective-novice-learners.md) [~M]; [Guidance that helps novices becomes redundant with expertise](claims/expertise-reversal-effect.md) [~S]
rows.change: Step-based tutoring with contingent hints and worked steps available; a coach or tutor agent rather than open chat
rows.if: Learners are novices in the domain

rows.basis: [Guidance that helps novices becomes redundant with expertise](claims/expertise-reversal-effect.md) [~S]; [Learning by teaching](claims/learning-by-teaching-improves-tutor-learning.md) [+S]
rows.change: Reduce step-level hinting; use the tutor for challenge problems, explanation checking or as a learner to teach
rows.if: Learners are already competent and practising for fluency or transfer

rows.basis: [GPT-4 access harmed the unaided exam](claims/gpt-base-harms-unassisted-exam-performance.md) [-M] (high school); [AI tutor beat active learning](claims/ai-tutor-beats-active-learning-post-test.md) [+M] (undergraduates); [ITS fostered declarative and procedural knowledge in vocational education](claims/its-vet-foster-declarative-procedural-knowledge.md) [+M] (systematic review, no pooled effect); [adult learners want human-in-the-loop AI](claims/human-in-the-loop-ai-design-pf.md) [+M] (focus groups)
rows.change: Keep the answer-withholding default; most LLM-tutor trials recorded here were undergraduates or high-school students, and the harm-after-withdrawal result was in high school. Leave decisions with the learner: adult learners asked for AI that points to what to improve rather than giving the final answer
rows.if: Adult or professional learners (higher education, workforce)

rows.basis: [Teachable agent improved fourth-graders' science reasoning](claims/ta-improves-basic-and-added-value-gains-fourth-grade.md) [+M]; [warning about AI mistakes raised seventh-graders' hint requests](claims/ai-fallibility-warning-increases-help-seeking.md) [+M]; [multi-turn interactions raised attack success on conventional risks three to five times](claims/dynamic-multi-turn-amplifies-conventional-risks.md) [-M] and [safety classifiers passed exam-answer and cheating requests as safe](claims/llama-guard-failure-cases-subtle-education-risks.md) [-M] (model evaluations, no learners)
rows.change: Prefer a structured tutor or teachable agent with teacher oversight to open chat; test the tutor's safety over long multi-turn conversations and against requests to cheat, not only single prompts, and do not rely on an off-the-shelf safety filter
rows.if: Children or young adolescents

rows.basis: [Guardrailed tutor with teacher-designed hints](claims/gpt-tutor-improves-practice-more-than-gpt-base.md) [+M]; [ITS improve achievement](claims/adaptive-learning-improves-outcomes.md) [+S]; [ITS help especially where knowledge is structured](claims/its-improve-outcomes-structured-domains.md) [+M] (review, no effect size)
rows.change: A step-based tutor with problem-specific hints written or checked by a teacher
rows.if: The goal is a procedure in a well-structured domain (mathematics, physics problems, programming)

rows.basis: [Requiring engagement before the AI unlocked cut verbatim AI text in final essays (27% against 47%, d = −0.47)](claims/engage-to-unlock-lower-ai-text-coverage.md) [+M]; [AI-assisted cover-letter practice improved unaided writing a day later](claims/ai-practice-improved-writing-skill-persisted-one-day.md) [+M] (after a lesson on the principles); [Bounded support gave the best independent writing](claims/genai-supported-performance-independent-divergence.md) [~M]; [originality gains vanished unaided](claims/chatgpt-free-use-originality-gains-vanish-unassisted.md) [~M]; [an LLM-assisted essay group did worse than a no-tool group across four sessions](claims/llm-group-worse-neural-linguistic-scoring-four-sessions.md) [-M] (small preprint, 18 completed the fourth session); [scaffolded GenAI augmented rather than replaced judgement in a design-thinking course](claims/genai-scaffolded-augments-human-judgment-design-thinking.md) [+M] (student reflections)
rows.change: Use the tutor for questioning and critique of the learner's draft, not for producing it; unlock the AI only after the learner's own attempt; an AI-improved version of the learner's own practice draft, after the attempt, can teach; assess independent work
rows.if: The goal is an ill-structured judgement (writing, design, ethics, clinical reasoning)

rows.basis: [Practice up, unaided exam down](claims/gpt-base-harms-unassisted-exam-performance.md) [-M]; [Effects small on standardized tests](claims/test-type-moderates-its-effects.md) [~M]; [g = 0.76 with AI allowed in the test, −0.06 without](claims/exam-environment-moderates-genai-learning-effects.md) [~M] (programming)
rows.change: Schedule tutor-off practice before it; measure unaided performance separately from tutored practice; do not forecast from studies whose test allowed the AI
rows.if: The assessment is unaided, or delayed, or at work

rows.basis: [Reflection prompt cut acceptance of wrong advice](claims/reflection-reduces-incorrect-ai-advice-acceptance.md) [+M]; [Human-AI tutoring raised MAP growth over AI alone](claims/human-ai-tutoring-improves-map-growth-over-ai-only.md) [+M]
rows.change: Answer-withholding by default, a hint ladder, logged reliance signals, and a named human handoff with a response time; add reflection prompts before accepting the tutor's answer
rows.if: Online self-paced or asynchronous, no instructor watching

rows.basis: [A structured tutor beat a holdout group that freely used consumer chatbots, over five weeks](claims/ambient-consumer-ai-did-not-close-tutor-gap.md) [+M] (small field experiment); [Structured prompting improved explanations; unprompted access did not](claims/structured-prompting-improves-open-ended-ai-learning.md) [+M]; [warning labels insufficient](claims/genai-warning-labels-insufficient-reliance.md) [-M]; [students named awareness of their reliance as the most useful outcome](claims/reliance-awareness-most-valued-outcome.md) [+M] (six interviews, programming course)
rows.change: Offer a structured tutor as well, and teach a structured way to use any chatbot (attempt first, ask for hints, check claims) rather than relying on a warning; make the learner's own reliance visible to them
rows.if: Learners will use a general chatbot anyway

rows.basis: [AI tutor beat active learning in less time](claims/ai-tutor-less-time-on-task.md) [+M] (one lesson, immediate test)
rows.change: A research-designed tutor can replace a lesson for an immediate outcome; do not extrapolate to a course
rows.if: Short time: one session or a single lesson

rows.basis: [Adaptive fading beat fixed fading in a step-based tutor](claims/adaptive-fading-worked-examples-benefits.md) [+W]; [tutoring agents' simulated students plateaued within 5–10 of 30 days, mostly for lack of a curriculum](claims/educlaw-bench-plateau-within-days.md) [-M] (simulated learners only)
rows.change: Fade tutor help across sessions on each learner's performance, add tutor-off checkpoints, and plan the curriculum the tutor follows rather than leaving it to the tutor; no claim here follows an LLM tutor over a course with real learners
rows.if: A course of many weeks

rows.basis: [Tutor CoPilot raised mastery 4 points](claims/tutor-copilot-raises-exit-ticket-mastery-4pp.md) [+S]; [Proactive tutoring had larger relative growth](claims/proactive-tutoring-larger-relative-map-growth.md) [~M]; [no significant proactive–reactive difference at the cutoff](claims/didc-cutoff-null-proactive-benefit-increases-below-cutoff.md) [~M]
rows.change: Give them AI suggestions in real time. Routing learners below a threshold to proactive human contact is plausible but not shown to beat on-request help; if you do it, compare the two
rows.if: Human tutors or mentors are available but stretched

rows.basis: [Conversational agents were well behind humans at helping the student](claims/conversational-agents-behind-human-helping-students.md) [~M]
rows.change: Narrow the tutor's scope to checkable tasks and accept that it may underperform a human at helping
rows.if: No human is available at all

rows.basis: [GPT-4 feedback flawed in about 35% of hints](claims/gpt4-feedback-66-percent-targeted-35-percent-flawed.md) [~M]; [convincing incorrect explanations](claims/genai-hallucination-convincing-incorrect-explanations.md) [-M]
rows.change: Do not let the tutor's judgement of mastery stand alone; validate its content and its errors, and assess with a human-scored or proctored task
rows.if: High stakes (certification, patient or client safety)

rows.basis: [Voice and text gave equivalent weekly mastery; voice doubled turns and questions at 2.8 times the cost](claims/voice-text-mastery-equivalent-interaction-transformed.md) [~M] (within-student, one five-week field experiment)
rows.change: Choose voice to buy engagement and questioning, text to buy the same measured mastery for less; measure both if it matters
rows.if: A voice tutor is planned instead of text

rows.basis: [GPT-4 and human tutor feedback produced no detected difference over six weeks](claims/gpt4-feedback-no-superior-linguistic-progress-enl.md) [~M] (equivalence not tested); [students preferring the human cited follow-up questions and speaking practice](claims/human-feedback-preference-face-to-face-reasons.md) [~M]
rows.change: AI feedback can extend a human tutor's feedback; keep the human for follow-up questions and spoken practice, and measure progress rather than assuming parity
rows.if: Learners writing in a second language want feedback on drafts

rows.basis: [Talking head added little](claims/autotutor-content-matters-not-talking-head.md) [~M]; [voice, not visual presence](claims/agent-effects-due-to-voice-not-visual-presence.md) [~M]; [visual-channel overload](claims/apa-visual-channel-overload.md) [-M]
rows.change: Spend effort on what the agent says and its voice before its face; avoid adding visual load on complex content
rows.if: An animated or avatar agent is planned

rows.basis: [Tutor plus peers gave the best unaided accuracy](claims/tutor-plus-peers-strongest-unassisted-math-accuracy.md) [+M]; [conversational-agent prompts improved individual and pair outcomes](claims/conversational-agent-prompts-improve-individual-and-dyad-outcomes.md) [+W] [but were felt as disruptive](claims/agent-interruptions-perceived-disruption-varies.md) [~W] (one experiment, reported second-hand); [judge agents propagated peer errors](claims/judge-verification-propagates-peer-errors.md) [-M]; [groups verifying chatbot solutions together supported problem solving](claims/collaborative-chatbot-answer-verification-problem-solving.md) [+M] (exploratory, grade 12 physics)
rows.change: Give the AI a bounded role (tutor or critic) and have the group verify its output together; do not use one AI agent to check another; time its prompts to pauses rather than interrupting
rows.if: Group work with an AI participant

rows.basis: [Multi-agent simulated-patient training raised OSCE-aligned scores (71.8% vs 55.6%)](claims/ma-scaffolding-improves-osce-exam-score.md) [+M]; [role-play failures rise after turn 6](claims/rpla-failure-onset-second-half-of-dialogue.md) [-M]
rows.change: Use multi-agent simulated patients with scaffolding for interview practice, with faculty review of errors; test long dialogues, where role-play failures cluster
rows.if: Health professions (clinical interviewing, diagnosis)

rows.basis: [Tutor CoPilot](claims/tutor-copilot-raises-exit-ticket-mastery-4pp.md) [+S] (tutors of K-12 students; not tested with teacher candidates)
rows.change: Use the tutor to support novice tutors or teachers in the moment (suggested moves), not to replace them
rows.if: Teacher education

rows.basis: [Checking AI claims against sources predicted decision-making gains](claims/checking-ai-claims-predicts-gains.md) [+M] (secondary school, socio-scientific issues; carried to business untested)
rows.change: Use the tutor to question the learner's analysis and to check claims against case data; keep the decision and justification the learner's
rows.if: Business or management courses (case analysis, decisions)

rows.basis: [Hint-not-solution was the hardest dimension, 6% to 81% across models](claims/hint-not-solution-most-challenging-dimension.md) [-M]; [learning by teaching an LLM improved assignments, not exams](claims/learning-by-teaching-llm-improves-assignments-projects.md) [~M]; [developers who used AI assistance scored 17% lower on a later comprehension test](claims/ai-assistance-lower-comprehension-17-percent.md) [-M] (cited study, steepest for full delegation); [in a project course, students who coded without AI kept high code comprehension while the heaviest AI users showed little](claims/no-ai-use-high-comprehension-level3-low.md) [-M] (descriptive, instructor-rated)
rows.change: Configure hint-not-solution behaviour and test it; small models frequently give direct code solutions
rows.if: Technology and computing courses

rows.basis: [Gen-AI effect on higher-order thinking was larger for high-SRL students (ES 0.86 vs 0.28)](claims/genai-srl-moderator.md) [~M]
rows.change: Add more external structure (planning prompts, check-ins, hint budgets) rather than open access
rows.if: Learners with low self-regulation

rows.basis: [ungrounded ChatGPT self-study taught 6 of 23 students a fabricated answer](claims/genai-self-study-fabrication-curated-resources.md) [-M]; [a robot tutor given the lecture slides cited them and made no false statements, while the control made ten](claims/kbd-manipulation-check-behavioral-differences-transcripts.md) [+M] (six transcripts); [students and lecturers want the tutor to have the official materials](claims/gsr-context-knowledge-materials-strategies-environment.md) [+M]; [the best retrieval settings differed between STEM and humanities](claims/rag-configuration-discipline-dependent-moodle-tutor.md) [+M] (automated evaluation)
rows.change: Ground it in the course's slides, notes and worked solutions, have it cite which it used, and tune retrieval per discipline
rows.if: The tutor would answer from its general knowledge, with no course materials given to it

rows.basis: [LLM feedback gave students marked by group or label less constructive criticism and more praise for the same essays](claims/marked-students-praise-withholding-bias.md) [-M] — a bias in the model's treatment of the label, not a property of the learners
rows.change: Leave the labels out of the prompt; personalise from the learner's work, and audit the tutor's feedback across groups for less criticism and more praise
rows.if: The tutor is to be given learner profile labels (group membership, disability, "unmotivated")

rows.basis: [higher state-test pass rates for Cognitive Tutor students receiving special education (35.7% against 10.9%) and with limited English (27% against 18.9%)](claims/cognitive-tutor-miami-dade-fcat-pass-rates.md) [+M] (no effect size, not randomised); [potential for marginalised students, contingent on safeguards](claims/ai-tools-potential-marginalized-students-contingent-safeguards.md) [~M] (review)
rows.change: Keep a step-based tutor inside teacher-led instruction and track these learners' unaided results separately; the evidence is a district comparison, not a trial
rows.if: Learners receiving special-education services or learning in a second language

rows.basis: [speech-recognition tutoring supports word identification, attention and motivation](claims/asr-tutoring-supports-word-identification-attention-motivation.md) [+M]; [time efficiencies over human tutoring](claims/intelligent-reading-tutor-time-efficiency-over-human-tutoring.md) [+M] (both from a vendor evidence summary, no effect sizes)
rows.change: A speech-recognition tutor that listens and supplies a word or hint at a miscue can give practice time a human cannot; keep a teacher reading the reports
rows.if: Young readers practising oral reading

rows.basis: [an agent that responded to detected gaming with exercises on the bypassed material halved gaming and improved those students' learning](claims/gaming-agent-reduced-gaming-improved-learning.md) [+W] (one classroom study, as a review reports it); [interest-personalised problems reduced gaming (d = 0.35)](claims/personalization-reduces-gaming-behavior.md) [+M] and [raised accuracy on the hardest skills](claims/personalization-improves-hard-kc-accuracy-algebra-its.md) [+M] (ninth-grade algebra, one randomised study); [staff of a technology-driven tutoring programme reported engagement as a challenge](claims/saga-implementation-engagement-challenges.md) [-M]
rows.change: Personalise problem contexts to learners' interests; when the log shows gaming, give the skipped material as supplementary exercises; check engagement over weeks, not only in the first session
rows.if: Learners are disengaged, or game the hints

rows.basis: [Minimal guidance is less effective for novices](claims/minimal-guidance-less-effective-for-novices.md) [-M]
rows.change: Make the concept available explicitly (a short explanation or modelled step) before or alongside the work in the anchor
rows.if: Learners are novices on the concept the anchor is meant to carry

rows.basis: [Seductive details can impair comprehension and transfer](claims/seductive-details-effect.md) [-M]
rows.change: Trim or play down decorative details; keep only distractors that are part of the task, and prompt for relevance judgements on those
rows.if: The anchor is a vivid story or video with much interesting but irrelevant detail, and learners have low prior knowledge

rows.basis: [Comparing cases side by side improves learning and transfer](claims/comparing-contrasting-cases-improves-learning.md) [+M]
rows.change: Give a second anchor or case with different surface details and the same concept, and have learners compare the two
rows.if: The goal is use of the concept in new situations

rows.basis: [Concrete materials help only when connected to the concept](claims/manipulatives-require-connection-to-concept.md) [~W] (manipulatives; carried to anchors by analogy)
rows.change: Make step 5 an explicit mapping: name the concept and show which parts of the anchor correspond to it
rows.if: The debrief is planned as a retelling of the story

rows.basis: [Part-task practice reduces load for absolute novices](claims/part-task-practice-reduces-load-for-novices.md) [~W]
rows.change: Isolate one component first, then return to the whole anchor
rows.if: The anchor's problem needs several new interacting ideas at once and learners are complete beginners

rows.basis: [Contingent scaffolding improves learning](claims/contingent-scaffolding-improves-learning.md) [+M] (one-to-one tutoring)
rows.change: Raise support when a group is stuck and lower it when it progresses, recording each intervention
rows.if: Small groups work in the anchor with a facilitator

rows.basis: [Guidance added to simulation inquiry modestly improves outcomes](claims/guidance-improves-inquiry-learning-outcomes.md) [+W]
rows.change: Build prompts and feedback into the environment instead of leaving the anchor open
rows.if: The anchor is a simulation or video that learners work through alone (`online-self-paced`)

rows.basis: [PS-I effects are negative for 2nd–5th graders](claims/psi-effect-increases-with-grade-level.md) [-M]
rows.change: Teach the concept first and use the anchor as application
rows.if: Learners are in the early primary years and the plan has them attempt the anchor's problem before any teaching

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Use one short anchor, connect it explicitly to the concept within the session, and end with one individual item on a new situation
rows.if: Only one session is available

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Score recall of the anchor separately from use of the concept on a new problem; only the second shows the concept travelled
rows.if: The assessment asks about the anchor's own story

rows.basis: [Guided rather than unassisted discovery](claims/minimal-guidance-less-effective-for-novices.md) [~S]; its studies did not use authentic assessment tasks, and the meta-analysis does not break results down by prior knowledge
rows.change: Spend the first half of the unit on component practice with worked examples; use a simpler, well-structured version of the task for the first draft; plan two revision cycles; give feedback on each component before the whole task.
rows.if: Learners are `novice` in the domain (first course, first placement)

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page
rows.change: Drop most component practice; give an ill-structured task in which learners define part of the problem; one draft with practitioner feedback; judge by a practitioner panel.
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` or practitioners (final-year students, continuing professional education)

rows.basis: [Authentic audiences](claims/authentic-audiences-improve-student-work.md) [+M]: second-graders wrote better for an external audience (one study, abstract only); the rest is untested
rows.change: Keep the task short and concrete with one product, one audience the children know of (another class, families), criteria as two or three "I can" statements, and teacher-led feedback rather than peer scoring.
rows.if: Learners are `child` (primary school)

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page's direct-instruction qualification
rows.change: Assess it with a conventional test or a short structured task; keep the authentic task for the capability that needs it, or use it as a capstone after the procedures are secure.
rows.if: The goal is a well-defined procedure or factual knowledge

rows.basis: [Trainees' reports on clinical scenarios](claims/contextualized-teaching-facilitates-transfer.md) [+W] (one qualitative study of neurosurgical nurses); [simulated cases judged unrealistic](claims/simucase-lacks-behavioral-authenticity.md) [~W] (10 graduate students, focus groups)
rows.change: Use structured clinical or practical stations with checklists and global ratings, or a case simulation, and check with learners whether the simulated case behaves like real clients.
rows.if: `workplace-clinical` or a placement-based course

rows.basis: [Peer assessment](claims/peer-assessment-improves-performance.md) [+M] (robust to online or offline delivery in the meta-analysis); [self-assessment training](claims/self-assessment-accuracy-is-low-without-training.md) [~S]; carried to authentic tasks untested
rows.change: Give the rubric and scored exemplars up front; have learners score an exemplar and see the expert's score before self-assessing; use structured peer review in a timed window; reserve teacher or practitioner judgement for the final product.
rows.if: `online-self-paced`, no teacher present

rows.basis: [Peer assessment](claims/peer-assessment-improves-performance.md) [+M]; [structured criteria not shown to beat freeform peer review](claims/peer-assessment-structured-criteria-improve-learning.md) [~M], so do not expect the rubric alone to lift the peer effect
rows.change: Use peer assessment with the rubric for the draft; teacher feedback on a sample plus whole-class feedback on common problems; double-score only a sample of finals and products near the threshold.
rows.if: Large class (more than about 60) or little assessor time

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Shrink the task to one realistic decision or product, give one feedback point before submission, and drop the public exhibition.
rows.if: Short time (one or two weeks, or a single session)

rows.basis: [Rubric scores spread across scorers](claims/engineering-rubric-low-scoring-reliability.md) [~W] (one class, six teams); the remedy is untested
rows.change: Use at least two tasks or stations, calibrate assessors on exemplars and check agreement before scores are released, set the threshold in advance, and keep a reassessment route.
rows.if: High stakes (grade, progression or licensure)

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page. [The rubric study with pre-service teachers](claims/rubrics-improve-student-work.md) [~M] found more stress and performance-avoidance with rubric use
rows.change: Rehearse privately with feedback first; make the first audience small and supportive; grade growth against criteria, not comparison with peers.
rows.if: Learners anxious or new to public performance

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page
rows.change: Let learners choose the context or product form where the target allows; give the rubric in plain language; score the target reasoning apart from language mechanics; allow oral or multimodal products.
rows.if: Mixed language backgrounds or unequal access to resources

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Include a live or observed part (an oral defence, a supervised station, a recorded process) and ask learners to explain decisions in the product.
rows.if: Learners use AI tools freely outside class

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Split the submission: the product as the audience would receive it, scored on audience criteria (relevance, clarity, usability), plus a short decision memo for the assessor (sources checked, priorities weighed, what is uncertain and how the product handles it), scored on the reasoning criteria; give feedback and the revision on both
rows.if: The real product goes to a client or audience who should not see the working (an advice letter, a patient leaflet, a pitch)

rows.basis: [Fluspeak](claims/fluspeak-good-beginners-poor-advanced.md) [~W] (good results for beginners on phonemes; one program, reported second-hand); [CAPT](claims/capt-strong-segmentals-weak-prosody.md) [~S]
rows.change: Start with segmentals and word stress on words they already know; use ASR read-aloud for segmentals; keep communicative tasks short and scripted at first.
rows.if: Learners are beginners (`novice`) with limited vocabulary

rows.basis: [Fluspeak](claims/fluspeak-good-beginners-poor-advanced.md) [~W] (poor for advanced learners seeking fluency); [immediate task repetition](claims/immediate-repetition-benefits-oral-performance.md) [+W]
rows.change: Weight the list towards thought groups, pausing, linking and intonation; use repeated retellings and listener feedback, not ASR, for these.
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` and want fluency or ease of understanding in long turns

rows.basis: [AI reading tool, prosody null](claims/ai-reading-progress-speed-accuracy-large-effects-prosody-null.md) [~M] (third-grade learners, oral reading, not spontaneous speech); [individual or peer ASR practice](claims/individual-work-best-asr-pronunciation-training.md) [~M] (unsettled; third-graders did best individually in one study)
rows.change: Keep segments to 5–10 minutes, use rhymes, chants and games for stress and rhythm; if ASR is used, short individual turns with an adult nearby. Expect prosody to move slowly.
rows.if: Learners are `child` (under 12)

rows.basis: [Adults and native-like pronunciation](claims/adults-find-pronunciation-harder-than-children.md) [~M] (narrative digest); the work-task focus is untested
rows.change: Take the feature list and tasks from their work talk (handovers, phone calls, explanations to clients); judge success by whether those listeners understand; set intelligibility, not accent, as the goal.
rows.if: Adults in work settings (nurses, call-centre staff, engineers) with named listeners

rows.basis: [First-language interference](claims/native-language-interference-shapes-pronunciation-errors.md) [~M]; the split is untested
rows.change: Teach the shared central features (stress, thought groups, final consonants) to the whole class; give segmental contrasts as individual self-practice from each learner's diagnosis.
rows.if: Mixed first languages in one class

rows.basis: [Resource scarcity and large classes](claims/resource-scarcity-large-classes-limit-pronunciation-feedback.md) [~M] (a review of Bangladeshi classrooms) names the constraint; [ASR diagnosis](claims/asr-diagnostic-identification-pronunciation-errors.md) [+M]; [guided ASR practice](claims/asr-guided-practice-improves-overall-pronunciation-accuracy.md) [+S], carried from Korean and other ESL/EFL learners
rows.change: Diagnose from a short read-aloud plus one spontaneous answer per learner, ideally screened by ASR transcripts; run segmental practice as ASR self-study; spend the teacher's minutes only on suprasegmental and fluency feedback and on the re-observation samples.
rows.if: One teacher for a large class, or scarce facilitator time (a volunteer tutor, a brief check-in)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Collect the diagnostic and re-observation samples as voice messages so every learner gives the same sample; pair remote and in-room learners for the communicative step by call; ASR keyboards on phones serve the segmental practice.
rows.if: Mixed modes (some learners remote, some in the room) or phone-only

rows.basis: Untested; short ASR programmes pooled to a negligible effect ([guided ASR practice](claims/asr-guided-practice-improves-overall-pronunciation-accuracy.md) [~S])
rows.change: Do not attempt the three-area arc. Record one spontaneous sample, give each learner one or two features that most disrupt understanding with a model and a self-practice routine, and arrange a later recording if possible.
rows.if: A single session only

rows.basis: Untested proposal; [explicit instruction](claims/explicit-communicative-pronunciation-instruction-works.md) [~S] (longer interventions showed larger effects)
rows.change: One feature per two lessons: 2 minutes hear, 4 minutes controlled practice, 4 minutes in a communicative exchange; at most three features in the term; re-observe in the last lesson.
rows.if: A fixed short time budget (for example 10 minutes a lesson for 6 weeks)

rows.basis: [Immediate task repetition](claims/immediate-repetition-benefits-oral-performance.md) [+W] (less anxiety, especially for less confident learners); [global and local errors](claims/global-versus-local-errors-correction.md) [+W]
rows.change: Practise in private first (recordings, ASR, pairs) before any whole-class turn; use repetition so the third telling feels easier; correct only errors that block understanding.
rows.if: Learners with low confidence or anxiety about speaking

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Teach perception and production by ear and gesture, not from spelling or phonetic symbols; avoid ASR transcript comparison until learners can read the text.
rows.if: Learners with low literacy in the target language

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: The learner keeps their recordings and decides who hears them; the teacher hears only the diagnostic and re-observation samples the learner shares; no class playback without consent.
rows.if: Recordings are private or sensitive

rows.basis: Untested proposal; [explicit instruction](claims/explicit-communicative-pronunciation-instruction-works.md) [~S] (drill gains overstate spontaneous gains)
rows.change: Keep it; score it as given, add a spontaneous-speech rating beside it if it measures only read-aloud or drills, and change only the feature list and the minutes per feature.
rows.if: The brief names its own routine, rubric or speaking test

rows.basis: Untested proposal; [form plus meaning](claims/form-and-meaning-focus-beats-form-only.md) [+W]
rows.change: Keep the performance whole; take the features from a recorded rehearsal, practise them in isolation for a few minutes, then rehearse the whole performance again for a listener.
rows.if: The goal is a whole performance for a real audience (a presentation, a client call)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Use it as the first compared case: record it, contrast with a model, and make it the first feature in the list.
rows.if: The learners' reported error is known (for example "people don't understand my numbers")

rows.basis: [Teachers value but seldom teach pronunciation](claims/teachers-value-pronunciation-but-seldom-teach-it.md) [~M] (14 teachers, one programme); [teachers unprepared](claims/esl-teachers-bangladesh-unprepared-pronunciation.md) [~M] and [no pronunciation assessment](claims/no-pronunciation-assessment-clt-bangladesh.md) [~M] (one review, Bangladesh)
rows.change: Limit the list to the seven central features with recorded models; use the re-observation samples as the programme's pronunciation assessment; seek short training in diagnosis.
rows.if: The teacher has no phonology training, or no pronunciation assessment exists in the programme

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Score the test's own criteria on practice samples; keep the spontaneous-speech re-observation; do not drop fluency features because the test weights accuracy.
rows.if: High stakes (a certification speaking test)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Keep each online exposition segment short, with an embedded check and worked material, and spend the in-person time on guided practice with feedback before independent work.
rows.if: Learners are `novice` in the content

rows.basis: untested proposal; the recorded synthesis is mostly higher education and professional training
rows.change: Run the online part in school time under supervision (rotation between stations or groups) rather than at home, and keep online segments short; give the teacher a view of who completed what.
rows.if: Learners are `child` (`pre-k-12`)

rows.basis: [Blended learning improves outcomes](claims/blended-learning-improves-outcomes.md) [~M], pooled mostly across higher education and professional training, with extra time and resources confounded
rows.change: Put content and repeated practice online where they can fit it around work; use in-person time for practice with equipment, cases or colleagues and for feedback on performance.
rows.if: Learners are `adult` working professionals (`adult-workplace`)

rows.basis: [Active learning improves exam performance](claims/active-learning-improves-exam-performance.md) [+M], tested against lecture in undergraduate STEM courses, not within a blend
rows.change: Reserve most in-person time for learners carrying out the task with feedback, not for exposition; move the exposition online.
rows.if: The goal is a `complex-skill` or `procedure` that needs practice with feedback

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Put spaced, self-checked practice online with immediate answers; keep in-person time for using the material and for checks of what was missed.
rows.if: The goal is mostly facts or vocabulary (`verbal-association`)

rows.basis: [SRL interventions in online and blended environments](claims/srl-interventions-moderate-effect-online-blended.md) [+M], pooled across 15 studies, populations not reported on the claim page
rows.change: Add planning prompts, a visible schedule with intermediate deadlines and self-monitoring checks; review them at the next in-person session.
rows.if: The online part is `online-self-paced` and learners have little experience of it

rows.basis: [Online continuing-education persistence](claims/online-continuing-education-persistence-lower-than-onground.md) [~W], fully online adult continuing education, associational; untested for blends
rows.change: Monitor completion each week, contact non-starters within the first week or two, and keep a named person learners can ask.
rows.if: No teacher present between sessions, or a large group

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Use a single online preparation task before the session and a short online follow-up; the course-level split does not apply.
rows.if: Only one session, or a few days

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Hold the summative assessment in person or proctored; keep the online checks low-stakes and formative so learners use them to monitor.
rows.if: High-stakes assessment

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Make the online part downloadable and usable on a phone, provide access time on site, and avoid live online slots that need a stable connection.
rows.if: Learners have limited devices or connectivity

rows.basis: [Comparing cases side by side improves learning and transfer](claims/comparing-contrasting-cases-improves-learning.md) [+M]; [Analogical reasoning improves transfer](claims/comparing-contrasting-cases-improves-learning.md) [+M]
rows.change: Present two or more cases that share the principle side by side and prompt for what is the same and why, rather than one case at a time
rows.if: The goal is applying a principle to new cases

rows.basis: [Analogical reasoning improves transfer](claims/comparing-contrasting-cases-improves-learning.md) [+M] (moderator in the meta-analysis)
rows.change: Reverse the order: have learners compare first and state the principle after, connected to what they found
rows.if: The plan states the principle first and then shows cases as illustrations

rows.basis: [Multiple cases from different perspectives support transfer in ill-structured domains](claims/cognitive-flexibility-theory-multiple-cases.md) [~M]
rows.change: Revisit several short cases under different themes; expect better transfer essays, and plan separate work for factual recall, which drill did better
rows.if: The domain is ill structured (the concept plays out differently case by case)

rows.basis: [Comparing cases: procedural gain, no conceptual gain in one algebra study](claims/comparing-contrasting-cases-improves-learning.md) [~M]
rows.change: After comparing solution methods, add an explicit explanation of why each works; comparison raised procedural knowledge and flexibility but not conceptual knowledge
rows.if: The goal is understanding why a mathematical method works, not only choosing a method

rows.basis: [Analogical reasoning improves transfer](claims/comparing-contrasting-cases-improves-learning.md) [~M]
rows.change: Add a later comparison or retrieval of the principle; benefits were larger on immediate than delayed tests
rows.if: The test that matters is weeks later

rows.basis: [Case-based learning improves exam performance](claims/case-based-learning-improves-exam-performance.md) [~M]
rows.change: Do not expect the case format alone to raise learning; a review judged the evidence inconclusive and said any benefit may come from the group work. Add individual analysis of a new case
rows.if: The course is in the health professions and relies on small-group case discussion

rows.basis: [Comparing cases side by side improves learning and transfer](claims/comparing-contrasting-cases-improves-learning.md) [+M] (undergraduates comparing two cases on one page)
rows.change: Put both cases on one screen with a written prompt to describe their similarities
rows.if: Learners work alone (`online-self-paced`)

rows.basis: [Case-based learning benefits depended on faculty-guided embedding](claims/genai-cbl-faculty-guided-conditional-benefits.md) [~W]
rows.change: Keep a faculty member guiding how the tool is used in each case; complex cases and team workflows showed null or unfavourable effects
rows.if: Cases are complex and supported by AI tools or team workflows (medical education)

rows.basis: no claim here tests case-based learning by prior knowledge; nearest: [Biomedical causal knowledge improves novice diagnostic accuracy on difficult cases](claims/biomedical-causal-knowledge-improves-novice-diagnosis-irrelevant-findings.md) [+M] and [Prior knowledge moderates scaffolding effectiveness](claims/prior-knowledge-moderates-scaffolding-effectiveness.md) [~M] (examples for lower levels, reflection for higher)
rows.change: Teach the concept or give a worked example before the cases, then compare
rows.if: Learners lack the concept the cases presuppose

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Add an individual comparison task on a changed case before the group discussion ends
rows.if: Many learners discuss one case in a large group

rows.basis: [Comparing cases side by side improves learning and transfer](claims/comparing-contrasting-cases-improves-learning.md) [+M]; [Co-regulation shows stronger relationships with the three CoI presences than self-regulation in an online case-based course](claims/co-regulation-stronger-presence-relationships-than-self-regulation.md) [~W]; [Some Chinese students felt uncomfortable with case-based learning due to lack of structured instruction content](claims/case-based-learning-uncomfortable-unstructured-instruction.md) [~W]; mentor role from [Mentor Support in Self-Paced Online Learning](patterns/mentor-support-in-self-paced-online-learning.md), untested for case work
rows.change: Put the cases side by side with a written comparison prompt; require a short individual written analysis of each new case; have the mentor read a sample and return the principle statement with feedback; add an asynchronous peer exchange on each case; recap the principle in writing; use cases from the learners' own workplaces where possible
rows.if: Learners work through cases self-paced online (`online-self-paced`), with a mentor available on demand

rows.basis: [Case-based learning benefits depended on faculty-guided embedding](claims/genai-cbl-faculty-guided-conditional-benefits.md) [~W]; [Controlled GenAI virtual-patient and communication studies reported short-term skill gains, but positive findings were not universal](claims/genai-virtual-patient-short-term-gains-mixed.md) [~M]; see [AI Tutoring](patterns/ai-tutoring.md) and [Practice with Simulated People](patterns/practice-with-simulated-people.md)
rows.change: Have the AI generate surface-varied cases holding the principle constant, and check each one before use; let it play the person in an interactive case; have it ask for the principle rather than supply it; judge the learner's individual analysis of a new case without the AI; keep a person reviewing complex cases
rows.if: An AI is the case partner: it writes or varies the cases, plays the client or patient, or questions the learner's analysis

rows.basis: [Virtual patients blended with traditional education improve knowledge more than traditional education alone](claims/vp-blended-knowledge-advantage.md) [+M]; [Virtual patients show larger advantages over passive traditional learning than over active learning](claims/vp-passive-versus-active-comparison.md) [~M]; [Virtual patients are as effective as traditional education for knowledge outcomes](claims/vp-traditional-knowledge-no-difference.md) [~M] (health professions)
rows.change: Use it alongside the case discussion, not in place of it; expect gains on reasoning and skills more than on recall; give feedback inside the case
rows.if: An interactive case simulation (virtual patient, branching case) is available

rows.basis: [Live simulations with real patients showed the greatest effects among simulation types](claims/simulation-type-moderates-effectiveness.md) [~M] (document-based least effective, g = 0.31, higher education)
rows.change: Build in decision points with consequences revealed in stages, or pair the document with a worked analysis for novices
rows.if: The cases are static documents only (a written case, a record, a work sample)

rows.basis: [In the initial skill acquisition phase, authentic video yielded higher overall observation assignment scores than virtual simulation](claims/av-outperforms-vs-total-observation-score.md) [~M]; [Virtual simulation stimulated higher self-reported purposefulness than authentic video](claims/vs-higher-purposefulness-reflection.md) [~M] (one design study, 34 candidates)
rows.change: Start with a simplified simulated classroom for reflection, then move to authentic classroom video for analysis and proposing support
rows.if: Teacher education: cases of classroom practice for observation

rows.basis: [International students wanted more global cases and closer connections between case analyses and their local work contexts](claims/lack-of-global-cases-local-relevance.md) [~W]
rows.change: Mix global and local cases, and ask learners to bring or adapt a case from their own work
rows.if: Learners come from varied countries or workplaces (international, working professionals)

rows.basis: untested in these domains in this wiki; the comparison evidence includes a negotiation task ([Comparing cases side by side improves learning and transfer](claims/comparing-contrasting-cases-improves-learning.md) [+M])
rows.change: Keep the comparison policy: two cases sharing one principle, an individual written recommendation before discussion, the principle stated after
rows.if: Business or technology cases (a strategy decision, an incident review, a troubleshooting case)

rows.basis: [Example-problem sequences reduce cognitive load](claims/worked-example-problem-sequences.md) [+M]; [Example-based sequences outperform problem-only practice](claims/worked-examples-with-practice-improve-transfer.md) [+M]
rows.change: Put modelling first: a worked or narrated example, then the learner's attempt, rather than starting with a problem
rows.if: Learners are new to this task

rows.basis: [Reciprocal teaching improves reading comprehension](claims/reciprocal-teaching-improves-reading-comprehension.md) [+M]; [Reciprocal teaching raises comprehension of poor readers](claims/reciprocal-teaching-raises-reading-comprehension-poor-readers.md) [+W]
rows.change: Use reciprocal teaching: model summarising, questioning, clarifying and predicting, then hand the discussion lead to learners
rows.if: The target is reading comprehension

rows.basis: [Reciprocal teaching improves reading comprehension](claims/reciprocal-teaching-improves-reading-comprehension.md) [~M]
rows.change: Expect a smaller gain than researcher-made tests show (median .32 against .88 for reciprocal teaching) and set expectations accordingly
rows.if: Success will be judged on a standardised test

rows.basis: [Contingent scaffolding improves learning](claims/contingent-scaffolding-improves-learning.md) [+M]
rows.change: Coach contingently: least help first, more after a failure, less after a success
rows.if: One-to-one or small-group coaching is possible

rows.basis: [Web-based cognitive apprenticeship required large instructor time](claims/web-based-ca-instructor-time-burden.md) [~W]
rows.change: Set limits on coaching time, and use recorded models or peer coaching for part of it; coaching without a time limit became a large, open-ended load for the instructor
rows.if: One instructor coaches a whole online cohort

rows.basis: [Fading support promotes transfer of responsibility](claims/fading-support-promotes-transfer-of-responsibility.md) [+M]
rows.change: Fade from complete to incomplete examples to independent problems across the cases, not in one step
rows.if: Support moves from worked examples to independent problems

rows.basis: [Worked-example guidance becomes less effective with expertise](claims/worked-examples-less-effective-with-expertise.md) [~M]
rows.change: Shorten or skip modelling and coaching for that learner and move to articulation and exploration
rows.if: A learner already performs the task unaided

rows.basis: [No significant exam differences in technical mathematics](claims/cognitive-apprenticeship-no-significant-exam-differences-technical-math.md) [-M]; [Anxiety rose while confidence grew](claims/cognitive-apprenticeship-attitude-anxiety-confidence-effects.md) [~M]
rows.change: Do not promise exam gains; one community-college quasi-experiment found none, and higher mathematics anxiety alongside more confidence. Track anxiety as an outcome
rows.if: The course replaces traditional instruction in technical mathematics and is judged on exams

rows.basis: [Scaffolded task progression shifts novices toward diagnosis](claims/scaffolded-task-progression-diagnostic-shift.md) [+W]
rows.change: Order tasks from completing a program to fixing a faulty one to building one; reasoning shifted toward diagnosis as tasks moved on
rows.if: Learners are learning to program or debug

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Move learners between phases on their unaided performance instead; no phase length is established
rows.if: The brief fixes a length for each phase (weeks of modelling, then coaching)

rows.basis: [Prior knowledge and self-assessment](claims/prior-knowledge-needed-for-accurate-self-assessment.md) [~M] and [self-assessment accuracy](claims/self-assessment-accuracy-is-low-without-training.md) [~M], both about judging one's own performance, carried to judging others'
rows.change: Use anchor exemplars with known quality, three or four criteria with described levels, teacher modelling each session, and the reference comparison after every round; keep criteria to what learners can see in the object. Delay judging classmates' work until alone judgments of anchors are within a level.
rows.if: Learners are `novice` in the domain (cannot yet tell strong from weak work unaided)

rows.basis: [Rubric guidance](claims/rubrics-improve-peer-feedback-quality.md) [~M]: in a graduate course a rubric changed feedback content but restrained reflective and divergent commentary
rows.change: Have them co-construct criteria, judge genuinely borderline cases, and record reasoned disagreement instead of forcing consensus; use a rubric for the shared vocabulary, not as a score sheet.
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` or practising professionals

rows.basis: [Peer assessment](claims/peer-assessment-improves-performance.md) [+M]: the meta-analysis includes primary students and found no reliable difference by education level; the configuration is untested
rows.change: Use two objects at a time, two or three criteria phrased as questions with picture or worked anchors, and a short spoken comparison in pairs; the teacher gives the reference each time.
rows.if: Learners are `child` (under 12)

rows.basis: [Rubric guidance](claims/rubrics-improve-peer-feedback-quality.md) [+M]: MOOC writing raters, benefit concentrated on subjective, complex criteria and negligible on simple ones
rows.change: Train raters on graded samples at each level before they judge; spend discussion time on these criteria and skip discussion of simple ones.
rows.if: The criteria are subjective or complex (quality of argument, audience fit), not simple and objective

rows.basis: [Rubric-referenced self-assessment](claims/rubrics-improve-student-work.md) [+M] (middle-school writers; pre-service teachers); [assessor benefit](claims/peer-assessment-benefits-assessor.md) [+M], correlational in its direct study
rows.change: End every session with the learner revising their own draft against the same criteria, after judging others' work; score the revision.
rows.if: The goal is better own work, not only better judgment

rows.basis: [Lateral-reading instruction](claims/civic-online-reasoning-instruction-improves-evaluation.md) [+M] (high-school and university students); [one-session checklist instruction](claims/checklist-evaluation-ineffective-online.md) [~M] did no better than the alternatives it was compared with
rows.change: Make leaving the site to check who is behind it and what others say (lateral reading) the criterion, rather than a checklist of on-page features; have the group compare what each member found off the page.
rows.if: The objects are online sources (credibility of websites, claims)

rows.basis: [Peer assessment](claims/peer-assessment-improves-performance.md) [+M] found no difference between online and offline delivery; [the assessor-benefit meta-analysis](claims/peer-assessment-benefits-assessor.md) [+M] found computer-mediated peer assessment did better than paper. The locking and thread rules are untested
rows.change: Collect each rating in a form that locks before others' ratings are visible; reveal all together; hold the discussion in a thread limited to criteria where ratings differ by a level or more; post the reference after the thread closes.
rows.if: `online-instructor-led` or asynchronous

rows.basis: [Peer judgment accuracy](claims/peer-feedback-accuracy-depends-on-expertise.md) [~M]: with a well-specified rubric, averaged ratings by AP English students correlated with expert scores about as well as teachers' did. Correlational, one subject
rows.change: Replace group consensus with the mean of four or five independent ratings per object, and give the reference to the whole class afterwards; discuss only the objects where the mean departs most from it.
rows.if: A large class, or no teacher reaches each group

rows.basis: [Rubric use](claims/rubrics-improve-student-work.md) [~M] raised stress and a performance-avoidance orientation in pre-service teachers; [anonymous sharing](claims/anonymity-mitigates-evaluation-apprehension.md) [~W] is the authors' account, untested
rows.change: Keep collaborative evaluation formative; grade only individual judgments of new objects against the reference, or the revised own work by the teacher; make peer work anonymous.
rows.if: High stakes: peer or group ratings would count towards marks

rows.basis: [Anonymous sharing](claims/anonymity-mitigates-evaluation-apprehension.md) [~W], authors' account of one undergraduate physics course, no test
rows.change: Private written ratings first, simultaneous reveal, rotate who speaks first, and allow anonymous submission of ratings to the teacher.
rows.if: Status differences or dominant voices in groups

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: One round: two anchors of known quality, alone judgment, reveal and compare, reference, then one new object judged alone. Do not attempt co-constructed criteria.
rows.if: `single-session`, no follow-up

rows.basis: [High-performing groups fail without collaboration](claims/high-performing-groups-fail-without-collaboration.md) [~W]
rows.change: Make it less divisible, or require each member to use another's part; groups of strong students still fail when they do not actually work together
rows.if: The task could be split into parts that members do separately

rows.basis: [Poor group leaders undermined discussion](claims/cooperative-conceptual-change-chemistry-misconceptions.md) [~W]
rows.change: Brief leaders to collect each member's view before settling an answer; leaders who rushed and imposed their view prevented discussion
rows.if: Student group leaders will run the discussion

rows.basis: [Co-construction needs personal construction for stable change](claims/personal-construction-required-stable-conceptual-change.md) [~W]
rows.change: Make step 6 a delayed individual check on matched and changed wording; agreement in the pair's talk often did not hold later
rows.if: The objective is measured at a delayed test

rows.basis: [Collaborative writing improves text quality](claims/collaborative-writing-improves-text-quality.md) [+M]
rows.change: Pair learners to plan and revise, then have each write a piece alone as the individual check in step 5
rows.if: The goal is writing

rows.basis: [Structuring interdependence did not change achievement online](claims/interdependence-type-no-achievement-effect-asynchronous.md) [~M]; [initial proposals, thinking-together preparation and a shared artefact supported joint work in a primary-school wiki](claims/pedagogic-design-characteristics-wiki-collaboration.md) [+M] (the authors' reading of their own study); [persistent text and drawings let students explain their postings to each other](claims/persistence-affordance-supports-collaborative-explanation.md) [+W] (design-based case, no comparison)
rows.change: Start with a shared prompt and response deadlines; have each member (or pair) post their own proposal before anyone builds on others', and work in a medium that keeps what was written in view (a shared document or wiki rather than calls). If individual checks are weak, change the task or the prompt, since roles or rewards alone did not change achievement
rows.if: The work is asynchronous online, in small groups

rows.basis: [Groups given the support more often reached near-equal participation](claims/tentative-support-equal-participation.md) [+M] (tentative, descriptive counts, no test statistic); [unequal participation went with lower satisfaction](claims/unequal-participation-lower-satisfaction.md) [~M] (satisfaction, not learning)
rows.change: Show members how much each has contributed (a group awareness display) with prompts when one member falls silent, and still judge learning by the individual check
rows.if: Online groups whose participation is uneven

rows.basis: [Large groups limited individual participation](claims/large-group-size-limited-participation-confidence.md) [~W]; [forum learning needs small groups](claims/forum-collaborative-learning-small-group-sizes.md) [~W] (an editorial's summary of a study)
rows.change: Use three or four per group, or rotate roles so each member carries out each step; in forums, keep discussion groups small
rows.if: Groups of four or five share one lab station or procedure, or a discussion forum has many participants

rows.basis: [Teacher orchestration matters as much as script design](claims/teacher-orchestration-over-script-design.md) [~W]; [no direct script effect on learning gains](claims/script-no-direct-effect-learning-gains.md) [-M] (d = 0.08, CI −0.39 to 0.56, two scripts compared)
rows.change: Script one or two named activities, plan the teacher's rounds of the groups as part of it, and judge it by the individual check; a script that visibly changes the talk may leave learning unchanged (more in the [principle's script row](principles/collaborative-learning.md#fitting-the-design-to-a-situation))
rows.if: A computer-supported collaboration script is used

rows.basis: [Collaborative reflection beat a script for knowledge about collaboration](claims/reflection-scaffold-beats-script-collaboration-knowledge.md) [+M] (150 university students, laboratory); [gains concentrated on information-pooling interactions](claims/gains-limited-to-information-pooling-interactions.md) [~M] (exploratory)
rows.change: After a joint task, have the group reflect together, with prompts, on how it worked, rather than relying only on a script that steers the interaction; choose tasks that require the interactions you want learned, since knowledge gained concentrated on the ones the task required
rows.if: Collaboration itself is the objective (how to work well in a group)

rows.basis: [Aligned problem perceptions predict self-reported, not measured, outcomes](claims/homogeneous-problem-perceptions-predict-regulation-success.md) [~M]
rows.change: Keep the self-report, but choose the next activity from the individual check, not from it
rows.if: The group will report how well it worked

rows.basis: [Open collaboration with AI, offloading and lower independent thinking](claims/offloading-mediation-lower-independent-hot.md) [-W]
rows.change: Set limits on AI use in the joint task and make the individual check AI-free
rows.if: Generative AI is available to the group

rows.basis: [Human pairs reported the most collaboration and social presence](claims/human-pairing-highest-collaboration-social-presence.md) [+W] (self-reported perceptions, one programming quasi-experiment)
rows.change: Keep a human partner where the aim includes collaboration or social presence; if an AI assistant is used, still check each learner's own performance
rows.if: Pair work might be done with an AI assistant instead of a human partner

rows.basis: [Extensive reading with peer interaction gave larger gains](claims/er-peer-interaction-greater-achievement-gains.md) [+W]; [group activities are no guarantee when students have not read](claims/cl-not-magic-wand-for-er-motivation.md) [~W] (the author's caution)
rows.change: Add regular peer discussion of what each has read, and check that members are reading before relying on it
rows.if: A reading programme asks pupils to read independently

rows.basis: [Teacher-as-scribe co-construction gave five-year-olds authorship and long focused engagement](claims/co-construction-scribe-teacher-fosters-composition-autonomy.md) [+W] (one recorded session; engagement, not learning)
rows.change: Let the group compose aloud with the teacher as scribe, leaving the content and the judgement of when it is finished to the children
rows.if: Learners are too young to write, and the goal is composing a text

rows.basis: [Individual-then-joint gave better delayed recall](claims/ic-structure-better-recall-than-ci-and-individual.md) [+M]; [building a whole map gave better recall, most of all in that order](claims/self-constructed-cm-better-recall.md) [+M] (226 undergraduates, one experiment)
rows.change: Have each member build a whole map alone first, then build one together, rather than filling in or sorting a given map
rows.if: The task is building a concept map or diagram from a text

rows.basis: [Neurodivergent and neurotypical students prefer different team sizes](claims/nd-prefer-teams-of-3-to-5-nt-prefer-pairs.md) [~W]
rows.change: Offer a choice between pairs and teams of three to five, and ask each learner; this is evidence about comfort, not learning
rows.if: Learners include neurodivergent students and group size is open

rows.basis: Roles and prompts: untested proposal. Prior joint experience: [groups experienced with similar tasks outperformed inexperienced groups on individual and delayed tests](claims/zambrano-2019-experienced-groups-outperform-inexperienced.md) [+M]
rows.change: Give roles and a talk prompt from the first session rather than starting light; give the group a practice task of the same kind before the target task, and keep groups together across sessions
rows.if: Learners are young or new to group work, or groups are newly formed for a complex task

rows.basis: [Mastery learning improves outcomes](claims/mastery-learning-improves-outcomes.md) [+M]
rows.change: Put a criterion check, correction and parallel recheck on each competency, as in mastery learning
rows.if: Each competency should be gated on demonstrated performance

rows.basis: [Self-paced mastery programmes reduce course completion](claims/self-paced-mastery-programs-reduce-college-course-completion.md) [-M]; [Learner pacing helped on complex material only](claims/learner-paced-beats-system-paced-complex-material.md) [~M]
rows.change: Keep checkpoints or deadlines and monitor who stalls; self-paced mastery courses lost more students, and learner control in general showed almost no effect
rows.if: Learners will set their own pace (`online-self-paced`, adult or college)

rows.basis: [Personalized learning effects vary with fidelity](claims/personalized-learning-effects-vary-with-fidelity.md) [~M]
rows.change: Expect small first-year effects that depend on how fully the practices are put in place; monitor implementation, not only outcomes
rows.if: A whole school or programme adopting personalised, competency-based progression

rows.basis: [CBE gatekeeper completion lower than comparison](claims/cbe-gatekeeper-completion-lower-than-comparison.md) [-W]
