rows.change: Do not assume completion will rise; one evaluation found slightly lower gateway-course completion for CBE participants than for students in the same colleges' conventional online and campus programmes, and credential-completion differences that varied by college and may reflect who chose CBE (no effect size printed). Compare against a matched group and report by college
rows.if: A community-college credential programme

rows.basis: [The reform's science guide packed many expected learnings into few class hours](claims/ciencias-ii-guide-overloaded-sequences.md) [-W]; [monitoring reports found teacher training for the reform insufficient](claims/reform-teacher-training-insufficient.md) [-W]; [competency-based progression was the least implemented component where grade-level content and testing pressed](claims/competency-progression-limited-grade-level-emphasis.md) [~M]
rows.change: Count the competencies each block expects against its hours before rollout and trim or regroup where they do not fit; give teachers training in planning activities for the competencies, not only an induction session; monitor what is actually taught. Evidence is one analysis of one national secondary-science reform
rows.if: A national or system-wide curriculum recast as competencies or "expected learnings", taught by existing teachers on a fixed timetable

rows.basis: [Placement test precision declines above the 40th percentile](claims/cmi-ela-test-precision-declines-above-40th-percentile.md) [~W]
rows.change: Check that the test is precise around the cut that places learners, not only overall; one placement test lost precision above the 40th percentile
rows.if: A placement test decides where each learner starts

rows.basis: [Adaptive mastery testing reduces length and preserves decisions](claims/adaptive-mastery-testing-reduces-length-preserves-decisions.md) [~W]
rows.change: An adaptive mastery test can cut length while reaching the same pass/fail decision for almost all learners
rows.if: Checks need to be short and frequent

rows.basis: [Tension between mastery and curricular coverage](claims/adaptive-mastery-versus-coverage-tension-null-result.md) [-W]; [Pacing calendars seen as impediments to mastery](claims/pacing-calendars-standardized-assessments-impediments.md) [~W]
rows.change: Map which competencies the test covers and protect time for the later ones; slow mastery of early topics can leave later tested topics untaught
rows.if: Learners will also sit a state test or a time-bound exam

rows.basis: [Contingent scaffolding improves learning](claims/contingent-scaffolding-improves-learning.md) [~M]
rows.change: Make the support depend on the learner's last response rather than a fixed sequence of hints
rows.if: Support between attempts is given by a tutor

rows.basis: [Whole-task practice improves transfer, an untested argument](claims/whole-task-performance-improves-transfer.md) [~W]
rows.change: Add an integrated whole task and recheck it; a set of single-competency passes is not evidence of integrated performance
rows.if: The goal is a `complex-skill` built from several competencies

rows.basis: [Mastery improves engagement and lowers attrition](claims/mastery-improves-engagement-attrition.md) [+W]
rows.change: Keep the group pace with individual correction; attrition was lower in group-based mastery classes
rows.if: Group-paced class moving through competencies together

rows.basis: [Coaching raised 12-month retention](claims/insidetrack-coaching-potentially-positive-persistence.md) [+M] but [not 24-month degree completion](claims/insidetrack-coaching-no-discernible-attainment-effect.md) [~M]; [planning prompts raised online completion](claims/planning-prompts-increase-mooc-completion.md) [+M]; [commitment devices are mixed](claims/commitment-devices-mixed-effectiveness-education.md) [~M]; none tested inside a competency-based programme
rows.change: Have the mentor open with a planning contact in which the learner sets milestones per competency; trigger mentor outreach on a missed milestone or repeated failed attempts, not on calendar dates; plan coaching across terms and measure persistence each term. Follow [mentor support in self-paced online learning](patterns/mentor-support-in-self-paced-online-learning.md)
rows.if: Online, asynchronous, self-paced, with mentors available (`online-self-paced`)

rows.basis: [Effects larger for lower-aptitude students](claims/mastery-learning-effects-larger-for-lower-aptitude-students.md) [~M]; [CBE gateway-course completion slightly lower](claims/cbe-gatekeeper-completion-lower-than-comparison.md) [-W]
rows.change: Keep the criterion the same for all and vary time and support; place by performance, and give the least-prepared learners the most mentor contact early. Do not assume self-pacing suits everyone: the one programme evaluation's authors proposed offering CBE as one option among several
rows.if: Learners start with very different preparation (open admission, adults returning)

rows.basis: untested: the wiki has no claim on credit for prior learning or prior-learning assessment
rows.change: Credit a competency only on a performance (a parallel-form task or a portfolio scored against the criterion), not on years of experience or self-report
rows.if: Adults bring work experience they want credited

rows.basis: [Simulation with deliberate practice beat traditional clinical education](claims/simulation-based-education-with-deliberate-practice-improves-clinical-outcomes.md) [+M]; [simulation effects smallest for communication](claims/simulation-effects-vary-by-complex-skill.md) [~M]
rows.change: Gate procedural competencies in simulation with a mastery standard, feedback on each attempt and repetition; give communication competencies more attempts and a blinded rating with a human standardised patient; see [practice with simulated people](patterns/practice-with-simulated-people.md)
rows.if: Health professions programme (clinical, procedural and communication competencies)

rows.basis: [Preservice candidates passed performance assessments more often than interns](claims/preservice-candidates-outpass-interns-on-tpas.md) [~M]; [licensure exams failed candidates of colour more without predicting effectiveness](claims/licensure-exams-disparate-fail-rates-no-effectiveness-prediction.md) [-M]; [probing feedback with revise-and-resubmit](claims/probing-feedback-revise-resubmit-evidence.md) [~W]
rows.change: Treat the licensure performance assessment as one gate among several; add mentor feedback on evidence from the candidate's own students with revise-and-resubmit; check pass rates by route and group before relying on any single gate
rows.if: Teacher education (field placement, teaching performance assessment)

rows.basis: [IT CBE completers averaged under two terms to a first certification course](claims/cbe-fast-completion-two-terms-certification-four-terms-credentials.md) [~M]; [35 percent completed a programme](claims/cbe-participants-completion-employment-wages.md) [~M]; [online labs judged more effective with instructor scaffolds](claims/online-labs-better-with-instructor-scaffolds.md) [+W]
rows.change: Map competencies to certification objectives, expect a fast group and a long tail, and track gateway-course completion against a comparison; keep instructor or mentor scaffolds and probes in online labs
rows.if: Technology or IT programme aligned to industry certifications

rows.basis: [deliberate practice raised real-estate licensing pass rates](claims/deliberate-practice-raises-licensing-pass-rate.md) [+W] (self-selected groups); otherwise untested in business programmes in the wiki
rows.change: Assess decisions and their justification on a case or simulation scored to a rubric, and practise conversations with an AI or human role-play partner before a rated performance with a different person
rows.if: Business programme (analysis, decisions, client or team conversations)

rows.basis: [Tutoring systems beat non-individualised instruction](claims/adaptive-learning-improves-outcomes.md) [+S]; [unrestricted GPT-4 lowered unaided exam scores](claims/gpt-base-harms-unassisted-exam-performance.md) [-M]; [human tutors added to AI tutoring raised growth](claims/human-ai-tutoring-improves-map-growth-over-ai-only.md) [+M]
rows.change: Use the tutor between attempts, set it to withhold answers, and take the competency check without it; route repeated failure or answer-seeking to a mentor. Follow [AI tutoring](patterns/ai-tutoring.md)
rows.if: AI tutors give practice toward a competency assessment

rows.basis: [AI standardised-patient practice raised OSCE-aligned scores](claims/ma-scaffolding-improves-osce-exam-score.md) [+M]; certification by AI role-play alone is untested in the wiki
rows.change: Allow repeated low-stakes attempts with rubric feedback and a debrief, then certify on a rated performance with a different person
rows.if: AI role-play partners rehearse an interpersonal competency

rows.basis: [An LLM assessor agreed with human raters about as well as one human](claims/llm-assessor-agrees-with-human-raters-3e.md) [~M]; [raters differ in severity](claims/raters-differed-severity-mfrm.md) [~M]; [AI not yet best practice for competency assessment](claims/ai-not-best-practice-competency-based-assessment.md) [~W]
rows.change: Use AI scores for formative feedback; for the advancement decision, have a person confirm, double-score a sample, and compare AI and human scores by group
rows.if: An AI scores or comments on competency evidence

rows.basis: [In one platform, students on a third attempt met the criterion only 14 percent of the time](claims/espark-post-quiz-mastery-failure-rate.md) [~W]
rows.change: Change the support (a mentor session, a worked example, a smaller task) before another attempt, and record any promotion without the criterion as such
rows.if: A learner reaches the attempt limit without meeting the criterion

rows.basis: [Guided against unguided discovery](claims/minimal-guidance-less-effective-for-novices.md) [~S]; the meta-analysis does not break results down by prior knowledge
rows.change: Teach what the instances are first; keep two or three candidate attributes and give the checklist; use only clear exemplars until the rule is stable; give feedback on each classification and state the rule soon after the induction rather than waiting for the class to find it.
rows.if: Learners are `novice` in the domain (cannot yet name the parts of an instance)

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page
rows.change: Skip the induction; give the definition and go straight to near misses and borderline cases, or ask them to generate the contrasting set.
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` or already use the concept

rows.basis: [Guided against unguided discovery](claims/minimal-guidance-less-effective-for-novices.md) [~S]: 112 third- and fourth-graders learning the control-of-variables procedure; not a concept-attainment lesson
rows.change: Prefer direct instruction of the procedure with examples. Keep concept attainment for categories with visible attributes (animals, shapes).
rows.if: Learners are `child` (under 12) and the target is a procedure (e.g. a fair test)

rows.basis: [Interleaving labelled category exemplars](claims/interleaving-improves-inductive-learning.md) [~M]: benefit for paintings, photographs and mathematical tasks, reversed for word-based categories; learners' ages and settings not reported on the claim page
rows.change: Visual: after a short block of clear exemplars, mix labelled instances of the neighbouring concepts, and warn learners that practice will feel harder. Verbal: present each concept's examples together (blocked) before any mixing, keep near misses to one attribute and the labels visible. Test both on new instances.
rows.if: The concept's instances are visual or perceptual (artists' styles, rock types, skin lesions) with confusable neighbours, or verbal (word categories, sentence types such as metaphor)

rows.basis: [Rule-example sequence](claims/rule-example-sequence-efficient-rule-introduction.md) [~W] (a 1966 report of early programmed-instruction work, not a test); [the task-type argument](claims/task-type-moderates-induction-error-usefulness.md) [~W]
rows.change: State the rule, give examples, then incomplete examples to complete; use contrasting cases to compare methods.
rows.if: The target is a rule or procedure, not a category

rows.basis: [Comparing cases](claims/comparing-contrasting-cases-improves-learning.md) [~M]: with seventh-graders, comparing methods raised procedural knowledge and flexibility, not conceptual knowledge
rows.change: Score explanation of the attributes separately from classification, and add a self-generated non-example task.
rows.if: The outcome is conceptual explanation, not only classification

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: The system gives the yes/no label after the learner commits a written hypothesis; show the hypothesis history beside the items; end with a classification set with feedback and a stated definition.
rows.if: `online-self-paced`, no teacher

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page
rows.change: Use concept attainment for the one or two concepts learners most often confuse; teach the rest definition-first with examples and non-examples.
rows.if: `single-session` and many concepts in the unit

rows.basis: Untested proposal (the case-comparison benefit was smaller on delayed tests, which is a reason to test late, not evidence for this pattern)
rows.change: Test on new, unlabelled instances including near misses and neighbouring concepts, at the delay that matters; do not use the practice items.
rows.if: High stakes, or assessment on new instances weeks later

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page
rows.change: Use visual or concrete instances alongside verbal ones, keep labels visible, and allow written or pointing responses so working memory is not spent on the attribute list.
rows.if: Language of instruction is not the learners' first language, or learners have reading or access needs

rows.basis: [Practice presence](claims/practice-presence-raises-cbi-posttest-achievement.md) [+M] for including practice (undergraduates, one computer-based lesson); the per-outcome dose and exemplar are untested proposals
rows.change: Add a worked or modelled example and at least one practised attempt with feedback per outcome before the graded task; show an exemplar against the criteria.
rows.if: Learners are `novice` on the assessed tasks

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Fewer, more integrated outcomes; assess on a realistic task in their own setting; cut practice of components they already perform.
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` or professionals

rows.basis: [Assessment for learning](claims/assessment-for-learning-improves-achievement.md) [+M] for formative checkpoints (K–12 syntheses); the "I can" wording is untested; the earlier page described the pattern as developed in higher education
rows.change: Write outcomes as short "I can…" statements the teacher shares and checks with learners; keep frequent low-stakes checkpoints with a revision step.
rows.if: Learners are children or adolescents (`pre-k-12`)

rows.basis: [HOCS clickers](claims/hocs-clickers-improve-locs-exam-performance.md) [~M] (one nonmajors biology course, `controlled-nonrandom`)
rows.change: Do not restrict practice to recall: include some questions at a higher level (explain, apply) in class practice.
rows.if: Goal is facts or recall (`verbal-association`) and the assessment is recall

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page. Assessor agreement is qualified on [Competency-Based Assessment](principles/competency-based-assessment.md)
rows.change: Assess a whole task with criteria and calibrated assessors; schedule whole-task practice across the course, not only at the end.
rows.if: Goal is a `complex-skill`

rows.basis: Untested proposal; the motivation claim is under Further evidence
rows.change: Do not grade it on a scale; assess the behaviour it should produce, or report it ungraded; give learners bounded choices within the aligned tasks.
rows.if: Goal is an attitude or disposition (`attitude-motivation`)

rows.basis: [Practice presence](claims/practice-presence-raises-cbi-posttest-achievement.md) [+M] (computer-based lesson, undergraduates); the audit is untested
rows.change: Build practice with immediate feedback into each module ahead of its assessed task; make criteria and exemplars part of the module; audit automatically scored items for recall-only questions.
rows.if: Setting is `online-self-paced` with no teacher present

rows.basis: [Active learning](claims/active-learning-improves-exam-performance.md) [+M] (undergraduate STEM; held across class sizes); [HOCS clickers](claims/hocs-clickers-improve-locs-exam-performance.md) [~M]
rows.change: Replace part of lecture with questions or problems answered in class that demand the outcome; use some at a higher level than the exam.
rows.if: Large lecture class, one session at a time

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page ("a single aligned lesson inside a misaligned course changes little")
rows.change: Audit the whole course, then align the one unit's outcome with an assessed item that exists; do not promise a course-level effect.
rows.if: Only one session or unit can be changed

rows.basis: [Exam questions at low levels](claims/exam-questions-concentrate-lower-bloom-levels.md) [~W] shows one university's papers sat mostly at comprehension and knowledge (`associational`); the response is an untested proposal
rows.change: Keep the outcomes you hold; add labelled practice on the examination's format; check its items' levels and record where they fall below the outcomes.
rows.if: High-stakes final assessment fixed externally

rows.basis: [Group rewards on every member's individual learning](claims/cooperative-learning-group-rewards-and-individual-accountability.md) [+M]
rows.change: In step 3, compute the team's recognition from members' individual quiz results or improvement, and say so at the start
rows.if: School-age learners, a programme of four weeks or more

rows.basis: [Structured peer tutoring outperforms unstructured](claims/structured-peer-tutoring-outperforms-unstructured.md) [+M]
rows.change: Script the tutor and tutee roles and train them; structured programmes gave larger gains than unstructured ones
rows.if: The format is peer tutoring

rows.basis: [Peer tutoring and response groups for English language development](claims/peer-tutoring-response-groups-positive-eld-effects.md) [+M]
rows.change: Use peer tutoring and peer response groups for language development
rows.if: The learners are English learners developing the language

rows.basis: [Cross-age peer tutoring: no significant oral-proficiency effect](claims/cross-level-peer-tutoring-null-oral-proficiency.md) [~W]
rows.change: Do not rely on tutoring alone; three months of daily sessions showed no significant gain
rows.if: The goal is oral proficiency through cross-age tutoring over a few months

rows.basis: [Secondary studies: STAD most, Jigsaw least successful](claims/secondary-cooperative-learning-newmann-thompson.md) [~W]
rows.change: Add an individual quiz that counts for the home team
rows.if: The structure chosen is jigsaw

rows.basis: [Interdependence type shifted the kind of interaction](claims/interdependence-type-shifts-interaction-nature.md) [~W]; [Structuring interdependence did not change achievement online](claims/interdependence-type-no-achievement-effect-asynchronous.md) [~M]
rows.change: Use roles in step 4 to organise the process; expect reward-only groups to drift off task; do not expect either to raise achievement
rows.if: Groups are asynchronous online

rows.basis: [Large groups limited individual participation](claims/large-group-size-limited-participation-confidence.md) [~W]
rows.change: Use groups of three or four, or rotate the roles across steps
rows.if: Lab groups of four or five share one procedure

rows.basis: [Poor group leaders undermined discussion](claims/cooperative-conceptual-change-chemistry-misconceptions.md) [~W]
rows.change: Train leaders to elicit each member's answer before the group settles one
rows.if: Student group leaders will run the discussion

rows.basis: [Neurodivergent and neurotypical students prefer different team sizes](claims/nd-prefer-teams-of-3-to-5-nt-prefer-pairs.md) [~W]
rows.change: Ask each learner's preferred group size; neurodivergent students in one survey were most comfortable in teams of three to five
rows.if: Learners include neurodivergent students

rows.basis: [A threefold staff development plan supported implementation](claims/threefold-cooperative-learning-staff-development-plan.md) [+W]
rows.change: Plan staff development with immersion sessions, peer observation and shared scripts before launch
rows.if: Instructors are new to cooperative structures

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Use a short structure (individual answer, pair discussion, individual re-answer) and skip the group reward
rows.if: One short session with no later unit

rows.basis: [Argumentation improves reasoning](claims/argumentation-improves-reasoning.md) [~M]
rows.change: After the round, have each learner write an argument on a new question; dialogic peer argumentation transferred to individual essays on new topics
rows.if: The target is learners' individual written argument

rows.basis: [Argumentation improves reasoning](claims/argumentation-improves-reasoning.md) [~M]
rows.change: Run repeated peer argument exchanges across months, not a single round; the transfer recorded came from a multiyear programme
rows.if: Learners are young adolescents and argument skill is a goal for the year

rows.basis: [Argument prompts and scaffolds produce knowledge gains](claims/argumentation-prompts-scaffolds-knowledge-gains.md) [+W]
rows.change: Give prompts that make them paraphrase the other side, criticise it, ask questions and synthesise, before and during the round
rows.if: Learners are new to arguing

rows.basis: [Parliamentary rules ban evidence and omit cross-examination](claims/parliamentary-rules-ban-evidence-and-omit-cross-examination.md) [-W]
rows.change: Allow cited evidence and add a cross-examination or question period, so research and evidence use stay part of the task
rows.if: The format bans published evidence or has no questioning period

rows.basis: [Unconstrained topic writing yields frivolous resolutions](claims/unconstrained-topic-writing-yields-frivolous-resolutions.md) [~W]
rows.change: Check each resolution supports competing, evidence-bearing claims; drop joke or one-sided topics
rows.if: Learners or the instructor write the resolutions freely

rows.basis: [Some discussion approaches improve comprehension](claims/structured-discussion-methods-improve-comprehension.md) [~M]
rows.change: Score reasoning and use of evidence, and collect an individual written position; more talk alone did not raise comprehension
rows.if: Participation or speaking time is how the activity will be assessed

rows.basis: [Considering the opposite reduces bias](claims/considering-the-opposite-reduces-bias.md) [~W]
rows.change: In the debrief, ask each learner what makes the opposing case strongest, or reverse sides for a second round
rows.if: The goal is perspective-taking or less one-sided judgement

rows.basis: [Collaborative argumentation benefits](claims/collaborative-argumentation-benefits-summary.md) [+W]
rows.change: Keep the collaborative argument but drop the win/lose judging, as in Structured Academic Controversy
rows.if: The goal is motivation or content learning, not debating skill

rows.basis: [Argumentation improves reasoning](claims/argumentation-improves-reasoning.md) [~M]
rows.change: Run the argument in a threaded forum or shared document with turn deadlines and scaffolding prompts
rows.if: The class is online or asynchronous

rows.basis: [Argumentation implementation challenges](claims/argumentation-implementation-challenges.md) [~W]
rows.change: Plan the preparation and debrief time up front, or run a shorter round on a topic already in the syllabus; time and curriculum fit are the commonest reported barriers
rows.if: Class time is short and the curriculum is full

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Switch to a synthesis format, or reframe the question so it does not ask anyone to argue against their own group
rows.if: The topic is personally charged for some learners

rows.basis: [Explicit instruction against unassisted discovery](claims/minimal-guidance-less-effective-for-novices.md) [+S]; the meta-analysis does not break results down by prior knowledge
rows.change: Keep steps 2–3 in full: explain first, two or three worked cases with explanation prompts and sentence starters before any case learners work alone; give hints in response to their explanations.
rows.if: Learners are `novice` on this idea

rows.basis: [Expertise reversal](claims/expertise-reversal-effect.md) [~M] (a review of cognitive-load studies; gives no crossover point)
rows.change: Skip the worked cases; go to boundary cases, comparison with a neighbouring idea, and use in a richer task, with selective feedback.
rows.if: Learners are `advanced`, or explain the idea correctly at step 1

rows.basis: [Misconceptions and refutation](claims/misconceptions-interfere-with-new-learning.md) [+M]; science and reading education, read from abstracts
rows.change: Make step 2 a refutation: state the wrong idea, show a case where it fails, explain why the correct idea succeeds; return to the discrepant case in later sessions and check at a delay.
rows.if: Learners hold a known, confident misconception (common in science: force and motion, seasons, heat)

rows.basis: Untested proposal; the self-explanation meta-analysis spans levels of education but the claim page does not report results by age
rows.change: Keep explanation prompts short and oral or pointing-based; use concrete, visible cases; check each child's prediction individually rather than by show of hands.
rows.if: Learners are `child` (under 12)

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page's scope ("not sufficient for highly complex skills alone")
rows.change: Use the [Direct Instruction pattern](patterns/direct-instruction.md) or [Guided Practice](principles/guided-practice.md) instead; keep one explanation prompt per worked case at most.
rows.if: The goal is a `procedure` the learner must carry out fluently, not an idea to explain

rows.basis: [Whole-task practice](claims/whole-task-performance-improves-transfer.md) [~M] (a design argument, not a study)
rows.change: Embed the idea in a whole task from the start rather than teaching it as a separate lesson first.
rows.if: The goal is a `complex-skill` performed as a whole

rows.basis: [Comparing cases](claims/comparing-contrasting-cases-improves-learning.md) [+M]; larger effects when learners look for similarities and the principle comes after, smaller on delayed tests
rows.change: Use at least two representations and two surface-different cases; in step 5, ask learners to say what the cases share before the principle is restated.
rows.if: The outcome is transfer to new contexts

rows.basis: [Practice present in a computer-based lesson](claims/practice-presence-raises-cbi-posttest-achievement.md) [+M] (undergraduates, one lesson, horizon not reported); the explanation-comparison step is untested
rows.change: Make every prompt require a typed explanation before the next screen; give worked explanations to compare against; include automatically checked prediction items with feedback; end with an unseen changed item.
rows.if: `online-self-paced`, no teacher

rows.basis: Untested proposal; [contingent support](claims/contingent-scaffolding-improves-learning.md) [~M] is shown one-to-one, and its classroom-scale effect is not
rows.change: Collect step 1 predictions and step 4 checks from every learner at once (cards, mini-whiteboards, a poll); address the commonest wrong idea with the whole class, then go to those still wrong.
rows.if: `classroom` with one teacher and a large group

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Run the five steps once, keep step 5 to one comparison, and record that understanding at a delay was not checked.
rows.if: `single-session` only

rows.basis: Untested proposal; the self-explanation claim notes that evidence for delayed gains is much more limited
rows.change: Judge readiness on an unseen changed item answered unaided, not on explanations given with prompts; add the delayed check.
rows.if: High stakes, or the test is weeks away

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page's guidance to vary representation and complexity
rows.change: Let learners predict and explain orally, by drawing or by choosing between given reasons before writing them; keep the representation visual; gloss terms the objective does not include.
rows.if: Instruction is in the learners' second language, or literacy is low

rows.basis: [Minimal guidance is less effective for novices](claims/minimal-guidance-less-effective-for-novices.md) [+S]
rows.change: Run the full sequence: brief elicitation, explanation and model, guided practice with checks, then hand over
rows.if: Learners cannot start the target task

rows.basis: [Worked examples' advantage over unassisted discovery](claims/worked-examples-largest-advantage-over-unassisted-discovery.md) [+M]
rows.change: Use worked examples as the model and build feedback into the guided items; worked examples beat unassisted discovery by more than direct teaching did
rows.if: `online-self-paced`, with no teacher to respond in the moment

rows.basis: [Productive failure improves conceptual learning](claims/productive-failure-improves-conceptual-learning.md) [~S]
rows.change: Put a short designed problem attempt before step 2 (the explanation), then teach the method and contrast it with their attempts
rows.if: Older learners and a conceptual or transfer objective

rows.basis: [Productive failure improves conceptual learning](claims/productive-failure-improves-conceptual-learning.md) [+S]
rows.change: Keep instruction first and keep the opening elicitation brief
rows.if: A procedure, or second to fifth graders

rows.basis: [Expertise reversal effect](claims/expertise-reversal-effect.md) [~S]
rows.change: Route them past the full explanation to varied or changed items; recheck later
rows.if: Some learners pass the opening elicitation and explain it

rows.basis: [Teacher-guided inquiry outperforms student-led](claims/teacher-guided-inquiry-outperforms-student-led.md) [+S]; [Guidance improves inquiry learning outcomes](claims/guidance-improves-inquiry-learning-outcomes.md) [+M]
rows.change: Keep the teacher leading the inquiry steps and add prompts and feedback rather than switching to lecture
rows.if: The design is inquiry-based (science lab, investigation)

rows.basis: [Domain moderates the unassisted-discovery deficit](claims/domain-moderates-unassisted-discovery-deficit.md) [+M]; [Explicit strategy instruction with short stories improves EFL reading comprehension](claims/explicit-strategy-instruction-short-stories-improve-efl-reading-comprehension.md) [+M] (one quasi-experiment, university EFL)
rows.change: Give explicit explanation and modelling priority; the deficit of unassisted discovery was largest in that domain. For reading-comprehension strategies, name and model one strategy at a time on short texts, then guide practice on new texts over several weeks
rows.if: The target is a verbal or social skill (discussion moves, reading strategies, interpersonal routines)

rows.basis: [Explicit grammar teaching outperforms implicit, for simple rules too](claims/explicit-teaching-complex-rules-only-advantage.md) [+S]; [Instructed learners outperform others on simple rules](claims/instructed-learners-outperform-others-simple-rules.md) [+M]; [Explicit teaching effective but not durable](claims/explicit-teaching-effective-but-not-durable.md) [~M]
rows.change: State and model the rule explicitly whatever its complexity, then reuse it in later communicative tasks and check it on a delayed test with new items, because durability is not established
rows.if: A second-language grammar target, simple or complex

rows.basis: [Active learning improves exam performance](claims/active-learning-improves-exam-performance.md) [+S]
rows.change: Keep the explanation short and give a large share of class time to guided practice with checks (problems, questions, discussion); a light sprinkling of activity is not what narrowed gaps
rows.if: Undergraduate lecture course, possibly large

rows.basis: [Flexible and scripted first-grade interventions both effective](claims/flexible-and-scripted-first-grade-interventions-both-effective.md) [+M] (one experiment, reported in a review; no difference between the two programmes is reported)
rows.change: Keep it explicit and practice-rich; a teacher able to adapt to diagnostic data can use a flexible programme, since a flexible and a fully scripted programme both beat typical practice. Script where teacher expertise is thin
rows.if: Struggling early readers in a small-group intervention

rows.basis: [Mastery learning improves outcomes](claims/mastery-learning-improves-outcomes.md) [+M]; [Self-paced mastery reduces course completion](claims/self-paced-mastery-programs-reduce-college-course-completion.md) [~M]
rows.change: Add a mastery check before each new unit and plan for extra time; in self-paced college courses, watch completion
rows.if: Learners may move on only after showing mastery

rows.basis: [Instruction effect peaks then diminishes](claims/instruction-positive-effect-peaks-then-diminishes.md) [~M]
rows.change: Schedule later practice and a delayed check with new items; do not judge the lesson on the immediate check
rows.if: The outcome is checked at the end of term, not the end of the lesson

rows.basis: [Lower adherence to scaffolding than to scripted components](claims/scaffolding-lower-adherence-than-scripted-components.md) [~M]
rows.change: Expect the responsive parts (prompting, adjusting support) to be delivered less faithfully than the scripted parts; train and observe those parts
rows.if: Many teachers will deliver the lesson from a script

rows.basis: [Direct Instruction gains depend on implementation support](claims/direct-instruction-gains-depend-on-implementation-support.md) [~M]
rows.change: Budget for training and coaching; gains appeared only where the programme was fully supported
rows.if: A school is adopting a scripted Direct Instruction programme

rows.basis: [ITIP lacks empirical evidence of improved achievement](claims/itip-lacks-empirical-evidence-achievement.md) [~M] (a review reported second-hand in an ERIC monograph)
rows.change: Judge it by student outcomes on the agreed instrument, not by teachers adopting the lesson format; the widely implemented ITIP model was found to lack evidence of raised achievement under typical school conditions
rows.if: A district trains all teachers in an explicit-lesson model (Hunter-style staff development)

rows.basis: [Isolated parts first, for novices](claims/part-task-practice-reduces-load-for-novices.md) [~M] (one experiment; sample and horizon not reported on the claim page)
rows.change: Keep the epitome very short (two or three ideas); pre-teach the one or two elements it depends on in isolation, then present the epitome; make each level small and end it with a learner-built synthesis.
rows.if: Learners are `novice` and the content is `high` in element interactivity

rows.basis: untested proposal; [advance organizers](claims/advance-organizers-improve-learning.md) [~M] found no special benefit for low-knowledge learners, so neither direction of an expertise effect is established for overviews
rows.change: Replace the epitome with the elicitation sketch; start at the first level they cannot explain; drop syntheses they can already produce.
rows.if: Learners are `intermediate` or `advanced` for this content

rows.basis: [Hierarchical organisation did not help low-ability students](claims/ability-moderates-hierarchical-organization-benefit.md) [~M] (college physics volunteers; untested in other groups)
rows.change: Do not rely on the hierarchy alone: add learner-built syntheses at every level, practice tasks at each level, and a check on the top-level ideas before moving down.
rows.if: Learners have weaker prior attainment in the subject

rows.basis: untested proposal; the study tested college and advanced high-school physics students, untested with children
rows.change: Make the epitome concrete (a picture, a story or a model of the whole), keep levels to one lesson each, and have the teacher lead the synthesis aloud before asking learners to arrange items.
rows.if: Learners are `child` or `adolescent`

rows.basis: [No detected effect on tasks resting on single details](claims/no-organization-effect-on-local-tasks.md) [~M] (a non-significant difference, not equivalence)
rows.change: Do not build an elaboration sequence; use a plain grouping and retrieval practice instead.
rows.if: The goal is `verbal-association` (facts, vocabulary, names)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Sequence whole tasks with [4C/ID](patterns/4cid-four-component-instructional-design.md) and use an elaboration sequence only for the supportive information around them.
rows.if: The goal is a `complex-skill` (whole-task performance)

rows.basis: [Organisation–task match](claims/organization-task-match-determines-benefit.md) [~M] (20 high-school physics students, two-week test)
rows.change: Put the ideas that task draws on at the top of the epitome and at the top of each synthesis; assess a matched task, not a recall of the outline.
rows.if: Assessment is high-stakes and uses one kind of task (e.g. deductive problems, or historical and contextual questions)

rows.basis: [Learners explicating the organisation](claims/strong-acquisition-tasks-improve-internalization.md) [+M] for the synthesis activity (same 20-student high-school experiment; untested online); the persistent map is an untested proposal
rows.change: Keep the epitome as a persistent map on every page, with the current level highlighted; make each synthesis an activity the system checks (arrange items into the map, mark the new detail), not a passage to read.
rows.if: `online-self-paced`, no teacher present

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Present the epitome and one level of elaboration only, end with one synthesis task and one application task; leave further levels for later sessions rather than compressing them.
rows.if: Time is one session (`single-session`) rather than a unit or course

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: State the epitome in short sentences with a labelled diagram; keep the same terms for the same ideas at every level; offer the synthesis as an arrange-or-label task rather than a written summary.
rows.if: Some learners study in a second language, or need accessible formats

rows.basis: [Guided play](claims/play-based-learning-improves-outcomes.md) [~M]: early-childhood meta-analysis, guided play ahead of direct instruction on early maths, shape knowledge and task switching and of free play on spatial vocabulary, no reliable difference on most outcomes; guided play, not emergent curriculum
rows.change: Use the full sequence: teacher-chosen entry points, daily observation notes, webbing with the children, threads of one to four weeks, and an adult in the activity guiding it toward the webbed ideas (asking, modelling, supplying tools) rather than leaving it as free play.
rows.if: Learners are `child` (preschool to early primary)

rows.basis: [Unassisted discovery](claims/minimal-guidance-less-effective-for-novices.md) [~S]: 5 distinct studies in its table; carried from discovery and inquiry tasks to an interest-led thread
rows.change: Keep the topic theirs but teach the content inside it explicitly: short demonstrations, worked examples or a visitor's explanation at the point learners need them, with feedback on what they make.
rows.if: Learners are `novice` on the content the thread leads into

rows.basis: Untested; the earlier page's high-school example
rows.change: Use the research-question route: two or three sessions to turn personal interests into investigable questions, then weeks of formal study with a stated method and a seminar or presentation. Map each question to the required outcomes before it is approved.
rows.if: Learners are `adolescent` or `adult` in a standards-driven course

rows.basis: [Co-design tools](claims/co-design-tools-support-balancing-standards-and-student-interests.md) [+M]: one teacher-researcher co-design team, self-report; teachers designing units, not learners' outcomes
rows.change: Draw the web with the standards beside it: mark which branch reaches which outcome, and steer between branches rather than abandoning the thread; cover what no branch reaches in short planned lessons. Collect learners' interests by more than one route (a short survey plus conversation), since question wording can change which learners rate a topic highly.
rows.if: Required standards or a fixed syllabus must be covered

rows.basis: [Interest-personalized problems](claims/personalization-improves-hard-kc-accuracy-algebra-its.md) [+M]: one randomised study, 145 ninth-grade Algebra I students in an intelligent tutor, better accuracy on hard expression-writing steps within one unit
rows.change: Keep the content fixed and let interests supply the contexts: write or choose problems and texts set in what learners said they care about. This is interest-based context, not emergent topic.
rows.if: The goal is a fixed skill (algebra expressions, decoding) and the topic cannot move

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Keep one shared record of questions and the web (a shared document or photo of the web board) that remote learners add to; give remote learners a branch they can pursue with what they have at home (photographs, interviews, local observation) and a slot to report back.
rows.if: Mixed modes: some learners join remotely while others are in the room, or learners are phone-only

rows.basis: Untested; the earlier page notes that webbing works best with more than one adult present
rows.change: Observe a different small group each day (four or five learners), so each learner is noted at least weekly; run one thread for the whole class with two or three branches rather than many threads; web with the class, not alone after hours.
rows.if: One teacher for many learners, no assistant

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Cut observation to one question per check-in ("what are you trying to find out?") written on a shared sheet; let learners keep their own question log; review the sheet once a week to choose the next branch.
rows.if: Scarce facilitator time (volunteers, a busy shift, one tutor checking in briefly)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Do not run an emergent curriculum; use the moves inside the plan: 5 minutes to collect questions about the entry point, 30 minutes on the activity with the class's chosen question as its focus, 10 minutes to share what was found and record questions for later.
rows.if: A single session only, or a fixed short time budget (for example 45 minutes)

rows.basis: Untested; [unassisted discovery](claims/minimal-guidance-less-effective-for-novices.md) [~S] for the guidance change only
rows.change: Keep it, and record interest and webbing in its categories; change only what the evidence says matters: an adult guiding the thread toward named ideas, and a check that the required content is reached. Use the brief's own rubric to judge the closing product.
rows.if: The brief names its own routine for observation, planning or assessment (its own record sheet, planning cycle, rubric or report categories)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Accept interest shown in talk, drawing, building and pointing, not only in written questions; write learners' questions down for them; use visual and concrete materials and visitors; keep the web pictorial.
rows.if: Learners with low confidence or literacy, or the language of instruction is not their first language

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Let the thread start from a problem or incident from their own work; keep it to sessions that fit the shift; close it on something usable at work (a revised procedure, a job aid in their own terms).
rows.if: Adults in a work setting

rows.basis: Untested proposal; [choice-rich infrastructure](claims/choice-rich-infrastructure-supports-productive-deviation-and-learning.md) [+M] describes two students whose games were shared publicly, one extreme case
rows.change: Agree the audience with the learners early; keep the product whole and in the learners' own form; rehearse once; the audience sees the product, not the teacher's notes.
rows.if: The thread ends in a product or performance for a real audience (families, another class, the public)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Let the learner decide whether the interest goes on the shared web; offer a private branch they pursue with the teacher, and keep notes about it out of displays.
rows.if: Private or sensitive interests (family events, identity, health)

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page's rationale
rows.change: Ask families what they would like the child to learn and add those topics as entry points; record where learners' interests and families' expectations diverge rather than resolving it for them.
rows.if: Learners or families hold expectations about what matters to learn that differ from the school's

rows.basis: Untested; [the low-income-schools argument](claims/low-income-schools-test-prep-crowds-out-interest-activities.md) [~W] is a theoretical commentary that such schools have the fewest resources for interest-driven activity, not a test of any design
rows.change: Ring-fence a small regular block (for example two 45-minute sessions a week) for the thread rather than abandoning it; use free materials and local visitors.
rows.if: A low-resourced school under heavy test pressure

rows.basis: [Autonomy support](claims/autonomy-supports-intrinsic-motivation.md) [+S]: 8 distinct studies in its table, including a meta-analysis of 128 experiments in which expected tangible rewards undermined intrinsic motivation for interesting tasks; carried to emergent threads untested
rows.change: Remove expected rewards for joining the thread; give informational feedback on what learners found and made.
rows.if: Rewards, points or grades attached to taking part

rows.basis: [Guided against unguided discovery](claims/minimal-guidance-less-effective-for-novices.md) [~S], carried from classroom and laboratory studies to games
rows.change: Open each session with a mentor modelling one decision aloud; one decision type per early session; feedback with the reason after every decision; fade prompts only when a learner justifies unprompted.
rows.if: Learners are `novice` to the practice

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page's "transformation" games
rows.change: Skip the early modelled sessions; build the unit around two or three atypical or breakdown cases; debrief on what their usual framing missed.
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` practitioners (continuing education, in-service)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Choose a practice whose decisions are visible and concrete (planning a park, running a shop); shorten sessions to 30–40 minutes; keep an adult in the mentor role; check the content separately.
rows.if: Learners are `child` or young `adolescent`

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page's constraint ("overkill for simple factual or procedural learning")
rows.change: Do not build an epistemic game; teach directly with practice and feedback, and use a short simulation only for applying it.
rows.if: The goal is facts or a procedure, not judgement

rows.basis: [Simulation training in the health professions](claims/simulation-based-education-improves-outcomes.md) [+M] (against no training); [practice-near content](claims/contextualized-teaching-facilitates-transfer.md) [+W] (nurses' perceptions)
rows.change: Use cases drawn from the learners' own workplace, a practitioner as mentor, and an outside-game task that matches a real work task; record transfer to work separately from in-game performance.
rows.if: `adult-workplace` learners in `workplace-clinical` training

rows.basis: Untested proposal; [feedback](claims/feedback-improves-learning.md) [+S] carried to software feedback
rows.change: Mentor characters must carry all guidance: a modelled decision before each new decision type, required written justification, scripted feedback with reasons, and a written debrief prompt at the end of each session. Expect weaker debriefs than with a person.
rows.if: `online-self-paced`, no teacher

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Keep the world playable in a browser on a phone (documents and decisions as text and images, no heavy 3D); give remote learners a named role with their own documents so the team must consult them; run the debrief in a shared document everyone writes in.
rows.if: Mixed mode: some learners in the room, some joining remotely, or phone-only

rows.basis: Untested proposal; the earlier page's role differentiation
rows.change: Run in teams of four with differentiated roles (departments); the teacher plays one mentor character for the whole class at set points, and teams check decisions against a written checklist from the epistemography between visits.
rows.if: One teacher or practitioner for many learners (30 or more)

rows.basis: Untested proposal; [Communities of Practice](principles/communities-of-practice.md) notes norms take a term to form
rows.change: Drop the full game: one case, one role, a modelled decision, one learner decision with feedback, and a 15-minute debrief on the frame. Do not expect a change in identity from one session.
rows.if: `single-session` only (one workshop)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Give the world's documents as short texts with audio and images; start with low-stakes decisions whose consequences can be undone; let learners justify orally or by choosing among stated reasons.
rows.if: Learners with low confidence or low literacy

rows.basis: Untested here; see [Authentic Assessment](patterns/authentic-assessment.md) and [Authentic Audiences and Purposes](principles/authentic-audiences-purposes.md)
rows.change: Keep the fiction's audience real: practitioners or residents read the final plan and respond; share their criteria at the brief; build a draft-review-revise step before the presentation.
rows.if: The final product goes to a real audience (a council, a client, a community group)

rows.basis: [Reliability is hard to define in epistemic games](claims/reliability-challenges-epistemic-games.md) [~W] (an argument); [longer play separated simulated learner types better](claims/longer-games-sharpen-wd-learner-differentiation.md) [~W] (simulated learners, not real ones)
rows.change: Grade the final product and an outside-game case against public criteria with two raters, not the play log; if the log is scored, play long enough to accumulate evidence and keep few, broad dimensions.
rows.if: The game will be used for high-stakes grading

rows.basis: [Disciplinary differences went unnoticed](claims/epistemic-games-reveal-unacknowledged-disciplinary-differences-in-teams.md) [~W]; [a shared outline turned unfocused talk into structured work](claims/organization-simulation-knowledge-practices-support-interdisciplinary-learning.md) [+W]; both descriptive, neither tests the move
rows.change: Ask each member at the start to state what evidence would convince them and when a framing is "done"; revisit it in the debrief; give the team a shared visible plan (flip chart, board).
rows.if: Interdisciplinary teams

rows.basis: Untested proposal; [the simulation synthesis](claims/simulation-based-education-improves-outcomes.md) [+M] found no consistent design feature, and fidelity was not among those it recorded
rows.change: Use a paper or document-based simulation (briefs, letters, maps, a budget sheet) with a teacher in role, rather than software; spend the budget on the epistemography.
rows.if: Little budget or time to build a world

rows.basis: [Activation](claims/activation-improves-learning.md) [~S] and [activation instructions](claims/prior-knowledge-activation-little-effect-on-retention.md) [~M]: topic activation alone did not help (primary pupils; one other experiment), carried to this routine
rows.change: Give the meaning of key terms and the gist first; make step 2 a checked account (compare with the text) rather than free recall; give a stem for every step for longer (sessions 1–5); correct each "learned" answer against the named idea.
rows.if: Learners are `novice` in the content, or the text is hard for them

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Make steps 2 and 3 implicit; spend the time on step 5, with learners generating questions and choosing the next source to answer them.
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` in the content

rows.basis: [Writing to learn](claims/writing-to-learn-improves-understanding.md) [~S]: effects were reduced in grades 6–8 and with longer assignments (a moderator in one meta-analysis, read from its abstract)
rows.change: Keep writing short (one or two sentences per step), answer steps 2 and 3 orally, and write only step 4.
rows.if: Learners are in grades 6–8, or young `child` writers

rows.basis: [Specific reflection prompts](claims/reflective-practice-improves-outcomes-when-structured.md) [+S] (engineering undergraduates; school writing-to-learn studies)
rows.change: Write a content-specific step 4 prompt for each session and score the answer against the named idea; keep the number of reflections constant rather than adding more.
rows.if: The goal is understanding of a `concept` or `principle` in a course

rows.basis: [Self-questioning](claims/self-questioning-improves-comprehension.md) [+S] (K–12 reading; reviews read from abstracts)
rows.change: Teach step 5 as question generation during reading as well as after it: model it, give stems, fade them.
rows.if: The goal is reading comprehension of content texts

rows.basis: Untested; the source's structured-discussion vocabulary routine ([strategy page](strategies/structured-discussion-vocabulary-anchoring.md))
rows.change: For each new term, give the meaning and an example first, then ask "What experiences, thoughts or associations do you have with this term that might help you remember it?"; learners record the dictionary meaning and a personal association.
rows.if: The goal is vocabulary

rows.basis: [Task value](claims/task-value-increases-motivation-and-engagement.md) [+M]: brief utility-value writing raised engagement and grades (two reviews); a separate intervention, carried to this step
rows.change: Weight step 3 towards usefulness: "How could this matter to you or to people you know?", two sentences, ungraded.
rows.if: Learners see no point in the content, or are from groups underrepresented in the subject

rows.basis: [Specific reflection prompts](claims/reflective-practice-improves-outcomes-when-structured.md) [+S] and [guided reflection](claims/guided-reflection-yields-more-higher-order-paragraphs-than-free.md) [+M], carried from undergraduates and graduate students to workplace learners
rows.change: Use a recent work incident or case as the experience; make step 4 a statement of what they would do differently and why; make step 5 a question to take to a colleague or the next shift.
rows.if: Adults in work settings (`adult-workplace`, `workplace-clinical`)

rows.basis: [Metacognitive prompts](claims/metacognitive-prompts-improve-learning.md) [+S]: in computer-based environments prompts helped, more so with feedback, task-specific and adaptive (meta-analysis read from its abstract)
rows.change: Embed the four prompts after each segment; after the learner commits a step 4 answer, show a model answer and ask them to mark what they missed; adapt the stem to the content of the segment.
rows.if: `online-self-paced`, no teacher

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Take every written answer in one shared channel (a shared document or chat) so remote and in-room answers are seen together; keep phone answers to one or two sentences; let remote learners answer step 3 privately.
rows.if: Mixed modes: some learners remote, some in the room, or phone-only

rows.basis: Untested; the "why did you choose this correct answer" move is the source's ([strategy page](strategies/question-correct-answers-not-errors.md))
rows.change: Have learners write steps 4 and 5; the facilitator reads a sample of five step 4 answers and responds to the whole group, asking one learner why a correct answer is correct; pairs check each other's answer against a model answer.
rows.if: One teacher for many learners, or scarce facilitator time (volunteers, a busy shift, a tutor checking in briefly)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Run one cycle on one experience; end with each learner's step 5 question written on an exit card and answered in a short follow-up message or handout.
rows.if: `single-session` only

rows.basis: Untested; from the source's precepts (students fail from too little information; the teacher as a model of language and inquiry)
rows.change: Answer steps 2 and 3 orally in pairs or in the first language; give a sentence frame for step 4; respond first to what is right in an answer; never read personal responses aloud without consent.
rows.if: Learners with low confidence or low literacy in the language of instruction

rows.basis: [Specific reflection prompts](claims/reflective-practice-improves-outcomes-when-structured.md) [+S], on prompt specificity, not on any named routine
rows.change: Keep it. Change only what the evidence says matters: make sure one item asks for the content idea with a content-specific prompt and is checked, and that one item asks what more needs to be known.
rows.if: The brief names its own routine for this (a KWL chart, "What? So what? Now what?", a journal template)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Turn step 4 answers into a short public explanation for that audience, written after the content check, and step 5 questions into the questions the product sets out to answer.
rows.if: The answers feed a product or performance for a real audience

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Score the step 4 answer against the content idea separately from the personal response; retest the idea on a new example after a delay; do not grade step 3.
rows.if: High stakes, or understanding must hold weeks later

rows.basis: [Guided against unassisted discovery](claims/minimal-guidance-less-effective-for-novices.md) [~S]; discovery tasks with mostly school learners and mixed domains, not placements or simulations; the meta-analysis does not break results down by prior knowledge
rows.change: Demonstrate the first loop's task with a worked example before the experience; let one or two variables vary; supply the debrief prompts and the vocabulary for stating the principle; check each learner's rule before the retry; keep this support for at least the first two loops.
rows.if: Learners are `novice` on the target task

rows.basis: Untested; the guided-discovery claim's narrative review argues the advantage of guidance recedes with prior knowledge, which no recorded study tests here
rows.change: Skip the demonstration; make the first experience ill-structured; have learners write their own debrief questions from the first loop; keep the changed attempt with feedback.
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` or experienced practitioners

rows.basis: [Hands-on learning](claims/manipulatives-improve-math-learning.md) [+M] (mathematics manipulatives, kindergarten to college); [guided against unassisted discovery](claims/minimal-guidance-less-effective-for-novices.md) [~S] (third and fourth graders learning a procedure); loop lengths untested
rows.change: Shorter loops (experience 10–15 minutes, debrief 5 minutes); concrete materials linked to the written or symbolic form in the same session; tell them what to try rather than only to explore; the teacher states the rule.
rows.if: Learners are `child`ren (under 12)

rows.basis: [Simulation with deliberate practice](claims/simulation-based-education-with-deliberate-practice-improves-clinical-outcomes.md) [+M]; medical education, procedural skills only
rows.change: Run the experience as simulated practice repeated to a stated mastery standard, feedback after each attempt, rising difficulty, then a debrief; move to the real setting only when the standard is met.
rows.if: `workplace-clinical`, a `procedure` or psychomotor skill

rows.basis: [Physical experience](claims/physical-experience-enhances-science-learning.md) [~M] (undergraduate physics; physical and virtual manipulation equally effective); [cognitive conflict](claims/cognitive-disequilibrium-motivates-conceptual-change.md) [+M] (science-education conceptual-change strategies)
rows.change: Make the experience a predict-then-manipulate task (physical or virtual), with a stated prediction before acting, and map the result onto the formula or diagram during the principle step; use a virtual lab when a physical one is not available.
rows.if: The goal is a science or mathematics `concept`

rows.basis: [Experiential learning benefits reported in human services education](claims/experiential-learning-engagement-skills-ethical-reasoning.md) [+W], second-hand, no design or effect size; otherwise untested
rows.change: Use cases or placements with structured debriefs; assess a decision on a new case observed later, not a journal; treat any self-reported gain as unconfirmed.
rows.if: The goal is professional judgement or a disposition

rows.basis: [Structured reflection](claims/reflective-practice-improves-outcomes-when-structured.md) [+M] for written specific prompts (a classroom engineering course); untested online
rows.change: Replace the live debrief with three written prompts after each task and a model answer to compare against; offer an automatically scored changed task as the retry.
rows.if: `online-self-paced`, no facilitator

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page's compressed-timeframe guidance
rows.change: One complete loop: a 15-minute experience, a 10-minute written debrief, a stated rule, one changed attempt; no second loop.
rows.if: `single-session`

rows.basis: Untested; [reflection in higher education](claims/reflective-practice-evidence-mixed-in-professional-education.md) [~M] reports peer interaction as a moderator, direction not stated on the claim page
rows.change: Debrief in pairs or threes against a written protocol; spend facilitator time on checking stated principles, where a wrong rule is hardest for peers to catch.
rows.if: Large cohort, one facilitator

rows.basis: [Learning-style matching](claims/learning-styles-matching-does-not-improve-learning.md) [-S]; [Kolb styles unchanged over a year](claims/kolb-learning-style-stable-over-one-year.md) [-W] and [no link to career choice](claims/kolb-inventory-limited-validity-career-and-personality.md) [-W], both second-hand reports in one review
rows.change: Drop the style diagnosis and the matching; run every learner through every stage.
rows.if: The program bundles the cycle with Kolb's Learning Style Inventory, or asks to start learners at their "preferred stage"

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page's constraint that graded reflection becomes a compliance artifact
rows.change: Assess the changed attempt and a new unaided task; do not grade journals for completion; score principle and performance separately.
rows.if: Credit attaches to reflection, or assessment is high-stakes

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page's personalization
rows.change: Written or recorded reflection, in the language they choose, before any group debrief; sentence starters for the prompts.
rows.if: Learners are uncomfortable reflecting in public, or reflect in a second language

rows.basis: [Assessment for learning improves achievement](claims/assessment-for-learning-improves-achievement.md) [+M]
rows.change: Place a written check with feedback inside or between units (a medium cycle) rather than only at the end; expect a small overall gain
rows.if: Unit-based school course (`pre-k-12`)

rows.basis: [Assessment for learning improves achievement](claims/assessment-for-learning-improves-achievement.md) [+M]; [Teachers changed lessons in response to formative information](claims/tefa-formative-information-changed-lessons.md) [+W] (teacher reports from one programme); [Programme teachers showed more complete contingent-teaching cycles](claims/mct-pd-more-complete-contingent-teaching-cycles.md) [+W] (teacher behaviour, one study; no student outcome recorded in the claim)
rows.change: Add professional development on interpreting responses, or a computer-based formative system, to the rollout; both did better than other approaches in one synthesis. Where teachers support small groups, include practice in the diagnose–adjust–check cycle itself. Ask teachers to record the lesson changes the responses led to
rows.if: Teachers are new to formative assessment

rows.basis: [Teachers judge more accurately with diagnostic cues](claims/diagnostic-cues-improve-teacher-judgment-accuracy.md) [+M]; [Non-diagnostic cues hinder teacher judgment accuracy](claims/non-diagnostic-cues-hinder-teacher-judgment-accuracy.md) [+M]; [Teachers fabricate student cues when judging from diagrams](claims/teacher-cue-utilization-fabricated-student-cues-diagram-only.md) [~W]; [A brief cue-diagnosticity intervention did not improve accuracy](claims/diagnosticity-intervention-no-accuracy-gain.md) [~W] (Dutch secondary teachers judging text comprehension, in experimental tasks with anonymous students)
rows.change: Give the teacher the learner's performance on the task and base each judgment on it; leave out or set aside impressions such as interest, effort or behaviour, and note which piece of work each judgment rests on. Do not count on a short briefing about which cues matter to raise accuracy
rows.if: The teacher judges each learner's understanding from their work (marking, reading checks, conferences)

rows.basis: [Short-answer checks outperform multiple-choice mainly when feedback follows](claims/feedback-determines-whether-short-answer-retrieval-outperforms-multiple-choice.md) [~M] (laboratory studies reported in one review chapter)
rows.change: Prefer multiple-choice items, which learners answer correctly far more often; switch to short-answer items once the correct answer will follow, where they came out slightly ahead
rows.if: No feedback can follow the check (it is scored later, or not returned)

rows.basis: [Retrieval practice improves long-term retention](claims/retrieval-practice-improves-retention.md) [+S]; [Feedback enhances retrieval practice](claims/feedback-enhances-retrieval-practice.md) [+S]; [Learners' correctness self-assessments are imperfect](claims/imperfect-correctness-self-assessment.md) [~M]; [Learners' feedback-skipping decisions diverge from the optimal rule](claims/skipping-decisions-diverge-from-computer.md) [~M] (one word-pair experiment)
rows.change: Make the check a recall attempt, return the correct answer after each error rather than after every item, decide what counts as an error by scoring rather than by letting learners skip feedback when they feel sure, and judge the branch by a check a day or more later
rows.if: The goal includes durable recall (facts, vocabulary, the steps of a procedure)

rows.basis: [Feedback after multiple-choice tests halves lure intrusions](claims/feedback-after-multiple-choice-tests-halves-lure-intrusions.md) [~M]
rows.change: Always return the correct answer; immediate or end-of-set feedback both work, and without it chosen lures are reproduced later
rows.if: The check will use multiple-choice items

rows.basis: [Feedback improves learning, varying with its information](claims/feedback-improves-learning.md) [+M]; [Feedback works best at task and process levels](claims/feedback-most-effective-at-task-and-process-levels.md) [~M]
rows.change: Make it say what to change in the task or the method, not only whether the answer was right
rows.if: Feedback after each check will be brief

rows.basis: [Pretesting enhances learning](claims/pretesting-enhances-learning.md) [+M] (laboratory studies with undergraduates, retention up to a week; not a diagnostic pretest used to plan teaching)
rows.change: Open with a short, low-stakes pretest on the coming material, followed by teaching that answers it; a pretest the teaching does not answer is wasted time
rows.if: There is time before a new topic

rows.basis: [Peer assessment improves performance](claims/peer-assessment-improves-performance.md) [+M]; [Structured criteria are not shown to improve peer assessment](claims/peer-assessment-structured-criteria-improve-learning.md) [~M]
rows.change: Add a peer-review round between draft and final version; freeform review is as effective as scripted
rows.if: The class is large and the work is extended (essays, projects)

rows.basis: [Self-assessment accuracy is low without training](claims/self-assessment-accuracy-is-low-without-training.md) [~M]; [Rubric-referenced self-assessment improved work](claims/rubrics-improve-student-work.md) [~M]; [Prior knowledge is needed for accurate self-assessment](claims/prior-knowledge-needed-for-accurate-self-assessment.md) [~M]; [Self-assessment improves self-regulated learning](claims/self-assessment-improves-self-regulated-learning.md) [+M]; [Self-assessment feedback reduced task-selection accuracy during learning](claims/self-assessment-feedback-reduced-learning-phase-task-selection.md) [-M] (one experiment: choices during learning were less accurate with such feedback, d = 0.46, most of it negative)
rows.change: Give them a rubric and a modelled example of self-assessment first; do not accept untrained self-ratings as accurate, least of all from the learners who are furthest behind; expect a small gain in strategy use rather than in scores. Telling learners how far their self-assessment missed their actual score does not by itself improve their choice of the next task
rows.if: Learners will self-assess before revising

rows.basis: [Diagnostic review gave larger writing gains](claims/diagnostic-review-larger-writing-gains.md) [+W]; [Diagnostic review class scored higher on process indicators](claims/diagnostic-review-higher-process-indicators.md) [+W]; [Group-by-cycle interactions for formative outcomes](claims/group-cycle-interactions-formative-outcomes.md) [+W] (two intact classes of 48, one quasi-experiment)
rows.change: Run several draft–diagnose–revise cycles, with the teacher reviewing the diagnosis with learners; plan for more teacher review time, not less, and judge the arrangement after several cycles rather than the first, since in the one study the gap on diagnostic accuracy, feedback comprehension, revision quality and self-assessment accuracy widened across three cycles
rows.if: Writing course with AI scoring available

rows.basis: [LLM diagnosis drops sharply on vague evidence](claims/vague-evidence-degrades-llm-diagnosis.md) [~M] (a benchmark of 18 models on handwritten mathematics work, not a classroom test); [High-level feedback should remain a human responsibility](claims/high-level-feedback-remains-human-responsibility.md) [~W] (a conceptual argument)
rows.change: Use it where the work states the reasoning explicitly: ask learners to show their steps, and route vague or partial responses to a teacher. Keep feedback on reasoning and synthesis with a person
rows.if: An LLM or other AI system will diagnose learners' work

rows.basis: [Contingent scaffolding improves learning](claims/contingent-scaffolding-improves-learning.md) [+M]; [Teachers changed lessons in response to formative information](claims/tefa-formative-information-changed-lessons.md) [~W]
rows.change: Make each next hint depend on the last response, and let the tutor see the learner's work as it happens
rows.if: One-to-one tutoring

rows.basis: [OpenSciEd formative practice limited by grading and time](claims/openscied-formative-assessment-feasibility-challenges.md) [~W]; [Faculty time limits targeted formative feedback](claims/formative-feedback-constraints-gateway-math.md) [~W]
rows.change: Choose fewer, aligned checks that each feed a planned decision, and share the reading with peers or software
rows.if: Teachers lack time to give feedback (many students, three-dimensional tasks)

rows.basis: [Wireless keypads convert a passive audience to active learners](claims/wireless-keypads-convert-passive-audience-to-active-learners.md) [+W] (the authors' account of their own lectures, no comparison); the frequency is an untested proposal
rows.change: Interrupt the lecture with multiple-choice questions, show the class's response distribution, and follow it at once with a related question or a discussion; decide the number of checks locally and record what changed after each
rows.if: A large lecture with a polling system, checking several times within one session

rows.basis: [Guided against unguided discovery](claims/minimal-guidance-less-effective-for-novices.md) [~S]: explicit instruction beat unassisted discovery, guided discovery beat other instruction; the meta-analysis does not break results down by prior knowledge, and is not of this pattern
rows.change: Teach the core ideas directly before research; give each research group a short, pre-selected source pack and a note frame; check each group's understanding before jigsaw.
rows.if: Learners are `novice` in the domain

rows.basis: [Reciprocal teaching](claims/reciprocal-teaching-improves-reading-comprehension.md) [+M] (16 studies); [especially poor readers](claims/reciprocal-teaching-raises-reading-comprehension-poor-readers.md) [+W] (a narrative review citing one study). Neither tests the whole pattern
rows.change: Make reciprocal teaching the main activity of research, with the teacher leading one group per session and modelling each move for several sessions before handing over; keep subtopics to three.
rows.if: Learners are younger readers, or struggling readers, in `primary` school

rows.basis: [Secondary review](claims/secondary-cooperative-learning-newmann-thompson.md) [~M]: only 33% of grade 10–12 studies were successful and jigsaw was least successful; [group rewards on individual learning](claims/cooperative-learning-group-rewards-and-individual-accountability.md) [+M]
rows.change: Do not rely on jigsaw alone: add team recognition built from individual quiz results, and a structured teaching protocol.
rows.if: Learners are in upper `secondary` (grades 10–12)

rows.basis: [Small-group learning in undergraduate STEM](claims/small-group-learning-improves-stem-achievement.md) [+M] (d = 0.51 against non-group instruction; does not separate structured from unstructured groups)
rows.change: Use the cycle for one unit a term; groups of 3–4; individual checks each week; keep lectures for core ideas.
rows.if: `postsecondary` STEM course

rows.basis: [Communities of practice principle](principles/communities-of-practice.md), whose evidence is descriptive; [mathematics PLC review](claims/plc-participation-changes-teacher-norms-understanding-practice.md) [+M] (a review of descriptive studies, no comparison). One phenomenological study of three PLC leaders (Prytula 2012) reports that [the PLC nurtured their metacognition](claims/plc-nurtures-teacher-metacognition.md) [+W], that [each leader's own metacognition shaped the work she led](claims/plc-leader-metacognition-shapes-led-work.md) [+W], and one leader's view that [disagreement catalysed learning](claims/plc-disagreements-catalyze-learning.md) [~W] (another adjourned to avoid conflict); a survey of small Chicago high schools found [higher reported trust and collaboration](claims/chrsi-teachers-higher-trust-collaboration-survey.md) [+W] (no effect size). None measures learning or practice against a comparison
rows.change: Make the theme a recurring problem of practice; each member researches a case or source and teaches it back; the shared task is a protocol or guide the team will use; observe practice afterwards, not only self-report. Give the facilitator time to plan what each meeting asks members to reflect on, and treat disagreement about a case as material for the next round rather than a reason to close the meeting.
rows.if: Adults in a work setting (a professional learning cohort, `workplace-clinical`)

rows.basis: Untested; reciprocal teaching's claim page says the routine needs sustained practice over multiple sessions
rows.change: Do not attempt the full pattern. Run one jigsaw on pre-read material with a teaching protocol and an individual check on every part; leave reciprocal-teaching handover out.
rows.if: `single-session` only

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Put each remote learner in a research group with at least one other remote learner or give the group a shared online document and audio channel; in jigsaw, the remote expert teaches from a shared screen with the protocol visible; collect individual checks online for everyone.
rows.if: Mixed modes: some learners remote, some in the room

rows.basis: Untested proposal; [learning by teaching](claims/learning-by-teaching-improves-tutor-learning.md) [~M] found interactive teaching better than non-interactive, so expect less benefit without live questions
rows.change: Replace live jigsaw with asynchronous teaching: each expert posts a short explanation and two questions; peers answer and the expert replies; an automatic individual quiz on every part decides progress.
rows.if: `online-self-paced` or phone-only, no live sessions

rows.basis: [Contingent scaffolding](claims/contingent-scaffolding-improves-learning.md) [~M]: evidence mostly from one-to-one tutoring; its claim page notes contingency across a whole class is hard. The rota is untested
rows.change: Use role cards and question stems so groups can run without the teacher; the teacher circulates on a fixed rota and checks each research group once before jigsaw; use written exit checks to decide which group to visit.
rows.if: One teacher for many groups (30+ learners)

rows.basis: Untested proposal; [positioning learners as sources](claims/positioning-students-as-sources-increases-productive-participation-in-science-discourse.md) [+M] widened participation in one lower-secondary science class (qualitative, no comparison group)
rows.change: Give each learner a defined, bounded role (questioner, summariser) and a rehearsal with the research group before teaching; let experts teach in pairs; accept spoken or drawn explanations in checks.
rows.if: Learners with low confidence or low literacy

rows.basis: [Group rewards on individual learning](claims/cooperative-learning-group-rewards-and-individual-accountability.md) [+M]; reciprocal teaching's [gap between standardised and researcher-written tests](claims/reciprocal-teaching-improves-reading-comprehension.md) [~M] is a reason to check with an independent measure
rows.change: Score every learner on every subtopic, add a teacher-led review of parts where peer-taught scores lag, and test at the delay that matters.
rows.if: High stakes: an individual exam on all content

rows.basis: Untested proposal; extends the earlier page's step of creating artifacts and sharing findings
rows.change: Make it the shared task in step 6 and name the audience at launch; still score individual understanding separately from the product.
