rows.if: A product or performance for a real audience (an exhibition, a guide for younger pupils, a report for a partner)

rows.basis: [Practice raises computer-based lesson posttest scores](claims/practice-presence-raises-cbi-posttest-achievement.md) [+M]
rows.change: Keep practice with feedback (event 6–7) above all; it was the one event whose removal lowered the posttest
rows.if: Time is short and events must be cut

rows.basis: [Removing single events did not reduce achievement](claims/single-event-removal-no-achievement-effect.md) [~M]
rows.change: One of them may be trimmed if time forces it; removing any one alone did not significantly lower an immediate posttest, but that is not evidence they do nothing
rows.if: Objectives, examples or a closing review would be cut

rows.basis: [The no-objectives group rated goal clarity highest](claims/no-objectives-group-most-positive-attitudes.md) [~M]; [Students notice missing practice and examples](claims/students-notice-missing-practice-and-examples.md) [~M]
rows.change: Also check performance on an unaided task; ratings did not track which events learners received
rows.if: The lesson will be judged on learner satisfaction ratings

rows.basis: [Minimal guidance is less effective for novices](claims/minimal-guidance-less-effective-for-novices.md) [+S]
rows.change: Run events 4 and 5 (presentation and guidance) in full
rows.if: Learners cannot begin the target task

rows.basis: [Expertise reversal effect](claims/expertise-reversal-effect.md) [~S]
rows.change: Shorten events 4 and 5 for them and move to performance, feedback and transfer
rows.if: Some learners already perform the target unaided

rows.basis: [Pretesting enhances learning](claims/pretesting-enhances-learning.md) [+M]; [Prior-knowledge activation had little effect on retention](claims/prior-knowledge-activation-little-effect-on-retention.md) [-M]
rows.change: Replace open "what do you know" recall with a few questions on the coming content; open activation showed little effect
rows.if: Learners have little relevant prior knowledge for event 3

rows.basis: [Retrieval practice improves long-term retention](claims/retrieval-practice-improves-retention.md) [+S]
rows.change: Make event 9 retrieval practice in later sessions rather than a review at the end of this lesson
rows.if: The target must be recalled weeks later

rows.basis: [Whole-task practice improves transfer (design argument)](claims/whole-task-performance-improves-transfer.md) [~W]
rows.change: Replace a single linear pass through the events with whole tasks of increasing complexity (see 4C/ID)
rows.if: The target is a complex skill with a transfer goal

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: State the objective briefly in performance terms and let learners check their own attempt against it
rows.if: `online-self-paced`, with learners directing their own work

rows.basis: Untested here; the feedback and gate steps rest on the claims in steps 3–4, none tested with novices separately
rows.change: Word banks and recognition items first, typed or spoken answers only after the first level is passed; feedback with the correct answer on every item; a criterion check on day 3 or later
rows.if: Learners are `novice` in the domain

rows.basis: Untested proposal; the earlier page's "difficulty should rise in response to growing skill"
rows.change: Placement check and test-out by level; harder settings (typed answers, mixed review) from the start; no points for easy items
rows.if: Learners are `advanced`, or already accurate

rows.basis: [Rewards claim](claims/rewards-undermine-intrinsic-motivation.md) [-S]: tangible rewards more detrimental for children than college students, laboratory tasks
rows.change: No tangible prizes for finishing lessons; points and badges for accuracy and effort, worded as information; no public individual ranking; a teacher sees the level map
rows.if: Learners are `child`ren (under 12)

rows.basis: Untested proposal; mastery evidence is from school and college courses ([mastery learning improves outcomes](claims/mastery-learning-improves-outcomes.md) [+M])
rows.change: Levels tied to job tasks passed at a criterion; no badges for completion or seat time; no ranking among colleagues; the manager sees criteria passed, not streaks
rows.if: `adult`s in a `workplace-clinical` setting (onboarding, compliance)

rows.basis: [Duolingo level analysis](claims/rdd-review-exercises-causal-leveling-up.md) [+M] (in-app items, one study); [gamified vocabulary, reported in a review](claims/quizizz-gamification-better-memorization.md) [+W]
rows.change: The full loop fits; check recall on new sentences a week after the level, outside the app
rows.if: Goal is `verbal-association` (vocabulary, terms, notation)

rows.basis: Untested; the earlier page's constraint "weak fit for complex open-ended performance"
rows.change: Use levels only for the itemisable parts (vocabulary, a calculation); the whole performance stays one task, judged on the brief's own rubric, outside the level map; do not split it into items to fit the gate
rows.if: Goal is a `complex-skill` or whole-task performance the brief wants kept whole (a conversation, a case, a project)

rows.basis: [Self-paced mastery reduces completion](claims/self-paced-mastery-programs-reduce-college-course-completion.md) [-M] (college PSI courses, carried to apps); [level prompts](claims/ab-tests-level-interventions-increase-lessons.md) [+M] (practice volume only)
rows.change: The software runs feedback, retries, checks and review; a weekly lesson target and a soft deadline per level; a streak that survives one missed day
rows.if: `online-self-paced`, no teacher

rows.basis: [Mastery effects vary with pacing](claims/mastery-learning-effects-vary-with-standard-pacing-and-test-type.md) [~M] (group-based programmes had larger effects, no game layer); [group-based mastery and attrition](claims/mastery-improves-engagement-attrition.md) [+M] (one synthesis)
rows.change: Learners work the levels on devices; the class keeps a common pace with a weekly level target; the teacher spends the session's last 10 minutes with learners who failed a check twice
rows.if: `classroom`, one teacher and many learners

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: One tool reached the same way by everyone; lessons short enough for a phone (about 10 items); no speed-ranked live rounds; level checks run in the tool, not on paper in the room
rows.if: Mixed modes: some learners remote, some in the room, or phone-only

rows.basis: Untested proposal; the attempt cap rests on [eSpark logs](claims/espark-post-quiz-mastery-failure-rate.md) [~W]
rows.change: Automate feedback, retries and checks; the facilitator spends about 5 minutes a week on a list of learners who failed a check twice or stopped practising, and contacts those
rows.if: Scarce facilitator time (volunteers, a busy shift, a tutor who checks in briefly)

rows.basis: Untested; no claim here tests a single session
rows.change: Do not build levels, streaks or a points economy; one short lesson with feedback and retry of missed items, one check at the end; claim nothing about persistence
rows.if: Time is a `single-session`

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: 2 minutes review, 10 minutes of one lesson with feedback and retries, 3 minutes for a level check when one is due; never two checks in one session
rows.if: A fixed short time budget per session (for example 15 minutes)

rows.basis: [Rewards claim](claims/rewards-undermine-intrinsic-motivation.md) [~S] (laboratory tasks, free-choice time; carried to apps)
rows.change: Keep the level map and informational feedback; drop expected points, prizes and streak rewards
rows.if: Learners already practise willingly, or find the task interesting

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Private progress only; a first level everyone passes; feedback with icons and audio; a failed check shown as "one more lesson", not a lost life
rows.if: Learners have low confidence or low literacy

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: The learner controls who sees levels and streaks; no shared boards; a teacher or employer sees only what the learner releases
rows.if: Progress or answers are private or sensitive (health, a second-chance course)

rows.basis: [Effects vary with test type](claims/mastery-learning-effects-vary-with-standard-pacing-and-test-type.md) [~M] (near-zero effects on standardised tests); [behavioural engagement](claims/behavioural-engagement-not-cognitive-engagement.md) [~M]
rows.change: Keep points formative; grade on an aligned task outside the app at the delay that matters; never grade on streaks or practice volume
rows.if: Levels or points feed a grade, or stakes are high

rows.basis: [Rewards claim](claims/rewards-undermine-intrinsic-motivation.md) [~S]; [mastery standard](claims/mastery-learning-effects-vary-with-standard-pacing-and-test-type.md) [~M]; the combination is untested
rows.change: Keep it; change only what the evidence says matters: points for accuracy and improvement rather than log-ins or completion, a level that opens on a check rather than on lessons finished, and an outside check beside the app's own
rows.if: The brief names its own routine (an app's XP, streaks or leagues; a class points chart; its own level criterion or rubric)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Use those as the levels and their criteria; do not substitute a level scheme of your own
rows.if: The brief gives its own categories or skill map (CEFR bands, a job's competency list)

rows.basis: [Simulated mastery learning](claims/problem-counts-by-knowledge-tracing-condition.md) [~W]: with 30 simulated students per condition, a streak rule gave more problems than knowledge tracing (about 17 against 11 for one problem type); simulated, not real learners
rows.change: Prefer a check on new items over a streak of correct answers; if a streak rule is kept, record how many items learners need to pass
rows.if: The criterion is set by an automated rule ("N correct in a row")

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Make it a feedback item: a near-miss answer shown beside the correct one, with the sentence that separates them, in the lesson and in the check
rows.if: The brief reports an error learners actually made

rows.basis: [Minimal guidance and novices](claims/minimal-guidance-less-effective-for-novices.md) [~S]; tested on discovery and inquiry, carried to production
rows.change: Teach the essential content explicitly first (step 2), provide the sources, use a blueprint template with one scene filled in, fix the product to 2 minutes, and check content individually before production.
rows.if: Learners are `novice` in the content

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Skip the content investigation to a short review; spend the time on exemplars and media criteria; let learners choose the audience and write their own criteria.
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` in the content but new to the media

rows.basis: Untested; the audience comparison with second graders ([authentic audiences](claims/authentic-audiences-improve-student-work.md) [+M]) concerned writing, not media
rows.change: One medium (narrated pictures, a poster with audio), roles named with pictures, the teacher scribes the storyboard, sessions of 30–40 minutes, and an audience they know (another class, families).
rows.if: Learners are `child` (primary age)

rows.basis: Untested proposal; [learning by teaching](claims/learning-by-teaching-improves-tutor-learning.md) [+M] supports making each learner explain their part, not tested with adults at work
rows.change: Make the product something colleagues will use (a 2-minute procedure video, a job aid), with a subject-matter expert reviewing the blueprint for accuracy before recording; individual check on the procedure itself.
rows.if: Learners are `adult` in a work setting (`workplace-clinical`, onboarding, professional development)

rows.basis: [Learner-constructed organizers did worse on transfer](claims/learner-constructed-graphic-organizers-outperform-provided.md) [~M], college readers of a text, carried by analogy
rows.change: Cap production at a third of the unit's time, use the simplest medium that carries the content, score content apart from polish, and run the individual content check at a delay.
rows.if: The goal is subject content; media literacy is incidental

rows.basis: [Interdisciplinary humanities units](claims/interdisciplinary-humanities-units-improve-interdisciplinary-competences.md) [+M]: one non-randomized middle-school study; units, not media production
rows.change: Plan the product with two subject teachers, each owning content criteria on the blueprint; ask for one scene that connects the two subjects explicitly.
rows.if: The goal includes cross-curricular or interdisciplinary learning

rows.basis: Untested proposal; the project-based meta-analysis ([project-based learning](claims/project-based-learning-improves-achievement.md) [+M]) excludes short single activities
rows.change: Drop production of new media: teams annotate or re-sequence provided clips or slides into a 1-minute explanation, present to another team, and answer one question each.
rows.if: `single-session` only

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Give remote members roles that work on a phone (script, narration, research, still photos); keep the blueprint in one shared document; present by screen share with questions in chat, and run the individual check in writing for everyone.
rows.if: Mixed mode: some learners remote, some in the room, or phone-only

rows.basis: Untested proposal; the blueprint check is the step most directly tied to the [content-quality concern](claims/learner-constructed-graphic-organizers-outperform-provided.md) [~M]
rows.change: Spend the facilitator's minutes on two checks only: the blueprint's content (5 minutes per team) and the individual explanation before presentation. Teams peer-review blueprints against the criteria list first; use templates so tool questions do not reach the facilitator.
rows.if: One teacher for many teams, or scarce facilitator time (volunteers, a busy shift, a tutor checking in briefly)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Allow pictures and speech instead of written text in the product and blueprint; give sentence frames for narration; let a learner present in a small group or by recording; keep the individual content check oral.
rows.if: Learners with low confidence, low literacy, or learning in a second language

rows.basis: [Authentic audiences](claims/authentic-audiences-improve-student-work.md) [+M] (product quality on writing); the [authentic audiences principle](principles/authentic-audiences-purposes.md) holds the conditions
rows.change: Agree with the audience what they need and whether they will respond; plan time to revise after their response; score the content against criteria and record the audience's reaction separately; get consent for anything public.
rows.if: The product goes to a real audience (a community partner, families, a public site)

rows.basis: [Rubric self-assessment](claims/rubrics-improve-student-work.md) [~M], with its stress and avoidance finding; [the grading argument for maker education](claims/grading-harms-maker-education-outcomes.md) [~W], an argument, not a test
rows.change: Grade content understanding individually as well as the team product; publish the criteria from the start; consider weighting process evidence (blueprint, revisions).
rows.if: High stakes: the product is graded for a qualification

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Keep it. Change only what the evidence says matters: add a content point per scene to the template, separate content from media rows on the rubric, and add one individual content check before presentation.
rows.if: The brief names its own routine (its own storyboard template, rubric, production checklist or presentation format)

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page's "handmade TV program" example
rows.change: Make the product live rather than recorded (a performance, a gallery walk, a radio-style reading), or record on one device in turn while other teams plan and rehearse.
rows.if: Little equipment (one device per class, no editing software)

rows.basis: [Minimal guidance](claims/minimal-guidance-less-effective-for-novices.md) [~S]; [part-task practice](claims/part-task-practice-reduces-load-for-novices.md) [~M] for high-element-interactivity tasks
rows.change: Teach the task's vocabulary and representations before the motivating attempt; keep the attempt to 10–15 minutes; give a structured investigation procedure and a teacher-led synthesis every session; fade only after the second unit.
rows.if: Learners are `novice` in the domain (cannot read the task's data or terms)

rows.basis: [Problem-first effects rose with grade level](claims/psi-effect-increases-with-grade-level.md) [~M] (school and university grades, not expertise as such); otherwise untested
rows.change: Skip most of the construct phase: state the idea, and spend the time on harder consequential tasks and new cases; let learners design their own investigation.
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` or already hold the idea

rows.basis: [Problem-first effects were negative for 2nd–5th graders](claims/psi-effect-increases-with-grade-level.md) [~M]
rows.change: Teach the idea first with concrete examples, then use the motivating task as the application; keep the "need to know" opening short and teacher-led.
rows.if: Learners are `child` (second to fifth grade)

rows.basis: [Productive failure](claims/productive-failure-improves-conceptual-learning.md) [~S] (no procedural advantage; reversal for domain-general skills); [PBL and basic knowledge](claims/pbl-null-basic-knowledge-positive-transfer.md) [~M]
rows.change: Teach the procedure or facts explicitly first; use the LfU arc only for the concept the procedure serves, and keep a separate check of basic knowledge.
rows.if: The target is a `procedure` or domain-general skill (e.g. designing a fair test), or factual recall

rows.basis: Untested in workplaces; [problem-first effects rose with grade level](claims/psi-effect-increases-with-grade-level.md) [~M], g = 1.03 for postgraduates and professionals (education settings, not workplace training)
rows.change: Use a real case from their work as the motivating task and a real decision as the refine task; run the construct phase as short guided analyses with a facilitator synthesis.
rows.if: `adult-workplace` learners, the task is their own work problem

rows.basis: Untested as a format; [time span](claims/psi-fidelity-time-span-interaction.md) [~M]: the fidelity benefit of problem-first designs tended to shrink for interventions of a few hours (marginal, p = .055)
rows.change: Keep one arc: 10-minute attempt, 30–40 minutes of guided investigation with a 10-minute synthesis, 15–20 minutes on one consequential task, 5 minutes to write the idea in their own words. Do not expect transfer evidence from one session.
rows.if: `single-session` only (one 60–90 minute block)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Give one slot each to motivate, construct and refine, and the fourth to the revisit a week later; cut the number of investigations, not the synthesis.
rows.if: A fixed short time budget across sessions (e.g. four 30-minute slots)

rows.basis: [Guidance in inquiry](claims/guidance-improves-inquiry-learning-outcomes.md) [+M] (the studies' settings are not reported on the claim page); otherwise untested
rows.change: The system shows the task, collects a typed attempt and questions, runs a guided simulation or data set with prompts and immediate feedback, then gives a worked statement of the idea that refers back to typical attempts, then the applied task with a self-explanation prompt.
rows.if: `online-self-paced`, no teacher

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Put the motivating task, the driving question and the class's collected questions in one shared document all can see; use data or readings that open on a phone; take attempts and explanations as typed or voice replies; run the synthesis so remote learners' findings are named.
rows.if: Mixed modes: some learners remote, some in the room, or phone-only

rows.basis: [Contingent scaffolding](claims/contingent-scaffolding-improves-learning.md) [~M]: its evidence is mostly one-to-one tutoring, and the claim page reports contingency is hard across a whole class
rows.change: Spend facilitator time on the syntheses, not the investigation; give groups written prompts and a checklist for the investigation; at each check-in ask one question ("what does your result tell you about the driving question?").
rows.if: One teacher for many learners, or scarce facilitator time (volunteers, a short check-in per group)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Make the motivating attempt low stakes (unscored, in pairs, oral or drawn); use visual data and short readings; give sentence frames for explanations.
rows.if: Learners with low confidence or literacy

rows.basis: [OpenSciEd enactment](claims/openscied-enactment-challenges-fatigue-pacing-pseudoagency.md) [~M] (teacher reports from one curriculum's field test); remedy untested
rows.change: Re-state the driving question and what is still unknown at the start of each session; keep the unit short enough that the refine task arrives within two to three weeks.
rows.if: A unit running several weeks, with interest fading

rows.basis: Untested; [whole-task practice](claims/whole-task-performance-improves-transfer.md) [+W] is an argument, not a test
rows.change: Make the audience's question the motivating task, so the need to know is theirs; check the product uses the idea and not only presentation; keep the whole performance whole rather than splitting it into items.
rows.if: The refine task is a product or performance for a real audience

rows.basis: [Inquiry-based teaching](claims/inquiry-based-teaching-improves-science-achievement.md) [+S] (teacher-led inquiry); [self-explanation](claims/self-explanation-improves-conceptual-understanding.md) [+S] on immediate tests
rows.change: Keep it; change only what the evidence says matters: add a synthesis that states the idea after the investigation, and one "why does this follow?" prompt in the applied task. If the rubric rewards tool use, keep that criterion and add an unaided use of the idea beside it.
rows.if: The brief names its own routine, rubric or categories (its own investigation template, scoring rubric or job aid)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Let learners choose whether to use their own case or a supplied one, and who sees their attempt; collect questions anonymously.
rows.if: The motivating material is private or sensitive (learners' own health, family or workplace data)

rows.basis: [Productive failure](claims/productive-failure-improves-conceptual-learning.md) [~S] (the benefit is in conceptual and transfer outcomes); the delay is untested
rows.change: Judge the unit by use and explanation of the idea on a new case at the delay that matters, plus a separate check of basic knowledge; do not judge it by the refine product alone.
rows.if: High stakes, or assessment on new cases weeks later

rows.basis: [Metacognitive prompts](claims/metacognitive-prompts-improve-learning.md) [~M]: in the online review, lower-prior-knowledge learners in one study needed training before prompts helped; carried to MOOCs
rows.change: Shorten segments to 3–5 minutes with worked examples; keep the start- and end-of-week prompts all course with model answers for the first three weeks; teach learners how to use the prompts in week 1 (one worked example of a plan and a self-check); give the reduced route early.
rows.if: Learners are `novice` in the domain, or have not studied online alone before

rows.basis: [One issuer reported that micro-credential stacks closed the gap between MOOC-Ed content and classroom practice](claims/friday-institute-mooc-ed-implementation-gap-micro-credentials.md) [+W] (a `q1` case report, no comparison)
rows.change: Offer a placement check to skip modules; replace content questions with an application task in their own workplace, with evidence of practice (a lesson plan, a recorded session, a reflection) reviewed against a rubric; consider stackable micro-credentials for the applied tasks.
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` or practising professionals (a teachers' PD MOOC)

rows.basis: Untested; the claims recorded here are about adults and university students
rows.change: Do not rely on open forums or self-pacing: assign the MOOC within a class, with a teacher setting weekly targets and reviewing the self-checks; keep forums closed to the class or moderated.
rows.if: Learners are `adolescent` or younger, or a school uses the MOOC

rows.basis: [Embodied music learning resists short videos and self-graded quizzes](claims/moocs-low-completion-embodied-music-learning.md) [-W] (a review's argument); [rubric-guided peer rating](claims/rubrics-improve-peer-feedback-quality.md) [~M], tested on writing, carried to performance
rows.change: Add recorded performance submissions judged against a rubric by calibrated peers, and periodic live sessions with an expert for a sample of learners; do not rest the skill on video and quizzes.
rows.if: The target is an embodied or performed skill (music, laboratory, clinical, a language spoken aloud)

rows.basis: [Rubric-guided peer rating](claims/rubrics-improve-peer-feedback-quality.md) [+M]: benefit concentrated on subjective, complex criteria; one study found less reflective feedback
rows.change: Calibrated peer review: a rubric of three or four criteria, two or three anchor samples rated before reviewing, three reviews per submission, staff spot-checks; tell reviewers to add one comment that is not on the rubric, since rubrics narrowed reflective comment.
rows.if: The final task is written or designed work too complex for machine scoring

rows.basis: [Automated grading bias](claims/automated-grading-bias-non-native-english.md) [-W] (a review's stated risk); [one platform's time saving](claims/mooc-nlp-grading-70-percent-time-reduction.md) [+W] is not evidence of fairness
rows.change: Audit the scorer on a sample by language background before use; keep a human or peer route for anyone who disputes a score; do not let an unaudited score decide a certificate.
rows.if: Open text is to be scored automatically, and learners write in a second language

rows.basis: [Implementation intentions](claims/implementation-intentions-improve-goal-attainment.md) [~S]: no effect for learners in collectivist cultures in the field experiments; the study-group alternative is untested
rows.change: Keep the week-1 planning activity, but do not count on it for completion everywhere; for those learners, add study groups formed by region or language, with a shared weekly goal.
rows.if: Learners come from many cultures, including collectivist ones

rows.basis: [Implementation intentions](claims/implementation-intentions-improve-goal-attainment.md) [+S]: worked when the obstacle was predictable and surmountable, not for lack of time; extension is untested
rows.change: Make the if-then plan name the obstacle and a fixed weekly slot; show it back at the midpoint; allow a two-week extension without penalty.
rows.if: Adults in work settings with predictable obstacles (shifts, family)

rows.basis: [Connectivist courses: some learners disconnected and demotivated](claims/connectivist-courses-student-agency-problems.md) [-W]; [one structural model linked autonomy, openness and interactivity with achievement](claims/connectivist-principles-positive-effect-achievement.md) [+W] (a survey's second-hand report)
rows.change: Use it only where learners can direct their own study; still give a weekly hub (a digest of learners' posts and the staff's pick), an orientation to the tools in week 1, and a named place to ask for help.
rows.if: The aim is networked, connectivist learning (learners build their own network of sources and peers)

rows.basis: Untested proposal. [SuaCode, a smartphone coding course, drew mostly intrinsically motivated learners](claims/suacode-african-students-intrinsically-motivated.md) [~W], and [free, accessible content was a weak reason for enrolling there](claims/free-accessible-content-weak-enrollment-motivator-suacode.md) [~W]; both are about motivation, not delivery
rows.change: Short downloadable segments with audio-only and transcript versions; quizzes that work on a small screen and offline; no task that needs a computer program the phone cannot run.
rows.if: Learners on phones only, or with costly data

rows.basis: Untested; see [Blended Learning](patterns/blended-learning.md) for dividing work between online and room
rows.change: Give the local group a facilitator guide: one weekly meeting of 45–60 minutes to work the hardest problem set together and discuss the week's question; the local group posts its answer to the forum so remote learners see it.
rows.if: Mixed modes: some learners take the MOOC together in a room (a campus course or an employer's study group) while others are alone

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Spend staff time only on a weekly summary of the commonest error, seeding the discussion question and spot-checking peer reviews; recruit former learners as community mentors; automate the reminder messages.
rows.if: One lead teacher, or a few hours of volunteer time a week, for thousands of learners

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Plan 6 hours in total: per week, 50 minutes of segments and questions, 30 minutes of the main practice task, 20 minutes of discussion or peer review, 10 minutes of planning and self-check, 10 minutes slack; drop forums rather than shorten practice.
rows.if: A fixed short time budget (e.g. 2 hours a week for 3 weeks)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Treat it as one segment-and-practice block, not a course: 3–4 short segments, questions after each, one practice task with a model answer, one planning question at the end ("when will you use this?").
rows.if: A single session only (a one-off open webinar or a single-module micro-course)

rows.basis: Untested proposal; [connectivist courses left some learners disconnected](claims/connectivist-courses-student-agency-problems.md) [-W], which is a reason to build early success in
rows.change: Captions and transcripts in plain language; a glossary per week; first-week tasks that cannot be failed (an introduction, a practice question with answer); allow audio or picture responses in the forum.
rows.if: Learners with low confidence or low literacy in the language of instruction

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Identity-checked, individually done final task (proctored or oral by sample), scored by staff or an audited scorer; keep peer review for formative work only.
rows.if: A credential with real stakes (credit, a job requirement)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Make reflections private by default; let the learner choose whether a piece goes to peer review; allow a display name in the forum; tell learners how many people can see a post.
rows.if: Learners will share private or sensitive material (their workplace, their health, their students)

rows.basis: Untested proposal; [Open Educational Resources](elements/open-educational-resources.md) for licences
rows.change: Keep the final product public and whole; peer review against the brief's own criteria before publication; offer the open licence choice from step 1 for learners' own work.
rows.if: Learners produce work for a real audience (an open resource, a performance, a public portfolio)

rows.basis: [Rubric-guided peer rating](claims/rubrics-improve-peer-feedback-quality.md) [~M] for the calibration; the rest untested
rows.change: Keep it; change only what the evidence speaks to: add anchor-sample calibration to its rubric, a planning prompt to its check-in, or a segment-length limit to its videos. If its rubric rewards use of a tool, keep that criterion and add one unaided check beside it.
rows.if: The brief names its own routine, rubric or check-in

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Submit and review the whole performance (one recorded presentation, one full design), not split into quiz items; the rubric's criteria divide the judgement, not the task.
rows.if: The brief wants a whole performance or product kept whole

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Use it as a worked contrast in the next week's first segment: the error, why it is tempting, and the correct version side by side; add one question on it.
rows.if: The brief reports an error learners actually made

rows.basis: [Mastery learning improves outcomes](claims/mastery-learning-improves-outcomes.md) [+M]; [Group-based mastery positive in every included study](claims/group-mastery-positive-achievement-all-studies.md) [+M]
rows.change: Use the full loop: unit check, corrective work, parallel recheck, then advance
rows.if: A course of cumulative units, with the course examination as the outcome

rows.basis: [Effects vary with standard, pacing and test type](claims/mastery-learning-effects-vary-with-standard-pacing-and-test-type.md) [~M]
rows.change: Set a high standard for each unit; record it and tell learners
rows.if: Choosing the cut score

rows.basis: [Self-paced mastery programmes reduce course completion](claims/self-paced-mastery-programs-reduce-college-course-completion.md) [-M]
rows.change: Add deadlines or pacing checkpoints, because self-paced mastery courses lose more students
rows.if: College course, self-paced (`online-self-paced` or Keller-style)

rows.basis: [Mastery improves engagement and lowers attrition](claims/mastery-improves-engagement-attrition.md) [+W]
rows.change: Keep the class together and run correction and enrichment in a shared loop; attrition was lower in group-based mastery classes
rows.if: Group-paced class with a teacher

rows.basis: [Intelligent tutoring systems improve achievement over non-individualised instruction](claims/adaptive-learning-improves-outcomes.md) [~M]; [Mastery platform longitudinal positive effects](claims/mastery-platform-longitudinal-positive-effects.md) [+W]
rows.change: Expect a gain against large-group teaching but not against human tutoring; check the gate on outcomes outside the platform
rows.if: Software will gate progress (adaptive or practice platform)

rows.basis: [eSpark learners rarely reached 80% after three attempts](claims/espark-post-quiz-mastery-failure-rate.md) [~W]; [Socratic condition needed twice the attempts](claims/socratic-more-attempts-many-never-reach-mastery.md) [~W]
rows.change: Set an attempt limit and change the correction after a failed recheck instead of repeating the same task; record any gap left at the limit
rows.if: Learners may need many attempts on a unit

rows.basis: [Gains persist at follow-up](claims/mastery-learning-gains-persist-at-follow-up.md) [+M]; [Group-based mastery improves retention](claims/mastery-improves-retention.md) [+M]
rows.change: Recheck each earlier unit at the start of the next one and again weeks later
rows.if: Retention after the course matters

rows.basis: [Mastery learning improves attitudes](claims/mastery-learning-improves-attitudes-toward-instruction.md) [+M]; [Positive affective effects](claims/mastery-positive-affective-effects.md) [+M]
rows.change: Mastery classes rated the instruction and the subject more favourably; tell learners what the criterion is and why
rows.if: Learners' attitudes or attrition are a concern

rows.basis: [Criterion-referenced tests need construct validation](claims/criterion-referenced-tests-need-construct-validation.md) [~W]
rows.change: Write a parallel form for rechecks that changes surface details and at least one relevant condition
rows.if: The check will be a quiz written by the teacher

rows.basis: [Pacing calendars seen as impediments to mastery](claims/pacing-calendars-standardized-assessments-impediments.md) [~W]
rows.change: Agree in advance how far the loop may extend a unit, and what gap is carried forward when time runs out
rows.if: A district pacing calendar fixes when topics are taught

rows.basis: [Orientation-week attrition online is twice that of on-campus first weeks](claims/orientation-week-attrition-double-online.md) [~M]; [after instruction starts, online and on-campus drop rates are about the same](claims/no-drop-rate-difference-after-instruction-starts.md) [~M]; [Planning prompts raised MOOC completion](claims/planning-prompts-increase-mooc-completion.md) [+M]; [brief belonging interventions improved first-year college outcomes](claims/belonging-interventions-improve-outcomes.md) [+M] (college entry, not self-paced courses)
rows.change: Put the planning contact and a personal reply in the first week, before any content, and the first scheduled check-in before the first milestone; consider a brief belonging message in the first contact
rows.if: Learners new to online or self-paced study, or in their first term

rows.basis: [Implementation intentions worked when obstacles were work or family, not lack of time](claims/implementation-intentions-improve-goal-attainment.md) [+S]; fading schedule is untested
rows.change: Keep the plan-and-obstacles activity, and let the learner choose check-in frequency after the first milestone; keep triggered outreach
rows.if: Experienced adult learners in work, choosing their own pace

rows.basis: [Ninth-grade early-warning systems on grades and attendance were followed by improvements](claims/ninth-grade-early-warning-systems-improvements.md) [+W] (a research agenda's summary); [parent text alerts about missing homework raised performance](claims/parent-text-alerts-incomplete-homework-raise-performance.md) [+M]
rows.change: Route alerts to a teacher or family as well as the learner, and act on grades and attendance signals
rows.if: Secondary-school or younger learners

rows.basis: [Coaching raised retention at 12 months](claims/insidetrack-coaching-potentially-positive-persistence.md) [+M]; [no detectable effect on degree completion at 24 months](claims/insidetrack-coaching-no-discernible-attainment-effect.md) [~M]
rows.change: Plan coaching across terms and measure persistence each term; do not expect completion to follow from one term's support
rows.if: The goal is completing a credential, not one course

rows.basis: [Instructor feedback raised lab scores more than AI feedback](claims/instructor-feedback-greater-lab-score-improvements-than-ai-feedback.md) [+M]; [Feedback, analytics and structured reflection strengthen learning in simulations](claims/analytics-feedback-reflection-strengthen-learning-gains.md) [+W] (a review's summary)
rows.change: Keep a person on feedback for graded performance work and on debriefing; use automated help for practice
rows.if: The goal is mastery judged on performance tasks (cases, labs, simulations)

rows.basis: [Taking a course online reduced college success compared with in person](claims/online-course-taking-reduces-college-success.md) [-M]; [A standard template heightened teaching presence in accelerated online courses](claims/course-template-supports-learner-presence.md) [+W]; [organization rated high while facilitation rated lower](claims/coi-presence-uneven-profile-mba.md) [~M]; [Personal messages had the largest association with satisfaction](claims/personal-messages-largest-satisfaction-effect.md) [+M]
rows.change: Use a consistent course layout with goals, due dates and feedback turnaround stated, and schedule personal messages rather than waiting for learners to ask; do not count the layout as facilitation
rows.if: Online, self-paced, asynchronous, no class meetings

rows.basis: untested proposal; [dropout is not concentrated at one lesson in most online courses](claims/tipping-point-hypothesis-insufficient-online-dropout.md) [~M]; reviews of behavioural economics argue that [abundant choice without structure may add to dropout](claims/choice-overload-college-dropout-lack-of-structure.md) [+W] and that [self-control problems explain much dropout](claims/self-control-problems-explain-dropout.md) [+W] (arguments about college and adolescents, not tests in self-paced courses)
rows.change: Set learner-chosen milestones in the planning contact and trigger outreach on missed milestones, not on calendar dates; give a recommended order and pace rather than an open menu
rows.if: Rolling enrolment with no deadlines

rows.basis: descriptive baselines only: [35% of consortium participants completed](claims/cbe-participants-completion-employment-wages.md) [~M]; [gatekeeper completion slightly lower than comparison students](claims/cbe-gatekeeper-completion-lower-than-comparison.md) [~M]; [about two terms to a first certification course, four to a credential](claims/cbe-fast-completion-two-terms-certification-four-terms-credentials.md) [+M]; the mentor model itself is untested
rows.change: Plan mentor contact across terms; record time to each competency and completion against the programme's own comparison group, and take the gatekeeper courses as the place to concentrate triggered outreach
rows.if: Competency-based programme, pace set by the learner, credential spanning several terms

rows.basis: [Time-focused plans forecast lower completion](claims/time-focused-plans-forecast-lower-mooc-completion.md) [~M]
rows.change: Keep contacts short and specific: name the one next activity; avoid plans phrased only as times
rows.if: Little learner time each week

rows.basis: [GEAR UP messaging did not raise persistence; broad caseloads may have limited it](claims/gear-up-advisor-caseload-limited-effectiveness.md) [~W]; [alert threshold changes reshape advisor workload](claims/threshold-change-governance-impact.md) [~W]; [a consecutive-failures rule concentrated alerts within a fixed budget](claims/sequential-risk-policy-concentrates-failures.md) [+W]; [serving new students first raised the share helped](claims/nsf-strategy-increases-helped-students-busy-normal-queues.md) [+W] and [did not change requests resolved or wait time](claims/scheduling-strategy-no-effect-resolved-requests-wait-time.md) [~W] (simulation of office hours); [workload and skill limit teachers' data use](claims/teacher-data-use-obstacles-workload-habits-skills.md) [-W]
rows.change: Use automated outreach for reminders and routing, reserve mentor time for replies and for learners with repeated failure; set an alert budget from what mentors can answer and fit the threshold to it (a consecutive-failures rule is a reasonable first trigger); in the request queue, answer learners not yet helped before repeat requesters; give mentors time and training to read the data
rows.if: Mentor caseload is large or mentor hours are limited

rows.basis: [Chatbot outreach raised A/B grades](claims/chatbot-outreach-increases-ab-grades.md) [+M]; [no spillover or next-term effects](claims/chatbot-no-spillover-medium-term-effects.md) [~M]; [agentic SRL coaching raised strategy use in one K-12 trial](claims/agentic-srl-coaching-rct-86-significant-strategy-gain.md) [+W]; [high recommendation, no attitudinal effect](claims/chatbot-student-attitudes-null-survey-selective.md) [~M]
rows.change: Use chatbot outreach that links to whatever human help exists (tutoring, office hours) and expect course-specific, short-lived effects; let the AI prompt planning, monitoring and reflection, and judge it on learning, not on how much learners like it
rows.if: No mentor at all; automated or AI support only

rows.basis: [Unrestricted GPT-4 access harmed performance after withdrawal](claims/gpt4-access-harms-learning-after-withdrawal.md) [-M]; [help-seeking shifted toward answer-seeking within sessions](claims/within-session-hs-shifts-toward-closure-srl-increases.md) [~M]; [students valued weekly closed-book tests beside a self-paced AI block](claims/weekly-tests-ranked-accountability.md) [+W]; [office-hours and forum use fell as LLMs spread](claims/help-seeking-decline-then-rise-dura-semester.md) [~M]; [weak effort regulation went with AI dependency](claims/effort-regulation-buffers-help-seeking-predicts-ai-dependency.md) [~M]; hand-off rules untested
rows.change: Require an attempt before hints, include regular unaided checks (a short closed-book test), hand off to a person on repeated answer-seeking without progress, and track whether use of human help falls
rows.if: An AI tutor answers content questions

rows.basis: [Standard prediction models had unequal true-positive rates across subgroups](claims/baseline-ml-models-biased-tpr-oulad.md) [-M]
rows.change: Keep a person on judgments that certify competence, and audit any risk model's misses by subgroup before using it to decide who gets contact
rows.if: High stakes (licensure, certification)

rows.basis: [Career coaches appeared to expand exposure to and completion of health sciences programmes](claims/coaching-expanded-program-exposure-completion.md) [+M] (associational)
rows.change: Add career or programme coaching that connects learners to the programme's next steps, and evaluate it against a comparison group
rows.if: Health professions programme

rows.basis: [Probing feedback with revise-and-resubmit moved one candidate, not another](claims/probing-feedback-revise-resubmit-evidence.md) [~W]; [instructor access to work-in-progress enabled coaching](claims/web-folders-enable-coaching.md) [+W]
rows.change: Give probing feedback that asks for evidence from the learner's own students, with a required revise-and-resubmit, and expect uneven progress
rows.if: Teacher education with clinical or field assignments

rows.basis: [Peer monitoring went beyond social presence in MBA learners](claims/peer-monitoring-exceeds-social-presence.md) [+W]; [learner presence showed as intentions, metacognition and peer monitoring](claims/learner-presence-three-qualities-mba.md) [+W]
rows.change: Make contributing peers visible and give feedback that is professionally relevant; learners evaluate peers for what they offer
rows.if: Business programme (for example an accelerated online MBA)

rows.basis: [Online labs seemed more effective to students when instructors were present with scaffolds and probes](claims/online-labs-better-with-instructor-scaffolds.md) [+W]; [students recommended office hours over LLMs](claims/students-recommend-office-hours-over-llms.md) [+M]
rows.change: Put instructor or mentor scaffolds and probes in online labs, and keep human office hours alongside AI help
rows.if: Technology or computing courses with labs

rows.basis: [Only about 10% attended optional drop-in tutorials](claims/drop-in-tutorials-improve-p1y-marks.md) [~M]; [chatbot effects differed by gender in one course](claims/chatbot-gender-heterogeneity-microeconomics-women.md) [~M]; [voluntary chatbot use was bimodal](claims/chatbot-engagement-bimodal-continuous-versus-superficial-users.md) [~M]; [survey response differed across groups](claims/chatbot-student-attitudes-null-survey-selective.md) [~M]; [demographic predictors give mixed gains](claims/mixed-evidence-demographic-predictor-performance.md) [~W]; [alert systems serve marginalized students only with governance and human oversight](claims/ai-tools-potential-marginalized-students-contingent-safeguards.md) [~W]
rows.change: Make the first contact proactive for everyone, track uptake and outcomes by subgroup, and do not target outreach by group membership or add group variables to a risk model; check who answers any satisfaction survey before reading it
rows.if: Concern about equity of who uses help

rows.basis: [Design principle effects are moderated by pacing and complexity](claims/design-principle-effects-moderated-by-pacing-and-complexity.md) [+M]; [Pacing moderates the modality effect](claims/modality-effect-moderated-by-pacing.md) [+M]
rows.change: Apply the configuration rules strictly (words beside the picture, narration rather than printed text, no extras); the design principles matter more when learners cannot pause
rows.if: A system-paced video, lecture or narrated animation

rows.basis: [Pacing moderates the modality effect](claims/modality-effect-moderated-by-pacing.md) [~M]
rows.change: Keep the words printed next to the picture; do not convert them to narration, which showed no benefit (slightly negative) when learners set the pace
rows.if: Learner-paced pages, slides or a website

rows.basis: [Integration benefit is larger for high element-interactivity material](claims/element-interactivity-moderates-contiguity-effect.md) [+M]; [Integrating related elements gives a large average benefit for novices](claims/integration-of-related-elements-large-mean-effect.md) [+M]; [Pretraining improves transfer](claims/pretraining-improves-transfer.md) [+M] (one VR experiment)
rows.change: Integrate each label or sentence into the picture at the point it describes, present spoken words with the matching part of an animation, and name the parts briefly before the lesson
rows.if: Complex material: a process with many interacting parts, and learners new to it

rows.basis: [Integration benefits may reverse for more experienced learners](claims/expertise-reversal-split-attention-redundancy-review.md) [~M]; [Segmentation benefits shrink with expertise](claims/segmentation-benefits-shrink-with-expertise.md) [~M]; [The integrated-illustration benefit was stronger for low-experience students](claims/illustration-integration-effect-stronger-for-low-experience-learners.md) [~M]
rows.change: Cut explanatory text that repeats what the diagram shows, and reduce segmentation; check on a transfer item rather than assuming
rows.if: Learners already know the content well

rows.basis: [Spoken–written advantages are larger for L2 and nonfluent readers](claims/reader-fluency-prior-knowledge-moderate-redundancy.md) [+M]; [Verbal redundancy does not help when images or animation are included](claims/images-animation-eliminate-redundancy-benefit.md) [~M]
rows.change: Give the words both spoken and written
rows.if: Second-language readers or less fluent readers, and the material has no picture or animation

rows.basis: [Redundancy principle](claims/redundancy-principle-mayer-2008.md) [+M]; [Verbal redundancy does not help when images or animation are included](claims/images-animation-eliminate-redundancy-benefit.md) [~M]
rows.change: Remove the duplicated text, or keep only key terms beside the picture; keep captions where access requires them
rows.if: A narrated animation carries the full narration as on-screen text

rows.basis: [Captioning second-language videos produces large benefits](claims/captioning-second-language-videos-large-benefits.md) [+M]; [captioned video improved L2 listening, generalising to new sentences and speakers](claims/bimodal-captioned-input-improves-segmentation.md) [+W] (reported second-hand)
rows.change: Add captions in the target language
rows.if: Video in a second language, for language learners

rows.basis: [Coherence principle](claims/coherence-principle-irrelevant-material-hurts-learning.md) [+M]; [Interesting but irrelevant details can impair learning](claims/seductive-details-effect.md) [~M]
rows.change: Leave out what the explanation does not need, and replace decorative images with ones that show the relation being explained
rows.if: The brief asks for engaging extras: stock photos, background music, anecdotes

rows.basis: [Animation beats static pictures for identifying motions](claims/animation-beats-static-pictures-for-identifying-motions.md) [+M]; [a single picture beats animation for spatial arrangements](claims/single-picture-beats-animation-for-spatial-arrangements.md) [~M]; [animation advantage larger when system-paced](claims/animation-advantage-larger-system-paced.md) [~M] and [with auditory commentary](claims/animation-advantage-larger-auditory-commentary.md) [~M]; [Contiguity effects do not differ between static and dynamic presentation](claims/static-dynamic-presentation-no-moderation.md) [~M]
rows.change: Choose by what the learner must identify: an animation for how parts move, a single static picture for how they are arranged (not a strip of snapshots, which helped neither); if an animation is used, prefer it system-paced with spoken commentary. The integration rules apply equally to both
rows.if: The choice is between a static diagram and an animation

rows.basis: [Segmenting improves retention and transfer](claims/segmenting-improves-multimedia-learning.md) [+M]; [Segmentation increases learning time](claims/segmenting-increases-learning-time.md) [~M]
rows.change: Break it into meaningful segments with a pause or "next" between them; allow for more study time
rows.if: A long continuous presentation, and learners are new to the content

rows.basis: [Learner flow control over animations was rarely used](claims/flow-control-unused-no-learning-correlation.md) [~W]; [strategy guidance beat unguided learner control](claims/strategy-guidance-beats-unguided-learner-control-immediate.md) [+M] (immediate tests only)
rows.change: Build the pauses into the presentation, or tell learners when to pause and replay (after each step, when a term is new), rather than counting on them to use the controls unprompted
rows.if: The plan relies on learners using pause and replay controls

rows.basis: Rebetez et al., one experiment, no effect sizes printed: [transfer benefited from animation only for learners studying collaboratively](claims/collaboration-enables-transfer-benefit-of-animation.md) [~W]; [snapshots were marginally helpful alone and harmful in dyads](claims/snapshots-detrimental-in-dyads-beneficial-individually.md) [~W]
rows.change: Animation is more worth its cost here; avoid adding snapshot strips of the key steps for pairs
rows.if: Learners will study the animation in pairs or small groups

rows.basis: [Multimedia-only stories helped comprehension (g+ = 0.39); stories that also had interactive features did not](claims/multimedia-only-benefits-interactive-features-detrimental.md) [+M] (meta-analysis). The gain was larger in studies of children the authors classed as disadvantaged (g+ = 0.66): a difference reflecting circumstances, not a property of the children or a cause
rows.change: Keep animated illustrations, sound and music that match the story; leave out hotspots, games and other interactive features
rows.if: A digital storybook for young children

rows.basis: Fifth graders [studied videos faster than equivalent illustrated texts](claims/videos-studied-faster-than-illustrated-texts-fifth-graders.md) [~W], [most of all the slowest readers](claims/videos-especially-beneficial-slower-readers.md) [+W] (studying rate, not learning); with 255 university students, [medium had no effect on integrating complementary sources](claims/no-medium-context-effect-integration.md) [~M] and [videos took longer to process](claims/videos-longer-processing-time-than-texts.md) [~W] (d = 0.52)
rows.change: For children and slower readers, consider a narrated video, and check comprehension rather than assuming it; for university students integrating several sources, choose on access and time, since the medium made no difference to understanding
rows.if: Choosing between a video and an illustrated text

rows.basis: Educators' focus groups: [generated animations can drop a defining constraint](claims/anvil-pedagogical-mismatch-risk.md) [~W]; expert reviewers of generated lecture videos [flagged voice, reveal timing and layout](claims/bespoke-free-text-voice-reveal-layout-issues.md) [~W]. Neither measures learning
rows.change: Check before use that the picture keeps the concept's defining constraint, that the synthetic voice reads numbers and pauses correctly, and that each slide element appears when the narration reaches it
rows.if: Narration, animation or slides generated by an AI tool

rows.basis: Conflicting, as on the [modality principle](principles/modality.md): [the modality effect was larger with head-mounted displays](claims/modality-effect-stronger-in-virtual-reality.md) [~M], but in a VR experiment with 61 learners [printed text beat narration on recall](claims/vr-reverse-modality-effect-recall.md) [-M]; [pretraining before VR improved real-task transfer](claims/pretraining-improves-transfer.md) [+M]
rows.change: Do not assume narration wins: pilot spoken and short anchored printed text on the brief's own test. Name the equipment's parts before the VR session
rows.if: An immersive VR headset lesson

rows.basis: [Spoken–written advantages are larger for retention than transfer](claims/outcome-constructs-test-formats-moderate-redundancy.md) [~M]
rows.change: Expect smaller gains from adding written text to narration, and judge the configuration on a transfer item in step 5
rows.if: The outcome is transfer, not recall

rows.basis: Untested here. The [SRL synthesis](claims/srl-interventions-moderate-effect-online-blended.md) [+M] does not break results down by prior knowledge
rows.change: Put more of each week into the content strand, with worked examples and self-checks, and keep discussion tasks to applying what was just shown; give feedback on every early piece.
rows.if: Learners are `novice` in the content

rows.basis: [Template and organisation ratings](claims/course-template-supports-learner-presence.md) [+W] from one accelerated online MBA, descriptive; the rest is the earlier page's guidance
rows.change: Use their work as the discussion material (cases from their own settings), let them facilitate earlier, and keep the content strand short; keep the fixed structure.
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` or practitioners (an MBA, a professional course)

rows.basis: [Online community required deliberate, planned effort](claims/online-community-requires-conscious-effort.md) [+W] (interviews with high-school e-teachers); the actions are untested
rows.change: Plan every interaction and the community-building explicitly; schedule live contact; keep the weekly structure strict and contact families or a school mentor after a missed week.
rows.if: Learners are `adolescent` in a web-based school course

rows.basis: [Implementation intentions](claims/implementation-intentions-improve-goal-attainment.md) [+S] (the two field experiments were in large online courses); the rest is untested
rows.change: Replace teacher feedback on each piece with automatic feedback on self-checks, a weekly teacher summary of common errors, and peer review against a rubric; keep the week-1 if-then plan; give the teacher's time to learners flagged by a missed week.
rows.if: `online-self-paced` with rolling enrolment, or one teacher for hundreds of learners

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Give remote learners their own small groups, or mixed groups that all work in the same online space, rather than letting the room talk and the remote learners listen; one person watches the online channel in every live session; post every product online.
rows.if: Some learners join from a shared room while others are remote (hyflex), or a site group joins a remote teacher

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Keep each content segment short and downloadable, give transcripts, allow text or voice replies in discussion, and avoid tasks that need a large screen; make live sessions optional with a recording and a written summary.
rows.if: Phone-only learners or low bandwidth

rows.basis: [Discussion board produced no corrective feedback](claims/discussion-board-no-negative-feedback-synchrony-required.md) [~M], one second-language study carried to other subjects
rows.change: Use a short recorded or written teacher reply in week 1 instead of a call; put corrective feedback into written comments on each graded piece, since asynchronous boards may surface no correction.
rows.if: No live sessions possible (time zones, shift work)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Cut the cycle to one content block and one discussion task a week; shorten the opening contact to the first two days; keep feedback within 48 hours, since there is no time to recover a missed week. In a one-week or single-session module, drop the group progression and use one structured task with a shared product.
rows.if: Accelerated term (6–8 weeks) or a single short module

rows.basis: [Implementation intentions](claims/implementation-intentions-improve-goal-attainment.md) [+S] (MCII helped most when the obstacle was predictable, such as work or family obligations); [withdrawal reasons](claims/withdrawal-reasons-similar-across-modalities.md) [~M] were led by no stated reason, transfer and schedule conflict in one programme, and [dissatisfaction was rarely the stated reason](claims/dissatisfaction-not-primary-drop-reason.md) [~W]
rows.change: Publish the full term's due dates in week 1; make the if-then plan name a work or family obstacle; offer a reduced catch-up route after a missed week.
rows.if: Adults in work settings, studying around jobs and family

rows.basis: [Information-exchange prompts produced more transactive discourse](claims/information-exchange-prompts-higher-transactivity.md) [+W], one asynchronous teacher-PD design study; discourse, not learning or practice change, was measured
rows.change: Build discussion prompts around exchanging what each brings (a lesson they taught, student work, a resource from their setting) and responding to others', rather than private reflection on their own understanding; have the group produce something usable in their work.
rows.if: Learners are teachers or other practitioners in online professional development

rows.basis: [Collaborative learning largely disappeared in the 2020 shift to remote instruction](claims/remote-shift-reduced-collaborative-learning.md) [+W] (case studies of 29 courses); that redesign keeps it, and that keeping it helps, are untested
rows.change: Keep its collaborative activities by redesigning them for the online space (small online groups with a shared product and a deadline) rather than replacing them with individual quizzes; put the fixed weekly structure in place first.
rows.if: A face-to-face course is moving online at short notice

rows.basis: [Interactivity, information sharing and a collaborative environment were associated with perceived social presence](claims/affordances-positive-social-presence-agentic-ai.md) [~W] in one survey (N = 398, structural model); perceived presence is not learning, and nothing in the wiki tests an AI agent inside this pattern
rows.change: Give it tasks that are interactive and that share information with the learner and the group, keep the human teacher's contact in week 1 and on graded work, and measure learning on the representative task, not learners' sense of presence.
rows.if: The course uses an AI agent or chatbot as a tutor, assistant or discussion partner

rows.basis: [Instructor face in lecture video showed no significant learning difference](claims/human-embodiment-video-presence-effects.md) [~W] (narrative review's second-hand report; not an equivalence test)
rows.change: Spend on short segments with questions after each rather than on filming the teacher; a face on screen is optional, and a short personal welcome video in week 1 can carry the social contact.
rows.if: Video production budget is small, or the brief asks for the teacher on camera in every video

rows.basis: [Implementation intentions](claims/implementation-intentions-improve-goal-attainment.md) [~S]: no effect on completion for learners in collectivist cultures in the field experiments
rows.change: Do not rely on the if-then plan alone; add the week-1 contact and early follow-up on missed weeks, and record completion by group.
rows.if: Learners from collectivist cultures, or the course depends on completion for its funding

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Give each week's page in plain language, a short video walk-through of the structure in week 1, sentence starters and model posts, and private channels for questions; let first contributions be in small groups, not the whole class.
rows.if: Learners with low confidence, reading difficulty or a first language other than the course's

rows.basis: [Discussion board produced no corrective feedback](claims/discussion-board-no-negative-feedback-synchrony-required.md) [~M]
rows.change: Hold a weekly synchronous session (text chat or video) for practice with correction; use the board for reflection and preparation.
rows.if: A language course, or any goal where errors must be corrected

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Make the group products build towards it across the term, with drafts reviewed by peers and the teacher, and plan a live or recorded presentation to the audience in the final week; keep individual assessment of each learner's part.
rows.if: The course ends in a product or performance for a real audience (a client, a public showcase)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Assess the representative task individually and under conditions close to the real one; do not count discussion participation towards more than a small share of the grade; report completion beside achievement.
rows.if: High stakes: a credential, licensure or a programme-required course

rows.basis: [Blended and online against face-to-face](claims/blended-learning-improves-outcomes.md) [~M]: the blended advantage came with extra time and resources; [taking a course online lowered grades in it and in later courses](claims/online-course-lower-grades-current-and-future.md) [~M] and [reduced progress in college](claims/online-course-taking-reduces-college-success.md) [~M] in one instrumental-variables study, [an estimate local to students with both options](claims/online-course-effects-local-to-dual-option-students.md) [~M]
rows.change: Record what besides the mode changed (time, materials, assessment, teacher) and compare like with like; do not credit the format with a gain, and do not assume parity either: where learners can choose, track their grades in later courses as well as this one, and keep an in-person route for learners who are falling behind online.
rows.if: The course is to be compared with its face-to-face version

rows.basis: [Interdependence type did not affect achievement](claims/interdependence-type-no-achievement-effect-asynchronous.md) [-M]; [reward interdependence raised positive attitudes to group work](claims/reward-interdependence-benefit-attitudes.md) [~M], both one experiment with undergraduate business majors
rows.change: Use a group product and a task that needs everyone's input; use roles to organise, not as the source of learning, and grade individual performance.
rows.if: Group work is required and the brief proposes roles or a group grade to make it work

rows.basis: [The PAIR-C study](claims/pair-c-scaffolding-shows-mixed-evidence-for-emergent-phenomena-instruction.md) [~M]: this population and domain, near transfer only
rows.change: Run the default arc as given, with the NetLogo moths and mice; add step 7 if they must teach recognizing emergence to pupils.
rows.if: Learners are pre-service or practicing teachers (`adult`, `postsecondary`) learning natural selection

rows.basis: Untested: the study's population was adults; [guidance in simulations](claims/guidance-improves-inquiry-learning-outcomes.md) [+M] reports age as a moderator without saying which way on its claim page
rows.change: Keep the five dimensions but give each one a question in plain words and a picture; use one simulation per session; the teacher runs a demonstration run before learners take over.
rows.if: Learners are `adolescent` (secondary science) or younger

rows.basis: [Guidance in inquiry](claims/guidance-improves-inquiry-learning-outcomes.md) [+M], across inquiry studies, not this pattern
rows.change: Add a 10-minute guided run of the interface before step 4; keep a prompt for every dimension through session 2; state the correct account at the end of session 1 rather than waiting for learners to reach it.
rows.if: Learners are `novice` in the domain and with simulations

rows.basis: Untested proposal; [the PAIR-C study](claims/pair-c-scaffolding-shows-mixed-evidence-for-emergent-phenomena-instruction.md) [~M] found no far transfer without it; [comparing analogous cases](claims/comparing-contrasting-cases-improves-learning.md) [+M] carried from negotiation cases; [simulation games](claims/simulation-near-transfer-robust-far-transfer-weak.md) [~W] support near transfer, far transfer less robust
rows.change: Do not stop after the target domain: add session 4's side-by-side comparison with a second, unrelated phenomenon, and test on a third.
rows.if: The goal is recognizing the same structure in other phenomena (`far-transfer`)

rows.basis: Untested; follows from the framework's own scope
rows.change: Do not use PAIR-C; use the sequential column alone as an explanation frame, or a worked causal chain.
rows.if: The phenomenon is a sequential process (digestion, a production line)

rows.basis: [Instruction that confronts misconceptions](claims/misconceptions-interfere-with-new-learning.md) [+S], science and reading studies, not this pattern
rows.change: Use those exact sentences as the misconceptions in step 6 and as the sequential column in step 3.
rows.if: Learners' reported errors are given ("the moths changed color to hide")

rows.basis: Untested
rows.change: Keep them; map each of the brief's categories to the dimension it violates rather than replacing them with the study's nine categories.
rows.if: The brief names its own misconception categories, rubric or explanation template

rows.basis: Untested; the tested package bundled annotations, prompts and feedback, so no single feature is isolated
rows.change: Keep it; change only what the evidence says matters: the side-by-side emergent/sequential contrast and one dimension-framed prompt per run.
rows.if: The brief names its own routine (its worksheet, prompts or exit ticket)

rows.basis: [Contingent scaffolding](claims/contingent-scaffolding-improves-learning.md) [~M]: evidence mostly from one-to-one tutoring, and the claim page notes that contingency across 30 students is hard
rows.change: Prepare a card per expected misconception with the dimension it violates and the correcting sentence; circulate during step 4 and answer from the cards; collect written explanations to read between sessions.
rows.if: One teacher for 25–35 learners

rows.basis: Untested; [guidance in simulations](claims/guidance-improves-inquiry-learning-outcomes.md) [+M] found the effect independent of guidance type
rows.change: Put the dimension prompts and the misconception cards inside the simulation worksheet so learners self-check; spend the facilitator's minutes only on learners whose rewritten explanation still has a controlling agent.
rows.if: Scarce facilitator time (a busy teacher, a short check-in)

rows.basis: [Guidance in simulations](claims/guidance-improves-inquiry-learning-outcomes.md) [+M], reported second-hand; untested for this pattern
rows.change: Embed one prompt per dimension in the simulation page; require a written prediction before each run; show a model five-dimension explanation after the learner submits theirs; offer the misconception cards as feedback keyed to common answers.
rows.if: `online-self-paced`, no teacher

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Use one simulation shared on screen by the teacher with learners calling the settings; remote learners write explanations in a shared document; on phones, use a short video of runs with the agent-level events marked instead of the live model.
rows.if: Mixed mode: some learners remote, some in the room; or phone-only

rows.basis: Untested; minutes are proposals
rows.change: Steps 1–6 in one session: elicit 5, dimensions on ants 8, contrast table 7, simulation with prompts 25, rewrite and correct 15; name in the plan that near transfer is the most this session can aim at.
rows.if: `single-session` only (about 60 minutes)

rows.basis: Untested
rows.change: Elicit 3, contrast table with the dimensions 7, one 10-minute run with prompts, rewrite 5; drop the ant example and the second case.
rows.if: A fixed short time budget (20–30 minutes)

rows.basis: Untested
rows.change: Learners say or draw their explanations; the contrast table uses icons (one arrow from a controller against many small arrows); misconceptions are corrected in a private exchange, not in front of the class.
rows.if: Low confidence or low literacy

rows.basis: Untested
rows.change: The learner decides who sees their explanation; the aim is to explain the mechanism the scientific account proposes, not to require assent; correct the model, not the learner's beliefs.
rows.if: The topic touches beliefs learners hold privately (evolution, for some learners)

rows.basis: Untested
rows.change: Assess with one whole explanation of a new phenomenon scored on the five dimensions, not split into separate items per dimension.
rows.if: A whole-task performance the brief wants kept whole (explaining an unseen phenomenon, teaching a mini-lesson)

rows.basis: Untested
rows.change: Have them build the contrast table and misconception cards for their pupils as the product; the audience is the class they will teach.
rows.if: A product for a real audience (pre-service teachers designing a lesson for pupils)

rows.basis: Untested; the study measured immediate gains only
rows.change: Test at the delay that matters on new items, including a far-transfer phenomenon; do not reuse the practice simulations.
rows.if: High stakes, or assessment weeks later

rows.basis: [Peer discussion improves conceptual understanding](claims/peer-discussion-improves-conceptual-understanding.md) [+M]
rows.change: Run the full cycle: individual vote, discussion of reasons, revote, isomorphic question alone, instructor explanation
rows.if: A lecture course with a polling system and conceptual content

rows.basis: [Peer discussion improves conceptual understanding](claims/peer-discussion-improves-conceptual-understanding.md) [+M]
rows.change: Keep both; the recorded comparison found the combination ahead of either alone
rows.if: Time pressure tempts the instructor to skip either discussion or explanation

rows.basis: [Higher-order clicker questions improve lower-order exam performance](claims/hocs-clickers-improve-locs-exam-performance.md) [+M]
rows.change: Write questions at application or analysis level rather than recall
rows.if: The exam has higher-order items

rows.basis: [Follow-up homework modestly boosts exam performance](claims/follow-up-homework-modestly-boosts-exam-performance.md) [+W]; [Clicker participation does not help the lowest quartile](claims/any-clicker-pattern-beats-absence-except-lowest-quartile.md) [~W]
rows.change: Add a short take-home reflection asking learners to explain the discussed question; completing it went with better performance on related exam items
rows.if: The lowest-performing students are a concern

rows.basis: [Correct-correct pattern predicts higher exam performance](claims/correct-correct-clicker-pattern-higher-exam-performance.md) [~W]
rows.change: Treat switchers as not yet secure; give an isomorphic item later, since only correct-correct students outperformed on related exam items
rows.if: Many learners switch to the correct answer on the revote

rows.basis: [Classroom quizzing improves exam performance](claims/classroom-quizzing-improves-exam-performance-across-grades-and-content.md) [+W]
rows.change: Expect some benefit from answering alone, but do not credit it to discussion; it is a different design
rows.if: The brief wants clicker questions without discussion, to save time

rows.basis: [Content gains but no reasoning gains](claims/reformed-pedagogy-content-gains-but-no-reasoning-gains.md) [~W]
rows.change: Add explicit reasoning instruction and a reasoning measure; concept-question practice did not move a reasoning test in one course series
rows.if: The goal includes general scientific reasoning

rows.basis: [Learning attributed to discussion, not technology](claims/learning-attributed-to-process-not-technology.md) [+W]; [Students saw fun and variation as the main impact](claims/clickers-fun-variation-over-learning.md) [~W]
rows.change: Say what the discussion is for; learners liked the routine and credited learning to the discussion rather than the device, but rated fun above learning
rows.if: Learners are pre-service teachers or others who may see clickers as a game

rows.basis: [Poor group leadership undermined discussion](claims/cooperative-conceptual-change-chemistry-misconceptions.md) [~W]
rows.change: Ask each member for a reason before the revote and vary groups; poor group leadership has been reported to cut discussion short
rows.if: Groups form freely and one member tends to decide

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Explain or pose a simpler bridging question before discussion, rather than discussing a shared misconception
rows.if: Fewer than about a third answer correctly on the first vote

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Explain briefly and move to a harder or changed question
rows.if: Nearly everyone answers correctly on the first vote

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Use the poll for the votes and breakout rooms of two or three for discussion, with the isomorphic item answered alone in the poll
rows.if: The class runs live online (`online-instructor-led`)

rows.basis: Untested proposal; the [Peer Learning principle](principles/peer-learning.md) carries the same caution
rows.change: Do not ask them to teach unstudied material. Teach it to the class first (or study a worked example together), then run the routine on it with an answer key on each card, so the partner can check.
rows.if: Learners are `novice` and meeting the material for the first time

rows.basis: [Older peers as tutors support gains for older and younger students](claims/tutoring-and-cross-age-peer-tutors-effective.md) [+W] (a narrative policy review, no data printed); limit: [cross-age tutoring showed no effect on oral proficiency](claims/cross-level-peer-tutoring-null-oral-proficiency.md) [~M]
rows.change: Use cross-level or cross-age pairs: the learner ahead teaches with a role card that makes them question rather than tell, and gets harder material to prepare. Check the taught learner alone, not only the pair.
rows.if: Some learners are well ahead (`advanced`) or the school can use older pupils

rows.basis: [K-PALS on Rapid Letter Sounds](claims/pals-k-pals-significant-rapid-letter-sound-gains.md) [+M] (2,959 kindergarten pupils in 67 schools; significant for workshop, booster and helper conditions alike); [PALS on first-grade literacy](claims/pals-strong-evidence-first-grade-literacy-es-023.md) [+M] (three studies, 1,501 pupils, average effect +0.23); fluency and comprehension effects in first grade were not significant ([three domains](claims/pals-wwc-effectiveness-ratings-three-domains.md) [~M])
rows.change: Use a short scripted routine on sounds and words with turn-taking and a simple correction move, three or more times a week, and train teachers with a workshop before starting.
rows.if: Kindergarten or first grade, early reading (letter sounds, decoding)

rows.basis: [Comprehension, learners with learning disabilities](claims/pals-potentially-positive-reading-comprehension-ld.md) [~M] (two trials, 40 and 20 pupils; effect sizes 0.60 and 0.91, neither significant); [fluency](claims/pals-potentially-positive-reading-fluency-ld.md) [~M]; [significant for the full sample, not the disability subsets](claims/pals-full-sample-significant-ld-subset-not.md) [~M]
rows.change: Keep the routine for reading, but do not rely on it alone: check each learner's comprehension and fluency individually every two weeks (proposal) and add adult-led small-group teaching for those not moving.
