rows.if: Learners with learning disabilities, in reading

rows.basis: [PALS showed no discernible effects on mathematics for learners with learning disabilities](claims/pals-no-discernible-math-effects-ld.md) [~M] (one trial, 40 pupils in grades 2–4); the mathematics peer-tutoring meta-analysis in [Peer Tutoring Improves Achievement](claims/peer-tutoring-improves-achievement.md) [+S] is across learners generally
rows.change: Do not expect the peer routine to carry it; keep explicit teacher instruction as the main route and use peer practice only for fluency on steps already taught, with an answer key.
rows.if: The goal is mathematics for learners with learning disabilities

rows.basis: [Nonresponders: PALS against adult tutoring, comprehension](claims/pals-mcmaster-comprehension-negative-effect.md) [-M] (41 first graders; effect −0.31, not significant); [alphabetics](claims/pals-first-grade-alphabetics-indeterminate-versus-adult-tutoring.md) [~M] and [fluency](claims/pals-fluency-no-significant-effects-first-grade.md) [~M] showed no difference
rows.change: Prefer one-to-one or small-group teaching by an adult for the skill they missed; keep the peer routine for practice, not as the intervention.
rows.if: Learners have already not responded to class-wide teaching (nonresponders)

rows.basis: [PALS for English learners](claims/pals-potentially-positive-reading-effects-ells.md) [~M] (99 pupils in grades 3–6, combined effect 0.31, no single measure significant); [Peer Tutoring and Response Groups on English language development](claims/peer-tutoring-response-groups-positive-eld-effects.md) [+M] (three trials); limit: [oral proficiency null](claims/cross-level-peer-tutoring-null-oral-proficiency.md) [~M]
rows.change: Run the routine on reading with roles in English and allow explanation in the first language where content is the goal; check oral language separately, since pairing alone may not move it.
rows.if: English learners

rows.basis: [PALS comprehension, Fuchs et al. 1997](claims/pals-potentially-positive-comprehension-effect-adolescent.md) [~M] (120 pupils, average age 9.8 despite the claim's "adolescent" label; 0.48, not significant after clustering); [Reciprocal Teaching Improves Reading Comprehension](claims/reciprocal-teaching-improves-reading-comprehension.md) [~M] (16 studies; much larger on experimenter-made than standardised tests)
rows.change: Use the comprehension activities (retell, shrink the paragraph to its main idea, predict and check) with learners leading in turn, after the teacher has modelled each. Measure on a new passage, not only the taught ones.
rows.if: Upper elementary or older learners, reading comprehension

rows.basis: Untested; carried from [Learning By Teaching Improves Tutor Learning](claims/learning-by-teaching-improves-tutor-learning.md) [+S], whose studies are not described on the claim page by age or setting
rows.change: Each colleague prepares one procedure or case, teaches it to another who must perform it or decide a variant, then they swap; the check is a short case decision made alone.
rows.if: Adults in work settings (staff teaching each other a procedure or case)

rows.basis: [Structured Peer Tutoring Outperforms Unstructured](claims/structured-peer-tutoring-outperforms-unstructured.md) [+M]; the sampling rule is an untested proposal
rows.change: Put the structure in the role cards and answer keys, not the adult: the adult samples two or three pairs a round, corrects the commonest error for everyone, and reads only the individual checks.
rows.if: `classroom` with one teacher for 25–30 learners, or scarce facilitator time (volunteers, a busy shift, one tutor dropping in)

rows.basis: Untested proposal; the tested contrast (teaching against studying) sets no duration ([Learning By Teaching Improves Tutor Learning](claims/learning-by-teaching-improves-tutor-learning.md) [+S])
rows.change: One cycle: 3 minutes to study the part, 5 to prepare, two 7-minute teaching turns with roles swapped, 5 for the individual check, 3 for the teacher's correction to the class. Report only immediate performance.
rows.if: A single session only, or a fixed short budget (for example 30 minutes)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Pair remote with remote and room with room, or give mixed pairs a shared document and an audio channel; time the teaching turns on a visible clock, since an untimed peer step is the one dropped.
rows.if: Mixed modes: some learners remote, some in the room

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Each learner records a 1–2 minute voice note or short text teaching one part; an assigned partner must reply within two days with an attempt and one question; the first learner answers. The individual check stays a short quiz the learner takes alone.
rows.if: `online-self-paced` or phone-only, no live session

rows.basis: Untested proposal; [teachers and pupils reported favourable impressions of PALS](claims/pals-favorable-teacher-student-impressions.md) [+M] (surveys, no learning measure)
rows.change: Pair with a trusted partner, let them rehearse their part privately first, allow teaching by showing or pointing, give sentence starters on the card, and keep the first weeks unassessed.
rows.if: Learners with low confidence, low literacy, or anxious about speaking

rows.basis: Untested proposal; training from [Structured Peer Tutoring Outperforms Unstructured](claims/structured-peer-tutoring-outperforms-unstructured.md) [+M]
rows.change: Keep it as given and run the teaching session on it; change only one thing the evidence says matters: train the roles once with a modelled error, or add the partner's attempt before the next step, or add one individual check.
rows.if: The brief names its own routine, script, rubric or categories (its own check-in, correction prompt, PALS manual)

rows.basis: [Teachers were least favourable towards PALS team components](claims/pals-favorable-teacher-student-impressions.md) [~M] (announcing the winning team, the point structure); group rewards were linked to larger effects in [peer-assisted learning](claims/peer-assisted-learning-improves-achievement.md) [~M]
rows.change: Keep points tied to each learner's own check if the brief wants them; drop the announcement of a winning team if teachers find it costly.
rows.if: A team or points competition is part of the brief

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: The learner controls what is shared and with whom: teach the concept on a neutral or invented example; each learner applies it to their own case privately.
rows.if: Material is private or sensitive (personal histories, health, incidents at work)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: The partner watches the whole performance and then asks and corrects against the brief's criteria (one strength, one change, one question), rather than splitting it into parts to teach.
rows.if: A whole-task performance the brief wants kept whole (a presentation, a clinical encounter, a lesson taught)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Use the partner as the rehearsal audience: each learner teaches or performs to a partner who asks what that audience would ask, before the real event.
rows.if: Learners will perform for a real audience (clients, a family, a public event)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Keep peer correction formative; grade only the individual check or product; record which explanations the teacher corrected.
rows.if: High stakes, or grades depend on the work

rows.basis: The randomized trial was in elementary schools: [fewer referrals](claims/swpbis-reduces-office-discipline-referrals.md) [+M], [less disruptive behaviour](claims/swpbis-reduces-disruptive-behavior.md) [+M] (ES 0.12), [strongest for children first exposed in kindergarten](claims/swpbis-strongest-kindergarten-exposure.md) [+M]; [clear behaviour expectations](claims/clear-behavior-expectations-strong-evidence-14-studies.md) [+M] (K–5, teacher-delivered); the token and fade are untested
rows.change: Picture-based setting matrix; teach each setting in place with role-play; frequent specific praise and a simple class-wide token, faded to intermittent praise by the second term. Start in kindergarten and keep the system running across grades; expect fewer referrals and small changes in teacher-rated behaviour over years, not a quick drop.
rows.if: Elementary school, `child` learners (K–5)

rows.basis: [Autonomy support](claims/autonomy-supports-intrinsic-motivation.md) [+S] and [rewards and interest](claims/rewards-undermine-intrinsic-motivation.md) [~S], carried from task-interest studies to school behaviour systems; the randomized trial's results are from elementary schools and are carried here untested
rows.change: Students co-write the expectations and the matrix; acknowledgment by specific verbal recognition, privileges and positive contact home rather than tokens; add self-monitoring early.
rows.if: Secondary school, `adolescent` learners

rows.basis: [Effects greatest for at-risk and high-risk children](claims/swpbis-effects-greatest-at-risk-high-risk-children.md) [+M]; [fewer referrals for at-risk children](claims/swpbis-reduces-odr-at-risk-high-risk.md) [+M]; [fewer special-education referrals](claims/swpbis-reduces-special-education-referral-at-risk.md) [+M] (one trial, elementary schools; the timing rule is untested)
rows.change: Run the universal tier first and fully; expect it to do most for these students; read Tier 2 nominations after a term of it rather than from the baseline list; track referrals, special-education referrals and counselling use for this group.
rows.if: Many students already rated at-risk or high-risk at baseline (a high-need school)

rows.basis: [Slower growth in teacher-rated bullying](claims/swpbis-reduces-growth-teacher-reported-bullying.md) [+M] and [rejection](claims/swpbis-reduces-growth-peer-rejection.md) [+M]; [both still rose in both conditions](claims/bullying-rejection-increase-approaching-middle-school.md) [~M]; adding a bullying programme is untested
rows.change: Keep the universal tier school-wide and start it in the earliest grades; expect bullying and rejection to grow more slowly rather than fall; add a programme aimed at bullying if the target is a decline.
rows.if: The target includes bullying or peer rejection

rows.basis: [Externalizing and total problems fell](claims/pbis-reduces-externalizing-total-problems-ed-self-contained.md) [+M] and [fidelity interacted with change](claims/tkss-fidelity-ancova-interaction-problem-behavior.md) [+M]: one pre-post study of 37 students, no comparison group
rows.change: Start with Tier 3: function-based plans tied to IEP goals; train the classroom teachers and check their skill in the practices before judging the plan.
rows.if: Students with emotional or behavioural disabilities in self-contained classes

rows.basis: [Suspensions did not differ in the randomized trial](claims/swpbis-no-effect-suspensions.md) [-M]; [suspension rates fell within SWPBIS schools and not within comparison schools, without the two being tested against each other](claims/swpbis-reduced-suspensions-not-comparisons.md) [~W]; [three-tier fidelity and fewer out-of-school suspensions](claims/pbis-three-tiers-fidelity-fewer-oss-pandemic.md) [+M] (one quasi-experiment, 2020–21); [severe sanctions less responsive](claims/exclusion-type-moderates-intervention-effect.md) [~M] (school-based programmes in general, not PBIS alone)
rows.change: Build Tier 3 in year 1 alongside the universal tier; set a written rule that suspension requires a team review of the student's data and plan; expect milder exclusions and referrals to fall first; compare against a school or year without PBIS, not only against the school's own baseline.
rows.if: The target is fewer out-of-school suspensions or permanent exclusions

rows.basis: [Empathic discipline](claims/brief-intervention-empathic-discipline-cuts-suspensions.md) [+M] (middle-school maths teachers); [tracking data by group](claims/exclusionary-discipline-harms-and-disproportionality.md) [+W]; in the randomized trial [sex and special-education status did not moderate the effects on bullying and rejection](claims/swpbis-main-effects-robust-across-demographics.md) [~M] (a null interaction, not a test of equal effects), so PBIS alone is not shown to narrow a gap
rows.change: Disaggregate every monthly review; write observable definitions for subjective referral categories; give all teachers the brief empathic-discipline exercise; set a target for the gap, not only the total.
rows.if: Discipline falls unevenly across student groups

rows.basis: [School-level reading and maths proficiency gains did not differ in the randomized trial](claims/swpbis-no-significant-achievement-effect.md) [~M] (37 schools; gains tended to favour SWPBIS schools, not significantly); [fewer socially-emotionally skilled children were held back a grade](claims/swpbis-reduces-grade-retention-skilled.md) [+M] (one of four baseline classes); [school-based programmes reduced exclusion by a small amount](claims/school-based-interventions-small-significant-reduction-exclusion.md) [+M]; the pairing is untested
rows.change: Pair PBIS with an academic intervention and measure each separately; do not report achievement as a PBIS outcome.
rows.if: The goal includes achievement

rows.basis: [Universal classroom management](claims/universal-classroom-management-reduces-problem-behavior.md) [+M]; [positive greetings at the door](claims/positive-greetings-at-the-door-improve-engagement.md) [+M] (middle school)
rows.change: Run the universal tier in one room: three to five posted expectations, taught in the first week, a greeting at the door, specific praise, a short consistent correction; keep a simple tally of incidents.
rows.if: One teacher, no school-wide system

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Keep Check In/Check Out to 2–3 minutes at each end of the day with a fixed adult; let teachers rate the card in seconds per period; review cards weekly in a 15-minute slot; reserve counsellor time for Tier 3.
rows.if: Scarce adult time (a mentor with a busy shift, volunteers, one counsellor for many students)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Do not attempt the full pattern; use the day to read the data, agree the expectations and setting matrix, and schedule the first week's lessons and the first monthly review.
rows.if: A single session or one training day only

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: First week: two 10-minute lessons for the two settings with most referrals; afterwards one 10-minute booster a week, rotating settings by the data.
rows.if: A fixed short time budget for teaching expectations (for example 10 minutes a week)

rows.basis: Untested; [Tier 1 fidelity showed no effect in the pandemic year](claims/pbis-tier1-fidelity-no-effect-pandemic-disciplinary-exclusions.md) [~M], when much schooling was remote
rows.change: Add an online setting to the matrix (camera, chat, turn-taking); acknowledge in chat or by message home; run check-in and check-out by message or short call; count remote incidents in the data.
rows.if: `mixed` mode: some students remote, some in the room, or phone-only

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page
rows.change: Emphasise predictable routines and one trusted adult; teach regulation skills beside the expectations; picture or spoken versions of the matrix; correct privately.
rows.if: Students with trauma histories, or low confidence or literacy

rows.basis: Untested proposal; the claims here are with school students
rows.change: Co-write a short set of norms with the group, acknowledge informally, and handle repeated problems individually; drop tokens and tiers of points.
rows.if: Adults in work or adult-education settings

rows.basis: Untested proposal; [three-tier fidelity](claims/pbis-three-tiers-fidelity-fewer-oss-pandemic.md) [+M] for the last change
rows.change: Keep it. Change only what the evidence bears on: make the expectations positively stated and taught, make acknowledgment specific, read fidelity before outcomes, and add the intensive tier if it is missing.
rows.if: The brief names its own routine (the school's existing rules, point card, referral form or fidelity tool)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Use its words in the expectations and matrix; do not substitute "safe, respectful, responsible" if the school already has three values.
rows.if: The school's own categories or criteria for behaviour (its referral categories, its values)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Keep individual data and plans to the team and family; show staff only setting-level data; let the student and family decide what the daily card says and who sees it.
rows.if: Behaviour data or plans concern sensitive matters (disability, trauma, family circumstances)

rows.basis: [Prior knowledge moderated which scaffold helped](claims/prior-knowledge-moderates-scaffolding-effectiveness.md) [~M]; [agents as coaches most useful for novices](claims/agents-most-effective-novice-learners.md) [~M]; [overheard dialogue beat monologue](claims/pal-dialogue-beats-monologue-recall-reasoning.md) [+W] (one experiment, reported in a review)
rows.change: Start with a modelled example, shown as a dialogue rather than a narration, and rubric prompts; move to self-assessment and reflection phases only after they meet the standard on a new scenario
rows.if: Learners are novices in this kind of encounter (`novice`)

rows.basis: [Reflection phases did more at higher education levels](claims/prior-knowledge-moderates-scaffolding-effectiveness.md) [~M]
rows.change: Drop the worked example, use harder scenarios with complications, and put the time into reflection after each attempt
rows.if: Learners are experienced practitioners (`advanced`)

rows.basis: [Teachable agent improved fourth-graders' gains](claims/ta-improves-basic-and-added-value-gains-fourth-grade.md) [+M]; carried from one quasi-experiment; [prep time, curriculum alignment and teacher confidence are reported barriers to K-12 simulations](claims/teacher-time-confidence-barriers-simulation-implementation.md) [-W] (teachers' reports, via a review)
rows.change: Use a teachable agent inside the regular curriculum, not as a separate activity; give teachers planning time, a curriculum map and a rehearsal of their own before the first lesson
rows.if: Learners are school-age, rehearsing by teaching

rows.basis: [Teachers describe AI companions as a low-stakes rehearsal space but tie acceptability to age](claims/ai-companion-rehearsal-space-struggling-students.md) [~W]; [primary teachers worry about AI reliability, age appropriateness and over-reliance](claims/teacher-constraints-responsible-ai-integration.md) [-W]; [teachers' most common concern is that agreeable companions remove the friction through which adolescents learn to sustain relationships](claims/agreeable-companions-remove-developmental-friction.md) [-W]; teachers' views, not outcomes
rows.change: Keep it a supervised, bounded rehearsal with an adult debrief; set age limits locally, and check the tool's reliability before pupils use it; have the character disagree, refuse and disappoint as a real peer would rather than please, and move the rehearsal on to people
rows.if: School-age learners would practise social or emotional situations with an AI character

rows.basis: [High-competency companion improved application](claims/high-competency-pal-improves-application.md) [+M]; [low-competency companion raised self-efficacy](claims/low-competency-pal-raises-self-efficacy.md) [~M]; one experiment with undergraduates, the sequence untested
rows.change: Pair a peer-level companion for early confidence-building sessions with a more competent one, or a stronger model, for sessions aimed at application; measure self-efficacy and performance separately
rows.if: The goal is confidence in the task as well as skill, and the simulated person is a fellow learner or companion

rows.basis: [Communication gained least from simulation](claims/simulation-effects-vary-by-complex-skill.md) [~M]; [MPathic-VR OSCE transfer](claims/mpathic-vr-osce-composite-transfer.md) [+M]
rows.change: Plan more attempts and richer feedback than for technical skills; rate the outcome with a human, blind to condition
rows.if: The goal is communication or interpersonal skill

rows.basis: [AI simulation inferior to SP for breast self-examination](claims/ai-simulation-inferior-bse-skills.md) [-M]; [limited effects for tactile skills](claims/ai-simulation-short-term-gains-nursing.md) [~M]; [AI mannequins mixed for psychomotor skills, LLM partners strongest for communication](claims/genai-llm-strongest-evidence-cognitive-communication.md) [~M]; [face-to-face simulation adds embodiment](claims/real-world-simulations-embodiment-affordances.md) [~M]
rows.change: Practise that component with a human standardized patient or a physical model, not an AI or screen-based person
rows.if: The goal includes a hands-on or physical-examination skill

rows.basis: [Multi-agent SP did not change diagnostic accuracy](claims/no-diagnostic-accuracy-difference.md) [~M]
rows.change: Score reasoning separately and add reasoning-specific practice; do not expect the conversational practice to carry it
rows.if: The goal is diagnostic or clinical reasoning as well as conversation

rows.basis: [High-information feedback outperforms corrective feedback](claims/feedback-improves-learning.md) [~S]; [feedback without reasons judged insufficient](claims/simucase-feedback-insufficient.md) [-M]; [learners value repeatable practice and recorded review](claims/learners-value-repeatable-practice-question-gaps.md) [~M]; [completers rated a self-service AI trainer engaging and easy to use](claims/sophie2-high-perceived-usability-and-value.md) [+W] (feasibility, not learning)
rows.change: Build specific, rubric-referenced feedback and a written debrief prompt into every attempt; allow unlimited low-stakes repeats; add a mentor review of a recorded encounter at the end of each scenario family
rows.if: Online, self-paced, no live facilitator (`online-self-paced`)

rows.basis: [An LLM assessor agreed with human raters about as well as individual human raters](claims/llm-assessor-agrees-with-human-raters-3e.md) [+M] (one validation, one rubric); the division of mentor time is untested
rows.change: Use an automated assessor for formative scoring of every attempt, and spend mentor time on the debrief of selected recordings and on the transfer rating
rows.if: Mentors or faculty have little time

rows.basis: [Large first-to-second run-through improvement](claims/mpathic-vr-repeat-runthrough-improvement.md) [+M]; [repetition did not transfer to a new task](claims/task-repetition-fluency-complexity-same-task-only.md) [~M]
rows.change: Run at least one baseline encounter, feedback and debrief, and a repeat; tell learners the gain on the repeat will be larger than on a new scenario
rows.if: Time is short (one session)

rows.basis: [Longer simulations associated with larger effects](claims/longer-simulation-duration-higher-effects.md) [+M]
rows.change: Spread scenarios over sessions and vary them; longer total practice is associated with larger effects
rows.if: Time allows several sessions

rows.basis: [Larger advantage over passive than active teaching](claims/vp-passive-versus-active-comparison.md) [~M]; [VPs better for skills, not knowledge](claims/vp-traditional-skills-advantage.md) [+M]
rows.change: Replace the passive component with simulated-person practice; expect less from replacing an active one
rows.if: A traditional, lecture-based component is being replaced

rows.basis: untested proposal; [human or conventional cases were sometimes rated more authentic](claims/genai-virtual-patient-short-term-gains-mixed.md) [~M]
rows.change: Use the simulated person for practice; keep the decision on a rated performance with a human standardized patient or examiner, and on the transfer probe
rows.if: Stakes are high (certification, licensure, a practical exam)

rows.basis: [AI practice reported as lowering foreign language anxiety](claims/ai-reduces-fl-anxiety-private-practice.md) [+M]; [nursing learners valued safe, repeatable, nonjudgmental AI practice](claims/ai-simulation-safe-practice-environments.md) [+W] (qualitative, 11 studies); [higher state anxiety with AI than SP in one trial](claims/ai-simulation-anxiety-divergent.md) [~M]
rows.change: Begin with private AI attempts, then observed ones; measure anxiety rather than assume it falls
rows.if: Learners report anxiety about practising in front of others

rows.basis: [Cybersickness reported in about 42% of VR users](claims/cybersickness-prevalence-vr-ar-immersive-learning.md) [-M]; [VR should reinforce, not substitute](claims/vr-reinforcement-not-substitute.md) [~W] (a review's interpretation)
rows.change: Keep sessions short, give a screen alternative and check for symptoms; use VR to add to live or real practice, not to replace it
rows.if: The plan uses VR headsets

rows.basis: [Adaptive patient's disclosure climbed while a prompt-only one stayed flat](claims/avp-climbing-disclosure-vs-static-flat.md) [+M]; [model and prompt moderate persona expression](claims/model-and-prompt-moderate-persona-expression.md) [~M]; [agents differed most on knowledge, least on role-play](claims/agents-differ-knowledge-not-role-performance.md) [~M]; [sycophancy may limit push-back](claims/sycophancy-limits-genai-pushback.md) [-W] (argument)
rows.change: Test persona consistency and disclosure rules before use, compare two runs of one persona, score its content accuracy separately from its role-play, test whether it resists where the real person would, and prefer a responsive design that discloses as the learner explores
rows.if: The simulated person is a prompted general LLM

rows.basis: [LLM classroom role-play cost $0.05–$0.10 a session](claims/educasim-low-cost-per-session.md) [+W] (one deployment, 150 users); costs of checking and debriefing not recorded in the wiki
rows.change: Use an LLM role-play partner for the repeated attempts and spend the money saved on checking the simulated person and on mentor debriefs and transfer ratings
rows.if: The budget is small or the cohort large

rows.basis: [AI corrective feedback and repeated practice reported to improve speaking](claims/ai-improves-speaking-proficiency-feedback-practice.md) [+W]; [AI simulates authentic interaction scenarios with tailored scaffolding](claims/ai-contextual-affordances-scaffolding-simulation.md) [+W] (both a systematic review's thematic coding, no effect sizes); [repetition did not transfer to a new task](claims/task-repetition-fluency-complexity-same-task-only.md) [~M]
rows.change: Use an AI conversation partner in simulated everyday or workplace scenarios with corrective feedback after each turn or exchange; vary the scenarios rather than repeating one, and rate speaking with a person at the end
rows.if: The goal is speaking in a second or foreign language

rows.basis: [GenAI tutorials ran longer, and only those groups told the patient the diagnosis and plan](claims/genai-history-taking-longer-tutorial-time.md) [~W]; [students treated the avatar as a question base](claims/genai-avatar-treated-as-question-base.md) [-W]; [recall did not differ by condition](claims/genai-recall-near-ceiling-no-condition-difference.md) [~W]; [learners rated the tutorial higher](claims/genai-virtual-patient-higher-perceived-tutorial-quality.md) [+W] (one mixed-methods study, four tutorial groups)
rows.change: Allow more time for the history (about ten minutes more in one study), add a phase in which learners explain the diagnosis and plan to the simulated person, and prompt open questions; do not expect better recall of the case from the simulated person alone
rows.if: The simulated person is used inside a problem-based or case tutorial

rows.basis: [MPathic-VR OSCE advantage](claims/mpathic-vr-osce-composite-transfer.md) [+M]; [multi-agent SP raised OSCE-aligned scores](claims/ma-scaffolding-improves-osce-exam-score.md) [+M]
rows.change: Use the virtual-human or LLM standardized patient for conversational practice with an OSCE-style rubric, a repeat run-through and a blinded OSCE at the end
rows.if: Health professions (history-taking, breaking bad news, interprofessional talk)

rows.basis: [Authentic video beat virtual simulation on analysis](claims/av-outperforms-vs-total-observation-score.md) [-M]; [simulation prompted more reflection](claims/vs-higher-purposefulness-reflection.md) [+M]; [LLMs may not unknow expert knowledge](claims/competence-paradox-llm-student-simulation.md) [-W]; [novice CS teachers who used an LLM classroom simulation viewed it positively](claims/educasim-positive-teacher-sentiment-254-sessions.md) [+W] (optional feedback, no outcome measure); mixed-reality avatar classrooms are untested in the wiki
rows.change: Pair simulated students with authentic classroom video and real placements; use the simulation for rehearsing responses and reflection, and the video for learning to read classrooms; validate simulated students against real student responses
rows.if: Teacher education (managing a class, responding to student thinking)

rows.basis: untested in business settings in the wiki; transported from [communication gained least](claims/simulation-effects-vary-by-complex-skill.md) [~M]
rows.change: Use the health-professions sequence with a business rubric; rate the outcome in a role-play with a different person or a real call, and treat the expected gain as the communication-skill estimate
rows.if: Business (sales, negotiation, customer, management or coaching conversations)

rows.basis: [Teaching a ChatGPT agent improved programming knowledge](claims/chatgpt-teachable-agent-knowledge-gains.md) [+M] but [not correctness](claims/chatgpt-teachable-agent-no-correctness-gain.md) [~M]; simulated clients untested in technology settings in the wiki
rows.change: For explaining and reviewing code, have learners teach a simulated learner and then check correctness separately; for client interviews, use a simulated client with rules for what it discloses
rows.if: Technology (requirements interviews, user support, explaining code, code review)

rows.basis: [LLM participants clarified stage goals and prompted reflection](claims/llm-participants-stage-goal-clarification.md) [+W] (focus groups); [an AI partner whose role was ambiguous and which tracked a group's decisions inaccurately lost the group's trust](claims/role-ambiguity-black-accent-trust-breakdown.md) [~W] (one group's case study, school students); [scripts improved collaboration skills](claims/cscl-scripts-large-effect-collaboration-skills.md) [+M] (human groups); [script features did not moderate effects](claims/script-level-moderator-not-significant.md) [~M] (human groups)
rows.change: Give the AI a defined role (clarifying the stage goal, keeping the group on topic, asking the questions people hesitate to ask), tell the group what that role is, check that it tracks the group's decisions accurately, and debrief the group, not only individuals
rows.if: An AI partner takes a role in a group discussion or collaboration script

rows.basis: [Minimal guidance is less effective for novices](claims/minimal-guidance-less-effective-for-novices.md) [-M]; [Elaborating without relevant prior knowledge lowered recall](claims/elaboration-without-prior-knowledge-harms-recall.md) [-M] (one experiment, university students)
rows.change: At step 2, teach the content first or alongside (short explanation, worked example, a short text to read before the group discusses the problem) and use the problem to apply it
rows.if: Learners are novices on the content the problem needs

rows.basis: [Part-task practice helped absolute novices on high-interactivity material](claims/part-task-practice-reduces-load-for-novices.md) [~M] (one experiment, not in PBL)
rows.change: Before the whole problem, give short practice on its key parts in isolation, then pose the integrated problem
rows.if: Learners are absolute novices and the problem has many interacting parts

rows.basis: [Problem-first improves conceptual learning when instruction follows](claims/productive-failure-improves-conceptual-learning.md) [+M]; [Larger effects when instruction builds on student solutions](claims/pf-fidelity-predicts-psi-effect-size.md) [+M]; [PS-I benefits appeared with high, not low, initial solution rates](claims/solution-rate-moderates-ps-i-benefits.md) [~W] (cross-study comparison)
rows.change: Run a short problem-first phase, have groups make their solutions visible, then build step 4's instruction on those solutions. Pilot the problem first: check that learners produce several ideas and make headway on it; if few get anywhere, teach first
rows.if: Learners can generate several partial solutions and the goal is conceptual

rows.basis: [Problem-first did not outperform instruction-first for social-science research methods](claims/pf-effect-not-replicated-non-stem-research-methods.md) [-M] (two quasi-experiments, tenth-graders), despite [a piloted problem of suitable complexity](claims/pf-problem-sweet-spot-complexity-pilot-tests.md) [~W]
rows.change: Treat problem-first as unproven there; prefer instruction first with the problem as application, or run problem-first as a comparison and measure it
rows.if: The domain is outside mathematics and science (for example, social-science methods)

rows.basis: [Guidance during initial problem solving does not improve learning from instruction](claims/initial-guidance-does-not-improve-learning-from-instruction.md) [~M]
rows.change: Do not steer toward the canonical method before step 4; guidance raised solution quality but not later learning
rows.if: The facilitator wants to hint learners toward the method during the problem phase

rows.basis: [PS-I shows no pooled benefit for procedural knowledge](claims/psi-procedural-knowledge-null-pooled-effect.md) [~M]
rows.change: Add targeted procedural practice after the consolidation; problem-first gave no procedural advantage
rows.if: Fluent execution of a procedure is part of the objective

rows.basis: [PS-I effects are negative for 2nd–5th graders](claims/psi-effect-increases-with-grade-level.md) [-M]
rows.change: Reverse the order: teach first, then pose the problem as application
rows.if: Learners are roughly 7–11 years old

rows.basis: [The fidelity benefit reverses for very short interventions](claims/psi-fidelity-time-span-interaction.md) [~M]
rows.change: Keep the problem phase short and the design simple, or teach first; do not cram the full sequence into a few hours
rows.if: Only one short session is available

rows.basis: [PBL: null or negative on basic knowledge](claims/pbl-null-basic-knowledge-positive-transfer.md) [~M]
rows.change: Add explicit review and practice of the facts the exam covers; do not count on the problem work to carry them
rows.if: The assessment is a basic-knowledge exam

rows.basis: [Tutor background did not predict learning](claims/tutor-background-meta-regression-not-predictive.md) [~M]; [Staff-tutored groups scored slightly higher than peer-tutored groups](claims/staff-tutoring-small-achievement-advantage-pbl.md) [~M] (one field experiment, health sciences)
rows.change: Give each facilitator the model solution, the target concept and a consolidation script; content background alone did not predict learning. Where facilitators are peers (senior students), give them the same materials and expect at most a small shortfall
rows.if: Facilitators are not content experts

rows.basis: [Small and medium tutorial groups gained self-directed-learning readiness; large groups declined](claims/tutorial-group-size-moderates-sdl.md) [~W] (one pre–post study reported in a review; a self-report scale, not achievement)
rows.change: Split into small or medium groups for the problem work, each with a clear role structure; do not run the self-directed phase as one large group
rows.if: Tutorial groups are large

rows.basis: [More lecture coverage went with less critical discussion in PBL sessions, but more willingness to speak](claims/scope-of-pbl-implementation-shapes-discussion.md) [~W] (one qualitative cross-curriculum study)
rows.change: Write problems the lectured content informs but does not settle; ask learners for questions and challenges, not a summary of the lecture
rows.if: Content is taught in lectures running alongside the problem sessions

rows.basis: [Online PBL groups followed the scripted sequence at first, then drifted to social bonding with fewer high-cognitive interactions](claims/pbl-group-sequence-derails-to-social.md) [~W] (one sequence-analysis study); the re-launch is an untested proposal
rows.change: Re-launch the group's script part-way through (new roles, a fresh argument task, a facilitator check-in), since a script that holds at the start does not hold by itself
rows.if: Group work runs online over several weeks

rows.basis: [Contingent scaffolding improves learning](claims/contingent-scaffolding-improves-learning.md) [+M] (one-to-one tutoring); [Learners using a staged-disclosure feedback agent valued their agency, but about two in five found it too indirect when they needed an explicit answer](claims/staged-feedback-survey-perceptions.md) [~W] (one self-selected survey); the self-paced version is an untested proposal
rows.change: Replace the facilitator with support that rises after a failed attempt (a hint, then a worked step) and falls after success, and show typical solutions before the consolidation; let a learner who has tried reach an explicit answer rather than only further hints
rows.if: Learners work alone (`online-self-paced`)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Collect solutions from a sample of groups and build the consolidation on the three or four most common
rows.if: One facilitator for many groups

rows.basis: [About half of students' written accounts showed collaborative learning rather than divided group work](claims/half-of-texts-showed-collaborative-learning.md) [~W] (one qualitative study, teacher education); the individual reobservation is an untested proposal
rows.change: Add the individual reobservation at step 5 and record who contributed what; a group product does not show what each member can do
rows.if: Group products will be the main evidence of learning

rows.basis: [Skills named: interpersonal, problem-solving, group](claims/pbl-skills-interpersonal-problem-solving-group.md) [+W]; [Attitudes named: valuing others' perspectives, interdependence, learning about self](claims/pbl-attitudes-valuing-interdependence-self.md) [+W]; [Knowledge described as generation, application, dissemination, plus pedagogical knowledge](claims/pbl-knowledge-generation-application-dissemination.md) [+W]; [Students rarely described higher-level cognitive or metacognitive gains](claims/minimal-reference-higher-level-processing-benefits.md) [~W] (all one qualitative study of 122 students; what learners said, not measured gains)
rows.change: Name and teach the skills learners themselves identify (interpersonal, problem-solving and group skills such as sharing roles and resolving conflict) and the attitudes (valuing others' perspectives, interdependence); before the first problem, prepare learners for group work (reading, discussing past good and bad group experiences, practising forming and running a team), as in the [prepare-and-assess strategy](strategies/prepare-and-assess-pbl-process-reflection.md); have learners reflect in writing on how their group worked and assess that reflection; do not expect learners to report gains in higher-level thinking unprompted
rows.if: Collaboration is itself an objective (for example, future teachers who will run group work)

rows.basis: [A teacher's departure from the written PBL sequence to respond to a real event deepened student-directed inquiry](claims/spontaneous-authenticity-in-pbl-deepens-student-directed-inquiry.md) [+W] (one grade-3 classroom case study; sufficient there, not shown to be general)
rows.change: Allow the facilitator to pause the script and let learners take up the event, then return to the target concept in the consolidation
rows.if: The written unit is tightly scripted, and a real event tied to the driving question arises during it

rows.basis: [AI-supported PBL scored higher than lecture in robotics programming](claims/ai-pbl-higher-posttest-academic-achievement.md) [~W] and [showed higher normalised gains than the control group](claims/ai-pbl-high-ngain-versus-control-low.md) [~W] (the same quasi-experiment); a systematic review of 50 studies lists as themes that [AI supports educator–student collaboration through real-time feedback and scaffolding](claims/ai-pbl-enhances-educator-student-collaboration.md) [~W] and [adaptive, personalised learning linked to engagement and problem solving](claims/ai-pbl-adaptive-personalized-engagement.md) [~W], with no comparisons or effect sizes on the claim pages; [Staged-disclosure feedback agent: agency valued, 39% found it too indirect, 43% reported repetition](claims/staged-feedback-survey-perceptions.md) [~W]
rows.change: Treat the AI support as part of the configuration to be evaluated; the one comparison recorded set AI-supported PBL against lecture, so it cannot separate the AI from the PBL. If an AI agent withholds answers to preserve learner agency, give it a route to an explicit answer after repeated attempts and check it does not repeat itself
rows.if: The brief adds AI tools to the problem phase and expects higher scores

rows.basis: [Contingent support](claims/contingent-scaffolding-improves-learning.md) [+M] and [fading](claims/fading-support-promotes-transfer-of-responsibility.md) [+M], from students, carried to teachers; [repeating one short lesson six times with small groups let a mentee revise her classroom management and build confidence](claims/repeated-short-lessons-scaffold-mentee-behaviour-management.md) [+W] (one preservice case); doses untested
rows.change: Keep the coach or mentor modeling in the teacher's own class for longer, observe weekly, debrief within a day, and fade only after two consecutive lessons at the agreed level; focus on one routine (often classroom management) at a time. For a student teacher, start with a short lesson (20–30 minutes) taught several times to small groups, revising between repetitions, before a whole class.
rows.if: New teachers in their first years, or student teachers on placement

rows.basis: [Expertise reversal](claims/expertise-reversal-effect.md) [~M] (trainees and students, not teachers); [content familiarity, not experience, predicted reform practice](claims/content-familiarity-predicts-reform-practice-experience-does-not.md) [~M] (one association study)
rows.change: Shorten modeling; start from the points where their current routine and the new practice clash; offer the principle and exemplars rather than a script; let them choose the video segment from the first cycle. Do not assume resistance from experience.
rows.if: Experienced teachers adopting a new practice or curriculum

rows.basis: [Content familiarity predicted reform practice](claims/content-familiarity-predicts-reform-practice-experience-does-not.md) [~M]: an association, not a test of content PD
rows.change: Add content study to the PD (doing the students' tasks as learners, then analysing them) before coaching the routine.
rows.if: Teachers with weak content knowledge in the subject the practice serves

rows.basis: [Buy-in is seen as mediating coaching](claims/teacher-buy-in-mediates-coaching-benefit.md) [~W]; [changed timing, offerings and credit drew in earlier non-participants](claims/nonparticipant-barriers-professional-development.md) [~W] (one program)
rows.change: Use video of colleagues of similar standing rather than expert demonstrators; start with a small practice that can succeed in one lesson; keep coaching separate from appraisal; offer timing and credit that suit them.
rows.if: Teachers with low confidence, or a team reluctant to take part

rows.basis: [Minimal success designing Constructive and Interactive activities after ICAP PD](claims/teachers-struggle-designing-interactive-activities.md) [-M]
rows.change: Make lesson design the practiced task: co-plan, get feedback on the plan, then enact and debrief. Do not expect a knowledge course to produce it.
rows.if: The target is teachers designing their own lessons with a framework, not running given ones

rows.basis: Untested proposal; [coaching aimed at a specific academic task](claims/coaching-academic-task-fidelity-higher-quality.md) [+M] supports narrowing the target, not the shortened format
rows.change: Coach one practice at a time; replace live observation with a 5–10 minute teacher-chosen video clip and a 20-minute debrief; run rehearsal and later cycles in pairs or trios with peer observers; give the coach's time to the teachers whose observed enactment is furthest from the target.
rows.if: One coach for many teachers, or scarce facilitator time (a coach across several schools, a busy term)

rows.basis: Untested proposal; [video self-observation](claims/video-self-observation-powerful-coaching-component.md) [+W] (web-mediated coaching, teachers' reports)
rows.change: Make filmed lessons the shared object for everyone; post clips before the meeting so remote teachers view them as the room does; pair each remote teacher with an in-room partner for rehearsal; debrief online within two school days.
rows.if: Some teachers join remotely while others are in the room, or coaching is wholly online

rows.basis: [Half of inservice activities lasted four hours or less, mostly talks or brief workshops](claims/expert-presenter-model-most-prevalent.md) [~W] (prevalence, not effect); [short, fragmented training is reported to hinder a holistic view](claims/systemic-approach-in-service-teacher-education.md) [-W]; the follow-up is untested
rows.change: Use it to model and rehearse one narrow practice and to set up a follow-up the school can run without the presenter: one peer observation with a look-for list within two weeks and one team meeting to review the clips. Do not promise changed practice from the session alone.
rows.if: Only a single session is available (an inset day, a one-off workshop)

rows.basis: Untested in this form; [coaching aimed at a specific academic task](claims/coaching-academic-task-fidelity-higher-quality.md) [+M]; [maintenance rarely measured](claims/coaching-maintenance-rarely-measured.md) [~M]
rows.change: Keep it; change only what the evidence says matters: make sure its focus is one observable practice, that feedback follows an enactment with students, and that one observation happens after support ends.
rows.if: The brief names its own routine (a district observation rubric, a PLC protocol, a lesson-study cycle, a coaching model already in use)

rows.basis: [Supervisory coaching shows mixed effects](claims/supervisory-coaching-mixed-teacher-student-outcomes.md) [~M] (16 K–12 studies, 6 met all quality indicators)
rows.change: Separate the coaching record from appraisal, or name plainly what the supervisor will see; expect mixed results and measure both teacher and student change.
rows.if: Coaching is run by supervisors or is tied to performance evaluation

rows.basis: [Ongoing PD and mentorship were described as critical to coaches' growth and confidence](claims/ongoing-pd-mentorship-critical-coach-growth.md) [+W] and [district leaders' active role in removing barriers](claims/district-leaders-active-role-coaching-success.md) [+W] (one three-year qualitative study across 32 districts); [the complexity of coaching responsibilities may fragment coaching](claims/coaching-complexity-may-fragment-impact.md) [-W] (an author's rationale, no data)
rows.change: Give coaches their own ongoing PD and a mentor; keep most of each coach's time for planning–observation–debrief cycles with teachers rather than spreading it across programme administration; have district leaders remove scheduling and access barriers and say plainly that trying a new practice is expected.
rows.if: A district or school system setting up or running a coaching programme (newly appointed coaches, coaches who also administer programmes)

rows.basis: [Monthly coaching sessions helped teachers integrate a writing tool with their instruction](claims/monthly-coaching-helped-teachers-integrate-mi-write.md) [+W] (one implementation study, no comparison); [coached teachers reported more frequent impactful technology use](claims/coaching-increases-impactful-technology-use-practices.md) [+W] (self-report survey); [teacher guides of four maths curricula differ in how much they explain the same practice](claims/hqim-teacher-guides-vary-in-educative-guidance-depth.md) [~W] (a materials review, no teacher outcome); [materials paired with coaching went with larger effects on instruction](claims/coaching-complementary-elements-moderators.md) [~M] (an association across studies)
rows.change: Coach the integration of the tool or materials into the teacher's own lessons, at least monthly, not the tool's features in a one-off session; before modeling, check how far the materials' teacher guide explains why each practice matters and how to do it, and supply that reasoning where it is thin; give teachers the materials alongside coaching.
rows.if: PD to adopt a classroom technology tool or new instructional materials

rows.basis: [Leader-teacher diffusion was uneven](claims/leader-teacher-diffusion-uneven.md) [~M] (one three-year program)
rows.change: Give lead teachers released time, principal support, and their own coaching on how to coach; plan for uneven spread and observe colleagues' practice, not the lead teachers' only.
rows.if: Scaling through lead teachers or train-the-trainer

rows.basis: [Hunter's ITIP lacked evidence of improved achievement as implemented under typical conditions](claims/itip-lacks-empirical-evidence-achievement.md) [-M] (a review reported second-hand)
rows.change: Pilot with observation of practice and a student measure before scaling; budget follow-up coaching rather than more presenter days.
rows.if: District- or statewide rollout of one PD model to all schools

rows.basis: Untested; the coaching claims are from K–12 classrooms
rows.change: Use the same cycle with a peer observer from the same department; let the observed session be a seminar, lab or online class; time the cycle to the teaching calendar (one cycle per three or four weeks of teaching).
rows.if: Higher-education faculty, teaching assistants or adult-education tutors (adults in work settings with little release time)

rows.basis: Untested proposal; see [lesson study](strategies/lesson-study.md)
rows.change: Use it as the end of the arc: the team plans, teaches and revises one research lesson observed by colleagues, with the debrief about students' responses, not the teacher's performance.
rows.if: A real audience for the teachers' work (a public research lesson, a showcase, a conference)

rows.basis: [Rule-example sequence](claims/rule-example-sequence-efficient-rule-introduction.md) [~W] (an argument from early programmed-instruction work, not a test); step sizes untested
rows.change: Smallest steps; rule then examples then incomplete examples; a cue on every early frame; remedial branch after two errors of one kind; remove cues over three sessions (dose table above).
rows.if: Learners are `novice` in the domain

rows.basis: Untested proposal; [faster step responses with higher proficiency](claims/higher-proficiency-faster-step-responses.md) [~W] is associational and from algebra tutors
rows.change: Place each learner with unprompted unit items; let those at criterion take the unit check directly; give larger steps and fewer cues to the rest.
rows.if: Learners are `intermediate` or `advanced`, or vary widely in prior knowledge

rows.basis: [Mastery programs raised examination performance](claims/mastery-learning-improves-outcomes.md) [+M] in college, high-school and upper-elementary settings; [group-based programs had larger effects](claims/mastery-learning-effects-vary-with-standard-pacing-and-test-type.md) [~M]; not frame-based programs
rows.change: Sessions of 10–15 minutes, a teacher present to see who is stuck, the class working through a unit by a shared date and taking its check together.
rows.if: Learners are `child` (upper primary) or in secondary school

rows.basis: [Feedback after retrieval](claims/feedback-enhances-retrieval-practice.md) [+M] (word pairs and classroom quizzes, not frames)
rows.change: Use the full sequence; constructed responses for recall; correct answer and reason after each error.
rows.if: The goal is a fact, rule or procedure with one right answer per step

rows.basis: [Outcome-only feedback impedes learning of complex tasks](claims/outcome-feedback-impedes-complex-task-learning-mcpl.md) [-W] (a review's report on a laboratory cue-learning paradigm); [induction and errorful learning suit some task types and not others](claims/task-type-moderates-induction-error-usefulness.md) [~W] (1966 argument)
rows.change: Do not build it from right/wrong frames. Use frames only for the prerequisite facts and rules; teach the whole task through worked examples, cases or practice with feedback on the reasoning ([worked examples](patterns/worked-examples.md), [direct instruction](patterns/direct-instruction.md)).
rows.if: The goal is a complex judgment, a design, an argument or an open problem

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Keep the whole task as the unit check and the goal; use frames only for the parts learners keep getting wrong, and return them to the whole task at once.
rows.if: The brief wants a whole-task performance kept whole (a full procedure at work, a case, a performance)

rows.basis: [Self-paced mastery programs reduced completion](claims/self-paced-mastery-programs-reduce-college-course-completion.md) [-M] (college PSI courses); reminders and contact are untested remedies
rows.change: Dated targets per unit, an automatic reminder at each missed date and a person who contacts anyone two targets behind; keep the unit gate.
rows.if: `online-self-paced`, no teacher, learners must finish by a date

rows.basis: [Group-based programs had larger effects than self-paced ones](claims/mastery-learning-effects-vary-with-standard-pacing-and-test-type.md) [~M]; the teacher's routine is untested
rows.change: The software or the printed program confirms each response; the teacher sees who is branched to remedial frames twice and goes to them; the class keeps a shared unit date and takes the unit check together.
rows.if: `classroom`, one teacher for many learners

rows.basis: Untested proposal (the old page's Programmed Tutoring descendant used a human tutor for hints)
rows.change: The program does all confirmation; the person's time goes only to learners stopped by the three-error rule, for 5 minutes each, with the stuck step shown to them.
rows.if: Scarce facilitator time (volunteers, a tutor checking in briefly, a busy shift)

rows.basis: [Intelligent tutoring systems did not outperform individual human tutoring or small-group instruction](claims/adaptive-learning-improves-outcomes.md) [~S]; carried from tutoring systems to programmed frames
rows.change: Keep the person; use frames for practice between sessions, not in place of the tutor.
rows.if: A human tutor or a small group is available for every learner

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: One frame per screen, responses by tapping a choice or typing a short answer, no frame that needs a printed sheet; the same dated schedule and unit check for both groups; remote learners get the contact by message.
rows.if: Some learners remote and some in the room, or phone only

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: One program of 20–30 minutes covering one rule or procedure, ending with five unprompted items; no unit gate across sessions, and a note to the learner of which steps to revisit.
rows.if: `single-session` only

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Placement 2 minutes, frames 10 minutes (about 15–20 frames), check 3 minutes; cut content rather than frames' response steps.
rows.if: A fixed short time budget (for example 15 minutes)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Early frames that most learners get right, audio for frame text, responses by selecting or pointing, the learner's record private to them; move to constructed responses once accuracy is steady.
rows.if: Learners with low confidence or low literacy

rows.basis: Untested proposal (the old page names military and corporate training as PI's main users)
rows.change: Place by unprompted items so known steps are skipped; frames use the learner's own job tasks and forms; the unit check is the job task.
rows.if: Adults in work settings

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Use them as given: the brief's check is the unit gate, its categories label the frames, its criterion is the cut score; change only step size, the response before the answer, and the immediate correction. Add no test, quiz or survey the brief did not ask for.
rows.if: The brief names its own check, rubric, criterion or categories

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Responses stay with the learner; a person sees only whether the unit check was passed, unless the learner chooses to share more.
rows.if: Private or sensitive material (health, finances, personal history)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Not a programmed-instruction goal; use frames only for prerequisite facts and conventions, and teach the product through drafts and feedback on the whole.
rows.if: A product or performance for a real audience

rows.basis: [Mastery effects were near zero on standardized tests in four studies with both kinds](claims/mastery-learning-effects-vary-with-standard-pacing-and-test-type.md) [~M]; [tutoring-system gains were smaller on standardized tests](claims/adaptive-learning-improves-outcomes.md) [~S]
rows.change: Write the unit checks as items the frames did not show; expect a smaller gain on the standardized test than on the course's own tests; check at the stated delay.
rows.if: High stakes, or an independent standardized test at the end

rows.basis: [Learner pacing helped on difficult questions in one experiment, while learner control in general showed almost no effect across 18 studies](claims/learner-paced-beats-system-paced-complex-material.md) [~M] (primary-school students, one animation)
rows.change: Cut it into short segments the learner advances, with pause and replay; do not expect learner control in general to help.
rows.if: Complex material presented as animation or video inside the program, or learners want to set the pace

rows.basis: [Unguided search learns less than explicit instruction](claims/minimal-guidance-less-effective-for-novices.md) [+S]; [part-task practice for novices](claims/part-task-practice-reduces-load-for-novices.md) [+M] (one experiment)
rows.change: Plan freeze points at every predictable gap from the starting check; keep project segments short (about 20–30 minutes); break complex routines into parts in the instructional space before whole use; give a worked example of each milestone.
rows.if: Learners are `novice` in the domain

rows.basis: [Guidance advantage recedes with prior knowledge](claims/minimal-guidance-less-effective-for-novices.md) [~S] (the narrative review within that claim); timing untested
rows.change: Test out of components at launch; freezes become rare and learner-requested; use the instructional space mainly for automaticity of routines; let them attempt conceptual gaps before any instruction.
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` or already hold most component skills

rows.basis: [Problem solving before instruction](claims/productive-failure-improves-conceptual-learning.md) [~S]: effects reversed for second to fifth graders and for domain-general skills
rows.change: Teach the concept first, then return to the project; do not rely on an unaided attempt first.
rows.if: Learners are `child` (roughly second to fifth grade) and a gap is conceptual

rows.basis: [Problem solving before instruction](claims/productive-failure-improves-conceptual-learning.md) [~S]; [guidance during the attempt did not improve later learning](claims/initial-guidance-does-not-improve-learning-from-instruction.md) [~M] (one article reporting two studies)
rows.change: Let the learner or team attempt it in the project for a bounded time (about 10–15 minutes), then freeze and teach, building on their attempts. Do not add hints during the attempt expecting a later gain.
rows.if: The gap is a concept learners can attempt (`conceptual-understanding`), older learners

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page (Reigeluth's speed criterion)
rows.change: Add a time limit to the gate and spaced timed reviews in later sessions; time the routine inside the project as well as alone.
rows.if: The target includes automaticity (a routine done fast, under load)

rows.basis: Untested proposal; [tutoring systems did not beat small-group instruction](claims/adaptive-learning-improves-outcomes.md) [~S], so grouping learners with the same gap is not a known loss
rows.change: Run the instructional space as prepared self-study stations or short teacher-led mini-lessons for the several learners who hit the same planned freeze point at once; keep individual gates as short written checks.
rows.if: One teacher for many learners, no tutoring system

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Spend the facilitator's minutes only on diagnosis and on learners who missed a gate twice; let practice, feedback and the gate run on prepared material or a system.
rows.if: Scarce facilitator time (volunteers, a busy shift, one tutor checking in briefly)

rows.basis: [Self-paced mastery programmes lowered completion](claims/self-paced-mastery-programs-reduce-college-course-completion.md) [-M], college PSI courses; [tutoring systems](claims/adaptive-learning-improves-outcomes.md) [+S]
rows.change: The system pauses the project, runs the practice and the gate, and resumes it; keep common milestone deadlines and send reminders; flag a learner who has not resumed within a week.
rows.if: `online-self-paced`, no teacher

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Keep the instructional space and the gate on the phone for everyone, so remote and in-room learners freeze the same way; hold team milestone checks in a shared call or document.
rows.if: Mixed modes (some learners remote, some in the room, or phone-only)

rows.basis: [Rewards on each member's individual learning](claims/cooperative-learning-group-rewards-and-individual-accountability.md) [+S], school cooperative learning, carried to project teams
rows.change: Grade part of the team's result on members' individual milestone checks; rotate which member presents each part.
rows.if: Team projects

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Run one milestone: 10 minutes launch, one planned freeze for the gap most learners will hit (15–20 minutes of instruction and a 5-item gate), 20 minutes back in the project. Name the further gaps for later.
rows.if: `single-session` only (one workshop)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Fit one cycle per session: 25 minutes project, up to 20 minutes instructional space for any frozen learner, 5 minutes back in the project or a milestone check; learners who did not freeze keep working.
rows.if: A fixed short time budget per session (for example 50 minutes)

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page (Reigeluth's real-world variant)
rows.change: Keep the project the real task; deliver the instructional space on a phone or terminal at the workplace; set gates on the routines the job needs.
rows.if: Adults in a work setting, the project is real work

rows.basis: [Authentic projects and self-efficacy](claims/authentic-projects-build-career-self-efficacy.md) [+W] (two qualitative accounts, no comparison); timing untested
rows.change: Freeze only before a public step, never during it; gate the skills the audience will see before the delivery date.
rows.if: The product or performance is for a real audience or client

rows.basis: Untested proposal; [whole-task practice for transfer](claims/whole-task-performance-improves-transfer.md) [+W] is an argument, not a test
rows.change: Do not split the performance into items; use the instructional space only between performances, and use the next whole performance as the gate for transfer, alongside a short check of the component.
rows.if: The brief wants the whole-task performance kept whole

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Keep it as given and use its criteria as the gates; add only an individual check of each component beside it if the rubric scores the team product alone.
rows.if: The brief names its own rubric, criteria or check-in routine

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Make the first gaps small and the first gates quick to pass; show rather than tell in the instructional space; let learners redo a gate privately.
rows.if: Learners have low confidence or low literacy

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: The learner chooses what goes into the shared project and who sees their gate results; the instructional space uses invented cases.
rows.if: Private or sensitive material (a learner's own business, health or family data in the project)

rows.basis: [Effects were much smaller on standardized than local tests](claims/mastery-learning-effects-vary-with-standard-pacing-and-test-type.md) [~M]; delay untested
rows.change: Gate on new items written for the purpose, not on the practice items; recheck the critical routines at a delay before certifying.
rows.if: High stakes (a licence, a safety-critical routine)

rows.basis: [Process goals outperform outcome goals for novices](claims/process-goals-outperform-outcome-goals-for-novices.md) [+S] (high-school writing; carried to other content); [self-assessment is low without training](claims/self-assessment-accuracy-is-low-without-training.md) [~S]
rows.change: Stay in Stage A for at least the first unit; write process goals, not score goals; give two set resources, not a menu; model a self-check on a worked example before any self-rating.
rows.if: Learners are `novice` in the content

rows.basis: Untested; carried from the earlier page's "some learners can self-direct immediately"
rows.change: Start at Stage B or C after the probe; let the learner draft the plan and the criteria, and keep only the checkpoints and the end comparison with an outside check.
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` or experienced practitioners in the field

rows.basis: Untested proposal; [SRL strategy instruction](claims/self-regulated-learning-improves-achievement.md) [+S] included primary pupils, but tested training, not handing over control
rows.change: Keep the teacher setting goals; hand over pace and the order of two or three tasks, with a daily visible tracker; release one further choice per term.
rows.if: Learners are `child` (primary age)

rows.basis: [Self-determination skills instruction for students with disabilities increases self-determination on some measures but not others](claims/self-determination-instruction-improves-outcomes.md) [+M]: a three-year campus-randomized trial with 371 high-school students raised one of two self-determination measures; outcomes were self-determination, not achievement
rows.change: Teach the component skills directly (choice-making, goal setting, self-advocacy) over months, and let the learner lead the planning meeting with a practised script.
rows.if: Learners with intellectual or learning disabilities, working toward their own goals (transition planning, an IEP)

rows.basis: [Self-paced courses lost more completers](claims/self-paced-mastery-programs-reduce-college-course-completion.md) [-M] (college PSI); [implementation intentions](claims/implementation-intentions-improve-goal-attainment.md) [~S] (helped completion in individualist cultures only)
rows.change: Keep dated weekly checkpoints with automated reminders; add an eight-minute goal, obstacle and if-then plan activity at enrolment; show each learner their plan against their progress weekly.
rows.if: `online-self-paced`, no facilitator

rows.basis: [Implementation intentions](claims/implementation-intentions-improve-goal-attainment.md) [~S] (no effect for learners in collectivist cultures in the online experiments); the cultural note on [autonomy support](claims/autonomy-supports-intrinsic-motivation.md) [~M] is the claim page's discussion, not a finding
rows.change: Do not rely on an if-then planning activity alone to raise completion; plan with a peer group or the facilitator, and present choices as options the teacher endorses.
rows.if: Learners come mostly from collectivist cultures, or schooling where choice reads as lack of guidance

rows.basis: [Not all students in connectivist courses could direct their own learning](claims/connectivist-courses-student-agency-problems.md) [~M] (second-hand reports from a review)
rows.change: Add the plan, checkpoints and a small cohort or buddy; give a default path learners may leave.
rows.if: Wide-open self-direction (open online course, networked learning, learners choose everything)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Make the check-in five minutes against the written plan: what was done, what is next, one obstacle; batch asynchronous replies twice a week; let peers check each other's plans between.
rows.if: Scarce facilitator time (volunteers, a busy shift, one tutor checking in briefly)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Run check-ins in small groups of 4–6 on a rota, each learner reporting against the plan in two minutes; the teacher reads only plans flagged as off track.
rows.if: One teacher or expert for many learners

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Keep the plan and tracker in one shared place that works on a phone; hold check-ins by short message or voice note for remote learners; put the menu in text, not a large file.
rows.if: Mixed modes: some in the room, some remote; phone-only learners

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Do not run the staged release; run steps 1 and 2 only (probe, a written plan with one if-then plan, a date), and hand the learner the plan to keep.
rows.if: A single session only

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Spend about 5 minutes on the plan, 30–35 on the chosen work, 5 on the self-check against the criterion; the plan revision moves to every second or third session.
rows.if: A fixed short time budget per session (e.g. 45 minutes)

rows.basis: Untested; [facilitated discussion felt empowering to one adult educator](claims/facilitated-self-directed-learning-empowers-adults.md) [+W] is one first-person reflection
rows.change: Tie the plan's goals to a task the learner does at work; let the employer's requirement fix the outcome and the learner choose route and pace; check-ins fit shift patterns.
rows.if: Adults in work settings

rows.basis: [Implementation intentions](claims/implementation-intentions-improve-goal-attainment.md) [+S]; [process goals](claims/process-goals-outperform-outcome-goals-for-novices.md) [+S]
rows.change: Keep it; change only what the evidence says matters: one if-then plan for the main obstacle, process goals for novices, dated checkpoints, and a self-rating compared with an outside check.
rows.if: The brief names its own routine for planning or review (its own learning contract, journal, check-in form, rubric)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Use them as the plan's goals and as the menu's labels; do not substitute this page's stages or criteria.
rows.if: The brief gives its own categories, criteria or competency framework

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: The learner controls who sees the plan and journal; the facilitator sees only what the learner chooses to share and the checkpoint dates.
rows.if: Private or sensitive material (personal goals, health, a reflective journal)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Let the learner plan the route to the whole product and set checkpoints on drafts of it; do not split it into separate exercises for evaluation.
rows.if: The product is for a real audience, or a whole-task performance the brief wants kept whole

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Write the plan with the learner, in short lines or pictures; offer two choices at a time; read the self-check aloud.
rows.if: Learners with low confidence or limited literacy

rows.basis: [Learner pacing helped on difficult questions in one experiment; learner control in general near zero](claims/learner-paced-beats-system-paced-complex-material.md) [~S]
rows.change: Segment the material and add pause points rather than relying on learners to pause; pace control alone did little.
rows.if: Complex multimedia or video content that learners pace themselves

rows.basis: [Hint budget managed poorly](claims/hint-budget-mismanaged-two-patterns.md) [~W] (one programming course pilot)
rows.change: Teach a deliberate rule for when to ask for help and record it in the plan; a budget alone rewarded learners who already had a strategy.
rows.if: An AI assistant or hint budget is available during self-directed work

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Fix the outcome and the assessment; hand over pace and resources only, and run a practice check under exam conditions before each stage release.
rows.if: High stakes: an exam or licence at the end

rows.basis: [Training plus a diary raised SRL knowledge and self-efficacy](claims/web-based-srl-training-with-diary-raises-srl-knowledge-and-self-efficacy-not-math.md) [~M]; [A diary alone gave no significant gains](claims/learning-diary-alone-no-significant-srl-gains-online-math-prep-course.md) [~M]
rows.change: Deliver step 2 as a short web-based training on the regulation steps, and pair it with a daily diary; do not run the diary alone
rows.if: `online-self-paced`, no instructor to model the steps

rows.basis: [Peer feedback groups added self-motivation, volition and reflection gains](claims/peer-feedback-groups-add-self-motivation-volition-reflection-gains-to-web-based-srl-training.md) [+M]
rows.change: Add peer-feedback groups to step 3, where learners comment on each other's plans and diaries
rows.if: A cohort that can work in small groups

rows.basis: [Review-notes prompt compliance predicts gains](claims/review-notes-compliance-predicts-learning-gains.md) [+W]; [Revise-summary compliance predicts gains](claims/revise-summary-compliance-predicts-learning-gains.md) [+W]; [Suggest-subgoal compliance predicts gains](claims/suggest-subgoal-compliance-predicts-learning-gains.md) [+W]; [Four explicit SRL prompts showed no learning effect](claims/no-learning-effect-for-four-explicit-srl-prompts.md) [~W]; [No learning effect for page-navigation monitoring prompts](claims/no-learning-effect-for-metacognitive-monitoring-prompts.md) [~M]; [Add-subgoal compliance may not help](claims/add-subgoal-prompt-compliance-may-not-help-learning.md) [~M]; [Compliance with suggested actions and essay scores, mixed](claims/compliance-suggested-actions-essay-scores-mixed.md) [~W]
rows.change: In step 3, prefer prompts that ask for a product (revise your summary, review your notes, set a subgoal) and check the product; prompts that only move learners through pages showed no link to learning, and after an add-subgoal prompt, learners who kept attending to the content gained more than those who complied. In a personalised-scaffold study, carrying out suggested review actions (review annotations, review the rubric) went with higher essay scores and note-taking after the last scaffold with lower. All are correlations of compliance with gains in small samples (7–28 learners), not experiments
rows.if: A computer-based environment that can check what learners do with a prompt

rows.basis: [Self-assessment accuracy is low without training](claims/self-assessment-accuracy-is-low-without-training.md) [~M]; [Prior knowledge is needed for accurate self-assessment](claims/prior-knowledge-needed-for-accurate-self-assessment.md) [~M]; [Prior knowledge moderates prompt direction](claims/prior-knowledge-moderates-prompt-direction-self-efficacy.md) [~W]; [Low-prior-knowledge students struggle to self-regulate](claims/low-prior-knowledge-students-struggle-self-regulation.md) [~W] (second-hand)
rows.change: In step 1, run the content probe first and keep the plan short or supplied; in step 2, model self-assessment on a worked example before asking learners to rate themselves; in step 3, prefer prompts after a segment (what went well, what to change) to prompts before it. In one experiment with apprentices, before-task prompts lowered self-efficacy growth for those with less prior knowledge and after-task prompts raised it; self-efficacy, not learning, was the outcome
rows.if: Learners have low prior knowledge of the content

rows.basis: [Self-scoring improves regulation accuracy, not on division for low and high performers](claims/self-scoring-regulation-accuracy-limited-division.md) [~W]; [Sixth-graders' monitoring accuracy low, no cue-prompt effect](claims/student-monitoring-accuracy-low-no-cue-prompt-effect-exp1.md) [~W]
rows.change: Before the judgement, have them score their own answer against a key; generating keywords or a summary first did not sharpen sixth-graders' judgements. Expect less gain for the lowest and highest performers and on harder tasks
rows.if: Learners judge how well they understood a text or solved a problem, children included

rows.basis: [Self-regulation predicted outcomes only with minimal worked examples](claims/self-regulation-predicts-domain-specific-mas-minimal-worked-examples.md) [~W]; [No approach differences in monitoring or reflecting](claims/no-approach-differences-monitoring-reflecting.md) [~W]
rows.change: In step 1, record whether the learner plans and checks unprompted, and add steps 2–3 for those who do not; outcomes under minimal guidance tracked learners' own regulation skill, and the instructional approach alone did not change how much learners monitored or reflected
rows.if: The materials give little guidance (minimal worked examples, discovery or inquiry)

rows.basis: [Teachers provide little explicit SRL support](claims/teachers-provide-little-explicit-srl-support.md) [+W]; [Benefit of strategy use rarely mentioned](claims/cognitive-capability-dominance-benefit-rarely-mentioned.md) [~W]; [Teachers see SRL as desirable but not feasible](claims/teachers-srl-desirable-but-not-feasible.md) [~W]; [SRI teachers modelled and evaluated strategies more](claims/sri-implementation-observations-modeling-evaluation.md) [+W]; [SRL-AIDE raised explicitness, not duration](claims/three-way-interaction-explicitness-not-duration.md) [~W]; [Explicit SRL instruction rare in both conditions](claims/explicit-srl-instruction-rare-primary-teachers-both-conditions.md) [~W]; [Low time and fidelity for predicting and purpose setting](claims/low-time-and-fidelity-engaged-reader-processes.md) [~W]
rows.change: In step 2, have the teacher name the strategy, model it and say when and why it helps; observe some lessons to see whether that happened. Unprompted, teachers rarely make strategies explicit or mention their benefit, and see SRL as desirable but hard to fit in; professional development raised observed modelling in one programme, raised explicitness in a simulation-based one, and left explicit instruction rare in another. Expect smaller effects than researcher-delivered trials
rows.if: Classroom teachers deliver the regulation teaching
